title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄序
萬曆己卯秋浙江當大比士
及期巡按監察御史謝師啟
適至寔綱紀之于時前御史
王曉聘至學正王天策等旣
就館而提學僉事喬因阜選
士三千有奇鱗集待試御史
===
曰如故事於是提調則左布
政使勞堪右參政胡定監試
則副使徐元氣吳自新考試
則天策與學正陳節而同考
試則屬之敎諭李衡蕭繼庠
周仕階及訓導魯近智梁鶴
鳴胡誥徐臬王大夔焉御史
punctuated:
《浙江鄉試錄》序

萬曆己卯秋，浙江當大比士。及期，巡按監察御史謝師啟適至，寔綱紀之。于時，前御史王曉聘至學正王天策等，旣就館；而提學僉事喬因阜選士三千有奇，鱗集待試。御史曰：「如故事。」於是提調則左布政使勞堪、右參政胡定，監試則副使徐元氣、吳自新，考試則天策與學正陳節，而同考試則屬之敎諭李衡、蕭繼庠、周仕階及訓導魯近智、梁鶴鳴、胡誥、徐臬、王大夔焉。御史
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the jimao year of the Wanli era (1579), Zhejiang was due to hold the triennial examination of scholars. When the appointed time arrived, Regional Investigating Censor Xie Shiqi 謝師啟 happened to arrive and took overall charge of the proceedings. At that time, Department Director of Schools Wang Tiance 王天策 and others, who had been invited to serve by the former Censor Wang Xiao 王曉, had already taken up residence in the examination compound; meanwhile, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner for Education Qiao Yinfu 喬因阜 had selected more than three thousand scholars, who gathered like fish scales awaiting the examination. The Censor said: "Proceed according to precedent." Thereupon, serving as Proctors were Left Administration Commissioner Lao Kan 勞堪 and Right Administration Vice Commissioner Hu Ding 胡定; serving as Surveillance Officials of the Examination were Surveillance Vice Commissioners Xu Yuanqi 徐元氣 and Wu Zixin 吳自新; serving as Examiners were Tiance and Department Director of Schools Chen Jie 陳節; and the duties of Associate Examiners were entrusted to County Directors of Schools Li Heng 李衡, Xiao Jixiang 蕭繼庠, and Zhou Shijie 周仕階, as well as Assistant Instructors Lu Jinzhi 魯近智, Liang Heming 梁鶴鳴, Hu Gao 胡誥, Xu Nie 徐臬, and Wang Dakui 王大夔. The Censor…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
宣言師啟來自
京師
上方採言官建白下禮官議正文
體敦士習冀得眞才以裨實
用是在諸執事耳今日事所
不竭誠盡慎稱
上意指者有如
===
天日諸執事敬諾凡再旬竣事得
雋九十人籍氏名與文之優
者為錄以
獻御史謂天策宜序序曰昔我
高皇帝起南服剖鴻濛而開
日月當是時天造未寧首聘青田
劉基浦江宋濂龍泉章溢麗
punctuated: 宣言：「師啟來自京師，上方採言官建白，下禮官議正文體、敦士習，冀得眞才以裨實用，是在諸執事耳。今日事，所不竭誠盡慎、稱上意指者，有如天日！」諸執事敬諾。凡再旬竣事，得雋九十人，籍氏名與文之優者為錄以獻。御史謂天策宜序，序曰：昔我高皇帝起南服，剖鴻濛而開日月。當是時，天造未寧，首聘青田劉基、浦江宋濂、龍泉章溢、麗
translation_en:
… proclaimed: "I, Shi Qi 師啟, have just come from the Capital. His Majesty has recently adopted the proposals of the speaking officials and sent them down to the officials of the Ministry of Rites to deliberate on rectifying literary style and fostering the customs of scholars, hoping to obtain true talent to benefit practical governance. This rests entirely with all of you officiating personnel. In today's undertaking, should anyone fail to exhaust his sincerity and exercise the utmost caution in order to fulfill His Majesty's intentions, may Heaven and the Sun bear witness!" All the officiating personnel respectfully assented.

In twenty days the work was completed, yielding ninety successful candidates. Their names and surnames, together with the finest of their essays, were compiled into a record to be presented to the throne. The Censor said that I, Tiance 天策, ought to write a preface.

My preface reads: In former times, our Exalted Emperor (Gao Huangdi 高皇帝, the Hongwu Emperor) arose in the southern domain, cleaving the primordial chaos and opening up the sun and moon. At that time, the founding of the dynasty was not yet settled, yet he first summoned Liu Ji 劉基 of Qingtian 青田, Song Lian 宋濂 of Pujiang 浦江, Zhang Yi 章溢 of Longquan 龍泉, and [Ye Chen 葉琛] of Li[shui 麗水]…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
水葉琛焉置禮賢館稱四先
生
一代人文自此始四先生者皆
浙產也自是海內文章浙斌
斌稱首云
列聖培養餘二百年以至嘉隆之
際文章無慮數變宣弘以前
===
學宗程朱法本韓歐大都不
詭於六經蓋猶有四先生遺
意焉乃後士璆璆脩古名愈
引而上實愈趨而下初綴齊
梁其敝也靡麗而不達既型
左馬其敝也剽襲而不融頃
乃出入二氏浸淫百家其敝
punctuated: 水葉琛焉，置禮賢館，稱「四先生」。一代人文自此始，四先生者，皆浙產也。自是海內文章，浙斌斌稱首云。列聖培養餘二百年，以至嘉、隆之際，文章無慮數變。宣、弘以前，學宗程、朱，法本韓、歐，大都不詭於六經，蓋猶有四先生遺意焉。乃後士璆璆脩古，名愈引而上，實愈趨而下：初綴齊、梁，其敝也靡麗而不達；既型左、馬，其敝也剽襲而不融；頃乃出入二氏，浸淫百家，其敝
translation_en:
… Ye Chen 葉琛 of Lishui 麗水, establishing the Hall for Honoring Worthies (Lixian guan 禮賢館) and calling them the "Four Gentlemen." The literary culture of the dynasty began from this, and those Four Gentlemen were all natives of Zhejiang. From then on, in writing throughout the realm, Zhejiang, refined and accomplished, has been acclaimed first.

Through more than two hundred years of nurturing by the successive Emperors, down to the transition between the Jiajing 嘉靖 (1522–1566) and Longqing 隆慶 (1567–1572) reigns, literary style underwent several changes in general. Prior to the Xuande 宣德 (1426–1435) and Hongzhi 弘治 (1488–1505) eras, learning honored Cheng Yi 程頤, Cheng Hao 程顥, and Zhu Xi 朱熹 as its masters, while compositional method took Han Yu 韓愈 and Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩 as its models; for the most part it did not deviate from the Six Classics, and indeed still retained the legacy of the Four Gentlemen. Afterward, however, scholars with tinkling ornaments [?] cultivated antiquity: the higher they reached in name, the lower they sank in reality. At first they pieced together the styles of the Qi 齊 and Liang 梁 dynasties, whose defect was being ornate yet failing to convey meaning; next they modeled themselves on Zuo Qiuming 左丘明 and Sima Qian 司馬遷, whose defect was plagiarizing without integration; and recently they have gone in and out of the Two Teachings (Buddhism and Daoism) and steeped themselves in the Hundred Schools, whose defect…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也遂詖遁而叛于經一切弁
髦先進務爲宏廓深遠至勦
空寂之敎混敬靜之中崇虛
玄之說加禮法之上是明心
而非格物貴放達而賤持守
内宇宙而外經常先神奇而
後日用彼且糠秕堯舜醯雞
===
周孔芻狗六經何有於四先
生顧其端不知何從而全浙
之士靡然嚮風化肖最速故
海内文章代變以浙爲候夫
浙海壖水國也浙水出三天
子都而委錢塘苕水出天目
而委震澤嚴陵爲桐寶婺姑
punctuated: 也遂詖遁而叛于經。一切弁髦先進，務爲宏廓深遠。至勦空寂之敎，混敬靜之中；崇虛玄之說，加禮法之上；是明心而非格物，貴放達而賤持守，内宇宙而外經常，先神奇而後日用。彼且糠秕堯、舜，醯雞周、孔，芻狗六經，何有於四先生？顧其端不知何從，而全浙之士靡然嚮風，化肖最速，故海内文章代變，以浙爲候。夫浙，海壖水國也。浙水出三天子都而委錢塘，苕水出天目而委震澤，嚴陵爲桐，寶婺、姑…
translation_en: … has been to become biased and evasive, rebelling against the Classics. They utterly cast aside the earlier generations of scholars as useless, striving instead for what is grandiose and abstruse. It has reached the point where they plagiarize the teachings of emptiness and quiescence, mingling them into reverence and tranquility; they exalt theories of vacuity and mystery, placing them above ritual and law; they affirm illuminating the mind while rejecting the investigation of things; they prize unrestrained emancipation while despising steadfast adherence; they treat the cosmos as internal while treating constant norms as external; and they put the marvelous first while putting daily application last. They even regard Yao and Shun as mere chaff and husks, the Duke of Zhou and Confucius as vinegar flies, and the Six Classics as straw dogs—so what do the Four Masters matter to them? Yet though one knows not whence this trend originated, the scholars of all Zhejiang have been swept along by the wind, transforming and imitating most rapidly; thus, as literary writing within the seas changes from generation to generation, Zhejiang serves as the indicator. Now Zhejiang is a land of waters along the coast. The Zhe River issues from the Three Emperors' Capital [Santianzidu] mountains and empties into Qiantang; the Tiao River issues from Mount Tianmu and empties into Lake Zhenze [Lake Tai]; in Yanling it forms the Tong River, and in Baowu and Gu[mie]…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
蔑為瀓會稽若耶檇李四明
赤城並海東甌括蒼山溪暎
帶與郡邑錯壤如繡蓋其民
明秀而雅化則水國之恒也
夫欲正文體在敦士習欲求
實用在得眞才士習敦則眞
才出方今急務
===
上意指所在嚮風而化肖必淅先
也
天子務學躬化於穆清數布
功令廣厲學官明示以
德意有司者勤宣之士知嚮方矣
策幸從諸執事後目披心惟
諸士所稱述率本原經術當
punctuated: 蔑為瀓；會稽、若耶、檇李、四明、赤城並海；東甌、括蒼山溪暎帶，與郡邑錯壤如繡。蓋其民明秀而雅化，則水國之恒也。夫欲正文體，在敦士習；欲求實用，在得眞才。士習敦則眞才出，方今急務，上意指所在，嚮風而化肖，必淅先也。天子務學，躬化於穆清，數布功令，廣厲學官，明示以德意，有司者勤宣之，士知嚮方矣。策幸從諸執事後，目披心惟，諸士所稱述，率本原經術，當
translation_en:
…Gumie form the Cheng River; Kuaiji, Ruoye, Zuili, Siming, and Chicheng border the sea; and the mountains and streams of Dong'ou and Guacang reflect and girdle one another, interlocking with the prefectures and districts like embroidery. Indeed, that its people are bright, refined, and readily transformed by elegant culture is the constant nature of a land of waters.

Now, if one wishes to rectify literary style, it lies in cultivating the habits of scholars; if one wishes to seek practical utility, it lies in obtaining genuine talent. When the habits of scholars are cultivated, genuine talent emerges. In the urgent tasks of the present moment, toward which His Majesty's intentions point, in turning toward the wind and being transformed into likeness, Zhejiang will surely be the first!

The Son of Heaven devotes himself to learning and personally effects transformation from the serene heights of the palace. He has repeatedly promulgated regulations on academic evaluation to broadly encourage the educational officials, clearly manifesting his virtuous intentions. The local authorities have diligently proclaimed them, and the scholars now know the direction toward which they should turn.

I, [Tian] Ce, have had the good fortune to follow behind the various officiating functionaries, perusing with my eyes and pondering in my heart. What the scholars have set forth is generally rooted in classical learning, fitting…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
實中竅識達於時務無詖遁
叛經之蔽其最爾雅者庶幾
復見四先生焉天策竊津津
喜語諸執事文體不正乎士
習不敦乎御史𨞬所爲程督
諸執事者斯殆可以籍手矣
雖然士庶幾者四先生之文
===
耳夫文也豈所以爲四先生
者乎顧文之外天策又安能
知焉昔青田籌畫浦江問學
龍泉麗水政事姑孰公且推
讓焉詩有之鼓鍾于宮聲聞
于外鶴鳴于九皐聲聞于天
四先生者非嘗挾藝自售如
punctuated: 實中竅，識達於時務，無詖遁叛經之蔽；其最爾雅者，庶幾復見四先生焉。天策竊津津喜語諸執事：「文體不正乎？士習不敦乎？御史𨞬所爲程督諸執事者，斯殆可以籍手矣！」雖然，士庶幾者，四先生之文耳。夫文也，豈所以爲四先生者乎？顧文之外，天策又安能知焉？昔青田籌畫，浦江問學，龍泉、麗水政事，姑孰公且推讓焉。《詩》有之：「鼓鍾于宮，聲聞于外。」、「鶴鳴于九皐，聲聞于天。」四先生者，非嘗挾藝自售，如
translation_en: … substantive and hitting the mark, their insight reaching the affairs of the day without the blind spots of biased, evasive, or classic-defying speech; in the most refined and elegant among them, one might almost see the Four Masters [of early Ming Zhejiang: Liu Ji 劉基, Song Lian 宋濂, Zhang Yi 章溢, and Ye Chen 葉琛] once again. I, Tiance 天策, privately and with great delight said to the various officers in charge: "Has the literary style not been rectified? Have the scholars' habits not been made earnest? With this, we may well have something to present in fulfillment of what the Regional Inspector (Yushitai 御史臺) charged and supervised us to do!" Even so, what the scholars approximate is merely the literary writing of the Four Masters. Yet is literary writing really what made them the Four Masters? Beyond their writing, however, how could I, Tiance, know of them? In former times, for strategic planning there was Qingtian 青田 [Liu Ji], for scholarship and learning there was Pujiang 浦江 [Song Lian], and for governance and administration there were Longquan 龍泉 [Zhang Yi] and Lishui 麗水 [Ye Chen]—even the Duke of Gushu 姑孰公 [Tao An 陶安] deferred to them. As the Book of Odes (Shi 詩) has it: "Bells are drummed in the palace, and their sound is heard outside"; "The crane cries in the nine marshes, and its voice is heard in heaven." Those Four Masters never peddled their skills to promote themselves, as in…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
今之比于鄉也宮鼓皐鳴而
聲聞及之士何可以不務實
乎哉諸士進矣使言果可以
得人也
斧扆帷幄造膝披心參决密謀賛
定大計今兹有青田
細旃廣厦
===
金馬石渠啓沃
聖心潤色
洪業今兹有浦江端臺法從名藩
長吏董正官常周咨民隱今
兹有龍泉麗水
國家所庶幾實用者不必他求
即此有餘用矣不然文雖似
punctuated: 今之比于鄉也，宮鼓皐鳴而聲聞及之，士何可以不務實乎哉！諸士進矣，使言果可以得人也，斧扆帷幄，造膝披心，參决密謀，賛定大計，今兹有青田；細旃廣厦，金馬石渠，啓沃聖心，潤色洪業，今兹有浦江；端臺法從，名藩長吏，董正官常，周咨民隱，今兹有龍泉、麗水。國家所庶幾實用者，不必他求，即此有餘用矣。不然，文雖似，
translation_en: … compete in the provincial examinations today; yet like bells struck in the palace or cranes crying in the marshes, their renown reached afar. How then could scholars fail to devote themselves to substance! Now the gentlemen have been advanced. If through their words one can truly obtain the right men: then before the imperial screen and within the tent of command, drawing near the throne to bare one's heart, participating in decisions on confidential counsels, and assisting in settling great plans—do we have a Qingtian (Liu Ji 劉基) here today? Upon the fine felt rugs in the spacious halls, at the Golden Horse Gate and the Stone Conduit Pavilion, enlightening and enriching the sacred mind of the Emperor and embellishing the grand enterprise of the dynasty—do we have a Pujiang (Song Lian 宋濂) here today? In the Censorate and the imperial retinue, or as senior officials in renowned provinces, rectifying official discipline and inquiring thoroughly into the hidden sufferings of the people—do we have a Longquan (Zhang Yi 章溢) and a Lishui (Ye Chen 葉琛) here today? Those whom the state hopes to employ for practical service need not be sought elsewhere; right here there are more than enough for its use. Otherwise, even if their writings resemble…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
才非其眞也御史所爲矢天
日而期稱塞者謂何夫地以
人重非能重人科以士重非
能重士毋寧使人謂是科也
眞才實用肩相比也踵相接
也夫浙山川未改於昔也而
謂此九十人也者遂無四先
===
生出於其間乎天策等竊望
之矣是舉也總緝文武訓齊
士萌則有巡撫提督軍務右
僉都御史吳善言彰軌示俗
以風譽髦則有巡鹽監察御
史李棟而工部主事胡緒南
京戶部主事馮述武將使屬
punctuated:
才，非其眞也。御史所爲矢天日而期稱塞者，謂何？夫地以人重，非能重人；科以士重，非能重士。毋寧使人謂是科也，眞才實用，肩相比也，踵相接也。夫浙山川未改於昔也，而謂此九十人也者，遂無四先生出於其間乎？天策等竊望之矣。
是舉也，總緝文武、訓齊士萌，則有巡撫提督軍務右僉都御史吳善言；彰軌示俗、以風譽髦，則有巡鹽監察御史李棟；而工部主事胡緒、南京戶部主事馮述武將使屬
translation_en:
… talent, it is not genuine. What, then, would become of that for which the Censor has sworn before heaven and the sun in the hope of fulfilling his duty? Now, a place gains prestige from its people, rather than being able to lend prestige to people; an examination gains prestige from its scholars, rather than being able to lend prestige to scholars. Would it not be better to cause people to say of this examination cohort that those of genuine talent and practical utility stand shoulder to shoulder and follow closely on one another's heels? The mountains and rivers of Zhejiang have not changed from what they were in the past; how could it be said that among these ninety men there will not emerge figures like the Four Masters? Tiance and my colleagues earnestly hope for this.

In this undertaking, overseeing civil and military affairs as well as instructing and regulating scholars and the common people was Grand Coordinator and Superintendent of Military Affairs, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Wu Shanyan 吳善言; manifesting norms and guiding customs so as to inspire distinguished talents was Salt-Control Investigating Censor Li Dong 李棟; while Ministry of Works Secretary Hu Xu 胡緒 and Nanjing Ministry of Revenue Secretary Feng Shuwu 馮述武, happening to arrive on official missions, …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
至胥偕燕喜焉諸圍棘之外
咸勞在公者則右布政使滕
伯輪左叅政張楚城右叅政
王湘右叅議陳詔任惟一副
使陳誥周良臣張希召僉事
須用賔唐本堯署都指揮僉
事蔣木鄧子龍也與勞始事
===
以
嵩賀行者則左叅議徐廷祼右叅
議張子仁署都指揮僉事莊
重也請書之御史曰如故事
遂書
河南鄭州儒學學正王天策
謹序
punctuated:
至，胥偕燕喜焉。諸圍棘之外，咸勞在公者，則右布政使滕伯輪、左叅政張楚城、右叅政王湘、右叅議陳詔、任惟一、副使陳誥、周良臣、張希召、僉事須用賔、唐本堯、署都指揮僉事蔣木、鄧子龍也；與勞始事、以嵩賀行者，則左叅議徐廷祼、右叅議張子仁、署都指揮僉事莊重也。請書之。御史曰：「如故事。」遂書。
河南鄭州儒學學正王天策謹序。
translation_en:
… arrived just in time, and both joined in the celebratory banquet. As for those outside the thorny enclosure of the examination compound who all labored in the public service, they were Administration Commissioner of the Right Teng Bolun 滕伯輪; Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left Zhang Chucheng 張楚城; Administration Vice Commissioner of the Right Wang Xiang 王湘; Assistant Administration Commissioners of the Right Chen Zhao 陳詔 and Ren Weiyi 任惟一; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Chen Gao 陳誥, Zhou Liangchen 周良臣, and Zhang Xizhao 張希召; Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Xu Yongbin 須用賔 and Tang Benyao 唐本堯; and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Jiang Mu 蔣木 and Deng Zilong 鄧子龍. Those who shared in the labors at the outset of the affair and then departed to offer imperial birthday congratulations were Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Left Xu Tingguan 徐廷祼, Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Right Zhang Ziren 張子仁, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Zhuang Zhong 莊重. When asked whether their names should be recorded, the Censor said, "Follow precedent." And so they have been recorded.

Respectfully prefaced by Wang Tiance 王天策, Director of Studies of the Subprefectural Confucian School of Zhengzhou in Henan.

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
士不可以不弘毅任重而道遠
質諸鬼神而無疑知天也百世以俟聖人
而不惑知人也是故君子動而世為天
下道行而世為天下法言而世為天下
則遠之則有望近之則不厭
賢者在位能者在職國家閒暇及是時明
其政刑雖大國必畏之矣詩云迨天之
===
未陰雨徹彼桑土綢繆牖戶今此下民
或敢侮予孔子曰為此詩者其知道乎
能治其國家誰敢侮之
易
天地養萬物聖人養賢以及萬民頤之時
大矣哉
九二之孚有喜也
夫易聖人所以崇德而廣業也知崇禮卑
崇效天卑法地
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

士不可以不弘毅，任重而道遠。
質諸鬼神而無疑，知天也；百世以俟聖人而不惑，知人也。是故君子動而世為天下道，行而世為天下法，言而世為天下則，遠之則有望，近之則不厭。
賢者在位，能者在職，國家閒暇，及是時，明其政刑，雖大國必畏之矣。《詩》云：「迨天之未陰雨，徹彼桑土，綢繆牖戶。今此下民，或敢侮予？」孔子曰：「為此詩者，其知道乎！能治其國家，誰敢侮之？」

易

天地養萬物，聖人養賢以及萬民，頤之時大矣哉！
九二之孚，有喜也。
夫《易》，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books (Sishu)

1. A gentleman may not be without breadth of mind and resolute endurance, for his burden is heavy and his course is long.
2. He presents himself before spiritual beings without question: he knows Heaven. He waits a hundred generations for a sage without perplexity: he knows men. Therefore, the movements of the superior man mark out for ages the path of All under Heaven; his actions are for ages a law to All under Heaven; his words are for ages a standard for All under Heaven. Those who are far from him look up to him with longing, and those who are near do not grow weary of him.
3. If men of virtue are in high positions and men of ability are in offices, and the state takes advantage of times of peace and leisure to clarify its governance and punishments, then even great states will certainly stand in awe of it. The Book of Odes (Shi) says: "Before the sky is dark with rain, I take the root-bark of the mulberry tree and bind tight my window and door. Now, you people below, who among you dares to insult me?" Confucius said: "Did not the maker of this ode understand the Way? If one is able to govern his state, who will dare to insult him?"

The Book of Changes (Yi)

1. Heaven and earth nourish the myriad things; the sage nourishes men of worth so as to reach the myriad people. Great indeed is the timeliness of Nourishment (Yi)!
2. The sincerity of the Nine in the Second Place brings joy.
3. By means of the Changes, the sages exalted their virtue and broadened their enterprise. Wisdom is exalted and ritual is humble; in being exalted one imitates Heaven, and in being humble one models oneself on Earth.

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
乾以君之
書
帝曰來禹汝亦昌言禹拜曰都帝予何言
予思日孜孜
九州攸同四隩旣宅九山刋旅九川滌源
九澤旣陂四海會同
不役耳目百度惟貞
唐虞稽古建官惟百內有百揆四岳外有
州牧侯伯庶政惟和萬國咸寧夏商官
===
倍亦克用乂明王立政不惟其官惟其
人
詩
羔裘豹飾孔武有力彼其之子邦之司直
羔裘晏兮三英粲兮彼其之子邦之彥
兮
旣齊旣稷旣匡旣敕
思齊大任文王之母思媚周姜京室之婦
大姒嗣徽音則百斯男
punctuated:
乾以君之。

書：
帝曰：「來！禹，汝亦昌言。」禹拜曰：「都！帝，予何言？予思日孜孜。」
九州攸同，四隩旣宅，九山刋旅，九川滌源，九澤旣陂，四海會同。
不役耳目，百度惟貞。
唐虞稽古，建官惟百；內有百揆、四岳，外有州牧、侯、伯，庶政惟和，萬國咸寧。夏商官倍，亦克用乂。明王立政，不惟其官，惟其人。

詩：
羔裘豹飾，孔武有力。彼其之子，邦之司直。羔裘晏兮，三英粲兮。彼其之子，邦之彥兮。
旣齊旣稷，旣匡旣敕。
思齊大任，文王之母，思媚周姜，京室之婦。大姒嗣徽音，則百斯男。
translation_en:
Qian rules over them.

Book of Documents (Shu):
The Sovereign said, "Come, Yu! Do you also make a splendid speech." Yu bowed and said, "Oh! Sovereign, what can I say? I think only of being diligent day by day."
Throughout the nine provinces a similar order was effected: the grounds along the waters in the four quarters were made habitable; the hills of the nine provinces were cleared of their timber and opened to passage; the sources of the nine rivers were cleared out; the nine marshes were banked up; and the four seas had their waters harmoniously brought together.
Do not be enslaved by your ears and eyes, and all your measures will be right.
Tang and Yu studied antiquity and established a hundred offices. At court there were the General Regulator and the Four Mountains; outside there were the Pastors of the Provinces and the Archer-lords and Earls. Thus the various departments of government went on harmoniously, and the myriad states all enjoyed repose. Under the Xia and Shang, the number of officers was doubled, and they were still able to maintain good governance. Ancient enlightened kings, in establishing their government, cared not so much about the number of the offices as about the men.

Book of Odes (Shi):
Lamb's fur, with leopard-skin cuffs, very martial and strong! That man there is the upholder of uprightness in the state. Lamb's fur, so splendid, with its three ornaments so bright! That man there is the ornament of the state.
You have been exact and expeditious; you have been upright and careful.
Reverent was Tai Ren, the mother of King Wen; loving was she to Zhou Jiang — a wife for the royal house. Tai Si inherited her excellent fame, and of her were born a hundred sons.

When he inspires them with awe, none fails to tremble and submit; he attracts and pacifies all the spirits, even to the Yellow River and the lofty peaks.
Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
In spring, the Marquis of Qi, a man of Song, a man of Chen, a man of Cai, and a man of Zhu met at Beixing. [Thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang] In summer, in the sixth month, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, and the Earl of Zheng, and together made a covenant at You. The Duke met the Marquis of Jin and the Viscount of Wu at Huangchi. [Thirteenth year of Duke Ai]

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其敎不易其俗齊其政不易其宜
是故情見而義立樂終而德尊
詩云豐水有芑武王豈不仕詒厥孫謀以
燕翼子數世之仁也
敎順成俗外內和順國家理治此之謂盛
德
第貳場
論
古之學者爲己
===
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢賜民今年田租之半詔〔文帝二年〕
擬唐以左僕射房玄齡爲太子少師誥〔貞觀十三年〕
擬虜酋俺答率西夷烏思藏鎖南堅參等
求
貢方物羣臣
賀表〔萬曆七年〕
判語〔五條〕
punctuated:
其敎，不易其俗；齊其政，不易其宜。
是故情見而義立，樂終而德尊。
《詩》云：「豐水有芑，武王豈不仕？詒厥孫謀，以燕翼子。」數世之仁也。
敎順成俗，外內和順，國家理治，此之謂盛德。

第貳場
論：
古之學者爲己。
詔、誥、表〔內科一道〕：
擬漢賜民今年田租之半詔〔文帝二年〕。
擬唐以左僕射房玄齡爲太子少師誥〔貞觀十三年〕。
擬虜酋俺答率西夷烏思藏鎖南堅參等求貢方物羣臣賀表〔萬曆七年〕。
判語〔五條〕：
translation_en:
… [cultivate] their teachings without changing their customs; they standardize their governance without changing what is suitable to them.
Therefore, genuine feelings are manifested and righteousness is established; when the music concludes, virtue is revered.
The Book of Odes (Shi) says: "By the Feng River grows the white millet; how could King Wu not take up the work? He bequeathed his plans to his grandsons, to give comfort and support to his sons." This was benevolence extending for several generations.
When instruction is compliant, it forms customs; when outside and inside are harmonious and compliant, and the state and family are well-ordered, this is called flourishing virtue.

Second Session
Discourse:
"The scholars of antiquity learned for their own sake."
Edict (zhao), Mandate (gao), or Memorial (biao) [examined on one topic]:
Imitation of a Han edict granting the people a reduction of half of this year's land tax [2nd year of Emperor Wen (178 BCE)].
Imitation of a Tang mandate appointing Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs (zuo puye) Fang Xuanling 房玄齡 as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent (taizi shaoshi) [13th year of the Zhenguan era (639)].
Imitation of a congratulatory memorial from the assembled officials on the barbarian chieftain Altan (Anda 俺答) leading the Western barbarians of Ü-Tsang (Wusizang 烏思藏), Sonam Gyatso (Suonan Jianshen 鎖南堅參), and others to request permission to present local products as tribute [7th year of the Wanli era (1579)].

text:
官員襲廕
磨勘卷宗
荒蕪田地
優恤軍屬
帶造段疋
第叄場
策五道
問王者假廟追崇祖考以廣孝思至鉅典
也蓋廟有時享有大祫位祝稱配倫紀
===
攸崇可不斤斤理順易則哉我
太祖高皇帝建
廟闕左崇
四親侑以
壽春諸王
成祖文皇帝建
廟北平崇
太祖
四親侑進如之因親及親世祝稱配章明矣
punctuated:
官員襲廕、磨勘卷宗、荒蕪田地、優恤軍屬、帶造段疋。

第叄場

策五道

問：王者假廟追崇祖考，以廣孝思，至鉅典也。蓋廟有時享、有大祫，位祝稱配，倫紀攸崇，可不斤斤理順易則哉？我太祖高皇帝建廟闕左，崇四親，侑以壽春諸王；成祖文皇帝建廟北平，崇太祖、四親，侑進如之。因親及親，世祝稱配，章明矣。
translation_en:
Hereditary Privilege for Officials; Reviewing Case Dossiers; Uncultivated Farmland; Compassionate Relief for Military Dependents; Supplementary Weaving of Satin Bolts.

Third Session

Five Policy Questions

Question: That a true king approaches the ancestral temple to posthumously venerate his ancestors and deceased father in order to broaden his filial thoughts is the most momentous of state rituals. Now, the ancestral temple has seasonal sacrifices and the great collective sacrifice (da xia); the tablet placements, invocatory titles, and auxiliary pairings are wherein human relationships and moral order are exalted—how could one not be meticulously attentive to keeping the principles harmonious and the norms straightforward? Our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu), established the ancestral temple to the left of the palace gates, venerating his Four Direct Ancestors and associating the Prince of Shouchun and the other princes with them in sacrifice. The Accomplished Progenitor, Emperor Wen (Chengzu), established the ancestral temple in Beiping, venerating the Grand Progenitor and the Four Direct Ancestors, and associating and advancing the others in the same manner. Extending affection from one's nearest kin to further kin, the generational invocations and matching tablets were manifestly clear.

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
列聖繼承誕章軌屬
憲宗純皇帝時已備
九廟至
世宗肅皇帝特進
獻考其時祫之禮或推自
太祖而上或斷自
太祖而下有祧無祧特享合享儻可得詳與且
九廟祀先制備矣迺時享祝辭間稱
八廟六廟五廟至已列六廟而猶仍五廟之稱
===
世次名義其於何乃歲暮
大祫祧廟咸升而以
壽春十五王配享議者謂諸王於
太祖爲伯爲兄爲姪而槩稱
皇曾伯祖順乎今位次孰當緒正
徽號孰當通列稱謂宜如何頃議下掌故具
上裁定之昭夏幽鬯垂之千億諸生宜悉著其
義而覽焉
問傳有之衆言殽亂折諸聖今之世去聖
punctuated:
列聖繼承，誕章軌屬。憲宗純皇帝時，已備九廟；至世宗肅皇帝，特進獻考。其時祫之禮，或推自太祖而上，或斷自太祖而下，有祧、無祧，特享、合享，儻可得詳與？且九廟祀先，制備矣；迺時享祝辭，間稱八廟、六廟、五廟，至已列六廟而猶仍五廟之稱，世次名義，其於何？乃歲暮大祫，祧廟咸升，而以壽春十五王配享。議者謂諸王於太祖爲伯、爲兄、爲姪，而槩稱「皇曾伯祖」，順乎？今位次孰當緒正，徽號孰當通列，稱謂宜如何？頃議下掌故，具上裁定之，昭夏幽鬯，垂之千億。諸生宜悉著其義而覽焉。
問：傳有之：「衆言殽亂，折諸聖。」今之世去聖
translation_en:
As the successive emperors inherited the throne, they broadly manifested the standard rules. By the time of Emperor Xianzong Chun (the Chenghua Emperor), the Nine Ancestral Temples were already complete; when it came to Emperor Shizong Su (the Jiajing Emperor), he specially elevated his Deceased Father Xian (Emperor Ruizong). Regarding the rites of the seasonal and collective sacrifices at that time—whether traced upward from Taizu or demarcated downward from Taizu, which tablets were removed to the distant-ancestor shrine and which were not, and when sacrifices were offered individually or collectively—can you perhaps give a detailed account of these? Moreover, with the Nine Temples for sacrificing to the ancestors, the institution was complete; yet in the invocatory prayers for the seasonal sacrifices, reference was occasionally made to eight temples, six temples, or five temples, to the point where even after six temples had been arrayed, the designation of "five temples" was still retained. In terms of generational sequence and the justification of names, how is this to be explained [?]? Furthermore, at the great collective sacrifice at the close of the year, the spirits from the shrines of removed ancestors are all brought up to join, and the fifteen princes headed by the Prince of Shouchun are associated in the offerings. Deliberators argue that those princes stood in relation to Taizu as uncles, elder brothers, or nephews; is it fitting, then, to refer to them all uniformly as "Imperial Great-Grand-Uncles"? At present, whose tablet positions ought to be rectified in their order, whose honorific titles ought to be comprehensively listed, and what should their forms of address properly be? Recently, deliberations have been handed down to the ritual authorities so that all may be submitted to His Majesty for final determination, making the rites resplendent in the visible world and reaching the unseen spirits, to be handed down for a hundred billion years. You students should fully set forth the principles involved so that they may be reviewed.

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
人遠矣竅言聿興塗塞耳目後生遞相
聞習愈益滅真將安所折衷乎即如孔
子自生民以來未有盛焉者也乃莊列
諸家極其詆訾而遷史信之一何無擇
之甚與試舉其一二商核焉正考父銘
鼎之詞與徵在禱於尼丘之事並著孔
子世家而郰曼父之母防山之反告則
檀弓備載之三都之墮夾谷之會信所
以存魯也假令其所以折衝之策第如
===
左氏所稱說亦殊不類哉亟見老聃盜
跖之徒輒至自失抑何憊也遇少源阿
谷之婦不厭與言毋乃瀆乎學琴師襄
何以遂見文王登泰山之巔何以望見
吳門之馬六尺之杖何以別親疎之倫
一飯之桃何以定貴賤之等狸歌原壤
曷弗絕之請討陳恒又奚校量焉以至
占桓僖之廟災誠始皇以遺讖萍實商
羊之異與夫黑牛白犢之生何其言盡
punctuated: 人遠矣，竅言聿興，塗塞耳目，後生遞相聞習，愈益滅真，將安所折衷乎？即如孔子，自生民以來未有盛焉者也，乃莊、列諸家極其詆訾，而遷史信之，一何無擇之甚與！試舉其一二商核焉。正考父銘鼎之詞，與徵在禱於尼丘之事，並著《孔子世家》，而郰曼父之母、防山之反告，則《檀弓》備載之。三都之墮、夾谷之會，信所以存魯也，假令其所以折衝之策第如左氏所稱說，亦殊不類哉！亟見老聃、盜跖之徒，輒至自失，抑何憊也！遇少源、阿谷之婦，不厭與言，毋乃瀆乎？學琴師襄，何以遂見文王？登泰山之巔，何以望見吳門之馬？六尺之杖，何以別親疎之倫？一飯之桃，何以定貴賤之等？狸歌原壤，曷弗絕之？請討陳恒，又奚校量焉？以至占桓、僖之廟災，誠始皇以遺讖，萍實、商羊之異，與夫黑牛、白犢之生，何其言盡…
translation_en: … the sages are far removed in time. Specious words [?] have arisen, stopping up ears and eyes. Later generations pass them down and study them, increasingly obliterating the truth—where, then, shall we turn for a balanced judgment? Take Confucius, for instance: since the birth of mankind, there has never been anyone greater than he. Yet the schools of Zhuangzi and Liezi disparaged him to the utmost, and Sima Qian's history (Shiji) gave credence to them—how utterly indiscriminate! Let us cite one or two examples to discuss and verify them. The words of Zheng Kaofu's tripod inscription and the affair of Yan Zhengzai praying at Mount Ni are both recorded in the "Hereditary House of Confucius" (Kongzi shijia), while the mother of Zou Manfu and the report upon returning from Mount Fang are fully documented in the "Tangong" chapter [of the Record of Rites]. The dismantling of the three capitals and the meeting at Jiagu were truly the means by which Lu was preserved; yet even supposing his strategies for repelling aggression were merely as Master Zuo (Zuozhuan) describes them, how utterly out of character that would be! Repeatedly going to see the likes of Lao Dan and Robber Zhi, and each time losing his composure—how pathetic that would be! Encountering the women of Shaoyuan and Agu and not tiring of conversing with them—would that not be improper familiarity? In learning the zither from Music Master Xiang, how did he come to see King Wen? Ascending the peak of Mount Tai, how could he gaze upon a horse at the gates of Wu? How could a six-chi staff distinguish the degrees of kinship, and how could a peach offered at a meal determine the ranks of noble and base? When Yuan Rang sang the "wildcat" song, why did Confucius not sever relations with him? In requesting to punish Chen Heng, why would he calculate the relative strength of forces? And when it comes to divining the fire in the temples of Dukes Huan and Xi, warning the First Emperor [of Qin] with a left-behind prophecy, the marvels of the duckweed fruit and the shangyang bird, and the birth of a white calf from a black cow—how is it that his words were all…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有徵而土精之惟專車之骨肅愼氏之
矢卽又一一物色之是果盡出于孔子
與抑亦好事者爲之無足稽也夫季由
傳誣子順變色瘠環蜚語孟子抗辭諸
生誦法孔子不宜嘿嘿任其哆言無當
而已試相與辨難之
問
國家之於需才至勤矣今歲大比當計羣吏
又進子大夫令與計偕凡以辨材而用
===
之也吾遂與子言辨材之方焉古者稱
人之賢通謂之才今考其所數爲材者
率德行也或以德稱而其所列爲德又
多材能之號蓋仲尼孟子之說書記所
稱高陽高辛氏之類可睹已自材德分
之說出而諸儒百家言人人殊矣有云
才下而德尊者有曰德易而才難者其
說何遵有云以德爲目以材自名者有
曰德立則五才無殆五見則德無位者
punctuated:
有徵，而土精之惟、專車之骨、肅愼氏之矢，卽又一一物色之，是果盡出于孔子與？抑亦好事者爲之，無足稽也？夫季由傳誣，子順變色；瘠環蜚語，孟子抗辭。諸生誦法孔子，不宜嘿嘿，任其哆言無當而已，試相與辨難之。

問：國家之於需才，至勤矣。今歲大比，當計羣吏，又進子大夫，令與計偕，凡以辨材而用之也。吾遂與子言辨材之方焉。古者稱人之賢，通謂之才，今考其所數爲材者，率德行也；或以德稱，而其所列爲德，又多材能之號。蓋仲尼、孟子之說，書記所稱高陽、高辛氏之類，可睹已。自材德分之說出，而諸儒百家言人人殊矣。有云才下而德尊者，有曰德易而才難者，其說何遵？有云以德爲目、以材自名者，有曰德立則五才無殆、五見則德無位者，
translation_en:
… proved true; and as for the anomaly [惟, read 怪] of the earth spirit, the bone that filled a whole cart, and the arrow of the Sushen clan, he even identified each of them one by one—did all of this truly come from Confucius? Or was it fabricated by meddlesome people and not worth verifying? When false rumors were spread about Jiyou (Zilu 子路), Zishun (Kong斌) changed countenance; when baseless gossip circulated about Jihuan (Yong Qu 癰疽 and侍人瘠環), Mencius protested strongly. You students recite and model yourselves on Confucius; you ought not remain silent and merely let them talk extravagantly and without foundation. Try to debate and refute these points together.

Question: The dynasty is most diligent in its need for talent. In this year of the Great Triennial Examination, when the various officials are to be evaluated, you gentlemen are also advanced and ordered to travel along with the reporting officials—all in order to discern talent and employ it. I shall therefore speak with you on the method of discerning talent. In antiquity, when praising a person's worthiness, it was generally called "talent" (cai 才). Yet if we examine today what they enumerated as talent, it was mostly moral conduct; conversely, sometimes people were praised for "virtue" (de 德), and yet what were listed as virtues were mostly designations for practical abilities. Indeed, in the teachings of Confucius and Mencius, and in what historical records say of the clans of Gaoyang and Gaoxin and the like, this can readily be seen. Ever since the theory separating talent and virtue emerged, the various Confucian scholars and hundred schools have each offered different views. Some say that talent is inferior and virtue exalted, while others say that virtue is easy and talent difficult—which doctrine should be followed? Some say that virtue is taken as the overarching category while talents are named after specific capacities, while others say that when virtue is established the five talents are free from peril, whereas when the five are displayed externally virtue loses its place—…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其義何稱於是方人者則曰某也德某
也才上德者曰與才有餘而德不足也
不若才不足而德有餘也而喜才者又
曰與其德勝於才也毋寧才勝德一人
之身異指殊好豈才德誠兩端乎意者
今之所謂才德非古之才德與將後世
之衡鏡亦與古異也吾觀今之好惡取
舍亦多岐矣若是而胡能無賣璞之誚
也又將無有懷璞而不能自明者乎夫
===
儒者持論要於其當固不可膠守舊聞
以耳食也吾嘗聞説劔相馬之術而得
相人之道焉今當與諸生究之共由大
道也
問氏族之敎遐哉尚矣古者因族立宗因
宗系姓重本之士靡不家聯戶比繩繩
而世守之烏睹所稱譜牒云廼近世宗
法廢而天下無世家司馬氏覽觀往古
始作帝紀述世家而議譜者往往宗焉
punctuated:
其義何稱？於是方人者則曰：「某也德，某也才。」上德者曰：「與才有餘而德不足也，不若才不足而德有餘也。」而喜才者又曰：「與其德勝於才也，毋寧才勝德。」一人之身，異指殊好，豈才德誠兩端乎？意者今之所謂才德，非古之才德與？將後世之衡鏡，亦與古異也？吾觀今之好惡取舍亦多岐矣，若是，而胡能無賣璞之誚也？又將無有懷璞而不能自明者乎？夫儒者持論，要於其當，固不可膠守舊聞，以耳食也。吾嘗聞説劔相馬之術，而得相人之道焉，今當與諸生究之，共由大道也。
問：氏族之敎，遐哉尚矣！古者因族立宗，因宗系姓，重本之士，靡不家聯戶比，繩繩而世守之，烏睹所稱譜牒云？廼近世宗法廢而天下無世家，司馬氏覽觀往古，始作帝紀，述世家，而議譜者往往宗焉。
translation_en:
…what meaning do these express? Consequently, those who evaluate people say: "So-and-so is a person of virtue; so-and-so is a person of talent." Those who prize virtue say: "Rather than having a surplus of talent and a deficiency of virtue, it is better to have a deficiency of talent and a surplus of virtue." Yet those who favor talent say in turn: "Rather than having virtue surpass talent, it is better for talent to surpass virtue." Within a single person, assessments differ and preferences diverge—are talent and virtue truly two separate extremes? Could it be that what is called talent and virtue today is not the talent and virtue of antiquity? Or is it that the balance scales and mirrors of later ages also differ from those of antiquity? As I observe the likes and dislikes, the selections and rejections of the present day, they too diverge in many directions. If it is like this, how can one avoid the ridicule of selling an uncarved rat as jade [賣璞]? And will there not also be those who clasp an uncarved jade in their bosom yet cannot make their worth known for themselves? Now, when Confucian scholars maintain a discourse, the essential thing is that it be fitting; surely one must not stubbornly cling to old hearsay and feed merely on what one hears. I have heard of the arts of discussing swords and judging horses, and from them have grasped the way of judging men; today I ought to investigate this thoroughly with you students, so that together we may follow the Great Way.

Question: Teaching regarding clans and lineages goes back to distant antiquity indeed! In ancient times, lineages were established on the basis of clans, and surnames were tied together on the basis of lineages. Gentlemen who valued their roots without exception linked their families and joined their households, maintaining them continuously from generation to generation—where did one ever see what are called genealogical registers? Yet in more recent ages, the lineage system fell into disuse and the realm had no hereditary houses. Sima [Qian 司馬遷] surveyed remote antiquity and first composed the "Basic Annal of the Emperors" and recounted the "Hereditary Houses," and those who discuss genealogies have time and again taken him as their model. …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
故漢譜萬姓並篇氏族魏立中正爰置
九品晉宋以後競相崇重百家有譜百
官有牒官氏有志至李唐尤盛矣氏族
姓系志錄並垂衣冠永泰篇目繁侈而
韻略韻譜又以聲辨族諸若此類議者
多有所是非以余所聞譜牒家言毋亦
有所祖述乎何其與古謬盭也君子慨
然思古宗法而勢不可行矣故於譜牒
致意焉昔宋世言宗譜者二家曰廬陵
===
歐陽氏曰眉山蘇氏今其法綦然覈也
亦可倣而行之否多士慕古昔而尊本
源懷敦睦之思幸爲我言其槩
問天下之法久則必敝敝則必通其變變
通所以救敝也然敝或從生焉然則法
終不可變乎利害得失固相倚伏而不
可絕乎將翟翦所謂舉大木者乎抑用
餤者之殊乎智者之所以搤掔深思諏
咨而求也往者畫里輪年而事民民患
punctuated:
故漢譜《萬姓》，並篇《氏族》；魏立中正，爰置九品；晉、宋以後，競相崇重。《百家》有譜，《百官》有牒，《官氏》有志。至李唐尤盛矣，《氏族》、《姓系》，志錄並垂；《衣冠》、《永泰》，篇目繁侈；而《韻略》、《韻譜》，又以聲辨族。諸若此類，議者多有所是非。以余所聞，譜牒家言，毋亦有所祖述乎？何其與古謬盭也？君子慨然思古宗法，而勢不可行矣，故於譜牒致意焉。昔宋世言宗譜者二家：曰廬陵歐陽氏，曰眉山蘇氏。今其法綦然覈也，亦可倣而行之否？多士慕古昔而尊本源，懷敦睦之思，幸爲我言其槩。

問：天下之法，久則必敝，敝則必通其變，變通所以救敝也；然敝或從生焉。然則法終不可變乎？利害得失，固相倚伏而不可絕乎？將翟翦所謂舉大木者乎？抑用餤者之殊乎？智者之所以搤掔深思、諏咨而求也。往者畫里輪年而事民，民患…
translation_en:
…Therefore, in the Han dynasty they compiled the Genealogy of Ten Thousand Surnames (Wanxing pu) alongside treatises on clans and lineages (Shizu pian); the Wei dynasty established the Impartial and Just (zhongzheng) officials and thereby instituted the Nine Ranks (jiupin); and from the Jin and Liu-Song dynasties onward, people vied with one another in prizing genealogical status. There was the Genealogy of the Hundred Clans (Baijia pu), the Register of the Hundred Officials (Baiguan die), and the Treatise on Official Clans (Guanshi zhi). By the time of the Li-Tang dynasty, this practice flourished even more: treatises and records on clans and surname lineages (Shizu zhi, Xingxi lu) were handed down together; works on eminent families and those of the Yongtai era (Yiguan, Yongtai) had prolific and extravagant headings; and the Rhyme Compendium (Yunlüe) and Rhyme Genealogy (Yunpu) further distinguished lineages by phonetic rhyme. Regarding all works of this sort, critics have found much to praise and to fault. From what I have heard, do not the teachings of the genealogists also have ancient precedents they follow? Why then are they so at odds with antiquity? Gentlemen sigh with longing for the ancient lineage system (zongfa), yet circumstances make it impossible to put into practice; therefore, they devote their attention to genealogical registers. In the past, during the Song dynasty, there were two masters who discussed clan genealogies: the Ouyang clan of Luling and the Su clan of Meishan. Today their methods remain extraordinarily rigorous and clear; can they also be emulated and put into practice or not? You many scholars admire antiquity, revere your origins, and cherish thoughts of kin harmony—please set forth the general outlines for me.

Question: When the laws of the empire have been in place for a long time, they inevitably deteriorate; when they deteriorate, one must adapt to change, for adaptation is the means to remedy deterioration. Yet new abuses sometimes arise right out of such changes. Can laws, then, never be changed after all? Do benefit and harm, gain and loss, inherently depend on and give rise to one another such that abuses can never be eradicated? Is it like what Zhai Jian called lifting a great timber? Or does it depend on the difference in those who administer the remedy [literally, "use the bait/food"]? This is why wise men clasp their wrists in deep reflection, inquiring and consulting in search of an answer. In the past, communities (li) were demarcated to serve in rotation by the year, and the people suffered…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
苦之故通計而賦之以弛民法良便也
而不便者復隨而摘其弊壤賦不均百
姓喁喁見病故有丈量均田之令意至
勤也無何而病者又見告矣夫彼摘者
告者寧無當乎然誠以是二者較之往
事終焉孰得也鄉約所以訓俗也而行
之不效世見詆焉迂保甲所以輯衆也
而法未徧行民已厭其擾然則是二者
卒不可行乎嗟夫井田封建先王之良
===
法也而時移勢變訟議紛紜古今一轍
所從來矣寧渠如前所云四事乎惟兹
四者子鄉黨父兄之計而異日者諸生
為吏之師也願聞所宜罷行之畫
punctuated: 苦之，故通計而賦之以弛民，法良便也。而不便者復隨而摘其弊。壤賦不均，百姓喁喁見病，故有丈量均田之令，意至勤也。無何，而病者又見告矣。夫彼摘者、告者，寧無當乎？然誠以是二者較之往事，終焉孰得也？鄉約所以訓俗也，而行之不效，世見詆焉迂；保甲所以輯衆也，而法未徧行，民已厭其擾。然則是二者，卒不可行乎？嗟夫！井田、封建，先王之良法也，而時移勢變，訟議紛紜，古今一轍，所從來矣，寧渠如前所云四事乎？惟兹四者，子鄉黨父兄之計，而異日者諸生為吏之師也。願聞所宜罷行之畫。
translation_en: …suffered bitterly from it, and therefore an overall calculation was made to levy the tax so as to give relief to the people [the Single Whip reform]. The law was truly convenient, yet those who found it inconvenient soon followed by pointing out its abuses. Because the land taxes were unequal and the common people were clamoring about their distress, there was the order to survey and measure the land to equalize the fields; the intention was most diligent. Before long, however, those aggrieved by it again came forward with complaints. Now, are those who point out flaws and those who bring complaints entirely without justification? Yet if we truly compare these two measures with past practices, which in the end is more advantageous? The community compact (xiangyue) is the means to instruct customs, yet when practiced without effect, the world disparages it as impractical; the mutual security system (baojia) is the means to bring the multitude into harmony, yet before the law has been universally implemented, the people already resent its disruption. Does this mean, then, that these two measures ultimately cannot be put into practice? Alas! The well-field (jingtian) and enfeoffment (fengjian) systems were the fine institutions of the former kings, yet as times changed and circumstances shifted, disputes and debates arose in profusion. Past and present follow the same track—it has been this way for a long time. How could it be limited merely to the four matters mentioned above? Still, these four matters are the concern of the fathers and elder brothers of your home communities, and in the future they will serve as guides for you students when you become officials. I wish to hear your plans regarding what ought to be abolished and what ought to be put into practice.
