title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也吳晉爭長晉長吳矣經先晉者紀常也吳僭
王矣經書子者正名也以合兩伯而言及者不
以吳先晉又不欲泯其寔以著其强而抑之也
夫此一會也而聖人惓惓若此者何哉蓋中國
有常尊夷狄無常盛所以治內御外者在我而
已惟玆晉也可後於吳哉固宗盟之長也墮其
世業而遽為吳下惡能振其式微之運乎經斯
世者欲使中國常處其尊以制夷狄不可無疆
治之猷矣吳也可先晉哉固僭王之夷也馮其
===
積威而晉不與校胡以遏其方張之勢乎經斯
世者欲使夷狄常處其卑以奉中國不可無制
御之策矣存亡者天也以人勝天則天可必徒
諉於天而拂天地之經以幸於無亡吾未見其
能國也順逆者理也以理勝勢則勢不足恃徒
狃於勢而忘冠屨之分以即安目前恐不可一
朝居也聖人至此有深慮焉故先晉狄吳而特
書及訓後世以治中國御四夷之道至深切矣
以此垂訓而後世猶有位上侯王之議稱臣突
punctuated: 也，吳、晉爭長。晉長吳矣，經先晉者，紀常也；吳僭王矣，經書「子」者，正名也；以合兩伯而言「及」者，不以吳先晉，又不欲泯其寔，以著其强而抑之也。夫此一會也，而聖人惓惓若此者，何哉？蓋中國有常尊，夷狄無常盛，所以治內御外者，在我而已。惟玆晉也，可後於吳哉？固宗盟之長也，墮其世業而遽為吳下，惡能振其式微之運乎？經斯世者，欲使中國常處其尊以制夷狄，不可無疆治之猷矣。吳也，可先晉哉？固僭王之夷也，馮其積威而晉不與校，胡以遏其方張之勢乎？經斯世者，欲使夷狄常處其卑以奉中國，不可無制御之策矣。存亡者，天也，以人勝天則天可必；徒諉於天而拂天地之經，以幸於無亡，吾未見其能國也。順逆者，理也，以理勝勢則勢不足恃；徒狃於勢而忘冠屨之分，以即安目前，恐不可一朝居也。聖人至此，有深慮焉。故先晉、狄吳而特書「及」，訓後世以治中國、御四夷之道，至深切矣。以此垂訓，而後世猶有位上侯王之議、稱臣突…
translation_en: … covenant], Wu and Jin contended for precedence. Jin was senior to Wu; that the Classic places Jin first records the constant norm. Wu had usurped the title of king; that the Classic writes "Viscount" rectifies names. That it uses the word "and" (ji) in bringing together the two hegemons is because it refuses to place Wu before Jin, yet also does not wish to obscure the reality, thereby making plain Wu's strength while curbing it. Now, in this single meeting, why was the Sage so earnestly concerned like this? It is because the Central States have an enduring尊 (dignity), whereas the barbarians do not have enduring ascendancy; the means to govern the interior and control the exterior lies solely within ourselves. Take this state of Jin: how could it be placed behind Wu? It was inherently the leader of the kindred covenants. If it ruined its hereditary achievement and suddenly fell beneath Wu, how could it revive its declining fortunes? Those who order the world, wishing to make the Central States always occupy their position of dignity so as to control the barbarians, cannot be without plans for vigorous governance. And as for Wu: how could it be placed before Jin? It was inherently a barbarian state that had usurped the title of king. Relying on its accumulated might, if Jin did not contest with it, how could its burgeoning power be checked? Those who order the world, wishing to make the barbarians always occupy their lowly position so as to serve the Central States, cannot be without strategies for control. Survival and ruin are matters of Heaven, yet when human effort prevails over Heaven, Heaven can be made certain; if one merely shifts the blame to Heaven and violates the constant principles of Heaven and Earth, hoping by luck to avoid ruin, I have never seen such a one able to preserve his state. Right and wrong are matters of principle, and when principle prevails over circumstantial power, such power is not worth relying on; if one merely grows accustomed to circumstantial power and forgets the distinction between cap and shoes, seeking only immediate peace for the moment, I fear one cannot remain secure for even a single morning. Coming to this point, the Sage had deep anxieties. Therefore he placed Jin first, treated Wu as barbarian, and specially wrote "and," instructing later generations in the Way of governing the Central States and controlling the four barbarians most deeply and earnestly. Even with this handed down as instruction, in later generations there were still deliberations to rank [chieftains] above marquises and kings, policies of declaring oneself a subject to the…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
厥之策甚至以父事之者嗟夫中國不能令則
夷狄進矣晉自平定以來政在家門民無所依
君日不悛以樂慆憂公室之卑其無日也又安
能與吳爭哉君子觀於黃池之會而知晉事不
可爲矣書曰無怠無荒四夷來王先治内也夫
禮記
凡居民材必因天地寒煖燥濕廣谷大川
異制民生其間者異俗剛柔輕重遲速
異齊五味異和器械異制衣服異宜脩
===
其教不易其俗齊其政不易其宜
同考試官教諭周批聖人治世求同於道不求
同於俗正所以宜民此作得㫖
考試官學正陳批醇正
考試官學正王批雋永
王者儲材之順無非因造化而順之也夫造化
之氣不一而民用亦以異矣居材者惡可弗順
乎是故惟脩其政教而已嘗謂聖王以利利天
punctuated:
厥之策，甚至以父事之者。嗟夫！中國不能令，則夷狄進矣。晉自平、定以來，政在家門，民無所依，君日不悛，以樂慆憂，公室之卑，其無日也，又安能與吳爭哉？君子觀於黃池之會，而知晉事不可爲矣。《書》曰：「無怠無荒，四夷來王。」先治内也夫！

《禮記》

「凡居民材，必因天地寒煖燥濕，廣谷大川異制，民生其間者異俗，剛柔輕重遲速異齊，五味異和，器械異制，衣服異宜，脩其教不易其俗，齊其政不易其宜。」

同考試官教諭周批：聖人治世，求同於道，不求同於俗，正所以宜民。此作得㫖。
考試官學正陳批：醇正。
考試官學正王批：雋永。

王者儲材之順，無非因造化而順之也。夫造化之氣不一，而民用亦以異矣，居材者惡可弗順乎？是故惟脩其政教而已。嘗謂聖王以利利天
translation_en:
… declaring themselves vassals to the Tujue (Turks), and even going so far as to serve them as a father. Alas! When the Central States cannot command, the barbarians advance. In Jin, ever since the reigns of Dukes Ping and Ding, political power had rested with the ministerial families and the people had nothing to rely upon; the ruler grew daily more unrepentant, drowning his sorrows in pleasure. The abasement of the ducal house was imminent—how then could it contend with Wu? When the gentleman observes the covenant at Huangchi, he knows that the affairs of Jin were beyond saving. The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "Without idleness or neglect, the four barbarian tribes will come to acknowledge the king's sovereignty." It is a matter of governing the interior first!

Record of Rites (Liji)

"In all cases of settling the people and accumulating materials for their use, one must adapt to the cold, warmth, dryness, and moisture of heaven and earth. Broad valleys and great rivers are differently formed, and the people born among them have different customs. Their temperaments—hard or soft, heavy or light, slow or quick—are differently proportioned; the five flavors are differently blended; implements and tools are differently fashioned; and garments are differently suited. One cultivates their instruction without changing their customs, and standardizes their governance without changing what is suitable to them."

Comment by Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Zhou: When the sage governs the world, he seeks uniformity in the Way, not uniformity in customs, which is precisely how he suits the people. This composition grasps the essential meaning.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Chen: Pure and orthodox.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang: Rich and enduring in flavor.

The compliance shown by a true king in accumulating materials for the people is nothing other than adapting to and complying with the operations of nature. Now, the vital forces of nature are not uniform, and the needs of the people differ accordingly; how could one who accumulates materials for them fail to comply with this? Therefore, he simply cultivates their governance and instruction, and nothing more. It has been said that when the sage kings benefit the…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
下而天下以其分取足焉所以左右之而善其
用于不窮者自有不易之道在也吾得之居民
材矣今夫民之材民用之莫非因天地而用焉
者也寒煖燥濕天地司之故凡居民材莫非因
天地而居焉者也夫聖王何爲而必因之也蓋
自二儀肇分谷之虛而廣也川之流而大也其
形制之判于天地者已不能比之而使同是以
民生其間者習俗性情殊焉五味器械衣服異
焉而材用之取于天地者亦不能强之而使一
===
此皆尚之爲俗安之爲宜不可得而易者也是
故以民之可同者同天下而不以民之本異者
病天下三綱五典皆敎也凡以植天常而立人
紀也不可不脩也至于俗之所在則不易焉何
者俗固天地之氣使之也吾因乎天地而何以
易焉也况敎行而俗自美又有不必易者乎禮
樂刑政皆政也凡以同民心而出治道也不可
不齊也至于宜之所在則不易焉何者宜固天
地之氣成之也吾因乎天地而無容易焉也况
punctuated: 下，而天下以其分取足焉，所以左右之而善其用于不窮者，自有不易之道在也。吾得之居民材矣。今夫民之材，民用之，莫非因天地而用焉者也。寒煖燥濕，天地司之，故凡居民材，莫非因天地而居焉者也。夫聖王何爲而必因之也？蓋自二儀肇分，谷之虛而廣也，川之流而大也，其形制之判于天地者，已不能比之而使同。是以民生其間者，習俗性情殊焉，五味、器械、衣服異焉，而材用之取于天地者，亦不能强之而使一。此皆尚之爲俗、安之爲宜，不可得而易者也。是故以民之可同者同天下，而不以民之本異者病天下。三綱五典皆敎也，凡以植天常而立人紀也，不可不脩也；至于俗之所在，則不易焉。何者？俗固天地之氣使之也，吾因乎天地，而何以易焉也？况敎行而俗自美，又有不必易者乎！禮樂刑政皆政也，凡以同民心而出治道也，不可不齊也；至于宜之所在，則不易焉。何者？宜固天地之氣成之也，吾因乎天地，而無容易焉也。况
translation_en:
… the realm, and the people of the realm draw sufficiency from it according to their lot; as for the means of assisting them and perfecting their utility inexhaustibly, there naturally exists an unchanging Way therein. I have grasped this in the principle of "settling the people's resources" (ju min cai).

Now, the resources of the people are used by the people, and none of them are used without adapting to Heaven and Earth. Cold and warmth, dryness and moisture are governed by Heaven and Earth; therefore, in all cases of settling the people's resources, none are settled without adapting to Heaven and Earth. Why must the sage-king necessarily adapt to them? Ever since the Two Primal Forces (Heaven and Earth) first separated—with valleys being hollow and vast, and rivers flowing and great—their configurations and forms as divided between Heaven and Earth could no longer be leveled and made identical. Therefore, among the people born within them, customs and temperaments differ, and the five flavors, implements, and clothing vary; thus the resources for use taken from Heaven and Earth likewise cannot be forced into uniformity. All of these—what they esteem becoming their customs (su), and what they find comfortable becoming their suitability (yi)—cannot be altered.

Therefore, the sage-king unifies the realm through that in which the people can be made the same, and does not distress the realm over that in which the people are inherently different. The Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues are all "instruction" (jiao); because they serve to establish the heavenly constants and set up human order, they must be cultivated. Yet when it comes to where local customs lie, he does not alter them. Why is this? Customs are indeed caused by the vital forces (qi) of Heaven and Earth; since I adapt to Heaven and Earth, why should I alter them? How much more so when, once instruction is carried out, customs naturally become admirable, so that there is even less need to alter them! Rites, music, punishments, and administration are all "governance" (zheng); because they serve to unify the minds of the people and bring forth the Way of order, they must be made uniform. Yet when it comes to where local suitability lies, he does not alter it. Why is this? Suitability is indeed formed by the vital forces of Heaven and Earth; since I adapt to Heaven and Earth, there is no room to alter it. How much more so when …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
善政而民咸宜又有不必易者乎夫觀俗與宜
之因也則民用日充而政教之基裕矣觀政與
教之脩也則民德日新而財用之流節矣聖王
所以能使民順治者惟其不以己與之也夫雖
然此大順之道也蓋先王以順道治天下六府
脩三事舉而俗宜之無害於治者則不拂民之
欲焉故周官一書九貢九賦九式每惓惓焉職
此耳吁經綸之迹具在也有關雎麟趾之意王
政至今存可也有天下者當念諸
===
教順成俗內外和順國家理治此之謂盛
德
同考試官教諭周批陽教陰教萬化所繇重矣
此作能發明旨義可錄
考試官學正陳批整飭
考試官學正王批明鬯
觀君后化成於天下而德之盛可知矣蓋君后
天下所觀化而德以運之者也曾謂德盛矣而
punctuated:
善政而民咸宜，又有不必易者乎？夫觀俗與宜之因也，則民用日充而政教之基裕矣；觀政與教之脩也，則民德日新而財用之流節矣。聖王所以能使民順治者，惟其不以己與之也夫！雖然，此大順之道也。蓋先王以順道治天下，六府脩，三事舉，而俗宜之無害於治者，則不拂民之欲焉。故《周官》一書，九貢、九賦、九式每惓惓焉，職此耳。吁！經綸之迹具在也，有《關雎》、《麟趾》之意，王政至今存可也，有天下者當念諸！
教順成俗，內外和順，國家理治，此之謂盛德。
同考試官教諭周批：陽教、陰教，萬化所繇，重矣。此作能發明旨義，可錄。
考試官學正陳批：整飭。
考試官學正王批：明鬯。
觀君后化成於天下，而德之盛可知矣。蓋君后，天下所觀化，而德以運之者也，曾謂德盛矣而
translation_en:
…and when government is good so that all looks well-suited to the people, is there any need to alter them? Indeed, when one observes how they follow local customs and what is suitable, the people's resources grow daily more abundant and the foundation of government and instruction becomes ample; when one observes how they cultivate government and instruction, the people's virtue is daily renewed and the flow of wealth and expenditure is regulated. The reason the sage kings were able to make the people compliant and well-governed was simply that they did not impose their own personal will upon them! Even so, this is the Way of Great Compliance. For the former kings governed all under heaven by the Way of compliance: the Six Treasuries were kept in order, the Three Affairs were carried out, and where local customs and suitabilities were not harmful to governance, they did not thwart the desires of the people. Therefore, in the book Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), the nine tributes, nine revenues, and nine expenditure regulations are repeatedly given earnest attention solely on account of this. Alas! The traces of their statecraft are all still present; if one possesses the spirit of the "Guanju" and "Linzhi" odes, the kingly government could survive even to this day. Those who possess all under heaven ought to bear this in mind!

"When instruction is complied with and forms customs, inside and outside are harmonious and compliant, and the state and family are well-ordered and governed: this is called flourishing virtue."

Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Zhou comments: "The yang instruction and yin instruction, from which the myriad transformations arise, are weighty indeed. This composition is able to elucidate the purport and meaning; it may be recorded."
Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies (xuezheng) Chen comments: "Well-ordered and disciplined."
Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies (xuezheng) Wang comments: "Clear and fluent."

When one observes the ruler and the queen bringing about transformation throughout all under heaven, the flourishing of their virtue can be known. For the ruler and the queen are those to whom all under heaven look for transformation, and it is through virtue that they set it in motion. Could it ever be said that when virtue is flourishing…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
大化有不洽者乎記昏義者及此謂夫朝廷四
方之極閨門風化之原吾於是而知建官立宮
以聽治所關乎化理大矣蓋天子秉陽剛之德
以端拱於上天下之男敎賴焉后備陰柔之德
以助理於內天下之婦順則焉今各脩其職以
聽治於內外也則敎行而化洽男之以知帥人
者翕然彝敎之大同外和而國無不治矣化行
而俗美女之以順爲正者怡然雍睦之無間內
順而家無不理矣敎化四達而禮俗維新治之
===
至也而皆天子與后倡之焉其德豈可以易言
哉吾知健順相成而惟皇之極以建陰陽合德
而元良之度克端其在君德則剛健中正之充
積者徵諸國之順治而可以窺其蘊矣否則化
理無本烏能使外治之脩耶其在后德則徽柔
懿恭之素聞者驗諸家之和理而可以想其盛
矣否則表率無基烏能使內職之脩耶吁君后
之德有關於治道如此則天子當必自脩厥德
以爲化民之本而正始於后者亦尚知慎重矣
punctuated: 大化有不洽者乎？記《昏義》者及此，謂夫朝廷，四方之極；閨門，風化之原。吾於是而知建官立宮以聽治，所關乎化理大矣。蓋天子秉陽剛之德以端拱於上，天下之男敎賴焉；后備陰柔之德以助理於內，天下之婦順則焉。今各脩其職以聽治於內外也，則敎行而化洽，男之以知帥人者，翕然彝敎之大同，外和而國無不治矣；化行而俗美，女之以順爲正者，怡然雍睦之無間，內順而家無不理矣。敎化四達而禮俗維新，治之至也，而皆天子與后倡之焉，其德豈可以易言哉？吾知健順相成，而惟皇之極以建；陰陽合德，而元良之度克端。其在君德，則剛健中正之充積者，徵諸國之順治而可以窺其蘊矣；否則化理無本，烏能使外治之脩耶？其在后德，則徽柔懿恭之素聞者，驗諸家之和理而可以想其盛矣；否則表率無基，烏能使內職之脩耶？吁！君后之德有關於治道如此，則天子當必自脩厥德以爲化民之本，而正始於后者亦尚知慎重矣…
translation_en: …the grand transformation not permeate everywhere? When the author of the Meaning of the Marriage Rite (Hunyi) touched upon this, he meant that the royal court is the standard for the four quarters, and the inner quarters are the source of moral transformation. From this I know that establishing offices and setting up palaces in order to attend to governance is of great consequence to transformative order. For the Son of Heaven holds to the virtue of yang firmness in ruling with solemn composure above, and the instruction of men throughout the realm relies upon him; the Empress possesses the virtue of yin gentleness in assisting governance within, and the obedience of women throughout the realm takes its model from her. Now, when each cultivates their duties to attend to governance in the outer and inner realms, instruction is carried out and transformation permeates: men, who lead others through wisdom, harmoniously unite in the great commonality of constant instruction, so that there is harmony without and no state goes unالتgoverned; transformation is carried out and customs are made beautiful: women, who take obedience as their correctness, joyfully dwell in unbroken concord, so that there is obedience within and no household goes unregulated. When instruction and transformation reach in all four directions and ritual customs are renewed, it is the perfection of governance; yet all of this is initiated by the Son of Heaven and the Empress—how could their virtue be spoken of lightly? I know that strength and顺 (compliance/gentleness) complement each other, and thereby the august standard is established; yin and yang unite their virtues, and thereby the measure of supreme goodness is made upright. As for the sovereign's virtue, the abundant accumulation of firm, strong, central, and正 (correct) qualities is attested in the compliant governance of the state, whereby one may glimpse its depth; otherwise, transformative order would have no root—how could it bring about the cultivation of outer governance? As for the Empress's virtue, the long-established reputation for fine gentleness and admirable reverence is verified in the harmonious regulation of the household, whereby one may imagine its flourishing; otherwise, setting an example would have no foundation—how could it bring about the cultivation of inner duties? Alas! Since the virtue of the sovereign and the Empress is so vital to the way of governance, the Son of Heaven must surely cultivate his own virtue as the root of transforming the people, and in rectifying the beginning with the Empress, he should also know to be circumspect…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
哉甞觀周禮設官九嬪世婦之職既詳且備下
逮女祝女史亦皆窈窕淑女以掌其事而宮闈
之間教無不存焉周家有道之長而教順明章
豈徒六官分職而已哉其本始固自有在也吁
此昏禮聖王重之記者以此垂訓其意深矣
第貳場
論
古之學者為己
===
同考試官教諭蕭 批 詞意都入玄思鏘然左國
豈經生所能
同考試官教諭李 批 立議以聖門為衡品列諸
子則為己之學自有根據非尋常操鉛槧者
考試官學正陳 批 卓然奧論
考試官學正王 批 思超調古
聖人之言有殫言者有約言者原本而逮末引
始而要終殫舉而顯言之者雅言也挈其體而
藏其用專其內而不及其外隱約而言之者變辭
punctuated:
哉！甞觀《周禮》設官，九嬪、世婦之職既詳且備，下逮女祝、女史，亦皆窈窕淑女以掌其事，而宮闈之間，教無不存焉。周家有道之長，而教順明章，豈徒六官分職而已哉？其本始固自有在也。吁！此昏禮聖王重之，記者以此垂訓，其意深矣。
第貳場
論
古之學者為己
同考試官教諭蕭，批：「詞意都入玄思，鏘然《左》、《國》，豈經生所能？」
同考試官教諭李，批：「立議以聖門為衡，品列諸子，則『為己』之學自有根據，非尋常操鉛槧者。」
考試官學正陳，批：「卓然奧論。」
考試官學正王，批：「思超調古。」
聖人之言，有殫言者，有約言者。原本而逮末，引始而要終，殫舉而顯言之者，雅言也；挈其體而藏其用，專其內而不及其外，隱約而言之者，變辭
translation_en:
…! If we examine the offices established in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), the duties of the Nine Imperial Concubines (jiupin) and the Hereditary Consorts (shifu) are both detailed and comprehensive. Extending down to the Female Invocators (nüzhu) and Female Scribes (nüshi), all were likewise modest, virtuous ladies charged with managing their affairs, so that within the palace quarters, instruction was nowhere absent. The enduring righteous rule of the House of Zhou, with its instruction in compliance so bright and manifest—how could it have been merely a matter of the Six Ministries dividing their duties? Its fundamental origin truly had its own source. Alas! The sage kings attached great weight to this rite of marriage, and the recorder handed down this teaching with profound intent indeed.

Second Session

Discourse

"The Scholars of Antiquity Learned for Themselves"

Associate Examiner and Instructor Xiao comments: "Both diction and meaning enter into abstruse reflection, resonating like the Zuo Tradition (Zuozhuan) and the Discourses of the States (Guoyu)—how could a mere student of the classics be capable of this?"

Associate Examiner and Instructor Li comments: "Setting up the argument with the Sage's school as the standard to evaluate and rank the various masters, the learning 'for oneself' naturally possesses a firm foundation; this is not the work of an ordinary wielder of writing brush and tablet."

Examiner and Instructor Chen comments: "An eminent and profound discourse."

Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: "Transcendent in thought, antique in tone."

Among the words of the Sage, there are those spoken exhaustively and those spoken concisely. Tracing the root to reach the branches, drawing from the beginning to sum up the end, enumerating exhaustively and speaking manifestly—these are standard words (yayan). Grasping the substance while concealing the function, focusing on the internal without touching upon the external, speaking subtly and concisely—these are modified expressions…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也變詞者聖人矯世厲俗從先進之意不可不
察也夫道通人已貫古今始於誠意正心而施
之家國天下皆吾性也是故蓄德非已也脩業
非人也爲已非內也爲人非外也合外內之道
也而子曰古之學者爲已今之學者爲人此何
以明焉豈古之人獨專已而遺人乎是楊朱之
爲我也夫楊子嗇一毛去名絕世疾仁義之多
岐詆堯舜伯夷爲讓名其道芻狗萬物以老子
爲宗此夫豢酒塞戸不饗客以餘者也豈吾所
稱爲已者哉謬於夫子之指矣夫子蓋見夫春
秋之世衆人域域貪夫殉財夸者死權遊士滑
稽俠士榮名烏睹所謂脩身繕性之道焉雖以
七十子之徒如顓孫端木卜商冉有四人者號
稱高第且也端木殖貨求也聚斂商也見紛華
而悅顓孫干祿以聞爲達並騖於世之温蠖溺
其身矣夫夫子蓋傷之若曰吾將兼人已殫舉而
告之乎其毋乃不察於世也吾且專舉而言之
反其所好而道其所亡儻可捄乎故曰古之學
punctuated: 也。變詞者，聖人矯世厲俗、「從先進」之意，不可不察也。夫道通人已，貫古今，始於誠意、正心，而施之家、國、天下，皆吾性也。是故蓄德非已也，脩業非人也；爲已非內也，爲人非外也，合外內之道也。而子曰：「古之學者爲已，今之學者爲人。」此何以明焉？豈古之人獨專已而遺人乎？是楊朱之爲我也。夫楊子嗇一毛，去名絕世，疾仁義之多岐，詆堯、舜、伯夷爲讓名，其道芻狗萬物，以老子爲宗，此夫豢酒塞戸、不饗客以餘者也。豈吾所稱「爲已」者哉？謬於夫子之指矣。夫子蓋見夫春秋之世，衆人域域，貪夫殉財，夸者死權，遊士滑稽，俠士榮名，烏睹所謂脩身繕性之道焉？雖以七十子之徒，如顓孫、端木、卜商、冉有四人者，號稱高第，且也端木殖貨，求也聚斂，商也見紛華而悅，顓孫干祿、以聞爲達，並騖於世之温蠖，溺其身矣夫！夫子蓋傷之，若曰：「吾將兼人已殫舉而告之乎？其毋乃不察於世也。吾且專舉而言之，反其所好而道其所亡，儻可捄乎！」故曰：「古之學
translation_en: … [shifted phrasing]. Shifted phrasing reflects the sage's intention to rectify the age, sharpen customs, and "follow the men of former times"—this must be carefully examined. Now the Way connects others and the self, penetrates antiquity and the present; beginning with making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind, and extending to the family, the state, and all under Heaven, all of it is our human nature. Therefore, accumulating virtue is not merely for oneself, and cultivating one's work is not merely for others; learning for oneself is not merely internal, and learning for others is not merely external—it is the Way that unites the external and the internal. Yet the Master said, "The learners of antiquity learned for themselves; the learners of today learn for others." How is this to be explained? Could it be that the people of antiquity focused exclusively on themselves and neglected others? That would be the egoism ("for oneself") of Yang Zhu 楊朱! Now Master Yang begrudged a single hair, cast off reputation and cut himself off from the world, detested the many branching paths of benevolence and righteousness, and slandered Yao 堯, Shun 舜, and Boyi 伯夷 as yielding for the sake of fame. His Way treated the myriad things as straw dogs, taking Laozi 老子 as his ancestor; he was like a man whose doorway is crammed with grain-fed meat and wine, yet who will not even treat his guests to the leftovers. How could this be what we call "for oneself"? It is utterly contrary to the Master's meaning. The Master doubtless saw that in the Spring and Autumn era, the multitude were hemmed in and frantic: greedy men sacrificed their lives for wealth, boastful men died for power, wandering persuaders practiced glib sophistry, and knights-errant gloried in fame—where could one see the so-called Way of cultivating the person and refining one's nature? Even among the followers of the seventy disciples, such as the four men Zhuansun 顓孫 [Zizhang 子張], Duanmu 端木 [Zigong 子貢], Bu Shang 卜商 [Zixia 子夏], and Ran You 冉有, who were renowned as top disciples—even so, Duanmu amassed goods, Qiu 求 [Ran You] gathered imposts, Shang [Bu Shang] delighted upon seeing worldly splendor, and Zhuansun sought official emolument and mistook notoriety for true attainment. Together they galloped into the murky confusion of the world, drowning their own persons in it! The Master doubtless grieved over this, as if to say: "Shall I exhaustively set forth both others and the self when instructing them? Surely that would fail to take account of the state of the world. Rather, I shall single out one side and speak of it, countering what they are fond of and discoursing upon what they have lost—perhaps then they can be saved!" Thus he said, "The learners of antiquity…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者爲己其指深矣其道大矣廣矣無所不包矣
飾貌理辭容容與與文矣方之而違舍智匿數
依誠託貞近質矣方之而谿疏布脫粟勳示爲
儉似也而欺兼愛尚同示人以廣似也而蕩踰
垣鑿坯咽李棄蔬以爲潔辟也孤犢三足堅白
異同以爲辨誕也篤靜致柔挫銳解紛以遊乎
無何有之鄉名曰陸沉離也槁形幻物譚乎六
合之外而漫行無所家使人眩焉亂也芥萬鍾
塗章冕文犧爲辱之義當焉而墜遠柔曼黜淫
===
辟捐詭靡之節當焉而卑辨繁緣設小物賓賓
然以灼於人焉而微端委結紱齊莊矜辭脩脩
然堂序之間而疏澄乎性情之端寤乎象意之
先察乎希微之際戒乎奧窔之中倫物非巨也
秋毫非細也須臾非近也終身非遠也進而受
非干利也退而讓非爲名高也不妄耦於人非
爲亢也其耦非私昵也不苟同於人非爲異也
其同非比黨也見善忻然如不及見不善悚然
而思貴而不盈而曰吾遇惠而不有而曰吾義
punctuated: 者爲己」，其指深矣，其道大矣、廣矣，無所不包矣！飾貌理辭，容容與與，文矣，方之而違；舍智匿數，依誠託貞，近質矣，方之而谿。疏布脫粟，動示爲儉，似也，而欺；兼愛尚同，示人以廣，似也，而蕩。踰垣鑿坯，咽李棄蔬，以爲潔，辟也；孤犢三足，堅白異同，以爲辨，誕也；篤靜致柔，挫銳解紛，以遊乎無何有之鄉，名曰陸沉，離也；槁形幻物，譚乎六合之外，而漫行無所家，使人眩焉，亂也。芥萬鍾，塗章冕，文犧爲辱之義，當焉而墜；遠柔曼，黜淫辟，捐詭靡之節，當焉而卑；辨繁緣，設小物，賓賓然以灼於人焉，而微；端委結紱，齊莊矜辭，脩脩然堂序之間，而疏。澄乎性情之端，寤乎象意之先，察乎希微之際，戒乎奧窔之中。倫物非巨也，秋毫非細也；須臾非近也，終身非遠也。進而受，非干利也；退而讓，非爲名高也。不妄耦於人，非爲亢也；其耦，非私昵也。不苟同於人，非爲異也；其同，非比黨也。見善忻然如不及，見不善悚然而思。貴而不盈，而曰「吾遇」；惠而不有，而曰「吾義」。
translation_en:
… learned for themselves.” How profound is its import! How great is its Way, how vast, leaving nothing unembraced!

Those who adorn their demeanor and polish their words with composed and leisurely grace appear refined, yet when measured against this Way, they go astray. Those who discard cleverness and conceal artifice, relying on sincerity and claiming uprightness, come close to plain substance, yet when measured against it, they are narrow and perverse. Those who wear coarse cloth and eat unpolished grain, constantly making a display of frugality, resemble it, yet they are deceitful; those who preach universal love and exalt conformity, showing breadth to others, resemble it, yet they are unrestrained. Those who leap over walls or break through unbaked mud walls to flee office, or swallow worm-eaten plums and discard gifted vegetables, taking this as purity, are eccentric; those who argue over “an orphan calf” or “a chicken having three feet,” or debate “hardness and whiteness” and “similarity and difference,” taking this as discrimination, are absurd; those who hold fast to stillness and attain softness, blunting their sharpness and untangling knots to roam in the realm of Nothingness, calling it “sinking on dry land,” are detached from reality; those who wither their forms and treat things as illusions, conversing beyond the six directions of the universe and wandering aimlessly without a home so as to dazzle people, are disorderly. The principle of treating a salary of ten thousand bushels as mere mustard grass, of viewing ceremonial emblems and caps as mud, and of regarding the embroidered sacrificial ox as a disgrace, loses its footing when measured against this Way; the integrity of keeping far from soft and alluring charms, rejecting licentiousness and depravity, and casting aside strange and extravagant customs, seems lowly when measured against it; discriminating trivial details and setting up petty matters so as to shine ostentatiously before others is minute when measured against it; wearing formal robes and tying official sashes, maintaining solemn gravity and guarded speech while standing neatly in the halls and schools, is superficial when measured against it.

Rather, one renders clear the very beginnings of nature and emotion, awakens to what precedes visible forms and conscious thoughts, examines the subtlest and faintest junctures, and remains vigilant within the innermost recesses. Human relationships and affairs of the world are not considered too vast, nor is the tip of an autumn hair considered too minute; a single moment is not considered too near, nor is a whole lifetime considered too distant. Advancing and accepting office is not to seek profit; retiring and yielding is not to win a lofty reputation. Refusing to associate indiscriminately with others is not out of arrogance, and when one does associate with others, it is not out of private intimacy. Refusing to agree casually with others is not to be contrarian, and when one does agree with others, it is not out of partisan cliquishness. Upon seeing goodness, one rejoices as if fearing to fall short of it; upon seeing evil, one reflects in trepidation. Being noble without becoming arrogant, one says, “It is merely my fortunate encounter”; bestowing kindness without claiming possession of the merit, one says, “It is merely my duty.” …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
德尊若愚業尊若夷譽而不居誹而不疑貌不
羡乎情言不羡乎行人知之若己人不知之亦
若己福不謂祥菑不謂殃窮達患難終始爲晝
夜寒暑之序矣若此者其唯仲尼乎大哉仲尼
之道也累世不能殫其學而恂恂然曰吾何知
問于老聃學于師襄咨于萇弘郯子蓋發憤忘
食不知其老也聘於列國行乎魯不合則去司
寇不能留廩丘不能祿焉戒于匡逐于衛厄于
陳蔡沮于晏嬰子西而絃歌不輟慍色不形焉
===
故其語由賜曰仁者不必信智者不必行良農
能爲稼而不能爲穡君子脩其道不能爲容而
他日又曰不怨天不尤人下學而上達知我者
其天乎夫不求容於人而求知於天爲己之學
斯其至矣乎是以顏淵簞食好學如愚孔子賢
之子若難仕孔子喜之聞曾皙浴沂風雩之言
則喟然進之原思讓宰粟不見謂廉子貢贖人
而不受金不見謂義子路餉長溝之役不見謂
仁夫三者美行也而聖人不取惡不誠也不貴
punctuated: 德尊若愚，業尊若夷。譽而不居，誹而不疑。貌不羡乎情，言不羡乎行。人知之若己，人不知之亦若己。福不謂祥，菑不謂殃。窮達患難，終始爲晝夜寒暑之序矣。若此者，其唯仲尼乎！大哉仲尼之道也！累世不能殫其學，而恂恂然曰：「吾何知？」問于老聃，學于師襄，咨于萇弘、郯子，蓋發憤忘食，不知其老也。聘於列國，行乎魯，不合則去，司寇不能留，廩丘不能祿焉。戒于匡，逐于衛，厄于陳、蔡，沮于晏嬰、子西，而絃歌不輟，慍色不形焉。故其語由、賜曰：「仁者不必信，智者不必行。良農能爲稼，而不能爲穡。君子脩其道，不能爲容。」而他日又曰：「不怨天，不尤人，下學而上達，知我者其天乎！」夫不求容於人，而求知於天，爲己之學，斯其至矣乎！是以顏淵簞食好學如愚，孔子賢之；子若難仕，孔子喜之；聞曾皙浴沂風雩之言，則喟然進之。原思讓宰粟，不見謂廉；子貢贖人而不受金，不見謂義；子路餉長溝之役，不見謂仁。夫三者，美行也，而聖人不取，惡不誠也，不貴
translation_en: When his virtue is exalted, he seems foolish; when his achievements are exalted, he seems ordinary. When praised, he does not claim credit; when slandered, he does not waver in doubt. His outward demeanor does not exceed his true feelings, nor do his words exceed his conduct. Whether others recognize him or do not recognize him, he remains just as he is in himself. Good fortune he does not call an auspicious omen, nor calamity a curse; failure and success, hardship and distress, from beginning to end are to him like the natural alternation of day and night, cold and heat. One who is like this—could it be only Zhongni [Confucius]? Great indeed is the Way of Zhongni! Successive generations cannot exhaust his learning, yet he modestly said, "What do I know?" He inquired of Lao Dan, studied under Music Master Xiang (Shi Xiang), and consulted Chang Hong and the Viscount of Tan (Tanzi); indeed, in his eager pursuit he forgot to eat and was unaware that old age was coming on. He traveled on missions among the various states and practiced his Way in Lu, departing whenever things did not accord with principle; the office of Minister of Justice (Sikou) could not detain him, nor could the fief of Linqiu retain him with its emoluments. He was put on guard in Kuang, driven out in Wei, stranded in Chen and Cai, and thwarted by Yan Ying and Zixi, yet his playing of stringed instruments and singing never ceased, and no look of resentment ever appeared on his face. Thus he spoke to You [Zilu] and Ci [Zigong], saying: "The humane person is not necessarily trusted; the wise person does not necessarily see his counsels put into practice. A good farmer can sow the grain, but cannot guarantee the harvest; a gentleman cultivates his Way, but cannot guarantee that he will be accepted." And on another day he also said: "I do not resent Heaven, nor do I blame men. I study what is below and penetrate what is above. The one who knows me—is it not Heaven!" Not seeking acceptance from men, but seeking to be known by Heaven: is this not the ultimate perfection of learning for oneself? Therefore, when Yan Yuan lived on a single bamboo dish of rice, loved learning, and appeared as though foolish, Confucius esteemed him as worthy; when Ziruo [Qidiao Kai] was hesitant to enter official service, Confucius was pleased with him; and when he heard Zeng Xi's words about bathing in the Yi River and enjoying the breeze on the Rain Altar, he sighed deeply and approved of him. When Yuan Si declined the grain allotment due to him as steward, he was not pronounced incorruptible; when Zigong ransomed captives from abroad and refused reimbursement from the state, he was not pronounced righteous; and when Zilu provided food for the laborers digging the Chang Ditch, he was not pronounced humane. Now, these three were admirable deeds, yet the Sage did not approve of them, because he disliked what was not genuine, and did not value…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
皎皎以為名沾沾以為德也沾沾者不廣皎皎
者易已惟誠也不見而章鶴鳴于九皐聲聞于
天陽氣暢於泱漭而萌乎淵泉有聲之聲不過
百里無聲之聲充乎四海故君子兢兢脩之冥
冥而德立名附焉德誠脩而名不著君子弗以
為患矣是夫子為己之說也若曰古之學者為
己可以及人今之學者為人必且喪己為己者
兩得之者也為人者兩失之者也隱約而具曲
而中包含而有深思矯世之言也昔者曾子甞
===
聞夫子速貧速朽之說以告有若有若曰夫子
有為言之也其語樊遲曰舉直錯諸枉能使枉
者直而子夏曰富哉言乎二子蓋有味乎夫子
之指也吾於夫子為己為人之說亦云
表
擬虜酋俺答率西夷烏思藏鎖南堅參等
求
貢方物羣臣
賀表〔萬曆七年〕
punctuated:
皎皎以為名，沾沾以為德也。沾沾者不廣，皎皎者易已。惟誠也不見而章，鶴鳴于九皐，聲聞于天，陽氣暢於泱漭，而萌乎淵泉。有聲之聲，不過百里；無聲之聲，充乎四海。故君子兢兢脩之冥冥，而德立名附焉。德誠脩而名不著，君子弗以為患矣。是夫子為己之說也。若曰：古之學者為己，可以及人；今之學者為人，必且喪己。為己者，兩得之者也；為人者，兩失之者也。隱約而具，曲而中，包含而有深思，矯世之言也。昔者曾子甞聞夫子速貧速朽之說，以告有若，有若曰：「夫子有為言之也。」其語樊遲曰：「舉直錯諸枉，能使枉者直。」而子夏曰：「富哉言乎！」二子蓋有味乎夫子之指也。吾於夫子為己為人之說亦云。

表

擬虜酋俺答率西夷烏思藏鎖南堅參等求貢方物羣臣賀表〔萬曆七年〕
translation_en:
…ostentatiously pure so as to gain renown, or smugly self-satisfied so as to pass for virtue. What is smugly self-satisfied lacks breadth; what is ostentatiously pure easily comes to an end. Only sincerity becomes manifest without being displayed: the crane cries in the九皋 (deepest marshes) and its voice is heard in Heaven; yang energy spreads across the vast expanse yet sprouts in the deepest springs. A sound that has audible voice carries no more than a hundred li; a sound that is voiceless fills the Four Seas. Therefore, the gentleman cautiously cultivates himself in the unseen, and thereby his virtue is established and renown attaches to it. If his virtue is genuinely cultivated and yet his name does not become prominent, the gentleman does not consider it a cause for distress. Such is the Master's doctrine of learning for oneself. It is as if to say: the learners of antiquity learned for themselves, and so were able to extend it to others; the learners of today learn for the sake of others, and so will inevitably lose themselves. Those who learn for themselves attain both; those who learn for the sake of others lose both. Concise yet complete, subtle yet hitting the mark, comprehensive and deeply reflective—these are words meant to rectify the age. In the past, Master Zeng (Zengzi 曾子) once heard the Master's remarks about wishing for speedy poverty and speedy decay, and repeated them to You Ruo 有若; You Ruo said, "The Master had a particular reason for saying this." And when the Master told Fan Chi 樊遲, "Raise the straight and set them over the crooked, and you can make the crooked straight," Zixia 子夏 said, "How rich a saying!" Those two disciples truly savored the Master's underlying meaning. I say the same of the Master's statement about learning for oneself and learning for others.

Memorial

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導魯批述今昔虜戎事歴歴如抵
掌詞亦莊整可錄
同考試官教諭周批美不忘規慮遠矣此子抱
忠悃者取之不獨詞也
考試官學正陳批屬對典則
考試官學正王批調雅詞嚴
萬曆七年某月某日虜酋俺答率西夷烏
思藏鎖南堅粲等求
===
貢方物伏蒙
聖慈嘉其款誠
賜賚有差臣等謹奉
表稱
賀者伏以
帝德光敷北裔稱藩於朔漠
王猷允塞西羌奉筐於崑崙聯四極之歸心創
萬年之
盛事慶傳彌宇頌協羣衷臣等誠懽誠抃稽首
punctuated:
同考試官訓導魯批：述今昔虜戎事，歴歴如抵掌，詞亦莊整，可錄。
同考試官教諭周批：美不忘規，慮遠矣。此子抱忠悃者，取之不獨詞也。
考試官學正陳批：屬對典則。
考試官學正王批：調雅詞嚴。

萬曆七年某月某日，虜酋俺答率西夷烏思藏鎖南堅粲等求貢方物，伏蒙聖慈嘉其款誠，賜賚有差，臣等謹奉表稱賀者。伏以帝德光敷，北裔稱藩於朔漠；王猷允塞，西羌奉筐於崑崙。聯四極之歸心，創萬年之盛事。慶傳彌宇，頌協羣衷。臣等誠懽誠抃，稽首
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Lu魯 comments: "He recounts past and present affairs concerning the northern and western nomads as clearly as pointing to the palm of one's hand, and the phrasing is also solemn and well-ordered; it is worthy of selection."
Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhou 周 comments: "While praising, he does not forget to offer admonition; his foresight is far-reaching indeed. This candidate harbors loyal sincerity—we select him not merely for his rhetoric."
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Chen 陳 comments: "The parallel couplets are classical and observant of standard rules."
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang 王 comments: "The tone is elegant and the diction is rigorous."

On a certain day of a certain month in the seventh year of the Wanli 萬曆 reign [1579], the northern chieftain Altan Khan (Anda 俺答) led the western barbarians of Ü-Tsang (Wusizang 烏思藏), Sonam Gyatso (Suonam Jiancan 鎖南堅粲) and others, to request permission to present local tribute. Humbly receiving Your Sacred Benevolence, which praised their sincere submission and bestowed rewards upon them according to their rank, we, Your servants, respectfully present this memorial of congratulation.

We humbly consider that as Imperial Virtue shines forth and spreads, the northern frontier tribes declare themselves vassals across the northern desert; as the Royal Plan is truly fulfilled, the western Qiang 西羌 offer up baskets of tribute from Kunlun 崑崙. This unites the allegiance of the four extremes and inaugurates a glorious event for ten thousand years. Joy spreads throughout the entire universe, and songs of praise harmonize in the hearts of all. Your servants, truly joyful and truly elated, bow our heads to the ground…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
首頓首竊惟
王者天地爲容并凾華貊
聖人日月所照莫不
尊親但上世或有弗懷書言猾夏然至仁待以
不殺詩咏來威桀尔匈奴陸梁胡苑蠢玆
羌屬肘腋華陽即五帝不得臣雖三王莫
能制秦號虎狼之國辟舍西河漢馳肩臂
之戯漏師馬邑嫖姚窮追姑衍僅取和親
天姫結好烏孫慙當嫚辱納呼韓於神爵
===
計熟羈縻置都護於偏垂兵殘勞費政衰
末葉雲擾腥羶世泰
明朝天開
清穆百年胡運猶遺種於祁連五蘊鉢師尚拂
廬於哈剌犁庭空幕秪聞策勝禦戎謝域
閉關未見功成奉
朔欣逢
今日特邁前猷玆蓋伏遇
皇帝陛下
punctuated: 首頓首。竊惟王者天地爲容，并凾華貊；聖人日月所照，莫不尊親。但上世或有弗懷，《書》言「猾夏」；然至仁待以不殺，《詩》咏「來威」。桀尔匈奴，陸梁胡苑；蠢玆羌屬，肘腋華陽。即五帝不得臣，雖三王莫能制。秦號虎狼之國，辟舍西河；漢馳肩臂之戯，漏師馬邑。嫖姚窮追姑衍，僅取和親；天姫結好烏孫，慙當嫚辱。納呼韓於神爵，計熟羈縻；置都護於偏垂，兵殘勞費。政衰末葉，雲擾腥羶；世泰明朝，天開清穆。百年胡運，猶遺種於祁連；五蘊鉢師，尚拂廬於哈剌。犁庭空幕，秪聞策勝禦戎；謝域閉關，未見功成奉朔。欣逢今日，特邁前猷。玆蓋伏遇皇帝陛下…
translation_en: …bowing our heads to the ground. We humbly reflect that the True King takes Heaven and Earth as his measure of tolerance, embracing both Chinese and foreign peoples alike; wherever the sun and moon of the Sage shine, there is none who does not revere and love him. Yet in high antiquity there were times when some did not submit in heart, so the Book of Documents (Shu) speaks of "disturbing the Xia [Chinese] realm"; nevertheless, supreme benevolence treated them by refraining from slaughter, and the Book of Odes (Shi) sings of "inspiring awe to make them come." How unruly were the Xiongnu, running rampant in the northern pastures; how foolishly restless were the Qiang tribes, pressing right against the flank of Huayang. Even the Five Emperors could not make them subjects, and though they were the Three Kings, none could bring them under control. Qin was called a state of tigers and wolves, yet it retreated several stages from Xihe; Han indulged in martial sport as of shoulder and arm, yet leaked its military plans at Mayi. The Piaoyao General pursued them to the bitter end at Mount Guyan, yet secured nothing more than a marriage alliance; a heavenly princess forged ties of amity with Wusun, yet shamefully endured insolent humiliation. Receiving Huhanye in the Shenjue era was a well-calculated policy of loose rein; establishing the Protector-General on the remote frontier exhausted the troops in toil and expense. When governance declined in later ages, the realm was thrown into cloud-like turmoil by rank-smelling nomads; when the world found peace under our Ming dynasty, Heaven opened an era of pure tranquility. Yet after the hundred-year fortune of the northern nomads, their remnant stock still lingered in the Qilian Mountains; and the masters of the alms-bowl and the Five Aggregates still pitched their felt tents in Qara [Hala]. Of plowing up their courts and emptying their desert camps, one only heard of victorious strategies for defending against the Western Jung; of renouncing foreign territories and closing the passes, one had not yet seen the accomplished merit of their accepting our calendar. Joyfully we encounter this present day, which far surpasses all former plans. This is because we humbly meet Your Majesty the Emperor…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
文武天成
英明神授
堯章煥
五位輯瑞萬方
舜孝隆
兩宮蕃釐百順
重公孤於鹽梅舟楫
化理登閎簡爪牙於炎朔金湯
聲靈布濩梯航日出爭睹漢官威儀冠帶月
===
支徧灑
天階雨露一家胡越無憂飲馬長城九塞管絃
共賀銷兵莫府惟玆俺荅裔出匈奴素逞
天驕寔先風靡北面
緹帷馳道爵加順義之王西遊星海析支禮
建仰華之寺葵依
丹闕已易狼子野心膜拜青蓮切尚沙門慈
敎豈直身為臣僕因之要領氐羌祗率堅
晜求通
punctuated: 文武天成，英明神授。堯章煥五位，輯瑞萬方；舜孝隆兩宮，蕃釐百順。重公孤於鹽梅舟楫，化理登閎；簡爪牙於炎朔金湯，聲靈布濩。梯航日出，爭睹漢官威儀；冠帶月支，徧灑天階雨露。一家胡越，無憂飲馬長城；九塞管絃，共賀銷兵莫府。惟玆俺荅，裔出匈奴，素逞天驕，寔先風靡。北面緹帷馳道，爵加順義之王；西遊星海析支，禮建仰華之寺。葵依丹闕，已易狼子野心；膜拜青蓮，切尚沙門慈敎。豈直身為臣僕，因之要領氐羌；祗率堅晜，求通
translation_en: … endowed by Heaven with both civil and martial virtues, and divinely granted heroic brilliance. With the resplendent elegance of Yao, You occupy the fifth-rank throne of honor and gather auspicious tokens of fealty from all regions; with the exalted filial piety of Shun, You revere the Two Palaces of the Empresses Dowager and receive abundant blessings and complete harmony. Placing high importance on the Three Dukes and Three Solitaries as Your seasoning salt and plum and Your vessels and oars, transformative governance reaches grand heights; selecting military talons and fangs for our impregnable fortifications from the blazing south to the frozen north, Your august prestige spreads far and wide. Scaling mountains and sailing seas from where the sun rises, foreign peoples vie to behold the majestic bearing of Han officials; bestowing caps and sashes upon the Yuezhi, the rain and dew of the Imperial Steps are sprinkled everywhere. With the northern Hu and southern Yue united as one family, there is no longer worry of watering warhorses at the Great Wall; amidst the music of pipes and strings across the nine frontier garrisons, all rejoice together over the melting down of weapons at the military headquarters. Now this Altan (Anda 俺荅), a descendant of the Xiongnu who had long indulged his arrogance as a "Proud Son of Heaven," has truly been the first to bow before the wind of Your moral influence. Facing north toward the crimson curtains and the imperial highway, he was granted the title of Shunyi Wang (Obedient and Righteous Prince); traveling west to the Sea of Stars (Xinghai 星海) and Xizhi (析支), he reverently built the Yanghua Temple (Temple of Admiring China). Turning like a sunflower toward the Vermilion Towers of the palace, he has already transformed his wolf-cub wildness of heart; prostrating himself before the Blue Lotus of the Buddha, he earnestly esteems the compassionate teachings of the śramaṇas (Buddhist monks). Not only has he himself become a vassal and servant, he has thereby also brought the Di and Qiang tribes under control; reverently leading the Jiankun (Kyrgyz) and other tribes, he seeks to establish …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
朝貢物陳壤奠羣空大宛之昆蹏表乞原封
筐篚吐蕃之氀罽横草日閒虎落洗戈夜
挽天河入
覲以春秋輸享遵往來鴈候開屯休戊巳折衝
停上下魚書雖
盛世不忘兵但暫息雲中之騎在
治朝豈愛佛惟遠懷徼外之人爰
錫絲言旌其懇款載
頒綺幣授以禪師偏譯拱辰環爻閭而繫組穹
===
居歸日睹陰羽而搖鼉盛矣
一統
皇輿大哉八埏
王會乾坤開闢而後未有兹勛
符命授繼以來獨當
鉅美是宜宣之
郊廟光昭
宗子之成功用以勒諸鼎彝永著
大君之有道上駕
punctuated: 朝貢，物陳壤奠，羣空大宛之昆蹏；表乞原封，筐篚吐蕃之氀罽。横草日閒虎落，洗戈夜挽天河。入覲以春秋，輸享遵往來鴈候；開屯休戊巳，折衝停上下魚書。雖盛世不忘兵，但暫息雲中之騎；在治朝豈愛佛，惟遠懷徼外之人。爰錫絲言，旌其懇款；載頒綺幣，授以禪師。偏譯拱辰，環爻閭而繫組；穹居歸日，睹陰羽而搖鼉。盛矣，一統皇輿；大哉，八埏王會！乾坤開闢而後，未有兹勛；符命授繼以來，獨當鉅美。是宜宣之郊廟，光昭宗子之成功；用以勒諸鼎彝，永著大君之有道。上駕
translation_en: …court tribute. Their offerings are arrayed as gifts of the soil, emptying the herds of Kunlun-hoofed steeds from Ferghana (Dayuan); their memorials beg for the restoration of original investitures, filling baskets with felt and woolens from Tibet (Tufan). Those who once trampled the grass now rest by day beside the bamboo palisades; those who wash their spears now draw down the Milky Way by night. They come to court for audience in spring and autumn, presenting their offerings in keeping with the seasonal migrations of the wild geese; we open military colonies and give rest to the Wuji Commandery, halting the tally-letters that passed up and down for frontier defense. Although a flourishing age does not forget warfare, it temporarily rests the cavalry of Yunzhong; in a well-governed court, how could there be a fondness for the Buddha? It is only to cherish from afar the peoples beyond the frontier. Thus Your Majesty bestows silken words of decree to commend their earnest sincerity, and again grants patterned silks and gifts, conferring the title of Chan Master (Chanshi). Through relay translation they turn toward the North Star, encircling the chanyu's court [?] with silken cords of office tied to their necks; from their domed felt tents they turn toward the sun, gazing upon the crane-feathered standards and beating their alligator-skin drums. Magnificent indeed is the unified imperial domain; great indeed is the royal gathering from the eight extremities! Since heaven and earth were first opened, there has never been such merit; since the Mandate's tallies have been conferred and succeeded, this alone claims the supreme beauty. It is fitting that this be proclaimed in the suburban altars and ancestral temple, brilliantly manifesting the accomplished work of the Eldest Son of the Lineage; and that it be inscribed upon the bronze tripods and sacrificial vessels, forever displaying that the Great Sovereign possesses the Way—surpassing…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
貢獒之治榮稱
獻雉之
朝臣等志固切於請纓籌實疎於借箸覩兩
階之干羽莫賛一詞同四海之謳歌惟勤
三祝伏願
柔遠能邇
居安思危
鳳沼集夔龍益密內修之計
雲臺收頗牧愈詳外攘之猷
===
御以和御以威固升平於
天保
莫不王莫不享宜豐大於
日中臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖欣躍屏營之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
punctuated: 貢獒之治，榮稱獻雉之朝。臣等志固切於請纓，籌實疎於借箸。覩兩階之干羽，莫賛一詞；同四海之謳歌，惟勤三祝。伏願柔遠能邇，居安思危。鳳沼集夔、龍，益密內修之計；雲臺收頗、牧，愈詳外攘之猷。御以和，御以威，固升平於《天保》；莫不王，莫不享，宜豐大於日中。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、欣躍屏營之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。
translation_en: … the governance that received the tribute of the mastiff, and gloriously rivaling the court that was presented with the white pheasant. Though Your servants' ambitions are earnest to request the long cord to bind foreign rulers, our strategic planning is truly too inept to borrow the chopsticks at Your table. Witnessing the shield-and-plume dances between the two staircases, we cannot add a single word of praise; joining the songs of the Four Seas, we can only be diligent in offering the three blessings. We humbly pray that You will be gracious to the distant and draw near those close at hand, and be mindful of danger while dwelling in security. May the Phoenix Pool gather ministers like Kui and Long, further refining the plans for internal governance; may the Cloud Terrace recruit generals like Lian Po and Li Mu, making ever more thorough the strategies for repelling external threats. Governing with harmony and governing with majesty, consolidate the ascending peace described in the ode "Heaven Protects" (Tianbao); with none failing to acknowledge Your kingship and none failing to bring tribute, properly maintain abundance and greatness as at the sun's zenith. Your servants, overcome with the utmost awe and joy as we gaze up at Heaven and look toward Your Sacred Majesty, reverently present this memorial of congratulations for Your Imperial hearing.

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第叁場
策
第一問
同考試官訓導胡批據禮議更
廟制此
朝廷誕章足垂
憲萬世者卽掌故案牒莫揣其指此作敷陳且悉本末奇瑋哉
同考試官訓導梁批儒者守章句闇于
===
國制何謂通今子纚纚條析之邃學玄覽士也
考試官學正陳批考據精覈非以臆決策者
考試官學正王批立議準禮語無空設
聖王之制禮也時爲大順次之宜於時者
不必襲古之故而鑿於今者則當協禮之
經時者與世推移之法也順者一定不易
之分也夫古今異宜損益異制辟若四時
還相爲令誰能執之使一哉而律數味臭
要各有定不可得而移也議禮者亦由是
punctuated:
第叁場

策

第一問

同考試官訓導胡批：據禮議更廟制，此朝廷誕章，足垂憲萬世者，卽掌故案牒莫揣其指。此作敷陳，且悉本末，奇瑋哉！
同考試官訓導梁批：儒者守章句，闇于國制，何謂通今？子纚纚條析之，邃學玄覽士也。
考試官學正陳批：考據精覈，非以臆決策者。
考試官學正王批：立議準禮，語無空設。

聖王之制禮也，時爲大，順次之。宜於時者，不必襲古之故；而鑿於今者，則當協禮之經。時者，與世推移之法也；順者，一定不易之分也。夫古今異宜，損益異制，辟若四時還相爲令，誰能執之使一哉？而律數味臭，要各有定，不可得而移也。議禮者亦由是
translation_en:
Third Session

Policy Essays (ce)

First Question

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor (xundao) Hu comments: Deliberating on reforming the ancestral temple system on the basis of ritual is a grand statute of the Imperial Court, sufficient to hand down as a model for ten thousand generations; even those in charge of historical precedents and archival records cannot fathom its purport. This essay sets it forth in detail and thoroughly grasps the roots and branches—how extraordinary and magnificent!
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Liang comments: Scholars cling to chapter and verse and are ignorant of the institutions of the dynasty; how can that be called understanding the present? You have analyzed the matter point by point in continuous order—truly a scholar of profound learning and far-reaching vision.
Examiner and Director of Studies (xuezheng) Chen comments: The evidentiary research is precise and thorough; this is not someone who answers policy questions by mere conjecture.
Examiner and Director of Studies Wang comments: The arguments are established in accordance with ritual, and no words are uttered in vain.

In the sage kings' institution of ritual, timeliness is the greatest principle, and accordance comes next. What is suited to the times need not repeat the precedents of antiquity; yet what is forced in the present ought to harmonize with the constant norms of ritual. "Timeliness" is the principle of shifting and changing along with the age; "accordance" is the fixed and unalterable allotment of things. Now, antiquity and the present differ in what is appropriate, and additions and abridgments differ in their institutional forms. It is just like the four seasons revolving in turn to govern the year—who could hold fast to them and make them uniform? Yet their pitch-pipes, numbers, flavors, and odors in essence each have their fixed determinations and cannot be altered. Those who deliberate on ritual also proceed from this…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
矣是故有以疏爲貴者有以數爲貴者總
之奉神明之統美報荅之情順仁孝之思
爲後世法程其義一也位次有列也版祝
有數也稱名有物也一不得其理卽陳信
愧而怨恫生矣物大之謂何蓋孔子入太
廟每事問執事以問諸生豈徒有所不知
審之也顧諸生者目不瞻宗廟之美足不
習駿奔之節其何藉以對雖然試頌言之
自古帝王之興曷不本始神聖肇廟祀以
===
仁祖考哉虞夏而往無述已見於王制曰
天子七廟三昭三穆與太祖之廟而七蓋
準乎商道矣有時享以祀在廟之主而舉
於四時有大祫以合已祧之主而行於歲
暮坐次曰位致詞曰祝揭主曰稱侑食曰
配雖不皆經見而禮宜具之未聞其有九
也九廟之制始自唐之玄宗至宋祔獻懿
以厭太祖而後世因沿遂不可變君子訾
之曰非古也夫禮有以多爲貴者王者德
punctuated:
矣。是故有以疏爲貴者，有以數爲貴者，總之奉神明之統，美報荅之情，順仁孝之思，爲後世法程，其義一也。位次有列也，版祝有數也，稱名有物也，一不得其理，卽陳信愧而怨恫生矣，物大之謂何？蓋孔子入太廟每事問，執事以問諸生，豈徒有所不知審之也？顧諸生者，目不瞻宗廟之美，足不習駿奔之節，其何藉以對？雖然，試頌言之。
自古帝王之興，曷不本始神聖、肇廟祀以仁祖考哉？虞、夏而往，無述已。見於《王制》曰：「天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七。」蓋準乎商道矣。有時享以祀在廟之主，而舉於四時；有大祫以合已祧之主，而行於歲暮。坐次曰位，致詞曰祝，揭主曰稱，侑食曰配，雖不皆經見，而禮宜具之，未聞其有九也。九廟之制，始自唐之玄宗，至宋祔獻、懿以厭太祖，而後世因沿，遂不可變。君子訾之曰：「非古也。」夫禮有以多爲貴者，王者德
translation_en:
… [proceeds from this]. Therefore, there are rites in which infrequency is valued, and rites in which frequency is valued; in sum, in upholding the lineage of the spirits, perfecting the sentiment of grateful reciprocation, complying with thoughts of benevolence and filial piety, and serving as a standard for later generations, their meaning is one and the same. The seating order has its ranks, the liturgical plaques and invocations have their prescribed numbers, and the appellations have their substantive grounds. If even one of these fails to attain its proper principle, then in setting forth one's good faith before the spirits there is shame, and resentment and grief arise—what then becomes of the saying that "the sacrificial vessels and offerings are grand" [cf. Book of Changes, Hexagram 45]? Indeed, when Confucius entered the Grand Temple, he asked about everything; when the Examiners now ask us students about this, is it merely to examine something that is not yet known? Yet for students whose eyes have never beheld the beauty of the ancestral temple and whose feet have never practiced the steps of swift attendance at sacrifice, on what can I rely to reply? Even so, let me venture to speak of it openly.

Since antiquity, in the rise of emperors and kings, how have they not traced their origins back to divine sages and founded temple sacrifices in order to show benevolent devotion to their ancestors and deceased fathers? Of Yu [Shun] and Xia and earlier, nothing is transmitted. What is seen in the "Royal Regulations" (Wangzhi) says: "The Son of Heaven has seven ancestral temples: three on the left (zhao) and three on the right (mu), which together with the temple of the Grand Progenitor make seven." This was probably modeled on the way of the Shang. There were seasonal sacrifices (shixiang) to worship the spirit tablets remaining in the temples, performed in the four seasons; and there was the great collective sacrifice (daxia) to unite the spirit tablets that had already been removed to the distant shrines (tiao), performed at the end of the year. The seating order was called "position" (wei), the delivered address was called "invocation" (zhu), the inscription on the spirit tablet was called "appellation" (cheng), and the companion at the sacrificial meal was called "associate" (pei); although these are not all found in the Classics, ritual propriety requires that they be provided—yet one never heard of there being nine temples. The institution of nine ancestral temples began with Xuanzong of the Tang; by the Song, Xianzhu and Yizu were enshrined alongside so that they overshadowed the Grand Progenitor (Taizu), and later generations followed the precedent until it could no longer be changed. Gentlemen criticized this, saying: "It is not the way of antiquity." Now in ritual, there are cases in which abundance is valued. When a true king's virtue…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
厚流光自仁率祖卽增七爲九何侈哉我
太祖高皇帝受命稽古首建
廟闕左以享
德
熙
懿
仁四親而
壽春諸王咸以次而侑享焉
文皇帝繼統上承
===
先德建廟北平以享
列祖
太祖四親而壽春諸王以次在侑於時廟數猶
未定也至
憲宗純皇帝以世代旣足始備
九廟之制四
列祖一
太祖一
成祖並
punctuated: 厚流光，自仁率祖，卽增七爲九，何侈哉！我太祖高皇帝受命稽古，首建廟闕左，以享德、熙、懿、仁四親，而壽春諸王咸以次而侑享焉。文皇帝繼統，上承先德，建廟北平，以享列祖、太祖四親，而壽春諸王以次在侑，於時廟數猶未定也。至憲宗純皇帝，以世代旣足，始備九廟之制，四列祖、一太祖、一成祖，並
translation_en:
… [whose virtue] is deep and whose glory flows far, proceeds from benevolence to honor his ancestors, even if he increases the seven [shrines] to nine, how is that extravagant?

When our Grand Progenitor the Exalted Emperor (Taizu Gao Huangdi 太祖高皇帝) received the Mandate and investigated antiquity, he first erected the ancestral temple to the left of the palace gate in order to sacrifice to his four immediate ancestors—Dezu (德祖), Xizu (熙祖), Yizu (懿祖), and Renzu (仁祖)—while the Prince of Shouchun (壽春王) and the other princes all shared in the sacrifices as correlates in order of precedence. When the Cultured Emperor (Wen Huangdi 文皇帝, i.e., the Yongle Emperor) succeeded to the line of rule, upholding the virtue of his predecessors, he erected the ancestral temple in Beiping (北平) to sacrifice to the successive imperial ancestors—the Grand Progenitor and the four immediate ancestors—with the Prince of Shouchun and the other princes serving as correlates in order of precedence; at that time, the number of temple shrines was still not fixed. Coming down to Emperor Xianzong the Pure (Xianzong Chun Huangdi 憲宗純皇帝), because the number of generations was now sufficient, he first completed the institution of the Nine Shrines: four for the successive ancestral progenitors, one for the Grand Progenitor (Taizu), one for the Accomplished Progenitor (Chengzu 成祖), together with…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
仁
宣
英三宗爲九而規制於是大定矣於時升祧之
禮猶未講也至
世宗肅皇帝以世數旣盈復更
九廟之制一
太祖一
成祖六
仁
===
宣
英
憲
孝
武並
獻帝升祔爲九而典禮於是乎益詳矣春月特
享則分祭於各室三時合享則共食於
前殿而已祧之廟不與焉時享之禮則以
太祖爲尊歲暮之祫則升
punctuated: 仁、宣、英三宗為九，而規制於是大定矣。於時升祧之禮猶未講也。至世宗肅皇帝以世數既盈，復更九廟之制，一太祖、一成祖、六仁、宣、英、憲、孝、武，並獻帝升祔為九，而典禮於是乎益詳矣。春月特享，則分祭於各室；三時合享，則共食於前殿，而已祧之廟不與焉。時享之禮，則以太祖為尊；歲暮之祫，則升
translation_en: … the three Ancestors—Renzong, Xuanzong, and Yingzong—making nine, and with this the institutional framework was largely settled. At that time, the rites for elevating and removing spirit tablets had still not been deliberated upon. When it came to Emperor Shizong Su, because the number of generations had reached its limit, he again altered the system of the Nine Temples: one for Taizu, one for Chengzu, six for Renzong, Xuanzong, Yingzong, Xianzong, Xiaozong, and Wuzong, together with Emperor Xian elevated and enshrined, making nine; and with this the ritual statutes became all the more detailed. For the individual offerings in the spring month, sacrifices are offered separately in each chamber; for the joint offerings in the other three seasons, they partake together in the Front Hall, while the ancestral tablets that have already been removed to the repository do not participate. In the rite of seasonal offerings, Taizu is held as the most honored; in the grand joint sacrifice at the close of the year, they elevate…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
四祖於上而祧廟之主咸出而共享焉當
憲廟時
四祖並列殆體
太祖之心乎而
九廟未足禮固不得而有祧也至
世廟之時
四祖並祧固尊
太祖之位乎而世數已足勢不容於無祧矣其
或祧或升之次合享分享之儀孰非酌之
===
今而諧揆之古而不悖者乎歷世滋久訛
舛相承鑿於名實莫可致詰矣以今日言
之弘治中時享祝文稱
八廟
太皇太后
皇考憲宗皇帝蓋親禰也而
九廟之數若減其一至嘉靖中
孝宗而上本七廟也而稱六及
仁宗奉祧猶六廟也而稱五偹損偹益何廟數
punctuated: 四祖於上，而祧廟之主咸出而共享焉。當憲廟時，四祖並列，殆體太祖之心乎？而九廟未足，禮固不得而有祧也。至世廟之時，四祖並祧，固尊太祖之位乎？而世數已足，勢不容於無祧矣。其或祧或升之次，合享分享之儀，孰非酌之今而諧、揆之古而不悖者乎？歷世滋久，訛舛相承，鑿於名實，莫可致詰矣。以今日言之，弘治中時享祝文稱八廟、太皇太后、皇考憲宗皇帝，蓋親禰也，而九廟之數若減其一。至嘉靖中，孝宗而上本七廟也而稱六；及仁宗奉祧，猶六廟也而稱五。偹損偹益，何廟數
translation_en: … the Four Ancestors above, and the spirit tablets from the shrine of removed ancestors (tiaomiao) are all brought out to partake together in the sacrifice. During the time of Emperor Xianzong (Xianmiao, r. 1465–1487), the Four Ancestors were arrayed together—was this not taking to heart the mind of Taizu? Moreover, since the number of Nine Ancestral Shrines (jiumiao) had not yet been filled, by ritual principle none could yet be removed. By the time of Emperor Shizong (Shimiao, r. 1522–1566), the Four Ancestors were all removed to the remote shrine—was this not honoring the position of Taizu? Moreover, since the number of generations was already complete, circumstances did not permit there to be no removal. As for the order of who was removed or elevated, and the ceremonies of joint sacrifice and separate sacrifice, which of them was not deliberated upon to harmonize with the present and measured against antiquity without contradiction? As generations passed and time grew long, errors and discrepancies were inherited one after another; forced interpretations confounded name and reality until they could no longer be sorted out. To speak of the present day: during the Hongzhi reign (1488–1505), the ritual prayer text (zhuwen) for the seasonal sacrifices addressed the Eight Shrines, the Grand Empress Dowager, and the Imperial Deceased Father Emperor Xianzong; these were the immediate ancestral shrines, yet the number of Nine Shrines seemed reduced by one. By the Jiajing reign (1522–1566), from Emperor Xiaozong upward there were originally seven shrines, yet they were referred to as six; and when Emperor Renzong was respectfully removed, there were still six shrines, yet they were referred to as five. Suddenly decreasing, suddenly increasing [? 偹損偹益, for 乍損乍益]—why is the number of shrines…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之不常耶五廟之中
仁宗並祧惟三廟設祭而祝文猶五是祭省而
祝增矣自
皇高祖憲宗至
皇考穆宗旣備六廟而
太祖
成
英三廟猶仍五廟之稱是廟加而祝減矣何謂
號之無定耶
===
壽春王於
太祖爲叔
霍丘七王爲兄而
寶應七王姪也
英廟時誤稱壽春及霍丘七王爲
皇高伯祖寶應七王爲
皇曾伯祖紊矣今世系益遠而槩稱爲
皇曾伯祖是紊而又紊也何稱名之弗當耶夫
禮順人情辨尊卑定名分明嫌疑使生者
punctuated: 之不常耶？五廟之中，仁宗並祧，惟三廟設祭，而祝文猶五，是祭省而祝增矣。自皇高祖憲宗至皇考穆宗，旣備六廟，而太祖、成、英三廟猶仍五廟之稱，是廟加而祝減矣。何謂號之無定耶？壽春王於太祖爲叔，霍丘七王爲兄，而寶應七王，姪也。英廟時，誤稱壽春及霍丘七王爲皇高伯祖，寶應七王爲皇曾伯祖，紊矣。今世系益遠，而槩稱爲皇曾伯祖，是紊而又紊也。何稱名之弗當耶？夫禮順人情，辨尊卑，定名分，明嫌疑，使生者
translation_en:
… be so inconsistent? Among the five temples, when Renzong was also removed to the distant ancestor shrine (tiao 祧), sacrifices were set out in only three temples, yet the ritual prayer text still spoke of five; thus the sacrifices were reduced while the prayer text increased them. From the August High-Great-Grandfather Xianzong down to the Deceased Imperial Father Muzong, six temples were already complete, yet for the three temples of Taizu, Chengzu, and Yingzong, the designation of five temples was still retained; thus the temples were increased while the prayer text reduced them. Why are the designations so unfixed?

The Prince of Shouchun (Shouchun wang 壽春王) was an uncle to Taizu, the seven princes beginning with the Prince of Huoqiu (Huoqiu wang 霍丘王) were his elder brothers, and the seven princes beginning with the Prince of Baoying (Baoying wang 寶應王) were his nephews. In the time of Yingzong, the Prince of Shouchun and the seven princes beginning with Huoqiu were erroneously addressed as August High-Great-Granduncles, and the seven princes beginning with Baoying as August Great-Granduncles, which was already a confusion of generational order. Now the generational lineage is even more distant, yet they are all uniformly addressed as August Great-Granduncles; this is compounding confusion upon confusion. Why are the appellations so inappropriate?

Now, ritual accords with human feelings, distinguishes superior and inferior, fixes names and statuses, and clarifies doubtful cases, causing the living to…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
辨於席也行者辨於途也而後理得順人
心得安焉幽明一也夫祭者察鬼神之情
通幽明之交先王用之以禮神而鬼神享
人倫明矣故曰宗廟之禮所以序昭穆也
燕毛所以序齒也烏有處非其位席非其
次稱非其名而足以成禮者乎難以享矣
我
皇上睿哲誠敬通于神明一抉紕繆而釐正之
至篤孝也愚無所識知謹輒以臆决夫
===
太廟者
太祖之廟也我
皇祖開天啓運功德無比
德祖雖尊不得以情掩義謂宜世享南面東侑
成祖其餘升遐則祔親盡則遷位止於九而勿
之過則升祧定而世次明矣諸廟
帝后並揭徽稱及時享而謹核之祭必一其祝
祝必一其廟使神各有麗則繁簡當而位
號秩矣由
punctuated: 辨於席也，行者辨於途也，而後理得順、人心得安焉。幽明一也。夫祭者，察鬼神之情，通幽明之交；先王用之以禮神，而鬼神享、人倫明矣。故曰：「宗廟之禮，所以序昭穆也；燕毛，所以序齒也。」烏有處非其位、席非其次、稱非其名，而足以成禮者乎？難以享矣。我皇上睿哲誠敬，通于神明，一抉紕繆而釐正之，至篤孝也。愚無所識知，謹輒以臆决。夫太廟者，太祖之廟也。我皇祖開天啓運，功德無比；德祖雖尊，不得以情掩義。謂宜世享南面，東侑成祖；其餘升遐則祔，親盡則遷，位止於九而勿之過，則升祧定而世次明矣。諸廟帝后，並揭徽稱，及時享而謹核之，祭必一其祝，祝必一其廟，使神各有麗，則繁簡當而位號秩矣。由
translation_en:
… are distinguished at their mats, and those who walk are distinguished on the road; only then is principle brought into harmony and the human heart set at ease. The realms of the unseen and the seen are one. Now, sacrifice is that by which one examines the dispositions of ghosts and spirits and communicates across the boundary of the unseen and the seen. The former kings used it to show ritual respect to the spirits, so that the ghosts and spirits enjoyed the offerings and human relationships were made clear. Therefore it is said: "The rites of the ancestral temple serve to order the generational sequence of zhao and mu; the banquet ordering by hair color serves to order seniority by age." How could anyone occupy what is not their proper position, sit at what is not their proper place in sequence, or be addressed by what is not their proper title, and yet suffice to accomplish the rites? It would be difficult for the spirits to enjoy the offerings!

Our August Emperor, sagely wise and sincerely reverent, communicates with the divine intelligence; at a single stroke he has exposed these errors and rectified them, which is the utmost of devoted filial piety. Ignorant and without knowledge as I am, I respectfully venture to offer my own humble judgment.

Now, the Grand Temple is the temple of Grand Progenitor (Taizu). Our August Ancestor opened up Heaven and inaugurated our destiny, his merit and virtue beyond compare; although Progenitor of Virtue (Dezu) is venerated, personal sentiment must not be allowed to obscure righteous principle. I would say that Grand Progenitor should for all generations enjoy the south-facing seat, accompanied on the east by Eminent Progenitor (Chengzu). As for the rest, when they ascend to the distant realm they should be enshrined, and when kinship ties are exhausted they should be removed to the distant shrines, the number of spirit tablets stopping at nine and not exceeding this; then rules for enshrinement and removal will be settled and the generational sequence will be clear. As for the Emperors and Empresses of the various temples, whose exalted titles are displayed together, when the seasonal sacrifices arrive they should be carefully verified: each sacrifice must have a unified invocatory prayer, and each invocatory prayer must correspond to a single temple, so that every spirit has its proper attachment; then elaboration and brevity will be appropriate and the positions and titles will be in order. Tracing from …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
太祖而上下之諸王之分雖百世可知也或者
謂詳定爲難惟各稱本爵而勿概以
皇曾伯祖加焉則稱謂有經而名言順矣世次
明則昭穆定位號秩則孚假易名言順則
觀聽諧釐此三者庶幾哉盡倫乎嘻猶其
疏節爾記曰有其舉之莫敢廢也言率古
也曰恥無其實而有其名言思義也昭穆
之制非古乎曷名其爲昭也居祖之左面
南而明巳爾曷名其爲穆也居祖之右面
===
北而穆巳爾今也廟分九室室各南向卽
大祫前殿亦南上而旁列本楹也而曰廟本一
也而曰九本同堂異室之制而猶仍昭穆
世次之稱其於義何居焉或者曰祭從先
祖夫有所受之也蓋自
闕左而巳然矣夫
聖祖之然也草創之未暇也
成祖之然也考据之未詳也至於
世廟斯不得巳而遷就之爾語曰禮失求之野
punctuated: 太祖而上下之，諸王之分，雖百世可知也。或者謂詳定爲難，惟各稱本爵，而勿概以皇曾伯祖加焉，則稱謂有經而名言順矣。世次明則昭穆定，位號秩則孚假易，名言順則觀聽諧。釐此三者，庶幾哉盡倫乎！嘻，猶其疏節爾。《記》曰：「有其舉之，莫敢廢也。」言率古也。曰：「恥無其實而有其名。」言思義也。昭穆之制，非古乎？曷名其爲昭也？居祖之左，面南而明巳爾。曷名其爲穆也？居祖之右，面北而穆巳爾。今也，廟分九室，室各南向，卽大祫前殿，亦南上而旁列。本楹也，而曰廟；本一也，而曰九；本同堂異室之制，而猶仍昭穆世次之稱，其於義何居焉？或者曰：「祭從先祖。」夫有所受之也，蓋自闕左而巳然矣。夫聖祖之然也，草創之未暇也；成祖之然也，考据之未詳也；至於世廟，斯不得巳而遷就之爾。語曰：「禮失求之野。」
translation_en: … the Grand Progenitor (Taizu 太祖) upward and downward, the proper distinctions among the various princes can be known even for a hundred generations. Some say that determining these details is difficult; yet if each is simply addressed by his own princely title, without indiscriminately prefixing 'Imperial Great-Grand-Uncle' (Huang zengbozu 皇曾伯祖) and the like, then the forms of address will follow a constant standard and names and words will be in accord with right principle. When generational order is clear, the zhao and mu (昭穆) positions are fixed; when titles and designations are properly ordered, sincere communion with the spirits is easily achieved; when names and words are in accord, what is seen and heard is harmonious. By rectifying these three matters, might we not come close to fulfilling the principles of human relationships! Alas, these are still only the broader outlines. The Record of Rites (Ji 記) says: 'What has once been instituted, none dares abolish'—meaning that one follows antiquity. It also says: 'One is ashamed to have the name without the reality'—meaning that one reflects on the true meaning. Is the system of zhao and mu not ancient? Why is the one called zhao ('luminous')? Simply because it occupies the left of the Founder, facing south toward the light. Why is the other called mu ('solemn')? Simply because it occupies the right of the Founder, facing north in solemn shade. Nowadays, the temple is divided into nine chambers, each chamber facing south; even at the Great Combined Sacrifice (daxia 大祫) in the front hall, the seats are arranged with the south as the place of honor and the rest lined up to the sides. What is actually a bay between pillars is called a 'temple'; what is actually a single building is called 'nine'; what is actually the system of 'the same hall with separate chambers' still retains the designations of zhao and mu generational order—on what principle does this rest? Someone may say: 'In sacrifices, follow the ancestors'—meaning that this was handed down to us, having been so ever since the temple was built to the left of the palace gate. Yet that our Sacred Ancestor (Shengzu 聖祖, the Hongwu Emperor) did so was because in the founding of the dynasty there was not yet leisure for it; that the Accomplished Ancestor (Chengzu 成祖, the Yongle Emperor) did so was because the textual investigation had not yet been made in detail; and when it came to the Temple of the Generation [Ancestors] (Shimiao 世廟, or the reign of Shizong 世宗), this was merely an unavoidable accommodation. As the saying goes: 'When the rites are lost, seek them in the countryside.' …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
今素封之家奉其始祖旁列四親犁然序
也安有生爲天子殁居一楹而屢世並列
廑廑然者商周之事豈其泯泯而奈何執
拘攣之説而隳閎廓之規躡沿流之蹤以
詘
神靈之尊乎草茅主臣雖然猶願有一言者革
除之嵗削紀錄矣而五載之
正朔何所於頒監國之君歸郕邸矣而八年
之
===
重器誰與爲守今死事諸臣巳蒙曠除
景帝位號旋巳議復宜下掌故略議享祀所宜
以補
聖朝禮儀之闕夫
敦孝洽仁以光駿惠之烈有
聖天子陳禮致義以崇繼序之功有賢輔相公
卿詩曰永言孝思孝思維則又曰於穆清
廟肅雝顯相此之謂也諸生所謂綿蕞者
而惡足以知之
punctuated: 今素封之家，奉其始祖，旁列四親，犁然序也。安有生爲天子，殁居一楹，而屢世並列、廑廑然者？商、周之事，豈其泯泯？而奈何執拘攣之説，而隳閎廓之規，躡沿流之蹤，以詘神靈之尊乎？草茅主臣。雖然，猶願有一言者：革除之嵗，削紀錄矣，而五載之正朔，何所於頒？監國之君，歸郕邸矣，而八年之重器，誰與爲守？今死事諸臣巳蒙曠除，景帝位號旋巳議復，宜下掌故，略議享祀所宜，以補聖朝禮儀之闕。夫敦孝洽仁，以光駿惠之烈，有聖天子；陳禮致義，以崇繼序之功，有賢輔相公卿。《詩》曰：「永言孝思，孝思維則。」又曰：「於穆清廟，肅雝顯相。」此之謂也。諸生所謂綿蕞者，而惡足以知之！
translation_en: Nowadays, even wealthy commoner families without official rank enshrine their founding ancestor with the four generations of immediate ancestors arrayed at the sides in clear, orderly sequence. How could those who in life were Sons of Heaven in death occupy a single bay, with several generations lined up side by side in such cramped fashion? Are the precedents of the Shang and Zhou dynasties utterly lost? Why then cling to narrow, fettered theories and ruin a grand and spacious design, following along in inherited ruts to diminish the august dignity of the sacred spirits? As a rustic commoner, Your Servant isfilled with awe and trepidation. Even so, I still wish to offer one further word: the years of the Jianwen era (1399–1402), whose reign title was expunged, have been struck from the records—yet from whom was the official calendar of those five years promulgated? The ruler who served as Regent of the State was returned upon his death to the status of the Princedom of Cheng—yet who was it that guarded the sacred vessels of sovereignty during those eight years? Now the various officials who died for the Jianwen cause have already received the magnanimous pardon of having their proscriptions lifted, and the imperial title of Emperor Jing (the Jingtai Emperor, r. 1450–1457) was subsequently restored after deliberation. It would be fitting to refer the matter to the authorities versed in institutional precedents to deliberate in outline on the proper sacrificial honors for them, so as to remedy the deficiencies in the ritual institutions of our Sacred Dynasty. Indeed, to deepen filial piety and spread benevolence so as to glorify the magnificent achievements of our ancestors, we have the Sage Son of Heaven; to set forth the rites and fulfill righteousness so as to exalt the merit of continuing the dynastic line, we have worthy Grand Secretaries, Chief Ministers, and Nine卿 (Nine Chief Ministers). The Book of Odes (Shijing) says: "Forever he cherishes filial thoughts; his filial thoughts are the model." And again it says: "Ah! solemn is the hallowed temple; reverent and harmonious are the illustrious assistants." This is what is meant. As for a student like myself—practicing mere rudimentary rituals with ropes and straw markers (mianzuo)—how could I be worthy of understanding such things!

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第二問
同考試官訓導王批邪說譸沸衞道者豈戅焉
辯固哉不得已也誠有藉于斯文
同考試官訓導徐批漢儒以博學目聖輒傅會
應引大敧不經此作敷答得旨
考試官學正陳批闡辯詳核
考試官學正王批議正辭綺
天下有竅言則聖人無眞詮竅言不作則
士不惑眞詮不贋則聖人益尊故一藝之
指必有師焉百家之市必有平焉當治敎
綦隆之世學術炳炳如日星然藉令其人
是非一不當則羣詫而異之攻而斥之矣
乃傳沿久遠睹記大盤率詆訾聖人以爲
常一唱羣和誰復詫異哉月旦稱朔車輈
亦稱朔五爵六燕飛易其處軒輊豈足憑
耶於乎往牒浩繁不可勝辯矣有如孔子
者自天地以來一人而已何亦稯稯然行
punctuated:
第二問

同考試官訓導王批：邪說譸沸，衞道者豈戅焉辯固哉？不得已也。誠有藉于斯文。
同考試官訓導徐批：漢儒以博學目聖，輒傅會應引，大敧不經。此作敷答得旨。
考試官學正陳批：闡辯詳核。
考試官學正王批：議正辭綺。

天下有竅言，則聖人無眞詮。竅言不作，則士不惑；眞詮不贋，則聖人益尊。故一藝之指，必有師焉；百家之市，必有平焉。當治敎綦隆之世，學術炳炳如日星然。藉令其人是非一不當，則羣詫而異之，攻而斥之矣。乃傳沿久遠，睹記大盤，率詆訾聖人以爲常，一唱羣和，誰復詫異哉？月旦稱朔，車輈亦稱朔；五爵六燕，飛易其處，軒輊豈足憑耶？於乎！往牒浩繁，不可勝辯矣。有如孔子者，自天地以來一人而已，何亦稯稯然行
translation_en:
Second Question

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Wang comments: When heterodox doctrines boil up in deceitful clamor, is it out of foolish stubbornness in disputation that defenders of the Way argue against them? They have no choice. Truly, one relies on this essay!
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Xu comments: Han-dynasty scholars viewed the Sage merely through the lens of广博 erudition, and thus constantly forced connections and citations, which were mostly [?] uncanonical. This composition elaborates its reply and grasps the main purport.
Examiner and Director of Studies Chen comments: The exposition and argumentation are detailed and well-verified.
Examiner and Director of Studies Wang comments: The arguments are orthodox and the diction is fine.

When there are specious words [?] in the world, the Sage has no true explanation; when specious words do not arise, scholars are not deluded; when the true explanation is not counterfeited, the Sage is all the more revered. Therefore, the principles of a single art must have a master, and a marketplace of a hundred families must have a standard of weights and measures. In an age when governance and moral instruction are at their utmost flourishing, scholarly learning shines brightly like the sun and stars. Even if a person makes a single misjudgment of right and wrong, the crowd will be astonished, regard it as strange, attack it, and reject it. Yet as traditions are handed down over a long time and what is seen and recorded becomes vast and tangled [?], people generally make a habit of slandering and disparaging the Sage; one leads the chant and the crowd echoes it—who anymore finds it astonishing or strange? The first day of the moon is called shuo, and the pole of a carriage is also called shuo [?]; five sparrows and six swallows, when flying, change their places—how can their relative weight on the scale be relied upon? Alas! Past records are vast and numerous, beyond what can be fully refuted. Take someone like Confucius (Kongzi): since heaven and earth began, there has been this one man alone. Why then were his actions also so crowded with…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
詘于鄉里而名毀當世也彼號爲知道則
有莊周列禦寇博物則有左丘明司馬遷
韓嬰劉向傳信則有家語檀弓國語諸書
亡慮數十家矣乃人人詆訾之如一口是
遵何說哉蓋其故有三孔子之在春秋恂
恂如也不務爲可喜可愕之事以爲名高
故當世之人竊姍唉孔子無足稱也是見
杜德幾者也不知孔子者也又有鉛槧佔
畢之倫稍欲文采表著于後世則竊以其
===
言託之乎孔子以取信來世彼其書庬雜
易以蔑實此所謂魯贋讒鼎之見也蓋知
孔子而不恤失其眞者也又有異端者流
見謂孔子之道病已也而心害之則設爲
問答駁論欲以悠繆之言陵駕其上而不
自量其不勝此衛蚳徙澤之見也蓋知孔
子而故抑之者也此三者雖于孔子無加
損然吾不可以無辨夫孔子宋之後也其
先正考父佐戴武宣三命滋益恭因銘諸
punctuated: 詘于鄉里，而名毀當世也？彼號爲知道，則有莊周、列禦寇；博物，則有左丘明、司馬遷、韓嬰、劉向；傳信，則有《家語》、《檀弓》、《國語》諸書，亡慮數十家矣。乃人人詆訾之如一口，是遵何說哉？蓋其故有三：孔子之在春秋，恂恂如也，不務爲可喜可愕之事以爲名高，故當世之人竊姍唉孔子無足稱也。是見杜德幾者也，不知孔子者也。又有鉛槧佔畢之倫，稍欲文采表著于後世，則竊以其言託之乎孔子，以取信來世；彼其書庬雜，易以蔑實，此所謂魯贋讒鼎之見也，蓋知孔子而不恤失其眞者也。又有異端者流，見謂孔子之道病已也而心害之，則設爲問答駁論，欲以悠繆之言陵駕其上，而不自量其不勝，此衛蚳徙澤之見也，蓋知孔子而故抑之者也。此三者雖于孔子無加損，然吾不可以無辨。夫孔子，宋之後也，其先正考父佐戴、武、宣，三命滋益恭，因銘諸
translation_en:
…thwarted in his conduct among his乡里 (home villages), and his reputation disparaged in his own age? Among those acclaimed for understanding the Way, there were Zhuang Zhou 莊周 and Lie Yukou 列禦寇; for broad learning, there were Zuo Qiuming 左丘明, Sima Qian 司馬遷, Han Ying 韓嬰, and Liu Xiang 劉向; and for transmitting reliable accounts, there are books such as the Kongzi jiayu (School Sayings of Confucius), the "Tan Gong" chapter [of the Record of Rites], and the Guoyu (Discourses of the States)—altogether dozens of schools and authors. Yet every one of them disparaged and found fault with him as if speaking with a single voice. On what grounds did they do this?

There are three reasons for it. In the Spring and Autumn period, Confucius was modest and unassuming; he did not strive to perform sensational or astonishing deeds in order to exalt his reputation, and so people of that age secretly mocked and laughed at Confucius as unworthy of praise. This was the view of those who saw only "the workings of blocked-up virtue" [a Zhuangzi allusion]; they were people who did not understand Confucius. Then there were the ranks of mere copyists and pedants who, wishing somewhat to make their literary flair known to posterity, secretly attributed their own words to Confucius in order to win credence from future generations. Because their writings were heterogeneous and motley, they easily obscured the truth. This is what may be called the view of the men of Lu offering a counterfeit Chan tripod; they were people who knew of Confucius, yet did not care that they were losing his true character. Furthermore, there were the adherents of heterodox teachings who, seeing that the Way of Confucius was detrimental to themselves and harboring envy in their hearts, fabricated dialogues and refutations, wishing to use absurd and specious words to place themselves above him without realizing their own inability to prevail. This is the view of the leech of Wei trying to move a marsh; they were people who knew Confucius, yet deliberately sought to belittle him.

Although these three groups neither add to nor detract from Confucius, I cannot leave the matter unexamined. Now, Confucius was a descendant of the state of Song. His ancestor Zheng Kaofu 正考父 assisted Dukes Dai 戴, Wu 武, and Xuan 宣; through three successive appointments he grew ever more reverent, and therefore inscribed upon…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其鼎孟僖子曰聖人有明德者其後必有
達人今其在孔丘乎蓋孔子聖人之後也
孔子之父曰叔梁紇母曰徵在始叔梁紇
求婚於顏顏問三女皆莫對少女徵在曰
惟父所制之遂以妻叔梁紇叔梁紇與徵
在禱于尼丘而生孔子孔子生而徇齊長
而聖惡有平時一不問父墓者使不遇聊
曼父之母將終不知耶五父衢之殯甚矣
史遷之誣也至於防墓旣已封之崇四尺
===
矣又何至不旋踵以壞耶門人反告不應
者三但以古不修墓爲解甚矣檀弓之無
据也魯有三桓猶人附喉之癭也孔子誠
欲墮其三都卽計不萬全肯出哉若不能
策其必勝而費人襲公公果入季氏之宮
登武子之臺靦靦然倉皇避之則謀不已
疎乎左氏蓋以趙鞅召晉陽之兵者目之
也非所以語孔子也夾谷之會齊人目中
無魯矣吾孔子立折其驕麾却萊夷戮其
punctuated: 其鼎。孟僖子曰：「聖人有明德者，其後必有達人，今其在孔丘乎！」蓋孔子，聖人之後也。孔子之父曰叔梁紇，母曰徵在。始叔梁紇求婚於顏，顏問三女，皆莫對。少女徵在曰：「惟父所制之。」遂以妻叔梁紇。叔梁紇與徵在禱于尼丘而生孔子。孔子生而徇齊，長而聖，惡有平時一不問父墓者？使不遇聊曼父之母，將終不知耶？五父衢之殯，甚矣史遷之誣也！至於防墓，旣已封之崇四尺矣，又何至不旋踵以壞耶？門人反告不應者三，但以「古不修墓」爲解，甚矣《檀弓》之無据也！魯有三桓，猶人附喉之癭也。孔子誠欲墮其三都，卽計不萬全，肯出哉？若不能策其必勝，而費人襲公，公果入季氏之宮，登武子之臺，靦靦然倉皇避之，則謀不已疎乎？左氏蓋以趙鞅召晉陽之兵者目之也，非所以語孔子也。夾谷之會，齊人目中無魯矣。吾孔子立折其驕，麾却萊夷，戮其
translation_en: … his tripod. Meng Xizi 孟僖子 said: "When a sage possesses illustrious virtue, among his descendants there will surely be an accomplished person; today, might that not be Kong Qiu 孔丘 [Confucius]!" Indeed, Confucius was the descendant of sages. Confucius's father was named Shuliang He 叔梁紇, and his mother was named Zhengzai 徵在. In the beginning, when Shuliang He sought marriage from the Yan 顏 family, Father Yan asked his three daughters, and none replied. The youngest daughter, Zhengzai, said: "It is solely as Father decides." Thereupon he gave her in marriage to Shuliang He. Shuliang He and Zhengzai prayed at Mount Ni (Niqiu 尼丘) and gave birth to Confucius. Confucius was quick and discerning from birth, and grew up to be a sage; how could there be someone who in ordinary times never once inquired after his father's grave? Had he not met the mother of Liao Manfu 聊曼父, would he have remained ignorant of it to the end? As for the temporary interment at the Wufu 五父 crossroads—how extreme is the fabrication of the Historian Sima Qian 司馬遷 (Shiqian 史遷)! And as for the grave at Fang 防, once it had already been mounded to a height of four feet, how could it have collapsed before they had even turned around? That he thrice failed to answer when his disciples returned to report it, merely offering "the ancients did not repair graves" as an excuse—how extreme is the groundlessness of the "Tangong" 檀弓 [chapter of the Record of Rites]! Lu's 魯 possession of the Three Huan 三桓 clans was like a goiter attached to a man's throat. If Confucius truly wished to demolish their three capitals, would he have been willing to make a move if his plan were not completely foolproof? If he could not calculate certain victory, and the men of Bi 費 attacked the Duke, so that the Duke indeed entered the palace of the Ji 季氏 clan and ascended the terrace of Wuzi 武子, shamefacedly and hurriedly fleeing them, would not the plan have been all too careless? Master Zuo 左氏 (Zuoshi) was probably viewing him in the same light as Zhao Yang 趙鞅 summoning the troops of Jinyang 晉陽; this is no way to speak of Confucius. At the meeting at Jiagu 夾谷, the men of Qi 齊 had no regard for Lu in their eyes. Our Confucius immediately broke their arrogance, waved back the Lai 萊 barbarians, executed their …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
侏儒歸我汶陽田此豈無不戰而屈人者
乎使僅如史記所載歷階而上堇堇然以
口舌爭是叱咤者曹沫藺相如等耳奚足
聖也蓋其料齊變詐請兩司馬以從備矣
故曰有文事者必有武備聖人乎折衝尊
俎之間豈以倉卒虛喝幸哉適周而見老
聃蓋問禮也莊子乃謂孔子見聃而歸三
日不譚曰吾見老子其猶龍乎丘之於道
其猶醯雞與吾不知天地之大全也是何
===
尊之之過也吾意莊周老聃之流欲藉孔
子以尊聃耳孔子嘗望季以敎其弟蹠矣
又安肯往見蹠也而莊子云見蹠泰山之
陽出門上車執轡三失曰疾走幾不免虎
口哉何聖人而愚若是今觀其所爲蹠語
此徒莊周欲詆堯舜孔子之道而託之于
蹠者也過泰山逢婦人而問焉嘆曰苛政
猛于虎此孔子之言也韓詩外傳則稱游
于少源見婦人亡蓍簪而泣嘆曰彼不忘
punctuated: 侏儒，歸我汶陽田，此豈無不戰而屈人者乎？使僅如《史記》所載，歷階而上，堇堇然以口舌爭，是叱咤者曹沫、藺相如等耳，奚足聖也！蓋其料齊變詐，請兩司馬以從，備矣。故曰：「有文事者必有武備。」聖人乎，折衝尊俎之間，豈以倉卒虛喝幸哉！適周而見老聃，蓋問禮也。《莊子》乃謂孔子見聃而歸，三日不譚，曰：「吾見老子，其猶龍乎？丘之於道，其猶醯雞與！吾不知天地之大全也。」是何尊之之過也！吾意莊周老聃之流，欲藉孔子以尊聃耳。孔子嘗望季以敎其弟蹠矣，又安肯往見蹠也？而《莊子》云見蹠泰山之陽，出門上車，執轡三失，曰：「疾走，幾不免虎口哉！」何聖人而愚若是？今觀其所爲蹠語，此徒莊周欲詆堯、舜、孔子之道，而託之于蹠者也。過泰山，逢婦人而問焉，嘆曰：「苛政猛于虎。」此孔子之言也。《韓詩外傳》則稱游于少源，見婦人亡蓍簪而泣，嘆曰：「彼不忘
translation_en: …the dwarfs, and caused them to return our lands of Wenyang—how could this have been accomplished without the capacity to subdue others without fighting? Had he merely ascended the steps and contended solely with tongue and lips, as recorded in the Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji), then he would have been no more than a blusterer on the level of Cao Mo or Lin Xiangru—how would that suffice to make him a sage? Rather, anticipating Qi's treachery and deceit, he had requested that the two Marshals (Sima) accompany the duke, making his preparations complete. Thus he said, "One who undertakes civil affairs must have military preparations." A sage indeed! Repelling the enemy over ritual goblets and stands, how could he have relied on lucky success through hasty, empty threats? When he went to Zhou and met Lao Dan, it was to inquire about the rites. Yet the Zhuangzi claims that after Confucius met Dan and returned, he did not speak for three days, and then said, "I have seen Laozi; is he not like a dragon? In relation to the Way, am I (Qiu) not like a vinegar gnat! I would not have known the great wholeness of Heaven and Earth." How excessive is this exaltation of him! In my view, Zhuang Zhou was a follower of Lao Dan and merely wished to use Confucius to exalt Dan. Confucius once reproached Liuia Ji for failing to instruct his younger brother Zhi [Robber Zhi]; how then would he have been willing to go and visit Zhi himself? Yet the Zhuangzi says that he went to see Zhi on the southern slope of Mount Tai, and that upon going out the gate and mounting his carriage, he dropped the reins three times, saying, "Drive fast! I nearly failed to escape the tiger's jaws!" How could a sage be so foolish as this? Looking today at the words it attributes to Zhi, this is merely Zhuang Zhou wishing to disparage the Way of Yao, Shun, and Confucius and putting those words into the mouth of Zhi. Passing by Mount Tai, he met a woman and had inquiries made of her, sighing, "Tyrannical government is fiercer than a tiger." These are indeed the words of Confucius. Yet the Outer Commentary to the Book of Songs by Master Han (Han shi waizhuan) claims that when he traveled to Shaoyuan, he saw a woman weeping over a lost yarrow-stalk hairpin, and sighed, "She does not forget…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其故矣此非孔子之言也禮男女有别以
明嫌也而田野之間輒從婦人語哉史記
載衛南子召見孔子自絺帷中再拜環珮
之聲璆然此誠孔子之事也至韓嬰則稱
孔子游于阿谷見處子珮瑱而浣者抽觴
與琴授子貢而與之語蓋詩多婦人之詞
韓說詩欲託諸婦人而藉孔子爲信顧言
何卑卑也學琴師襄傳紀之矣乃謂久之
見有人焉黯然而黑頎然而長眼如望羊
===
心期四方襄辟席再拜曰此文王之操也
何其誕也語曰思之惟精其形乃成豈謂
是與登泰山之巔傳載之矣至謂望見吳
閶門外有白馬繫者引顔回問焉回曰見
之若一疋練也又誕之誕者也語曰不視
之見其見萬里殆不然矣六尺之杖以别
親疎之倫其說蓋見諸呂氏春秋及賈誼
新書謂子貢自其家來孔子舉杖磬折而
問其父母已放杖而問其兄弟已乃曳杖
punctuated: 其故矣。」此非孔子之言也。禮，男女有别以明嫌也，而田野之間輒從婦人語哉？《史記》載衛南子召見孔子，自絺帷中再拜，環珮之聲璆然，此誠孔子之事也。至韓嬰則稱孔子游于阿谷，見處子珮瑱而浣者，抽觴與琴授子貢而與之語。蓋《詩》多婦人之詞，韓說《詩》，欲託諸婦人而藉孔子爲信，顧言何卑卑也！學琴師襄，傳紀之矣，乃謂久之見有人焉，黯然而黑，頎然而長，眼如望羊，心期四方，襄辟席再拜曰：「此文王之操也。」何其誕也！語曰：「思之惟精，其形乃成。」豈謂是與？登泰山之巔，傳載之矣，至謂望見吳閶門外有白馬繫者，引顔回問焉，回曰：「見之若一疋練也。」又誕之誕者也！語曰：「不視之見，其見萬里。」殆不然矣。六尺之杖以别親疎之倫，其說蓋見諸《呂氏春秋》及賈誼《新書》，謂子貢自其家來，孔子舉杖磬折而問其父母，已放杖而問其兄弟，已乃曳杖
translation_en: … forgotten what was old to her.” These are not the words of Confucius.
