title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
士不可以不弘毅任重而道遠
同考試官教諭蕭批語意周到刋落陳詞可稱
雄作者之林矣宜首錄
同考試官教諭李批弘毅任道作者類多分析
意㫖支離此篇得之
考試官學正陳批典則可式
===
考試官學正王批格古詞精
大賢之厚望於士者以爲士之不易也夫任重
已難矣矧任之遠乎苟不弘且毅烏能勝其責
哉曾子論士之道如此若曰人之所志者不廣
故其所以自待者薄彼烏知乎大道之責於吾
身而不可以已乎吾是以望士深也何則論士
者必觀其量是故以弘爲貴弘者心之容德也
必也充其本然之量而恢恢乎如有容焉否則
其量不足稱矣不可也觀士者必於其守是故
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
「士不可以不弘毅，任重而道遠。」
同考試官教諭蕭批：語意周到，刋落陳詞，可稱雄作者之林矣，宜首錄。
同考試官教諭李批：弘毅任道，作者類多分析，意㫖支離，此篇得之。
考試官學正陳批：典則可式。
考試官學正王批：格古詞精。

大賢之厚望於士者，以爲士之不易也。夫任重已難矣，矧任之遠乎？苟不弘且毅，烏能勝其責哉？曾子論士之道如此。若曰：人之所志者不廣，故其所以自待者薄。彼烏知乎大道之責於吾身，而不可以已乎？吾是以望士深也。何則？論士者必觀其量，是故以弘爲貴。弘者，心之容德也。必也充其本然之量，而恢恢乎如有容焉；否則，其量不足稱矣，不可也。觀士者必於其守，是故
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
"A scholar-official cannot but be broad-minded and resolute, for his burden is heavy and his road is long."
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Xiao: The expression and meaning are thorough, stripping away hackneyed phrases. It can truly claim preeminence in the forest of writers and ought to be recorded in first place.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Li: Regarding being broad-minded and resolute and taking the Way as one's burden, writers generally tend to split them up in their analysis, making the import fragmented; this essay has grasped it.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Chen: Classical in standard, worthy of serving as a model.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Wang: Archaic in form and refined in diction.

The reason the Great Worthy placed such high hopes in the scholar-official is that it is not easy to be a scholar-official. Now, bearing a heavy burden is difficult enough; how much more so when that burden must be carried far! If one is not both broad-minded and resolute, how can one be equal to the responsibility? Such was Master Zeng's discussion of the Way of the scholar-official. It is as if he said: Because people's aspirations are not broad, what they expect of themselves is slight. How could they know that the responsibility of the Great Way rests upon our own persons and cannot be set aside? That is why I place deep hopes in the scholar-official. Why is this? Those who evaluate a scholar-official must observe his capacity; therefore, broad-mindedness is prized. Broad-mindedness is the encompassing virtue of the mind. One must fulfill one's inherent capacity so that it is vast and all-embracing; otherwise, one's capacity is not worth speaking of, and that will not do. Those who observe a scholar-official must look at his steadfastness; therefore…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以毅爲貴毅者心之恒德也必也養其固有之
能而亹亹然其有恒乎否則其守不足稱矣不
可也夫士何以必期於弘也蓋任之不重器不
廣者或可勝也而士之所任至大蓋天下莫能
載也而皆加諸其身誠重矣其重若此而豈可
以勉疆勝者乎吾見褊中之士鮮不仆矣夫士
何以必期於毅也蓋行之不遠力不足者猶得
勉焉而士之所任且久蓋引之不見其終也
而皆運諸其心誠遠矣其遠若此而豈可以朞
===
月守者乎自非强毅之士廢不中道矣夫士可
以不任重則已如必任重其必由弘乎士可以
不道遠則已如必道遠其必由毅乎具是二者
以肩重致遠士之全德也雖然原本其道不外
乎仁仁則無私無私則弘矣仁則無欲無欲則
不屈而毅矣由此言之任重道遠卽爲弘毅而
弘毅名者非二道也一以貫之曾子之所唯也
是故大人之道通乎天下是其弘也六尺可託
受而全之蓋其毅也夫
punctuated: 以毅爲貴。毅者，心之恒德也。必也養其固有之能，而亹亹然其有恒乎！否則，其守不足稱矣，不可也。夫士何以必期於弘也？蓋任之不重，器不廣者或可勝也。而士之所任至大，蓋天下莫能載也，而皆加諸其身，誠重矣。其重若此，而豈可以勉疆勝者乎？吾見褊中之士鮮不仆矣。夫士何以必期於毅也？蓋行之不遠，力不足者猶得勉焉。而士之所任且久，蓋引之不見其終也，而皆運諸其心，誠遠矣。其遠若此，而豈可以朞月守者乎？自非强毅之士，廢不中道矣。夫士可以不任重則已，如必任重，其必由弘乎！士可以不道遠則已，如必道遠，其必由毅乎！具是二者，以肩重致遠，士之全德也。雖然，原本其道，不外乎仁。仁則無私，無私則弘矣；仁則無欲，無欲則不屈而毅矣。由此言之，任重道遠，卽爲弘毅，而弘毅名者，非二道也。一以貫之，曾子之所唯也。是故大人之道，通乎天下，是其弘也；六尺可託，受而全之，蓋其毅也夫。
translation_en: … takes resolute endurance as precious. Resolute endurance is the constant virtue of the mind. One must nourish one's inherent capability, working tirelessly with constancy! Otherwise, one's steadfastness will not be worth mentioning, and one will not do. Why must a scholar-gentleman be expected to have breadth of mind? Because if a burden is not heavy, even someone of narrow capacity might be able to bear it. Yet what the scholar-gentleman takes upon himself is supremely great—indeed, nothing in the world can carry it, and all of it is placed upon his person; truly it is heavy! When its weight is like this, how could it be borne merely through forced effort [reading 疆 as 強]? I have seen that narrow-minded scholars rarely fail to collapse under it. And why must a scholar-gentleman be expected to have resolute endurance? Because if a journey is not distant, even someone of insufficient strength may still manage to strive through it. Yet what the scholar-gentleman takes upon himself is also prolonged—indeed, drawn out without an end in sight, and all of it must be revolved within his mind; truly it is distant! When its distance is like this, how could it be maintained for just a month or a year? Unless one is a scholar of strong and resolute endurance, one will give up halfway [? 廢不中道, perhaps for 鮮不中道廢 "rarely fail to give up halfway"]. Now, if a scholar-gentleman could avoid bearing a heavy burden, that would be the end of it; but if he must bear a heavy burden, it must surely be through breadth of mind! If a scholar-gentleman could avoid a distant course, that would be the end of it; but if he must travel a distant course, it must surely be through resolute endurance! Possessing both of these so as to shoulder a heavy burden and reach a distant goal is the complete virtue of the scholar-gentleman. Even so, tracing the source of this Way, it is nothing other than humaneness (ren). Where there is humaneness, there is no selfishness, and where there is no selfishness, there is breadth of mind; where there is humaneness, there is no selfish desire, and where there is no selfish desire, one is unyielding and thus possesses resolute endurance. Speaking from this perspective, bearing a heavy burden and traveling a distant course are themselves breadth of mind and resolute endurance, and what are called breadth of mind and resolute endurance are not two separate Ways. "One thread binding it all together"—this was what Master Zeng (Zengzi) assented to. Therefore, the Way of the great man reaches throughout the world—such is his breadth of mind; he can be entrusted with a young orphan ("six-foot" ward), receiving the charge and preserving it whole—such indeed is his resolute endurance!

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
質諸鬼神而無疑知天也百世以俟聖人
而不惑知人也是故君子動而世爲天
下道行而世爲天下法言而世爲天下
則遠之則有望近之則不厭
同考試官訓導魯批洞悉理道之原而詞足以
發可式
同考試官教諭周批君子制作貫天人之理非
深知此理者不能言是作窺其奧矣
===
考試官學正陳批文義莊雅
考試官學正王批理明詞正
君子通乎天人之故而達之天下後世矣蓋天
人之理天下後世同也君子明此以制作其孰
能違之哉且夫爲治之道強世者誣作聰明者
亂皆所不行也是故幽如鬼神而君子之制作
乃能質之而無疑者是遵何道哉蓋天者理之
原而鬼神則效天之靈者也君子心通乎天而
於動靜通復之端盈虛消息之故爲能窮其神
punctuated:
質諸鬼神而無疑，知天也；百世以俟聖人而不惑，知人也。是故君子動而世爲天下道，行而世爲天下法，言而世爲天下則。遠之則有望，近之則不厭。
同考試官訓導魯批：洞悉理道之原，而詞足以發，可式。
同考試官教諭周批：君子制作，貫天人之理。非深知此理者不能言，是作窺其奧矣。
考試官學正陳批：文義莊雅。
考試官學正王批：理明詞正。
君子通乎天人之故，而達之天下後世矣。蓋天人之理，天下後世同也；君子明此以制作，其孰能違之哉？且夫爲治之道，強世者誣，作聰明者亂，皆所不行也。是故幽如鬼神，而君子之制作乃能質之而無疑者，是遵何道哉？蓋天者，理之原，而鬼神則效天之靈者也。君子心通乎天，而於動靜通復之端、盈虛消息之故，爲能窮其神…
translation_en:
"He presents his institutions before ghosts and spirits without any doubt arising, which shows that he knows Heaven; he waits a hundred generations for a sage without any perplexity, which shows that he knows men. Therefore, the movements of the superior man become for generations the Way of the world; his conduct becomes for generations the law of the world; and his words become for generations the standard of the world. Those who are far from him look up to him with longing, and those who are near do not grow weary of him."
Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Lu comments: Thoroughly grasps the source of principle and the Way, and the diction is sufficient to bring it forth; it can serve as a model.
Associate Examiner Instructor Zhou comments: The creation of institutions by the superior man penetrates the principles of Heaven and humanity. None who do not deeply understand this principle could speak of it; this essay has peered into its profundities.
Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Chen comments: The meaning and style are dignified and elegant.
Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang comments: The reasoning is clear and the diction upright.
The superior man comprehends the causes of Heaven and humanity, and extends them throughout the world and to later generations. For the principles of Heaven and humanity are the same throughout the world and in later generations; when the superior man illuminates these in creating institutions, who could go against them? Moreover, in the Way of governance, those who force the world fall into falsehood, and those who affect cleverness bring disorder; neither can be put into practice. Therefore, obscure as ghosts and spirits are, by what Way is it that the superior man's institutions can be presented before them without a doubt? Because Heaven is the source of principle, and ghosts and spirits manifest the numinous efficacy of Heaven. The superior man's mind communicates with Heaven, and with regard to the beginnings of movement and stillness, free flow and return, and the causes of waxing and waning, growth and decline, he is able to exhaust their mysteries…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而知其化焉則所作者合於天之機也而亦所
以洩鬼神之機也質之夫何疑哉遠如後聖君
子之制作乃能俟之而不惑者非曰億之也蓋
理不遠於人而後聖則立人之極者也君子心
通乎人而於欲惡取舍之情升降汙隆之宜焉
能探其微而推其變焉則所作者合於人之心
也而亦所以符後聖之心也俟之又何惑哉夫
既可以俟後聖夫且可以質鬼神而況於民乎
是故古今異時也君子動之而世世之道存焉
===
行為法也言為則也洋洋乎垂之為謨訓者將
萬年如一日矣是故民生異俗也君子創之而
人人遵道焉遠有尊也近有親也蒸蒸然會歸
于皇極者合萬民為一心矣何則天不二人亦
不二故也嚮非此理之同則古今之異尚彼此
之異宜君子亦安得而強齊之哉雖然帝王之
法雖其盡善也代亦有變遷焉安能一一而世
守之乎蓋天人之理萬世不變其所變者迹也
故曰五帝殊時不相沿樂三王異代不襲禮其
punctuated: 而知其化焉，則所作者合於天之機也，而亦所以洩鬼神之機也，質之夫何疑哉？遠如後聖，君子之制作乃能俟之而不惑者，非曰億之也。蓋理不遠於人，而後聖則立人之極者也。君子心通乎人，而於欲惡取舍之情、升降汙隆之宜，焉能探其微而推其變焉，則所作者合於人之心也，而亦所以符後聖之心也，俟之又何惑哉？夫既可以俟後聖，夫且可以質鬼神，而況於民乎？是故古今異時也，君子動之，而世世之道存焉。行為法也，言為則也，洋洋乎垂之為謨訓者，將萬年如一日矣。是故民生異俗也，君子創之，而人人遵道焉。遠有尊也，近有親也，蒸蒸然會歸于皇極者，合萬民為一心矣。何則？天不二，人亦不二故也。嚮非此理之同，則古今之異尚，彼此之異宜，君子亦安得而強齊之哉？雖然，帝王之法雖其盡善也，代亦有變遷焉，安能一一而世守之乎？蓋天人之理，萬世不變，其所變者迹也。故曰：「五帝殊時，不相沿樂；三王異代，不襲禮。」其
translation_en:
…and comprehends its transformations; thus what he establishes accords with the subtle workings of Heaven, and is also that by which the subtle workings of ghosts and spirits are revealed. When presenting it before them, what doubt could there be?

As for what is as distant as the future sages, that the superior man's institutions can await them without perplexity is not a matter of mere conjecture. For principle is not far from humanity, and the future sages are those who establish the ultimate standard of humanity. The superior man's mind comprehends humanity, and regarding the sentiments of desire, aversion, adoption, and rejection, as well as the appropriateness of rise and fall, decline and flourishing, he is able [?] to probe their subtleties and deduce their changes; thus what he establishes accords with the human mind, and is also that which tallies with the minds of the future sages. In awaiting them, what perplexity could there be either?

Now, since his work can both await the future sages and be presented before ghosts and spirits, how much more so with the common people! Therefore, although antiquity and the present are different eras, when the superior man acts, the Way for generation after generation is preserved therein. His conduct becomes the law for the Empire, and his words become the pattern for the Empire; grandly handed down as counsels and instructions, ten thousand years will be as a single day. Therefore, although the people live with different customs, when the superior man initiates institutions, everyone follows the Way. Far away, they revere him; nearby, they feel affection for him; advancing harmoniously to converge upon the August Ultimate, the myriad people are united as one mind. Why is this? Because Heaven is not dual, and humanity is not dual either. Were it not for the sameness of this principle, given the different preferences of antiquity and the present and the different suitability of this and that, how could the superior man forcibly make them uniform?

Nevertheless, although the laws of the emperors and kings are utterly good, ages also undergo changes and transitions; how can every single detail be preserved from generation to generation? For the principle of Heaven and humanity does not change over ten thousand generations; what changes are the outward traces. Thus it is said: "The Five Emperors lived in different times and did not continue one another's music; the Three Kings belonged to different dynasties and did not inherit one another's rites." Their…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
所損益以宜民也時也通乎時者其於天人也
深乎
賢者在位能者在職國家閒暇及是時明
其政刑雖大國必畏之矣詩云迨天之
未陰雨徹彼桑土綢繆牖戶今此下民
或敢侮予孔子曰為此詩者其知道乎
能治其國家誰敢侮之
同考試官訓導胡批孔子賛詩之詞類從實講
殊失本旨此作深於理者
同考試官訓導梁批詞嚴義正發國家圖治之豫
無踰此作
考試官學正陳批發意精到
考試官學正王批明健該雅
大賢論治而取諸豫徵諸聖人焉蓋治貴未然
也由其道可以威天下周公仲尼豈欺我哉孟
子見戰國之君闇於遠慮苟幸旦夕無事而以
為安故言曰有國家者孰不好榮而惡辱哉亦
punctuated:
所損益以宜民也，時也。通乎時者，其於天人也深乎！

「賢者在位，能者在職，國家閒暇，及是時，明其政刑，雖大國必畏之矣。《詩》云：『迨天之未陰雨，徹彼桑土，綢繆牖戶。今此下民，或敢侮予？』孔子曰：『為此詩者，其知道乎！能治其國家，誰敢侮之？』」

同考試官訓導胡批：孔子賛《詩》之詞，類從實講，殊失本旨。此作深於理者。
同考試官訓導梁批：詞嚴義正，發國家圖治之豫，無踰此作。
考試官學正陳批：發意精到。
考試官學正王批：明健該雅。

大賢論治而取諸豫，徵諸聖人焉。蓋治貴未然也。由其道可以威天下，周公、仲尼豈欺我哉！孟子見戰國之君闇於遠慮，苟幸旦夕無事而以為安，故言曰：有國家者，孰不好榮而惡辱哉？亦
translation_en:
…what they abridged or augmented in order to suit the people was a matter of timeliness. He who comprehends timeliness—how profound is his understanding of Heaven and man!

"When worthy men are in positions of authority and able men are in office, and the state enjoys leisure, if one takes advantage of this time to clarify its governance and penal laws, even great states will certainly stand in awe of it. The Book of Odes (Shijing) says:
'Before the sky grows dark with rain,
I strip that mulberry-root bark
And bind tight the window and door.
Now you people below,
Dare any of you affront me?'
Confucius said: 'Did the maker of this ode not know the Way! If one is able to govern his state and family well, who dares affront him?'"

Associate Examiner Hu, Assistant Instructor, comments: Confucius's words in praise of the Ode are usually explained too literally by candidates, which completely misses the fundamental purport. This essay is one that penetrates deeply into the principle.
Associate Examiner Liang, Assistant Instructor, comments: The diction is rigorous and the meaning upright; in bringing out the foresight needed when a state plans for good governance, nothing surpasses this composition.
Examiner Chen, Director of Studies, comments: It brings out the meaning with precision and thoroughness.
Examiner Wang, Director of Studies, comments: Lucid, vigorous, comprehensive, and elegant.

The great worthy, in discussing governance, takes his lesson from foresight and verifies it by the sages. For in governance, what is prized is acting before trouble arises. By following this Way, one can overawe the world—would the Duke of Zhou and Confucius (Zhongni) deceive us? Mencius saw that the rulers of the Warring States were blind to far-sighted plans, merely counting themselves fortunate to have no trouble from morning to evening and taking that for security. Therefore he spoke, saying: Among those who possess states and families, who does not love glory and hate disgrace? And…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
孰不可反辱而爲榮也失在不審其道而怠於
時也時乎其當國幸無事之日乎爲今計者誠
知失士者弱得士者强而簡厥賢能之士與之
共位與之共職也而托之以國家又知得時者
昌失時者荒而乘此閒隙之時與之明政與之
明刑也以脩緝其廢墜則朝有政而國有人内
用寧而外用固無論小國將大國亦吾畏矣是
爲圖治於未亂至計也周公之詩不云乎迨天
之未陰雨徹彼桑土綢繆牖户公之憂治世而
===
托之拮据之智者也今此下民或敢侮予者公
之謀王室而幸其備豫之詞也孔子嘗讀是詩
以爲知道蓋穆然咨嗟有周公之思焉故曰能
治其國家誰敢侮之儻所謂云閒暇者亦仲尼
之意乎如當可以有爲之暇而不爲未雨之計
慆盈燕佚隳政棄士及其有事駭而圖之豈有
及乎求不辱其國無時矣是以三五之盛皆繇
任賢六經之治貴於未亂而况生乎三五聖神
之後者乎其憂思曷可勝道哉夫國雖常安而
punctuated: 孰不可反辱而爲榮也？失在不審其道而怠於時也。時乎，其當國幸無事之日乎！爲今計者，誠知失士者弱、得士者强，而簡厥賢能之士，與之共位、與之共職也，而托之以國家；又知得時者昌、失時者荒，而乘此閒隙之時，與之明政、與之明刑也，以脩緝其廢墜。則朝有政而國有人，内用寧而外用固，無論小國，將大國亦吾畏矣。是爲圖治於未亂至計也。周公之詩不云乎：「迨天之未陰雨，徹彼桑土，綢繆牖户。」公之憂治世而托之拮据之智者也。「今此下民，或敢侮予」者，公之謀王室而幸其備豫之詞也。孔子嘗讀是詩，以爲知道，蓋穆然咨嗟，有周公之思焉。故曰：「能治其國家，誰敢侮之！」儻所謂云「閒暇」者，亦仲尼之意乎！如當可以有爲之暇，而不爲未雨之計，慆盈燕佚，隳政棄士，及其有事，駭而圖之，豈有及乎？求不辱其國，無時矣。是以三五之盛，皆繇任賢；六經之治，貴於未亂。而况生乎三五聖神之後者乎？其憂思曷可勝道哉！夫國雖常安，而…
translation_en: …who cannot turn disgrace back into glory? Their failure lies in not discerning the proper Way and growing negligent of the opportune time. And what is that time? Surely it is the days when the state is fortunate enough to be free of trouble! In taking counsel for the present, if a ruler truly understands that losing worthy men brings weakness while gaining them brings strength, and therefore selects men of virtue and ability to share offices and duties with them, entrusting the state to their care; and if he further understands that seizing the moment brings prosperity while missing it brings ruin, and therefore takes advantage of this time of leisure to clarify governance and penal laws with them, thereby repairing and restoring what has fallen into neglect—then the court will have sound administration and the state will have capable men, internal affairs will be tranquil and external defenses secure, so that not only small states, but even large states will stand in awe of us. This is the supreme plan for securing order before disorder arises. Does not the ode of the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong) say: "Before the sky darkens with rain, I strip the mulberry roots and bind fast the window and door"? Here the Duke expressed his anxiety for an age of order through the metaphor of the bird's toiling wisdom. And the lines "Now among the people below, who would dare to insult me?" are the Duke's words in taking counsel for the royal house and rejoicing in its advance preparation. When Confucius (Kongzi) read this ode, he considered that the Duke understood the Way; he sighed in deep reverence, sharing the thoughts of the Duke of Zhou, and thus said: "If one is able to govern his state and family, who will dare to insult him?" Perhaps what Mencius called "a time of leisure" was also the very meaning of Confucius (Zhongni)! If, during a time of leisure when much can be accomplished, a ruler makes no plans before the rain comes, indulging in arrogance, complacency, and idle pleasure, ruining administration and abandoning worthy men, and only when trouble strikes tries in panic to deal with it—how could it not be too late? Never again will he find a time to save his state from disgrace. Therefore, the flourishing of the Three Dynasties and Five Emperors all stemmed from employing the worthy, and the governance of the Six Classics prized acting before disorder arose. How much more so for those born after the sage and divine rulers of the Three Dynasties and Five Emperors! How could their anxious thoughts ever be fully recounted? For even though a state may enjoy constant peace, one must…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
常不可忘憂以爲安也其憂也將至矣以爲憂
也其安也可保矣
易
天地養萬物聖人養賢以及萬民頤之時
大矣哉
同考試官訓導梁批講養萬物萬民處含上養
德養身二意融會貫通發人所未發者宜式
同考試官教諭李批頤時處作者多泛畧獨此
===
篇發揮時義透徹邃養之士也錄之
考試官學正陳批氣象宏大可取
考試官學正王批理精氣暢
觀養道貫乎天人而其大可知矣蓋天地盡物
聖人盡民其養一也頤之時不其大哉彖傳極
言而賛之意謂頤之爲道固在於養德養身矣
然於民物無濟未大也其惟天地聖人乎彼天
地司覆載而握養物之權使神有未運化何由
溥耶茲則動撓以鼓其機暄潤以彰其美性命
punctuated:
常不可忘憂。以爲安也，其憂也將至矣；以爲憂也，其安也可保矣。

《易》：「天地養萬物，聖人養賢以及萬民，頤之時大矣哉。」

同考試官訓導梁批：講「養萬物」、「萬民」處，含上「養德」、「養身」二意，融會貫通，發人所未發者，宜式。
同考試官教諭李批：「頤時」處，作者多泛畧，獨此篇發揮時義透徹，邃養之士也，錄之。
考試官學正陳批：氣象宏大，可取。
考試官學正王批：理精氣暢。

觀養道貫乎天人，而其大可知矣。蓋天地盡物，聖人盡民，其養一也，頤之時不其大哉！《彖傳》極言而賛之，意謂：頤之爲道，固在於養德、養身矣；然於民物無濟，未大也。其惟天地聖人乎！彼天地司覆載，而握養物之權，使神有未運，化何由溥耶？茲則動撓以鼓其機，暄潤以彰其美，性命
translation_en:
… must never forget anxiety. If one considers the state secure, then cause for anxiety will soon arrive; if one considers it cause for anxiety, then its security can be preserved.

Book of Changes (Yi): "Heaven and earth nourish the myriad things; the sage nourishes the worthy in order to reach the myriad people. Great indeed is the timeliness of Nourishment (Yi)!"

Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Assistant Instructor: In expounding "nourishing the myriad things" and "the myriad people," it encompasses the two preceding ideas of "nourishing virtue" and "nourishing the body," synthesizing them thoroughly and expressing what others have not yet expressed. It is worthy of serving as a model.
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: On the passage regarding "the timeliness of Nourishment," most writers are vague and cursory. This essay alone brings out the meaning of timeliness with complete penetration. He is a scholar of deep cultivation; record it.
Comment by Examiner Chen, Director of Studies: Its spirit and scale are grand; it is acceptable.
Comment by Examiner Wang, Director of Studies: The reasoning is precise and the vital breath flows smoothly.

When we observe how the Way of nourishment runs through both Heaven and humanity, its greatness can be known. Indeed, heaven and earth fulfill the nature of things, and the sage fulfills the nature of the people; their nourishment is one and the same. Is not the timeliness of Nourishment great indeed! The Commentary on the Judgments (Tuanzhuan) speaks of this to the utmost in praise of it, meaning to say: The Way of Nourishment certainly lies in nourishing virtue and nourishing the body; yet if it offers no benefit to the people and things, it is not yet great. Does this not belong solely to heaven, earth, and the sage! Now, heaven and earth preside over covering and bearing up, holding the authority to nourish things. If their mysterious spirit did not operate, how could transformation be universally diffused? Here, through movement and stirring they rouse its vital mechanism, and through warmth and moisture they manifest its beauty, so that the nature and destiny…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
爲之各正也太和爲之保合也咸取足於天地
之養矣聖人作君師而任養民之責使賢有未
親澤何由廣耶兹則隆大烹之儀崇詔祿之典
阜財倚之而民遂其生也敷敎藉之而民復其
性也咸取足於聖人之養矣夫莫大乎天地而
萬物養焉斯時也天無遺覆而成象於乾地無
遺載而效法於坤蓋充滿於宇宙而不可以涯
涘窺矣頤道至此其諸大造之功乎莫大乎聖
人而萬民養焉斯時也仰敎思者而有同尊懷
===
容保者而有同親蓋洋溢於中外而不可以疆
域限矣頤道至此其諸大同之治乎吁觀養於
天地而知頤道察乎上下矣觀養於聖人而知
頤道參乎造化矣人其可以小視之哉抑論天
地先聖人以開智聖人後天地以成能而參贊
之責在聖人不在天地蓋天地之道賴聖人以
裁成天地之宜賴聖人以輔相而左右乎民者
即智周乎萬物無非聖人事也故曰聖人天地
之用
punctuated: 爲之各正也，太和爲之保合也，咸取足於天地之養矣。聖人作君師而任養民之責，使賢有未親，澤何由廣耶？兹則隆大烹之儀，崇詔祿之典，阜財倚之而民遂其生也，敷敎藉之而民復其性也，咸取足於聖人之養矣。夫莫大乎天地，而萬物養焉。斯時也，天無遺覆而成象於乾，地無遺載而效法於坤，蓋充滿於宇宙而不可以涯涘窺矣。頤道至此，其諸大造之功乎！莫大乎聖人，而萬民養焉。斯時也，仰敎思者而有同尊，懷容保者而有同親，蓋洋溢於中外而不可以疆域限矣。頤道至此，其諸大同之治乎！吁！觀養於天地，而知頤道察乎上下矣；觀養於聖人，而知頤道參乎造化矣。人其可以小視之哉？抑論天地先聖人以開智，聖人後天地以成能，而參贊之責在聖人不在天地。蓋天地之道賴聖人以裁成，天地之宜賴聖人以輔相，而左右乎民者，即智周乎萬物，無非聖人事也。故曰：聖人，天地之用。
translation_en:
… are each rectified by them, and supreme harmony is preserved in union by them; all draw their sufficiency from the nourishment of Heaven and Earth. The sage acts as ruler and teacher and bears the responsibility of nourishing the people; if the worthy are not yet drawn close, how could his beneficence be made broad? Here, however, he exalts the rites of the great sacrificial feast and honors the statutes for conferring emoluments; the enrichment of wealth depends on them so that the people fulfill their livelihood, and the spreading of instruction relies on them so that the people recover their nature—all draw their sufficiency from the nourishment of the sage.

Now, nothing is greater than Heaven and Earth, and the myriad things are nourished therein. At this time, Heaven leaves nothing uncovered and forms images in Qian; Earth leaves nothing unsupported and models patterns in Kun; indeed, it fills the universe and cannot be fathomed by any shore or limit. When the Way of Nourishment (Yi) reaches this point, is it not the achievement of the Great Creator? Nothing is greater than the sage, and the myriad people are nourished thereby. At this time, those who look up to his instructive thoughts share a common reverence, and those who cherish his tolerant protection share a common affection; indeed, it overflows within and without and cannot be bounded by any frontier. When the Way of Nourishment reaches this point, is it not the governance of Great Unity?

Ah! Observing nourishment in Heaven and Earth, one knows that the Way of Nourishment is manifest above and below; observing nourishment in the sage, one knows that the Way of Nourishment participates in creation and transformation. How could anyone regard it as something small? Moreover, if we consider that Heaven and Earth precede the sage to open up wisdom, while the sage follows Heaven and Earth to bring capabilities to completion, the responsibility of participating and assisting lies with the sage and not with Heaven and Earth. For the Way of Heaven and Earth relies on the sage to regulate and complete it, and the appropriateness of Heaven and Earth relies on the sage to assist and further it; thus, guiding and supporting the people—even to wisdom encompassing the myriad things—is nothing other than the business of the sage. Therefore it is said: The sage is the function of Heaven and Earth.

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
夫易聖人所以崇德而廣業也知崇禮卑
崇效天卑法地
同考試官訓導梁批說用易處點出易書中知
禮德業本色語極有體認關鍵子其深於易者乎
同考試官教諭李批體式端莊詞意精爽善言
易學者宜錄以式
考試官學正陳批理明詞達
考試官學正王批純正典雅
===
大傳論易有資于聖學擴之配天地焉夫易貫
三才而一之也聖人用之以擴知禮則德業之
崇廣不與天地配哉夫子贊其至也若曰發聖
人之精者易也周聖人之用者亦易也吾嘗執
此以徵其至矣彼聖人之德本至崇也而其所
以日進于高明者一洗心之密為之耳易其德
之所由崇乎聖人之業本至廣也而其所以日
底于博厚者一化裁之變為之耳易其業之所
由廣乎何也德之崇也本於知聖人有見于易
punctuated:
夫《易》，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。

同考試官、訓導梁批：說用《易》處，點出《易》書中知、禮、德、業本色，語極有體認關鍵，子其深於《易》者乎？
同考試官、教諭李批：體式端莊，詞意精爽，善言《易》學者，宜錄以式。
考試官、學正陳批：理明詞達。
考試官、學正王批：純正典雅。

大傳論《易》有資于聖學，擴之配天地焉。夫《易》貫三才而一之也，聖人用之以擴知、禮，則德、業之崇廣，不與天地配哉？夫子贊其至也，若曰：發聖人之精者，《易》也；周聖人之用者，亦《易》也。吾嘗執此以徵其至矣。彼聖人之德本至崇也，而其所以日進于高明者，一洗心之密為之耳，《易》其德之所由崇乎！聖人之業本至廣也，而其所以日底于博厚者，一化裁之變為之耳，《易》其業之所由廣乎！何也？德之崇也本於知，聖人有見于《易》
translation_en:
"Now the Changes (Yi) is that by which the sages exalt their virtue and broaden their enterprise. Wisdom is exalted and ritual is humble; the exalted emulates heaven, and the humble takes earth as its pattern."

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Liang comments: In explaining how the Changes is used, the essay brings out the true character of wisdom, ritual, virtue, and enterprise within the Book of Changes. Its phrasing shows a deep personal grasp of the key points—surely you are one who is profound in the Changes!
Associate Examiner and Instructor Li comments: The form and style are dignified, and the wording and meaning are incisive and brisk. This is someone skilled at discussing the learning of the Changes; it should be recorded as a model.
Examiner and Director of Studies Chen comments: The principles are clear and the expression is fluent.
Examiner and Director of Studies Wang comments: Pure, orthodox, and classically elegant.

The Great Commentary (Dazhuan) discusses how the Changes aids sagely learning, expanding it to match heaven and earth. Now, the Changes penetrates the Three Powers and unites them as one. When the sages use it to expand their wisdom and ritual, do not the exaltation of their virtue and the breadth of their enterprise match heaven and earth? The Master praised its perfection, as if to say: That which brings forth the essence of the sages is the Changes; that which encompasses the functioning of the sages is likewise the Changes. I have held to this in order to attest to its perfection. Now, the virtue of the sages is inherently most exalted, yet that by which it daily advances toward lofty brilliance is simply the subtlety with which it purifies the mind—is not the Changes that whereby their virtue becomes exalted! The enterprise of the sages is inherently most broad, yet that by which it daily attains to wide thickness is simply the transformation through which it tailors and regulates—is not the Changes that whereby their enterprise becomes broad! Why is this? The exaltation of virtue is rooted in wisdom. The sages, perceiving that the Changes…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
具方知足以通神明之德也而窮之于心則識
見自超卓矣何崇如之業之廣也本於禮聖人
有見于易具典禮足以定天下之業也而循之
于身則踐履自篤實矣何卑如之吾知高明上
覆語崇至天極也今則盡天所覆而無一理之
不知夫固與高明同一崇矣謂不足以憲天耶
博厚下載語卑至地極也今則盡地所載而無
一理之不體夫固與博厚同一卑矣謂不足以
應地耶吁觀知崇效天則德之崇可推也觀禮
===
卑法地則業之廣可推也然皆不外乎易焉大
哉易也斯其至矣雖然易理原具足于吾心也
聖人之用易非必求之易也用吾心之易耳虛
靈不昧有真知焉中正無邪有至禮焉使不求
知禮于易而求知禮于心則德自我崇業自我
廣效天法地者皆在我矣夫是之謂心易噫學
易者當自得之
書
帝曰來禹汝亦昌言禹拜曰都帝予何言
punctuated:
具方知，足以通神明之德也，而窮之于心，則識見自超卓矣，何崇如之！業之廣也本於禮，聖人有見于易具典禮，足以定天下之業也，而循之于身，則踐履自篤實矣，何卑如之！吾知高明上覆，語崇至天極也；今則盡天所覆而無一理之不知，夫固與高明同一崇矣，謂不足以憲天耶？博厚下載，語卑至地極也；今則盡地所載而無一理之不體，夫固與博厚同一卑矣，謂不足以應地耶？吁！觀知崇效天，則德之崇可推也；觀禮卑法地，則業之廣可推也。然皆不外乎易焉。大哉易也，斯其至矣！雖然，易理原具足于吾心也。聖人之用易，非必求之易也，用吾心之易耳。虛靈不昧，有真知焉；中正無邪，有至禮焉。使不求知禮于易，而求知禮于心，則德自我崇，業自我廣，效天法地者皆在我矣。夫是之謂心易。噫！學易者當自得之。

書
帝曰：「來，禹！汝亦昌言。」禹拜曰：「都，帝，予何言？
translation_en:
… possesses squareness and wisdom sufficient to penetrate the virtue of spiritual illumination, and when he exhausts it in his mind, his insight naturally becomes transcendent and outstanding—what could be as exalted as this! The breadth of great accomplishments is rooted in ritual propriety. The sage sees that the Book of Changes (Yi) possesses canonical rites sufficient to settle the accomplishments of the world, and when he follows them in his own person, his actual practice naturally becomes sincere and substantial—what could be as lowly and grounded as this! I know that what is lofty and bright covers from above, so when speaking of exaltedness, Heaven is the ultimate; now, exhausting all that Heaven covers without a single principle remaining unknown, he indeed shares the same exaltedness as the lofty and bright—how could one say this is insufficient to model oneself on Heaven? What is broad and thick supports from below, so when speaking of lowliness, Earth is the ultimate; now, exhausting all that Earth supports without a single principle remaining unembodied, he indeed shares the same lowliness as the broad and thick—how could one say this is insufficient to correspond to Earth? Ah! By observing how exalted wisdom emulates Heaven, the exaltedness of virtue can be inferred; by observing how lowly ritual propriety takes Earth as its standard, the breadth of accomplishments can be inferred. Yet none of this lies outside the Changes. Great indeed are the Changes—herein lies their perfection! Even so, the principles of the Changes are originally complete within our own minds. When the sage uses the Changes, he does not necessarily seek them in the Changes themselves; he merely uses the Changes of his own mind. In the empty, numinous, and unobscured mind, there is true wisdom; in what is central, correct, and without depravity, there is supreme ritual propriety. If one does not seek wisdom and ritual propriety in the Changes, but seeks them in the mind, then virtue becomes exalted through oneself, accomplishments become broad through oneself, and that which emulates Heaven and takes Earth as its standard lies entirely within oneself. This is what is called the Changes of the mind. Alas! Those who study the Changes ought to attain this for themselves.

Book of Documents (Shu)
The Emperor said, "Come, Yu! You also make a splendid speech." Yu bowed and said, "Oh! Emperor, what can I say? …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
予思日孜孜
同考試官訓導徐批舜禹求言保治之心發揮
透徹虞廷明良氣象可想見矣錄之
同考試官訓導胡批典謨文字當以温厚和平
為主此作得之
考試官學正陳批雅暢可誦
考試官學正王批義盡詞醇
聖君切于求言而大臣心于保治焉甚矣盛治
===
之當保也帝以言求之禹以心效之此君臣之
相與以有成歟且夫先天下而成治功者固難
後天下而保治功者尤難有虞以舜為之君以
禹臯為之臣惟欲恊心以保治耳帝舜聞臯陶
之謨而其心未已也乃來禹而命之曰治必貴
于共濟言不厭于多聞知人之謨臯陶既已昌
言矣然言或有不盡于知人者汝亦竭祗承之
初志以慰吾翕受之懷矣乎安民之謨臯陶既
已昌言矣然言或有不盡于安民者汝亦殫克
punctuated:
予思日孜孜。」
同考試官訓導徐批：舜、禹求言保治之心，發揮透徹，虞廷明良氣象可想見矣。錄之。
同考試官訓導胡批：典謨文字，當以温厚和平為主，此作得之。
考試官學正陳批：雅暢可誦。
考試官學正王批：義盡詞醇。
聖君切于求言，而大臣心于保治焉。甚矣，盛治之當保也！帝以言求之，禹以心效之，此君臣之相與以有成歟？且夫先天下而成治功者固難，後天下而保治功者尤難。有虞以舜為之君，以禹、臯為之臣，惟欲恊心以保治耳。帝舜聞臯陶之謨，而其心未已也，乃來禹而命之曰：「治必貴于共濟，言不厭于多聞。知人之謨，臯陶既已昌言矣，然言或有不盡于知人者，汝亦竭祗承之初志，以慰吾翕受之懷矣乎？安民之謨，臯陶既已昌言矣，然言或有不盡于安民者，汝亦殫克
translation_en:
… I think only of exerting myself unremittingly day by day."

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor (xundao) Xu: The minds of Shun and Yu in seeking counsel and preserving good governance are thoroughly expounded here; one can readily envision the spirit of an enlightened ruler and virtuous ministers at the court of Yu [Shun]. Record it for publication.

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Hu: Essays on the "Canons" and "Counsels" [of the Book of Documents] should make warmth, depth, harmony, and balance their main principles; this composition achieves that.

Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies (xuezheng) Chen: Elegant and fluent, worthy of recitation.

Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang: The meaning is exhaustive and the diction pure.

The sage ruler is earnest in seeking counsel, while the great minister sets his heart on preserving good governance. How imperative it is that flourishing governance be preserved! The Emperor sought it through words, and Yu rendered his service through his heart—was it not by this mutual engagement of ruler and minister that their achievements were brought to completion? Moreover, taking the lead in the world to accomplish the work of governance is certainly difficult, yet following through to preserve that work of governance for the world is harder still. The house of Yu had Shun as its ruler and Yu and Gao Yao as its ministers; their sole desire was to unite their hearts in preserving good governance. When Emperor Shun heard the counsels of Gao Yao, his mind was still not satisfied; he therefore called Yu forward and charged him, saying: "Governance necessarily prizes cooperative effort, and one can never tire of hearing abundant counsel. As for counsels on knowing men, Gao Yao has already spoken splendid words; yet should there be matters not fully exhausted in knowing men, will you not also pour forth your original intent of reverent compliance so as to comfort my desire to receive advice broadly? As for counsels on giving peace to the people, Gao Yao has already spoken splendid words; yet should there be matters not fully exhausted in giving peace to the people, will you not also devote to the utmost your…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
艱之夙心以副吾樂取之願矣乎夫帝之望于
禹者亦既切矣乃禹之心則有出于言之外者
于是從而拜之致其敬焉嘆而美之啓其聽焉
遂復于帝曰人君之求言也每欲資諸人人臣
之進言也不必出于巳皐陶之謨至矣予何言
哉予惟思成功之不易而兢業之念日切于中
孜孜焉夙夜之匪懈也思保泰之惟艱而寅恭
之忱日廛諸慮孜孜焉朝夕之靡遑也有盡者
言雖不容于强聒無窮者心寔不敢以遽忘予
===
之自效于帝者唯此而已外此又何言哉噫帝
求昌言不以既聖而忘交脩之益禹思孜孜不
以既治而廢交儆之忠君臣恊心以保治如此
有虞之治所以不可及歟大抵人臣事君事之
以言者其效淺事之以心者其效深彼不本諸
忠愛之心而徒滋于議論之末竟何益于治哉
故皐陶陳謨而終之以思日賛賛大禹進言而
先之以思日孜孜古大臣之用心類如此後之
爲人臣者可以深長思矣
punctuated: 艱之夙心，以副吾樂取之願矣乎！」夫帝之望于禹者，亦既切矣；乃禹之心，則有出于言之外者。于是從而拜之，致其敬焉；嘆而美之，啓其聽焉。遂復于帝曰：「人君之求言也，每欲資諸人；人臣之進言也，不必出于巳。皐陶之謨至矣，予何言哉？予惟思成功之不易，而兢業之念日切于中，孜孜焉夙夜之匪懈也；思保泰之惟艱，而寅恭之忱日廛諸慮，孜孜焉朝夕之靡遑也。有盡者言，雖不容于强聒；無窮者心，寔不敢以遽忘。予之自效于帝者，唯此而已，外此又何言哉？」噫！帝求昌言，不以既聖而忘交脩之益；禹思孜孜，不以既治而廢交儆之忠。君臣恊心以保治如此，有虞之治，所以不可及歟！大抵人臣事君，事之以言者，其效淺；事之以心者，其效深。彼不本諸忠愛之心，而徒滋于議論之末，竟何益于治哉？故皐陶陳謨，而終之以「思日賛賛」；大禹進言，而先之以「思日孜孜」。古大臣之用心類如此，後之爲人臣者，可以深長思矣。
translation_en:
… long-held mindfulness of difficulties, so as to fulfill my wish to gladly draw upon the good of others?" Now, what the Emperor hoped for from Yu was indeed earnest; yet Yu's mind held something that went beyond mere words. Thereupon he bowed to him to express his reverence, and sighed in admiration to awaken the Emperor's attention. He then replied to the Emperor, saying: "When a ruler seeks counsel, he always wishes to draw upon others; when a minister offers counsel, it need not originate from himself. Gao Yao's counsels are already supreme—what more can I say? I only reflect on how accomplishment is not easy, so that thoughts of cautious diligence grow daily more urgent within me, working untiringly without slackening day or night; I reflect on how preserving peace and prosperity is truly difficult, so that sincere reverence daily occupies my thoughts, working untiringly without leisure morning or evening. What has a limit is speech, which does not permit forced prattling; what is inexhaustible is the mind, which truly dares not suddenly forget. How I devote myself to the Emperor is through this alone; beyond this, what else is there to say?"

Alas! The Emperor sought splendid words, not forgetting the benefit of mutual cultivation just because he was already a sage; Yu thought of untiring diligence, not abandoning the loyalty of mutual admonition just because order was already achieved. Sovereign and minister united their minds to preserve good governance like this—is this not why the governance of the Yu dynasty could never be equaled? Broadly speaking, when a minister serves his ruler, serving him with words yields shallow results, whereas serving him with the mind yields deep results. Those who do not root themselves in a mind of loyalty and devotion, yet merely multiply superficial discussions—what benefit do they ultimately bring to governance? Therefore, when Gao Yao set forth his counsels, he concluded them with "thinking daily of assisting and aiding"; when the Great Yu offered his words, he prefaced them with "thinking daily of untiring diligence." The mindfulness of the great ministers of antiquity was generally like this; those of later ages who serve as ministers may well ponder this deeply and at length.

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
唐虞稽古建官惟百內有百揆四岳外有
州牧侯伯庶政惟和萬國咸寧夏商官
倍亦克用乂明王立政不惟其官惟其
人
同考試官訓導徐批體裁莊整詞意簡嚴是經
義之嘉者
同考試官訓導胡批此作詞理精確深得成王
訓官之意宜錄以式
===
考試官學正陳批嚴重無冗語
考試官學正王批典雅之文
帝王建官以成治要在得人而已夫得人運治
之本也唐虞夏商之治皆由是致之耳備官云
乎哉成王訓官而先之以此蓋謂致治以建官
爲先建官以擇人爲要自昔大猷之世所以制
治保邦者率是道也盍自唐虞夏商之事而觀
之乎彼唐虞之建官也稽古定制其數則惟百
焉內建揆岳總其綱外建牧伯司其紀體統相
punctuated:
唐虞稽古，建官惟百，內有百揆四岳，外有州牧侯伯，庶政惟和，萬國咸寧。夏商官倍，亦克用乂。明王立政，不惟其官，惟其人。

同考試官訓導徐批：體裁莊整，詞意簡嚴，是經義之嘉者。
同考試官訓導胡批：此作詞理精確，深得成王訓官之意，宜錄以式。
考試官學正陳批：嚴重無冗語。
考試官學正王批：典雅之文。

帝王建官以成治，要在得人而已。夫得人，運治之本也。唐虞夏商之治，皆由是致之耳，備官云乎哉？成王訓官而先之以此，蓋謂致治以建官爲先，建官以擇人爲要，自昔大猷之世，所以制治保邦者，率是道也。盍自唐虞夏商之事而觀之乎？彼唐虞之建官也，稽古定制，其數則惟百焉。內建揆、岳總其綱，外建牧、伯司其紀，體統相
translation_en:
"Tang and Yu studied antiquity and established a hundred offices. At court there were the General Regulator (Baikui) and the Four Peaks (Siyue); in the provinces there were the Provincial Pastors (Zhoumu) and Feudal Lords (Houbo). Thus the various departments of government were harmonious, and the myriad states were all at peace. Under the Xia and Shang, the number of offices was doubled, and they too were able to achieve good governance. In establishing governance, enlightened kings cared not so much about the number of offices as about the men who filled them." [Classic of History (Shujing), "Officers of Zhou" (Zhouguan)]

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Xu: Its form is solemn and well-ordered, its diction and meaning concise and rigorous; this is an admirable essay on the Classics.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Hu: The diction and reasoning of this composition are precise and exact. It deeply grasps King Cheng's intention in instructing his officials, and ought to be recorded as a model.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Chen: Dignified and weighty, without superfluous words.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang: A piece of classical elegance.

When sovereigns establish offices in order to accomplish good governance, the essential point lies simply in obtaining the right men. Now, obtaining the right men is the root of conducting governance. The good governance of Tang, Yu, Xia, and Shang was in every case brought about by this means; how could it be a mere matter of filling the full complement of offices? When King Cheng instructed his officials and began with these words, he meant to say that in bringing about good governance, establishing offices comes first, and in establishing offices, selecting the right men is what is essential. From of old, in eras of great plans, the means by which rulers regulated governance and secured the state invariably followed this way. Why not observe this from the affairs of Tang, Yu, Xia, and Shang? In establishing offices, Tang and Yu studied antiquity to fix their system, and the number was but a hundred. At court they established the General Regulator and the Four Peaks to oversee the main principles; in the provinces they established the Pastors and Feudal Lords to manage the subsidiary threads. With the hierarchy mutually…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
維而政善民安唐虞之所以致治者可考也夏
商之建官也因時異制其數則惟倍焉總內治
者倍揆岳總外治者倍牧伯繁簡適宜而亦克
用乂夏商之所以致治者可考也夫唐虞古之
明王也而其治成于惟百之官是唐虞之立政
不惟其官之備也相師相讓誰非帝臣惟其人
而已矣夏商古之明王也而其治成于惟倍之
官是夏商之立政不惟其官之多也克宅克俊
誰非王佐亦惟其人而已矣羣哲輔而庶績熈
===
帝王之脩政也無異道相道得而萬國理帝王
之圖治也有同功予也遠嘉唐虞之風近守夏
商之法能無訓迪厥官也哉嗟夫爲政在人取
人以身有欽明濬哲之德斯能用九德六德之
臣有祗台懋昭之德斯能用卽宅卽俊之臣成
王欲正治官而夙夜祗勤于德可謂知所本矣
此周室得人之盛所以于今爲烈也然則人君
之建官以圖治者其惟本諸身而後可
詩
punctuated:
維而政善民安，唐、虞之所以致治者可考也。夏、商之建官也，因時異制，其數則惟倍焉。總內治者倍揆、岳，總外治者倍牧、伯，繁簡適宜，而亦克用乂，夏、商之所以致治者可考也。夫唐、虞，古之明王也，而其治成于惟百之官。是唐、虞之立政，不惟其官之備也；相師相讓，誰非帝臣？惟其人而已矣。夏、商，古之明王也，而其治成于惟倍之官。是夏、商之立政，不惟其官之多也；克宅克俊，誰非王佐？亦惟其人而已矣。羣哲輔而庶績熈，帝王之脩政也無異道；相道得而萬國理，帝王之圖治也有同功。予也遠嘉唐、虞之風，近守夏、商之法，能無訓迪厥官也哉？」嗟夫！爲政在人，取人以身。有欽明、濬哲之德，斯能用九德、六德之臣；有祗台、懋昭之德，斯能用卽宅、卽俊之臣。成王欲正治官，而夙夜祗勤于德，可謂知所本矣。此周室得人之盛，所以于今爲烈也。然則人君之建官以圖治者，其惟本諸身而後可。

《詩》
translation_en:
… linked together, so that governance was good and the people were at peace; how Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun] achieved good order can thus be examined. When the Xia and Shang established offices, they varied their institutions according to the times, and their number was doubled. Those who oversaw internal administration were double the General Regulators and Pastors of the Four Mountains, and those who oversaw external administration were double the Regional Pastors and Regional Earls. Complexity and simplicity suited what was appropriate, and they too were able to achieve order thereby; how the Xia and Shang achieved good order can thus be examined. Now, Tang and Yu were enlightened rulers of antiquity, and their governance was accomplished through just a hundred officials. Thus in establishing governance, Tang and Yu did not rely merely on the completeness of their offices; emulating one another and yielding to one another, who among them was not a true minister to the sovereign? It depended only on finding the right men! The rulers of Xia and Shang were also enlightened rulers of antiquity, and their governance was accomplished through double the number of officials. Thus in establishing governance, the Xia and Shang did not rely merely on the multitude of their offices; able to occupy their posts and prove themselves men of eminent talent, who among them was not a true assistant to the king? It likewise depended only on finding the right men! When a host of wise men assist and all achievements flourish, emperors and kings follow no different Way in cultivating governance; when the Way of prime ministership is attained and the myriad states are well-ordered, emperors and kings share the same merit in planning for good rule. As for myself, admiring from afar the ethos of Tang and Yu, andใกล้ keeping close to the laws of Xia and Shang, how could I fail to instruct and guide my officials?"

Alas! Governance lies in getting the right men, and selecting men is done through the ruler's own person. Only when one possesses the virtues of reverent illumination [like Yao] and profound wisdom [like Shun] can one employ ministers of the nine virtues and the six virtues; only when one possesses the virtues of reverent self-cultivation [like Yu the Great] and strenuous manifestation of virtue [like Tang of Shang] can one employ ministers who are able to occupy their posts and show eminent talent. When King Cheng wished to rectify his governing officials, he was reverently diligent in cultivating his virtue from morning to night—he may truly be said to have understood the root of the matter! This is why the flourishing abundance of capable men obtained by the House of Zhou shines so gloriously down to the present day. This being so, a ruler who establishes offices in order to plan for good governance can succeed only after rooting it in his own person.

Book of Odes (Shijing)

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
思齊大任文王之母思媚周姜京室之婦
大姒嗣徽音則百斯男
同考試官訓導魯批咏任姒懿德無餘蘊而詞
格端嚴冠冕文也
同考試官教諭蕭批莊重爾雅文逼西京非老
於文學不能
考試官學正陳批詞意高遠
考試官學正王批古雅不羣
===
周人歌任姒之賢所以明文王之聖也夫國之
興皆由內德茂也觀於任姒之賢相繼也而文
王之聖周道之興所從來矣且夫世德不閎者
祥不遠內教不備者化不章我觀周道而嘆先
后文王之德之隆也由前言之則齊莊之大任
實唯文母焉乃及王季惟君子之攸行共我周
姜亶婦順之明序自其莊有禮也而可以道敬
焉自其媚所尊也而可以作睦焉故自摯仲來
歸大任有身而肅雝緝熙之德徽柔懿恭之度
punctuated:
「思齊大任，文王之母，思媚周姜，京室之婦。大姒嗣徽音，則百斯男。」

同考試官訓導魯批：咏任、姒懿德無餘蘊，而詞格端嚴，冠冕文也。
同考試官教諭蕭批：莊重爾雅，文逼西京，非老於文學不能。
考試官學正陳批：詞意高遠。
考試官學正王批：古雅不羣。

周人歌任、姒之賢，所以明文王之聖也。夫國之興，皆由內德茂也。觀於任、姒之賢相繼也，而文王之聖、周道之興，所從來矣。且夫世德不閎者祥不遠，內教不備者化不章，我觀周道，而嘆先后文王之德之隆也。由前言之，則齊莊之大任，實唯文母焉；乃及王季，惟君子之攸行；共我周姜，亶婦順之明序。自其莊有禮也，而可以道敬焉；自其媚所尊也，而可以作睦焉。故自摯仲來歸，大任有身，而肅雝緝熙之德、徽柔懿恭之度，
translation_en:
"Reverent was Tai Ren, the mother of King Wen; loving was she toward Zhou Jiang—a wife in the capital house. Tai Si inherited her admirable renown, and a hundred sons were born to her."

Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Lu comments: It sings of the admirable virtue of Tai Ren and Tai Si without leaving anything unexpressed, while its diction and form are dignified and solemn—a crowning piece of writing.
Associate Examiner, Instructor Xiao comments: Solemn and refined, its style approaches that of the Western Han; none but a veteran of literature could achieve this.
Examiner, Subprefectural Erudite Chen comments: The diction and conception are lofty and far-reaching.
Examiner, Subprefectural Erudite Wang comments: Classically elegant and extraordinary.

When the people of Zhou sang of the worthiness of Tai Ren and Tai Si, it was in order to make manifest the sageliness of King Wen. Indeed, the rise of a state always stems from the flourishing of domestic virtue. Looking at how the worthiness of Tai Ren and Tai Si succeeded one another, one sees whence the sageliness of King Wen and the rise of the Way of Zhou came. Moreover, where hereditary virtue is not vast, auspiciousness does not reach far; where domestic instruction is not complete, moral transformation does not shine forth. I observe the Way of Zhou and sigh in admiration at the exalted virtue of the former sovereign, King Wen. Speaking in terms of what went before, the reverent and grave Tai Ren was truly the mother of King Wen; coming to King Ji, she followed only the conduct of her lord, and in serving our Zhou Jiang, she truly fulfilled the clear order of wifely obedience. From her being grave and observant of ritual propriety, she could lead the way in reverence; from her being loving toward her elder, she could foster harmony. Therefore, from the time the second daughter of the Zhiprince came as a bride and Tai Ren became pregnant, the virtue of solemn harmony and radiant continuity, and the demeanor of admirable gentleness and exemplary respect…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其敎已胎於此矣吾是以明天之篤生文祖而
爲發其祥者如此也嗣時厥後則窈窕之大姒
載紹前休矣勤儉專靜則葛覃卷耳之思慈惠
周容有樛木螽斯之咏是以和氣致祥而明兆
厥祚麟趾錫羨而有百其昌於是武周纘戎諸
姬競爽而陳蔡衛霍之昭郇雍曹滕之穆我周
大啓於此矣吾是以明天之多助文祖而爲作
之合者如此也吁周人可謂善頌先王之美者
矣享其成必遡其始思其德不忘其内豈虛語
===
哉匡衡有言妃匹之際生民之始后夫人之行
必侔乎天地而後可以奉神靈之統吾讀關雎
諸詩及於正月之章而觀周之所以興與其所
以失之者蓋三代一轍不可勝鏡矣是詩也寧
獨升歌美誦而已哉蓋曰内外上下世世同聽
之亦所以勸也
薄言震之莫不震疊懷柔百神及河喬嶽
同考試官訓導魯批薄震懷柔發明得旨是文
punctuated:
其敎已胎於此矣。吾是以明天之篤生文祖，而爲發其祥者如此也。嗣時厥後，則窈窕之大姒載紹前休矣。勤儉專靜，則《葛覃》、《卷耳》之思；慈惠周容，有《樛木》、《螽斯》之咏。是以和氣致祥，而明兆厥祚；麟趾錫羨，而有百其昌。於是武、周纘戎，諸姬競爽，而陳、蔡、衛、霍之昭，郇、雍、曹、滕之穆，我周大啓於此矣。吾是以明天之多助文祖，而爲作之合者如此也。吁！周人可謂善頌先王之美者矣。享其成必遡其始，思其德不忘其内，豈虛語哉！匡衡有言：「妃匹之際，生民之始，后夫人之行，必侔乎天地，而後可以奉神靈之統。」吾讀《關雎》諸詩及於《正月》之章，而觀周之所以興與其所以失之者，蓋三代一轍，不可勝鏡矣。是詩也，寧獨升歌美誦而已哉？蓋曰内外上下，世世同聽之，亦所以勸也。
薄言震之，莫不震疊，懷柔百神，及河喬嶽。
同考試官訓導魯批：薄震懷柔，發明得旨，是文
translation_en:
… its instruction was already conceived right here. By this I understand how Heaven devotedly gave birth to the Cultured Ancestor (King Wen) and brought forth his auspiciousness in such a manner. Following this afterward, the graceful Tai Si carried on the former excellence. In her diligence, frugality, focused devotion, and quietude, there were the thoughts captured in the odes "Ge tan" (The Spreading Kudzu) and "Juan er" (The Cocklebur); in her kindness, benevolence, and all-encompassing tolerance, there were the songs of "Jiu mu" (The Down-curving Trees) and "Zhong si" (The Locusts). Therefore, harmonious氣 (vital energy) brought about auspiciousness, clearly heralding the dynastic fortune; the "Lin zhi" (Toes of the Unicorn) bestowed abundance, and a hundredfold was its prosperity. Thereupon, King Wu and the Duke of Zhou carried on the great enterprise, the various Ji-clan princes vied in brilliance, and with the Zhao-generation states of管 [Guan—text has 陳 Chen], Cai, Wei, and Huo, and the Mu-generation states of Xun, Yong, Cao, and Teng, our Zhou dynasty was grandly inaugurated from this. By this I understand how Heaven richly assisted the Cultured Ancestor and made a match for him in such a manner. Ah! The people of Zhou may well be called skillful in praising the virtues of their former kings. In enjoying the completion, they necessarily traced back to its beginning; in contemplating his virtue, they did not forget his inner helpmeet—how could these be empty words! Kuang Heng匡衡 once said: "The union of royal consorts is the beginning of the people's life; the conduct of queens and consorts must equal Heaven and Earth, and only then can they uphold the lineage of the divine spirits." When I read the various odes beginning with "Guan ju" (The Osprey's Cry) down to the stanzas of "Zheng yue" (The First Month), and observe that whereby the Zhou rose and that whereby it lost the mandate, indeed the Three Dynasties followed a single track, offering inexhaustible lessons to mirror. Could this ode be merely for ascending the hall to sing and reciting in praise? Rather, it means that inner and outer, high and low, generation after generation should listen to it together, as a means of encouragement.

"He shakes them with awe, and none fail to tremble and submit; hecherishes and appeases all the spirits, even to the Yellow River and the lofty peaks." [Book of Odes, "Shi mai" 時邁]

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Lu comments: "'Shaking with awe' and 'cherishing and appeasing' are elucidated in a way that grasps the main purport. This is a composition …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之復古者
同考試官教諭蕭批神人受職天所命也此作
陳義剴當可録
考試官學正陳批詞旨嚴密
考試官學正王批純雅傑作
周德之達于人神天命之也夫王者承天命以
主神人者也治人而人懾之事神而神享之不
可以卜天意乎時邁之詩若曰天人相與之際
甚焉著明國家禎祥之兆示諸行事我周之見
===
右於天而序之也其効可睹已維天難忱而視
聽在人人心即天也吾將卜之人心乎今之如
四嶽而朝同軌也固以輯瑞也而非以作威也
而百辟嚮風焉鸞旂所至而奉共述職者莫不
率從也聲靈所薄而展采錯事者莫敢寧處也
凡我胙土侯甸要荒咸懍懍以蕃王室而永世
守之矣此固周道之對於天下也而天之所興
人不能違抑亦其明徵哉維天於穆而朕兆於
神鬼神亦天也吾且稽之神休乎今之脩五禮
punctuated:
之復古者。
同考試官教諭蕭批：神人受職，天所命也。此作陳義剴當，可録。
考試官學正陳批：詞旨嚴密。
考試官學正王批：純雅傑作。
周德之達于人神，天命之也。夫王者，承天命以主神人者也。治人而人懾之，事神而神享之，不可以卜天意乎？《時邁》之詩若曰：天人相與之際，甚焉著明，國家禎祥之兆，示諸行事。我周之見右於天而序之也，其効可睹已。維天難忱，而視聽在人，人心即天也，吾將卜之人心乎？今之如四嶽而朝同軌也，固以輯瑞也，而非以作威也，而百辟嚮風焉。鸞旂所至，而奉共述職者，莫不率從也；聲靈所薄，而展采錯事者，莫敢寧處也。凡我胙土，侯、甸、要、荒，咸懍懍以蕃王室，而永世守之矣。此固周道之對於天下也，而天之所興，人不能違，抑亦其明徵哉！維天於穆，而朕兆於神，鬼神亦天也，吾且稽之神休乎？今之脩五禮
translation_en:
…that restores antiquity.

Associate Examiner and Instructor Xiao's comment: That spirits and humans accept their charges is ordained by Heaven. This composition sets forth the meaning incisively and appropriately; it deserves to be recorded.

Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Chen's comment: Its diction and purport are rigorous and closely reasoned.

Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Wang's comment: A pure, refined masterpiece.

That the virtue of Zhou reached both humans and spirits was because Heaven ordained it. Now, a true king is one who receives the Mandate of Heaven to preside over spirits and humans. When he governs humans and humans stand in awe of him, and when he serves the spirits and the spirits enjoy his offerings, can one not thereby divine the will of Heaven? The ode "Timely Progression" (Shimai) seems to say: The interaction between Heaven and humankind is supremely manifest, and the auspicious omens of the state are revealed in actual deeds. That our Zhou was favored by Heaven and succeeded to the throne—its efficacy can already be seen!

Heaven is hard to rely upon, yet its seeing and hearing reside in the people; the hearts of the people are themselves Heaven. Shall I divine it in the hearts of the people? Now, when the king goes to the Four Peaks and holds court for all within the same carriage gauge, it is assuredly to gather the jade tokens of investiture, and not to display intimidating majesty—yet the hundred lords turn toward his influence. Wherever the bell-decked banners arrive, among those who offer tribute and report on their duties, there is none who does not follow and obey; wherever his renown and靈-majesty reach, among those who unfold their ceremonial splendor and carry out their charges, there is none who dares to rest at ease. All who have been granted soil by us, in the Baron, Royal, Pacified, and Wild Domains, are filled with reverent awe to serve as a screen to the royal house and guard it for endless generations. This is assuredly how the Way of Zhou responds to the expectations of all under Heaven; yet what Heaven raises up, humans cannot oppose—is this not also its clear proof?

Heaven is profoundly august, yet its subtle signs appear in the spirits; ghosts and spirits are also Heaven. Shall I further examine it in the blessings of the spirits? Now, when he cultivates the five rites…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而徧羣祀也凡以竭款也而非以徼福也而百
神受命焉信至乎淵泉而翕河嘉嚮也德鬯於
升燎而介丘釐祉也凡在祀典上下方祇咸禔
禔以祜王國而永言享之矣夫寧獨周德之假
於明神哉天之所助鬼神從之意者其貞符耶
占之人心旣如彼稽之神貺又如此信乎天之
右序我周也我其受之何以保之庶幾哉無忝
於天之子乎於乎周人之善言天也而又善事
天也颺震疊之威張懷柔之祥而卒以求懿德
===
保右命闋焉夸而不誕美而規豈若晚世之窮
遊登禪而徒以徼誣美號者也自文武之道缺
諸侯解弛河竭山隤周德微矣以是詩觀之尤
信
春秋
春齊侯宋人陳人蔡人邾人會于北杏〔莊公十有三年〕
夏六月公會齊侯宋公陳
侯鄭伯同盟于幽〔莊公二十有七年〕
punctuated:
而徧羣祀也，凡以竭款也，而非以徼福也，而百神受命焉。信至乎淵泉，而翕河嘉嚮也；德鬯於升燎，而介丘釐祉也。凡在祀典，上下方祇，咸禔禔以祜王國，而永言享之矣。夫寧獨周德之假於明神哉？天之所助，鬼神從之，意者其貞符耶！占之人心旣如彼，稽之神貺又如此，信乎天之右序我周也！我其受之，何以保之？庶幾哉無忝於天之子乎！於乎！周人之善言天也，而又善事天也。颺震疊之威，張懷柔之祥，而卒以求懿德、保右命闋焉。夸而不誕，美而規，豈若晚世之窮遊登禪，而徒以徼誣美號者也？自文、武之道缺，諸侯解弛，河竭山隤，周德微矣，以是詩觀之，尤信。
《春秋》
「春，齊侯、宋人、陳人、蔡人、邾人會于北杏〔莊公十有三年〕；夏六月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、鄭伯同盟于幽〔莊公二十有七年〕。」
translation_en:
…and offer sacrifices universally to all the spirits, this is entirely to exhaust our sincere devotion, and not to seek blessings; yet the hundred spirits accept our charge. Sincerity reaches down to the deep springs, and the united River responds favorably; virtue rises fragrantly in the ascending altar fires, and the great mountains bestow happiness. All those recorded in the sacrificial canon, the spirits above and the earthly deities of the quarters below, harmoniously bless the royal state and forever accept its offerings. Now, is this merely the virtue of Zhou reaching the bright spirits? Whom Heaven aids, the ghosts and spirits follow—perhaps this is its true auspice! Divining it in the hearts of men, it is already like that; examining it in the blessings of the spirits, it is also like this. Truly, Heaven favors and orders our Zhou! As we receive it, how shall we preserve it, so that we may perhaps bring no shame to the Son of Heaven? Alas, how well the men of Zhou spoke of Heaven, and how well too they served Heaven! They proclaimed the majesty that caused trembling and awe, and displayed the auspicious signs of pacifying the spirits, yet concluded the ode with seeking admirable virtue and preserving the favored mandate. It is grand yet not extravagant, full of praise yet admonitory—how could it be like later ages, exhausting themselves in imperial tours and ascending the mountains for the Feng and Shan sacrifices merely to seek false and flattering titles? Once the Way of Kings Wen and Wu fell into disrepair, the feudal lords grew lax, the rivers dried up and the mountains collapsed, and the virtue of Zhou declined; viewing it through this ode, one believes it all the more.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

"In spring, the Marquis of Qi, an officer of Song, an officer of Chen, an officer of Cai, and an officer of Zhu met at Beixing [Thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang]. In summer, in the sixth month, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, and the Earl of Zheng, and together made a covenant at You [Twenty-seventh year of Duke Zhuang]."

text:

考試官學正陳批明健
考試官學正王批爾雅
春秋于創伯者與其始而幸其成也夫春秋之
義盟會無專桓始伯而與之伯成而幸之儻亦
衰世之意乎考之北杏之會齊平宋難也齊其
始伯乎君子曰王迹旣熄諸夏攘攘所望以維
持之者誰與不有伯者將安適矣今桓也起而
===
圖之四國羣然而戴之奔走玉帛之會罔敢後
焉是雖未稟於鞏洛之命也而控大國扶小國
捄亂恤難以共謀尊獎之義而紓左衽之患者
不在玆乎吾不意侯伯失職之時而桓爲能經
營天下若此也經故於齊獨書爵與之也幽之
盟陳鄭服于齊也桓之伯張乎此矣君子曰伯
圖方啓人心皇皇所藉以羽翼之者列國耳若
猶貳焉其若之何今桓也徐而俟之鄭亦幡然
而從之周旋壇坫之盟歸于好焉此寧無迫於
punctuated:
同考試官訓導王批：是鏗鏗能爲左、國語者，錄之。
考試官學正陳批：明健。
考試官學正王批：爾雅。

《春秋》于創伯者，與其始而幸其成也。夫《春秋》之義，盟會無專，桓始伯而與之，伯成而幸之，儻亦衰世之意乎？考之北杏之會，齊平宋難也，齊其始伯乎？君子曰：王迹旣熄，諸夏攘攘，所望以維持之者誰與？不有伯者，將安適矣！今桓也起而圖之，四國羣然而戴之，奔走玉帛之會，罔敢後焉。是雖未稟於鞏洛之命也，而控大國、扶小國，捄亂恤難，以共謀尊獎之義，而紓左衽之患者，不在玆乎？吾不意侯伯失職之時，而桓爲能經營天下若此也！經故於齊獨書爵，與之也。幽之盟，陳、鄭服于齊也，桓之伯張乎此矣。君子曰：伯圖方啓，人心皇皇，所藉以羽翼之者列國耳。若猶貳焉，其若之何？今桓也徐而俟之，鄭亦幡然而從之，周旋壇坫之盟，歸于好焉。此寧無迫於
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Wang: This is someone whose ringing prose captures the style of the Zuo Tradition (Zuozhuan) and the Discourses of the States (Guoyu); record it for publication.
Comment by Examiner, Director of Studies Chen: Clear and vigorous.
Comment by Examiner, Director of Studies Wang: Refined and classical.

Toward the founder of the霸 (hegemony), the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) approves of his beginning and rejoices in his success. Now according to the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals, covenants and assemblies are not to be convened on one's own authority. Yet when Duke Huan of Qi first initiated the hegemony, the Classic approved of him, and when his hegemony was established, it rejoiced in it—is this not perhaps a reflection of an age of decline? Examining the assembly at Beixing, where Qi pacified the troubles in Song, was this not the beginning of Qi's hegemony? The gentleman says: After the traces of the true king had died out and the Chinese states were thrown into turmoil, upon whom could one pin hopes to hold the realm together? Without a hegemon, where could anyone turn? Now Huan rose up to plan for this, and the four states gathered together to support him, hastening to the assembly of jade and silk with none daring to lag behind. Although this was not undertaken by command from the royal capital at Gong and Luo, yet did not the work of restraining great states and supporting small ones, rescuing from disorder and relieving distress, jointly planning the righteous cause of honoring and upholding the royal house, and alleviating the threat of falling under barbarian rule ("buttoning robes on the left") rest right here? I would not have expected that at a time when the regional lords and earls had failed in their duties, Huan would be able to bring order to the realm like this! Therefore, the Classic uniquely records the noble title for Qi alone, thereby expressing approval of him. At the covenant at You, Chen and Zheng submitted to Qi, and Huan's hegemony expanded from this point. The gentleman says: When the hegemonic enterprise had just begun and people's minds were still unsettled, what he relied upon as his wings of support were solely the various states. If they still harbored duplicity, what could be done about it? Now Huan calmly waited for them, and Zheng too had a change of heart and followed him, participating in the covenant at the altar and returning to amicable relations. Could this have been wholly free of compulsion from…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
臨淄之威乎而大國畏小國懷講信脩睦以大
振匡糾之勢而表東海之烈者寔賴之矣吾不
意叔伯靡同之日而桓猶能聯率人心若此也
經於是盟特書同幸之也不然則伯者之事毋
乃羞而不道乎抑因是而見桓伯之難也夫以
齊之强豈不可遂得志於諸侯哉而北杏以來
十餘年廑廑始成其爲伯者何也周室雖衰文
武成康之澤猶在人心故黍離而降天下傷之
二三諸侯一旦欲驅而宗齊豈易易乎嗚呼王
===
道之入人深遠矣
公會晉侯及吳子于黃池哀公十有三年
同考試官訓導王 批 非顓門明於春秋之旨者
不能道也
考試官學正陳 批 該暢
考試官學正王 批 簡明
春秋紀夷夏之會而酌辭以示訓焉夫夷而先
夏不可訓也此黃池之會春秋深致意歟是會
punctuated:
臨淄之威乎？而大國畏、小國懷，講信脩睦，以大振匡糾之勢，而表東海之烈者，寔賴之矣。吾不意叔伯靡同之日，而桓猶能聯率人心若此也。經於是盟，特書「同」，幸之也。不然，則伯者之事，毋乃羞而不道乎？抑因是而見桓伯之難也。夫以齊之强，豈不可遂得志於諸侯哉？而北杏以來十餘年，廑廑始成其爲伯者，何也？周室雖衰，文、武、成、康之澤猶在人心。故《黍離》而降，天下傷之。二三諸侯，一旦欲驅而宗齊，豈易易乎？嗚呼！王道之入人深遠矣。

公會晉侯及吳子于黃池（哀公十有三年）
同考試官訓導王批：非顓門明於《春秋》之旨者，不能道也。
考試官學正陳批：該暢。
考試官學正王批：簡明。

《春秋》紀夷夏之會，而酌辭以示訓焉。夫夷而先夏，不可訓也，此黃池之會，《春秋》深致意歟！是會
translation_en:
… the awe of Linzi [Qi]? Yet that the great states stood in fear and the small states were won over, cultivating good faith and promoting harmony so as to greatly rouse the momentum of rectifying and uniting the realm and to display the glorious enterprise of the Eastern Sea—truly it depended on this. I would not have expected that in an age when the regional lords were no longer united, Duke Huan was still able to bind and lead men's hearts like this. That the Classic at this covenant specially records "together" (tong) is because it rejoices in it. Otherwise, would not the affairs of the hegemons be something shameful and not even spoken of? Or perhaps through this we can also see the difficulty of Duke Huan's hegemony. With the strength of Qi, how could he not have immediately gotten his way among the feudal lords? Yet for more than ten years since Beixing, he barely managed to establish his hegemony—why was that? Although the House of Zhou had declined, the beneficence of Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang still remained in men's hearts. Thus from the time of the ode "Millet Lush" (Shuli) onward, the world grieved for it. If two or three feudal lords were suddenly to be driven to pay allegiance to Qi, how could that be easy? Alas! The Kingly Way had entered deeply and far into the hearts of men.

"The Duke met the Marquis of Jin and the Viscount of Wu at Huangchi" (Thirteenth year of Duke Ai).
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Wang comments: None but a specialist who clearly understands the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) could express this.
Examiner and Director of Studies Chen comments: Comprehensive and fluent.
Examiner and Director of Studies Wang comments: Concise and clear.

The Spring and Autumn Annals records the meeting between barbarians and the Chinese states, weighing its words carefully to set forth a lesson. For barbarians to take precedence over the Chinese states cannot be taught as a model; is this not why the Spring and Autumn Annals devotes such deep attention to the meeting at Huangchi? title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也吳晉爭長晉長吳矣經先晉者紀常也吳僭
王矣經書子者正名也以合兩伯而言及者不
以吳先晉又不欲泯其實以著其強而抑之也
夫此一會也而聖人惓惓若此者何哉蓋中國
有常尊夷狄無常盛所以治內御外者在我而
已惟玆晉也可後於吳哉固宗盟之長也墮其
世業而遽爲吳下惡能振其式微之運乎經斯
世者欲使中國常處其尊以制夷狄不可無彊
治之猷矣吳也可先晉哉固僭王之夷也馮其
===
積威而晉不與校胡以遏其方張之勢乎經斯
世者欲使夷狄常處其卑以奉中國不可無制
御之策矣存亡者天也以人勝天則天可必徒
諉於天而拂天地之經以幸於無亡吾未見其
能國也順逆者理也以理勝勢則勢不足恃徒
狃於勢而忘冠屨之分以即安目前恐不可一
朝居也聖人至此有深慮焉故先晉狄吳而特
書及訓後世以治中國御四夷之道至深切矣
以此垂訓而後世猶有位上侯王之議稱臣突
punctuated: 也，吳、晉爭長。晉長吳矣，經先晉者，紀常也；吳僭王矣，經書「子」者，正名也；以合兩伯而言「及」者，不以吳先晉，又不欲泯其實，以著其強而抑之也。夫此一會也，而聖人惓惓若此者，何哉？蓋中國有常尊，夷狄無常盛，所以治內御外者，在我而已。惟玆晉也，可後於吳哉？固宗盟之長也，墮其世業而遽爲吳下，惡能振其式微之運乎？經斯世者，欲使中國常處其尊以制夷狄，不可無彊治之猷矣。吳也，可先晉哉？固僭王之夷也，馮其積威而晉不與校，胡以遏其方張之勢乎？經斯世者，欲使夷狄常處其卑以奉中國，不可無制御之策矣。存亡者，天也，以人勝天則天可必；徒諉於天而拂天地之經，以幸於無亡，吾未見其能國也。順逆者，理也，以理勝勢則勢不足恃；徒狃於勢而忘冠屨之分，以即安目前，恐不可一朝居也。聖人至此，有深慮焉，故先晉、狄吳而特書「及」，訓後世以治中國、御四夷之道，至深切矣。以此垂訓，而後世猶有位上侯王之議、稱臣突…
translation_en: … [Regarding this covenant], Wu and Jin contended for precedence. Jin normally held precedence over Wu, so the Classic's placing Jin first records the constant norm; Wu had usurped the title of King, so the Classic's writing "Viscount" rectifies names; and its using the word "and" (ji) in bringing the two hegemons together refuses to place Wu ahead of Jin while also not wishing to obscure the reality, thereby exposing Wu's brute strength and yet suppressing it. Now, in this single meeting, why was the Sage so earnestly attentive as this? It is because the Central States have a constant dignity, whereas the barbarians do not have constant flourishing; the means to govern the interior and control the exterior lie simply within ourselves. Now as for this state of Jin, could it be placed after Wu? It was assuredly the leader of the kindred covenants; if it ruined its hereditary achievement and suddenly fell beneath Wu, how could it revive its declining fortunes? Those who order the world, wishing to make the Central States always occupy their position of dignity so as to control the barbarians, cannot lack a plan for vigorous governance. And as for Wu, could it be placed before Jin? It was assuredly a barbarian state that had usurped the title of King; relying on its accumulated might, if Jin did not contest with it, how could its burgeoning momentum be checked? Those who order the world, wishing to make the barbarians always occupy their lowly position so as to serve the Central States, cannot lack a strategy for control and mastery. Survival and ruin belong to Heaven, yet when human effort overcomes Heaven, Heaven can be made certain; if one merely shifts the blame to Heaven and violates the invariable norms of Heaven and Earth, hoping by luck to avoid ruin, I have never seen such a one able to preserve his state. Right order and perversity belong to principle, and when principle overcomes situational force, situational force is not worth relying upon; if one merely grows accustomed to situational force and forgets the distinction between cap and shoes in order to seek immediate ease, I fear one could not abide in it for a single morning. Coming to this point, the Sage had deep anxieties; therefore he placed Jin first, treated Wu as barbarian, and specially wrote "and," instructing later generations in the Way of governing the Central States and controlling the four barbarian tribes most deeply and earnestly. Even though he handed down instruction in this manner, in later generations there were still proposals to rank [barbarian chieftains] above marquises and princes, strategies of declaring oneself a subject to the Turks [?]…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
厭之策甚至以父事之者嗟夫中國不能令則
夷狄進矣晉自平定以來政在家門民無所依
君日不悛以樂慆憂公室之卑其無日也又安
能與吳爭哉君子觀於黃池之會而知晉事不
可爲矣書曰無怠無荒四夷來王先治內也夫
禮記
凡居民材必因天地寒煖燥濕廣谷大川
異制民生其間者異俗剛柔輕重遲速
異齊五味異和器械異制衣服異宜脩
===
其教不易其俗齊其政不易其宜
同考試官教諭周批聖人治世求同於道不求
同於俗正所以宜民此作得旨
考試官學正陳批醇正
考試官學正王批雋永
王者儲材之順無非因造化而順之也夫造化
之氣不一而民用亦以異矣居材者惡可弗順
乎是故惟脩其政教而已嘗謂聖王以利利天
punctuated:
厭之策，甚至以父事之者。嗟夫！中國不能令，則夷狄進矣。晉自平、定以來，政在家門，民無所依，君日不悛，以樂慆憂，公室之卑，其無日也，又安能與吳爭哉？君子觀於黃池之會，而知晉事不可爲矣。《書》曰：「無怠無荒，四夷來王。」先治內也夫！

《禮記》
「凡居民材，必因天地寒煖燥濕，廣谷大川異制。民生其間者異俗，剛柔輕重遲速異齊，五味異和，器械異制，衣服異宜。脩其教，不易其俗；齊其政，不易其宜。」
同考試官教諭周批：聖人治世，求同於道，不求同於俗，正所以宜民，此作得旨。
考試官學正陳批：醇正。
考試官學正王批：雋永。

王者儲材之順，無非因造化而順之也。夫造化之氣不一，而民用亦以異矣，居材者惡可弗順乎？是故惟脩其政教而已。嘗謂聖王以利利天
translation_en:
…policies of declaring oneself a vassal to the Turks [reading 突厭 as 突厥], and even going so far as to serve them as a father! Alas! When the Central States cannot command, the barbarians advance. In Jin, since the reigns of Dukes Ping and Ding, government power had resided with the ministerial families and the people had nothing to rely upon. Its rulers daily failed to reform, masking their worries with pleasures. The abasement of the ducal house was imminent—how then could it contend with Wu? When the gentleman observes the covenant at Huangchi, he knows that the affairs of Jin were beyond salvage. The Book of Documents says: "Without idleness or neglect, the four barbarian tribes will come to acknowledge the king's sovereignty." One must first govern the interior!

Record of Rites (Liji)
"In all cases of settling the people and accumulating resources, one must adapt to the cold, warmth, dryness, and moisture of heaven and earth. Broad valleys and great rivers are differently formed, and the people born among them have different customs; their剛 [firmness], 柔 [pliancy], lightness, heaviness, slowness, and quickness are of different temperaments; the five flavors are differently blended; implements and tools are differently fashioned; and garments are differently suited. Cultivate their teachings without changing their customs; unify their governance without changing what is suitable to them."

Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: When the sages governed the world, they sought uniformity in the Way, not uniformity in customs, which was precisely how they suited the people. This composition grasps the main point.
Examiner Chen, Director of Studies, comments: Pure and orthodox.
Examiner Wang, Director of Studies, comments: Rich and lasting in meaning.

The compliance with which a true king stores up resources is nothing other than adapting to and complying with the creative forces of nature. Now, the vital energies of nature are not uniform, and what the people use consequently differs as well. How could one who settles and accumulates resources fail to comply with them? Therefore, he simply cultivates his governance and teachings, and nothing more. I have maintained that the sage kings benefited the world with what is beneficial…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
下而天下以其分取足焉所以左右之而善其
用于不窮者自有不易之道在也吾得之居民
材矣今夫民之材民用之莫非因天地而用焉
者也寒煖燥濕天地司之故凡居民材莫非因
天地而居焉者也夫聖王何爲而必因之也蓋
自二儀肇分谷之虛而廣也川之流而大也其
形制之判于天地者已不能比之而使同是以
民生其間者習俗性情殊焉五味器械衣服異
焉而材用之取于天地者亦不能强之而使一
===
此皆尚之爲俗安之爲宜不可得而易者也是
故以民之可同者同天下而不以民之本異者
病天下三綱五典皆敎也凡以植天常而立人
紀也不可不脩也至于俗之所在則不易焉何
者俗固天地之氣使之也吾因乎天地而何以
易焉也況敎行而俗自美又有不必易者乎禮
樂刑政皆政也凡以同民心而出治道也不可
不齊也至于宜之所在則不易焉何者宜固天
地之氣成之也吾因乎天地而無容易焉也況
punctuated: 下，而天下以其分取足焉。所以左右之而善其用于不窮者，自有不易之道在也，吾得之「居民材」矣。今夫民之材，民用之，莫非因天地而用焉者也；寒煖燥濕，天地司之，故凡居民材，莫非因天地而居焉者也。夫聖王何爲而必因之也？蓋自二儀肇分，谷之虛而廣也，川之流而大也，其形制之判于天地者，已不能比之而使同。是以民生其間者，習俗性情殊焉，五味、器械、衣服異焉，而材用之取于天地者，亦不能强之而使一。此皆尚之爲俗，安之爲宜，不可得而易者也。是故以民之可同者同天下，而不以民之本異者病天下。三綱五典，皆敎也，凡以植天常而立人紀也，不可不脩也；至于俗之所在，則不易焉。何者？俗固天地之氣使之也，吾因乎天地，而何以易焉也？況敎行而俗自美，又有不必易者乎！禮樂刑政，皆政也，凡以同民心而出治道也，不可不齊也；至于宜之所在，則不易焉。何者？宜固天地之氣成之也，吾因乎天地，而無容易焉也。況
translation_en: … the world, and the world draws sufficiency from it according to each person's lot. Thus, in assisting them and perfecting their resources so that they are inexhaustible, there is naturally an unchanging Way present; I have found this in "stocking resources for the people." Now as for the resources of the people, when the people use them, in every case they use them by adapting to Heaven and Earth; cold and warmth, dryness and dampness are governed by Heaven and Earth, and therefore whenever one stocks resources for the people, in every case one stocks them by adapting to Heaven and Earth. Why must the sage-king necessarily adapt to them? Indeed, since the Two Primal Forces first separated—the valleys being empty and broad, the rivers flowing and great—the physical forms divided between Heaven and Earth could already no longer be aligned and made identical. Therefore, among the people born within these spaces, their customs and temperaments differ, their five flavors, implements, and clothing vary, and the resources and utilities they draw from Heaven and Earth likewise cannot be forced into uniformity. All of these are what they esteem as custom and rest in as suitability, which cannot be altered. Therefore, he unites the world through that in which the people can be united, and does not burden the world over that in which the people are inherently different. The Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues are all instruction; because they serve to establish heavenly constants and set up human standards, they must be cultivated. Yet when it comes to where customs lie, they are not altered. Why is this? Customs are indeed caused by the vital energies of Heaven and Earth; since we adapt to Heaven and Earth, why would we alter them? How much more so when, as instruction is carried out, customs naturally become admirable, so that there is no need to alter them! Rites, music, punishments, and administration are all governance; because they serve to unite the minds of the people and bring forth the Way of order, they must be made uniform. Yet when it comes to where suitabilities lie, they are not altered. Why is this? Suitabilities are indeed formed by the vital energies of Heaven and Earth; since we adapt to Heaven and Earth, there is no room to alter them. How much more so when…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
善政而民咸宜又有不必易者乎夫觀俗與宜
之因也則民用日充而政教之基裕矣觀政與
教之脩也則民德日新而財用之流節矣聖王
所以能使民順治者惟其不以己與之也夫雖
然此大順之道也蓋先王以順道治天下六府
脩三事舉而俗宜之無害於治者則不拂民之
欲焉故周官一書九貢九賦九式每惓惓焉職
此耳吁經綸之迹具在也有關雎麟趾之意王
政至今存可也有天下者當念諸
===
教順成俗內外和順國家理治此之謂盛
德
同考試官教諭周 批 陽教陰教萬化所繇重矣
此作能發明旨義可錄
考試官學正陳 批 整飭
考試官學正王 批 明鬯
觀君后化成於天下而德之盛可知矣蓋君后
天下所觀化而德以運之者也曾謂德盛矣而
punctuated:
善政而民咸宜，又有不必易者乎？夫觀俗與宜之因也，則民用日充，而政教之基裕矣；觀政與教之脩也，則民德日新，而財用之流節矣。聖王所以能使民順治者，惟其不以己與之也夫！雖然，此大順之道也。蓋先王以順道治天下，六府脩，三事舉，而俗宜之無害於治者，則不拂民之欲焉。故《周官》一書，九貢、九賦、九式，每惓惓焉，職此耳。吁！經綸之迹具在也，有《關雎》、《麟趾》之意，王政至今存可也，有天下者當念諸！

「教順成俗，內外和順，國家理治，此之謂盛德。」
同考試官教諭周批：陽教陰教，萬化所繇，重矣。此作能發明旨義，可錄。
考試官學正陳批：整飭。
考試官學正王批：明鬯。

觀君后化成於天下，而德之盛可知矣。蓋君后，天下所觀化，而德以運之者也，曾謂德盛矣，而
translation_en:
… the governance is good and the people all find it suitable, so that there is even less need to change what they find suitable? Now, when we observe the following of local customs and what is suitable to the people, we see that the people's resources become daily more abundant, and the foundation for governance and instruction becomes ample; when we observe the cultivation of governance and instruction, we see that the people's virtue is daily renewed, and the expenditure of wealth and resources becomes regulated. The reason the sage kings were able to bring the people into compliant order was simply that they did not impose their own personal will upon them! Even so, this is the Way of Great Compliance. Indeed, when the former kings governed the world through the Way of compliance, the Six Treasuries were kept in order and the Three Affairs were carried out, while in matters of local custom and suitability that posed no harm to governance, they did not go against the desires of the people. Therefore, throughout the book of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), the nine tributes, nine revenues, and nine fiscal allotments are repeatedly and earnestly emphasized precisely because of this. Alas! The traces of their statecraft are all still present. If one possesses the spirit of the "Guanju" and "Linzhi" odes, kingly governance could survive even to this very day. Those who possess the empire ought to bear this in mind!

"Instruction and compliance form customs; within and without there is harmony and compliance, and the state and family are well-ordered and governed: this is called Abundant Virtue."
Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhou's comment: Instruction in the yang principle and instruction in the yin principle are the source from which all transformations arise—weighty indeed! This essay is able to elucidate the essential meaning and is worthy of selection.
Examiner, Director of Studies Chen's comment: Well-ordered and disciplined.
Examiner, Director of Studies Wang's comment: Clear and fluent.

When we observe the sovereign and the empress bringing moral transformation to completion throughout the world, the abundance of their virtue can be known. For the sovereign and the empress are those to whom the world looks for transformation, and it is through virtue that they set it in motion. Could it ever be said that when virtue is abundant,…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
大化有不洽者乎記昏義者及此謂夫朝廷四
方之極閨門風化之原吾於是而知建官立宮
以聽治所關乎化理大矣蓋天子秉陽剛之德
以端拱於上天下之男教賴焉后備陰柔之德
以助理於內天下之婦順則焉今各脩其職以
聽治於內外也則教行而化洽男之以知帥人
者翕然彝教之大同外和而國無不治矣化行
而俗美女之以順爲正者怡然雍睦之無間內
順而家無不理矣教化四達而禮俗維新治之
===
至也而皆天子與后倡之焉其德豈可以易言
哉吾知健順相成而惟皇之極以建陰陽合德
而元良之度克端其在君德則剛健中正之充
積者徵諸國之順治而可以窺其蘊矣否則化
理無本烏能使外治之脩耶其在后德則徽柔
懿恭之素聞者驗諸家之和理而可以想其盛
矣否則表率無基烏能使內職之脩耶吁君后
之德有關於治道如此則天子當必自脩厥德
以爲化民之本而正始於后者亦尚知慎重矣
punctuated: 大化有不洽者乎？記《昏義》者及此。謂夫朝廷，四方之極；閨門，風化之原。吾於是而知建官立宮以聽治，所關乎化理大矣。蓋天子秉陽剛之德以端拱於上，天下之男教賴焉；后備陰柔之德以助理於內，天下之婦順則焉。今各脩其職以聽治於內外也，則教行而化洽，男之以知帥人者，翕然彝教之大同，外和而國無不治矣；化行而俗美，女之以順爲正者，怡然雍睦之無間，內順而家無不理矣。教化四達而禮俗維新，治之至也，而皆天子與后倡之焉，其德豈可以易言哉！吾知健順相成，而惟皇之極以建；陰陽合德，而元良之度克端。其在君德，則剛健中正之充積者，徵諸國之順治而可以窺其蘊矣；否則化理無本，烏能使外治之脩耶？其在后德，則徽柔懿恭之素聞者，驗諸家之和理而可以想其盛矣；否則表率無基，烏能使內職之脩耶？吁！君后之德有關於治道如此，則天子當必自脩厥德以爲化民之本，而正始於后者亦尚知慎重矣…
translation_en:
…there could be a case where the great transformation is not pervasive? The writer of the "Meaning of the Marriage Rites" (Hun yi) reached this point. He meant that the court is the standard for the four quarters, and the inner quarters are the source of moral transformation. From this I know that establishing offices and setting up palaces in order to attend to governance is of great consequence to transformative order. For the Son of Heaven holds to the virtue of yang firmness to sit in dignified composure above, and the instruction of men throughout the realm relies upon him; the Empress possesses the virtue of yin gentleness to assist in ordering the inner domain, and the obedience of women throughout the realm takes its model from her. Now, when each cultivates their duties in attending to the governance of the outer and inner domains, instruction is carried out and transformation becomes pervasive. Men, who lead others through knowledge, are united in the great harmony of constant instruction; with harmony in the outer domain, there is no state that is not well governed. When transformation is carried out and customs are made beautiful, women, who take obedience as their correctness, are joyful in uninterrupted concord; with obedience in the inner domain, there is no household that is not well ordered. When instruction and transformation reach in all four directions and ritual customs are renewed, this is the perfection of governance—and all of it is initiated by the Son of Heaven and the Empress. How could their virtue be spoken of lightly!

I know that vigour and obedience complement one another, and thereby the august standard is established; yin and yang unite their virtues, and thereby the measure of supreme goodness is made upright. With regard to the sovereign's virtue, the abundant accumulation of firm vigour and central correctness can be glimpsed in its inner depth when verified against the compliant governance of the state; otherwise, transformative order would have no root, so how could it bring about the cultivation of outer governance? With regard to the Empress's virtue, her long-standing reputation for admirable gentleness and fine reverence can be imagined in its flourishing fullness when tested against the harmonious ordering of the household; otherwise, setting an example would have no foundation, so how could it bring about the cultivation of inner duties? Ah! Since the virtue of the sovereign and the Empress is of such consequence to the way of governance, the Son of Heaven must surely cultivate his own virtue as the root of transforming the people, and in rectifying the beginning with the Empress, he should also know to be circumspect…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
哉嘗觀周禮設官九嬪世婦之職旣詳且備下
逮女祝女史亦皆窈窕淑女以掌其事而宮闈
之間敎無不存焉周家有道之長而敎順明章
豈徒六官分職而已哉其本始固自有在也吁
此昏禮聖王重之記者以此垂訓其意深矣
第貳場
論
古之學者爲己
===
同考試官敎諭蕭批詞意都入玄思鏘然左國
豈經生所能
同考試官敎諭李批立議以聖門爲衡品列諸
子則爲己之學自有根據非尋常操鉛槧者
考試官學正陳批卓然奧論
考試官學正王批思超調古
聖人之言有殫言者有約言者原本而逮末引
始而要終殫舉而顯言之者雅言也挈其體而
藏其用專其內而不及其外隱約而言之者變辭
punctuated:
哉！嘗觀《周禮》設官，九嬪、世婦之職旣詳且備，下逮女祝、女史，亦皆窈窕淑女以掌其事，而宮闈之間，敎無不存焉。周家有道之長，而敎順明章，豈徒六官分職而已哉？其本始固自有在也。吁！此昏禮聖王重之，記者以此垂訓，其意深矣。

第貳場
論
古之學者爲己

同考試官敎諭蕭批：詞意都入玄思，鏘然《左》、《國》，豈經生所能？
同考試官敎諭李批：立議以聖門爲衡，品列諸子，則爲己之學自有根據，非尋常操鉛槧者。
考試官學正陳批：卓然奧論。
考試官學正王批：思超調古。

聖人之言，有殫言者，有約言者。原本而逮末，引始而要終，殫舉而顯言之者，雅言也；挈其體而藏其用，專其內而不及其外，隱約而言之者，變辭
translation_en:
…indeed! I have observed that in the establishment of offices in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), the duties of the Nine Imperial Concubines (jiupin) and the Hereditary Consorts (shifu) were already detailed and complete; extending down to the Female Invocators (nüzhu) and Female Scribes (nüshi), all were likewise modest and virtuous ladies who took charge of their affairs, so that within the palace quarters there was nowhere that instruction did not exist. That the House of Zhou enjoyed a long-lasting reign of moral order, with its teachings of compliance bright and manifest—how could this merely be a matter of the Six Ministries dividing their duties? Its fundamental origin certainly had its own basis. Alas! Such was the marriage rite that the sage kings attached great weight to it, and the recorder handed down this instruction by means of it; his meaning was profound indeed.

Second Session
Discourse
"The ancients who learned did so for themselves" (Gu zhi xuezhe wei ji)

Associate Examiner and Instructor Xiao comments: Both diction and meaning enter into abstruse thought, ringing like the Zuo Tradition (Zuozhuan) and the Discourses of the States (Guoyu)—how could a mere student of the classics be capable of this?
Associate Examiner and Instructor Li comments: In establishing its argument, it takes the gate of the Sage as its standard to rank and evaluate the Various Masters; thus learning for oneself naturally possesses a solid foundation. This is no ordinary writer wielding lead and wooden tablets.
Examiner and Director of Studies Chen comments: A preeminent and profound discourse.
Examiner and Director of Studies Wang comments: Transcendent in thought, antique in tone.

Among the words of the Sage, there are those spoken exhaustively and those spoken succinctly. Tracing from the root to reach the branches, drawing from the beginning to sum up the end, enumerating exhaustively and stating things explicitly—these are his standard words (yayan). Grasping the substance while concealing the function, focusing exclusively on the internal without touching upon the external, and speaking in an implicit and succinct manner—these are his modified expressions…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也變詞者聖人矯世厲俗從先進之意不可不
察也夫道通人己貫古今始於誠意正心而施
之家國天下皆吾性也是故蓄德非己也脩業
非人也爲己非內也爲人非外也合外內之道
也而子曰古之學者爲己今之學者爲人此何
以明焉豈古之人獨專己而遺人乎是楊朱之
爲我也夫楊子嗇一毛去名絶世疾仁義之多
岐詆堯舜伯夷爲讓名其道芻狗萬物以老子
爲宗此夫豢酒塞戸不饗客以餘者也豈吾所
===
稱爲己者哉謬於夫子之指矣夫子蓋見夫春
秋之世衆人域域貪夫殉財夸者死權遊士滑
稽俠士榮名烏睹所謂脩身繕性之道焉雖以
七十子之徒如顓孫端木卜商冉有四人者號
稱高第且也端木殖貨求也聚斂商也見紛華
而悅顓孫干祿以聞爲達並騖於世之温蠖溺
其身矣夫子蓋傷之若曰吾將兼人己殫舉而
告之乎其毋乃不察於世也吾且專舉而言之
反其所好而道其所亡儻可捄乎故曰古之學
