punctuated: 也。變詞者，聖人矯世厲俗，從先進之意，不可不察也。夫道通人己，貫古今，始於誠意正心，而施之家國天下，皆吾性也。是故蓄德非己也，脩業非人也；爲己非內也，爲人非外也：合外內之道也。而子曰：「古之學者爲己，今之學者爲人。」此何以明焉？豈古之人獨專己而遺人乎？是楊朱之爲我也。夫楊子嗇一毛，去名絶世，疾仁義之多岐，詆堯、舜、伯夷爲讓名，其道芻狗萬物，以老子爲宗，此夫豢酒塞戸、不饗客以餘者也。豈吾所稱爲己者哉？謬於夫子之指矣！夫子蓋見夫春秋之世，衆人域域，貪夫殉財，夸者死權，遊士滑稽，俠士榮名，烏睹所謂脩身繕性之道焉？雖以七十子之徒，如顓孫、端木、卜商、冉有四人者，號稱高第，且也端木殖貨，求也聚斂，商也見紛華而悅，顓孫干祿、以聞爲達，並騖於世之温蠖，溺其身矣。夫子蓋傷之，若曰：「吾將兼人己，殫舉而告之乎？其毋乃不察於世也。吾且專舉而言之，反其所好而道其所亡，儻可捄乎！」故曰「古之學
translation_en: … [expedient] expressions. Expedient expressions reflect the Sage's intent to rectify the age, invigorate customs, and follow the predecessors; this must be carefully examined. Now, the Way connects others and the self, penetrates antiquity and the present, begins with making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind, and extends to the family, the state, and all under Heaven—all of this is our innate nature. Therefore, accumulating virtue is not merely for oneself, and cultivating one's enterprise is not merely for others; acting for oneself is not merely internal, and acting for others is not merely external: it is the Way that unites the external and the internal. Yet the Master said, "In antiquity, those who learned did so for themselves; today, those who learn do so for others." How is this to be explained? Could it be that the people of antiquity focused solely on themselves and neglected others? That would be the egoism ("acting for myself") of Yang Zhu 楊朱! Now, Master Yang begrudged a single hair, cast aside reputation and broke with the world, detested the many branching paths of benevolence and righteousness, and slandered Yao 堯, Shun 舜, and Boyi 伯夷 as yielding merely for the sake of reputation. His Way treats the myriad things as straw dogs, taking Laozi 老子 as its ancestor; this is like someone whose house is stuffed with fine meats and wine, yet who refuses to treat guests even with the leftovers. How could this be what we call "learning for oneself"? It is utterly contrary to the Master's meaning! The Master saw that in the world of the Spring and Autumn period, the multitude were hemmed in and restless: greedy men sacrificed their lives for wealth, boastful men died for power, wandering persuaders practiced slick sophistry, and knights-errant gloried in fame—where could one see the so-called Way of cultivating the person and mending one's nature? Even among the followers of the seventy disciples, such as the four men Zhuansun 顓孫 [Zizhang 子張], Duanmu 端木 [Zigong 子貢], Bu Shang 卜商 [Zixia 子夏], and Ran You 冉有 [Ran Qiu 冉求], who were acclaimed as top disciples—even so, Duanmu amassed goods, Qiu 求 gathered imposts, Shang 商 delighted upon seeing worldly splendor, and Zhuansun sought official emolument and mistook notoriety for true distinction. Together they galloped into the murky confusion of the world and drowned themselves in it. The Master was grieved by this, as if to say: "Should I combine both others and the self, and exhaustively set forth the whole teaching for them? That would perhaps fail to take stock of the state of the world. I shall instead single out one aspect to speak of, countering what they are fond of and pointing out what they have lost—perhaps then they can be saved!" Thus, when he said, "In antiquity, those who learned…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者爲己其指深矣其道大矣廣矣無所不包矣
飾貌理辭容容與與文矣方之而違舍智匿數
依誠託貞近質矣方之而谿疏布脫粟動示爲
儉似也而欺兼愛尚同示人以廣似也而蕩踰
垣鑿坯咽李棄蔬以爲潔辟也孤犢三足堅白
異同以爲辨誕也篤靜致柔挫銳解紛以遊乎
無何有之鄉名曰陸沉離也槁形幻物譚乎六
合之外而漫行無所家使人眩焉亂也芥萬鍾
塗章冕文犧爲辱之義當焉而墜遠柔曼黜淫
===
辟捐詭靡之節當焉而卑辨繁緣設小物賓賓
然以灼於人焉而微端委結紱齊莊矜辭脩脩
然堂序之間而疏澄乎性情之端寤乎象意之
先察乎希微之際戒乎奧窔之中倫物非巨也
秋毫非細也須臾非近也終身非遠也進而受
非干利也退而讓非爲名高也不妄耦於人非
爲亢也其耦非私昵也不苟同於人非爲異也
其同非比黨也見善忻然如不及見不善悚然
而思貴而不盈而曰吾遇惠而不有而曰吾義
punctuated: 者爲己。」其指深矣，其道大矣、廣矣，無所不包矣。飾貌理辭，容容與與，文矣，方之而違；舍智匿數，依誠託貞，近質矣，方之而谿；疏布脫粟，動示爲儉，似也而欺；兼愛尚同，示人以廣，似也而蕩；踰垣鑿坯，咽李棄蔬，以爲潔，辟也；孤犢三足，堅白異同，以爲辨，誕也；篤靜致柔，挫銳解紛，以遊乎無何有之鄉，名曰陸沉，離也；槁形幻物，譚乎六合之外，而漫行無所家，使人眩焉，亂也；芥萬鍾、塗章冕、文犧爲辱之義，當焉而墜；遠柔曼、黜淫辟、捐詭靡之節，當焉而卑；辨繁緣、設小物，賓賓然以灼於人焉，而微；端委結紱，齊莊矜辭，脩脩然堂序之間，而疏。澄乎性情之端，寤乎象意之先，察乎希微之際，戒乎奧窔之中。倫物非巨也，秋毫非細也；須臾非近也，終身非遠也。進而受，非干利也；退而讓，非爲名高也。不妄耦於人，非爲亢也，其耦非私昵也；不苟同於人，非爲異也，其同非比黨也。見善忻然如不及，見不善悚然而思。貴而不盈，而曰吾遇；惠而不有，而曰吾義。
translation_en: … learned for themselves.” Its purport is profound, and its Way is great and broad, leaving nothing unembraced! When one adorns one’s appearance and polishes one’s words with calm and easy poise, it looks refined, yet compared against this Way it is errant; when one discards cleverness and conceals calculation, relying on sincerity and claiming rectitude, it approaches substance, yet compared against this Way it is narrow and perverse; wearing coarse cloth and eating unhulled grain, demonstrating frugality in every action, resembles it, yet is deceitful; universal love and prizing uniformity, displaying breadth of mind to others, resembles it, yet is unrestrained; vaulting over walls and breaking through unbaked bricks to flee office, or swallowing wormy plums and discarding gifted vegetables to count as pure, is eccentric; arguing that an orphaned calf has no mother or a chicken has three feet, or debating “hard and white” and “similarity and difference” to count as eloquent, is absurd; holding fast to quiescence and attaining suppleness, blunting sharpness and untangling knots so as to wander in the realm of nothingness—what is called “sinking on dry land”—is detached from reality; withering one’s frame and treating things as illusions, discoursing beyond the six directions of the cosmos while wandering aimlessly without a home to dazzle others, is chaotic; the righteousness that regards ten thousand measures of grain as ablade of grass, official insignia and ceremonial caps as mud, and the embroidered sacrificial ox as disgrace, collapses when measured against it; the integrity that shuns soft seductions, rejects licentious depravity, and casts aside specious extravagance, seems lowly when measured against it; distinguishing intricate trimmings and setting out minor ritual objects, attentively seeking to shine before others, is petty; wearing ceremonial robes and tying official sashes, maintaining solemn gravity and guarded speech, moving with measured grace between hall and school, is still superficial. Instead, it purifies the very beginnings of human nature and emotion, awakens prior to images and concepts, discerns at the border of the subtle and imperceptible, and maintains vigilance in the hidden recesses of the house. Human relations and things of the world are not considered vast, nor is the tip of an autumn hair considered minute; an instant is not considered near, nor is a whole lifetime considered distant. Advancing to accept office is not to seek profit; withdrawing to yield is not to court a lofty reputation. Not carelessly pairing with others is not out of arrogance, and when one does pair with others it is not out of private intimacy; not casually agreeing with others is not to be contrarian, and when one does agree it is not out of partisan clique. Seeing goodness, one rejoices as though unable to reach it; seeing evil, one reflects in trepidation. Being noble without arrogance, one says, “It is merely my fortunate encounter”; bestowing favors without claiming possession of them, one says, “It is merely my duty.” …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
德尊若愚業尊若夷譽而不居誹而不疑貌不
羡乎情言不羡乎行人知之若亡人不知之亦
若亡福不謂祥菑不謂殃窮達患難終始爲晝
夜寒暑之序矣若此者其唯仲尼乎大哉仲尼
之道也累世不能殫其學而恂恂然曰吾何知
問于老聃學于師襄咨于萇弘郯子蓋發憤忘
食不知其老也聘於列國行乎魯不合則去司
寇不能留廩丘不能祿焉戒于匡逐于衛厄于
陳蔡沮于晏嬰子西而絃歌不輟慍色不形焉
===
故其語由賜曰仁者不必信智者不必行良農
能爲稼而不能爲穡君子脩其道不能爲容而
他日又曰不怨天不尤人下學而上達知我者
其天乎夫不求容於人而求知於天爲己之學
斯其至矣乎是以顏淵簞食好學如愚孔子賢
之子若難仕孔子喜之聞曾晳浴沂風雩之言
則喟然進之原思讓宰粟不見謂廉子貢贖人
而不受金不見謂義子路餉長溝之役不見謂
仁夫三者美行也而聖人不取惡不誠也不貴
punctuated: 德尊若愚，業尊若夷，譽而不居，誹而不疑，貌不羡乎情，言不羡乎行，人知之若亡，人不知之亦若亡。福不謂祥，菑不謂殃，窮達患難，終始爲晝夜寒暑之序矣。若此者，其唯仲尼乎！大哉仲尼之道也！累世不能殫其學，而恂恂然曰：「吾何知？」問于老聃，學于師襄，咨于萇弘、郯子，蓋發憤忘食，不知其老也。聘於列國，行乎魯，不合則去，司寇不能留，廩丘不能祿焉。戒于匡，逐于衛，厄于陳、蔡，沮于晏嬰、子西，而絃歌不輟，慍色不形焉。故其語由、賜曰：「仁者不必信，智者不必行。良農能爲稼而不能爲穡，君子脩其道不能爲容。」而他日又曰：「不怨天，不尤人，下學而上達，知我者其天乎！」夫不求容於人而求知於天，爲己之學，斯其至矣乎！是以顏淵簞食好學如愚，孔子賢之；子若難仕，孔子喜之；聞曾晳浴沂風雩之言，則喟然進之。原思讓宰粟，不見謂廉；子貢贖人而不受金，不見謂義；子路餉長溝之役，不見謂仁。夫三者美行也，而聖人不取，惡不誠也，不貴
translation_en: …Though his virtue is lofty, he appears foolish; though his achievements are exalted, he remains unassuming. When praised, he does not claim credit; when slandered, he does not waver in doubt. His demeanor does not exceed his true feelings, nor do his words exceed his actions. Whether others recognize him or not, he remains as though oblivious to it. Good fortune he does not call an auspicious omen, nor calamity a disaster; adversity, success, and hardship are to him from beginning to end like the natural succession of day and night, winter and summer. One who is like this—could it be only Zhongni [Confucius] 仲尼! Great indeed is the Way of Zhongni! Successive generations cannot exhaust his learning, yet with modest humility he said, "What do I know?" He inquired of Lao Dan 老聃, studied under Music Master Xiang (Shi Xiang 師襄), and consulted Chang Hong 萇弘 and the Viscount of Tan (Tanzi 郯子); indeed, in his eager pursuit he forgot to eat and was unaware of the onset of old age. He visited the various feudal states in response to invitations and practiced his Way in Lu 魯, departing when he found no agreement; the office of Minister of Justice (sikou 司寇) could not keep him, nor could the fief of Linqiu 廩丘 retain him with its emolument. Threatened at Kuang 匡, driven out of Wei 衛, reduced to extremity between Chen 陳 and Cai 蔡, and thwarted by Yan Ying 晏嬰 and Zixi 子西, he never ceased singing to his stringed instrument and never showed a look of resentment. Thus, in speaking to You 由 [Zilu 子路] and Ci 賜 [Zigong 子貢], he said: "The humane person is not necesariamente trusted; the wise person's counsel is not necessarily put into practice. A good farmer can sow, yet cannot guarantee the harvest; a gentleman cultivates his Way, yet cannot guarantee acceptance." And on another day he said: "I do not complain against Heaven, nor do I blame men. I study what is below and penetrate what is above. Is it not Heaven that knows me!" Not seeking acceptance from men, but seeking to be known by Heaven—is this not the ultimate perfection of learning for oneself? Therefore, when Yan Yuan 顏淵, living on a bamboo dish of rice, loved learning and appeared as if foolish, Confucius カ lauded his worthiness; when Ziruo 子若 [Qidiao Kai 漆雕開] was hesitant to take office, Confucius was pleased with him; and when he heard Zeng Xi's 曾晳 words about bathing in the Yi 沂 River and enjoying the breeze at the rain altars, he sighed deeply and approved of him. Yet when Yuan Si 原思 declined his grain allowance as a steward, he was not called incorruptible; when Zigong 子貢 ransomed captives without accepting reimbursement from the state, he was not called righteous; and when Zilu 子路 fed the laborers digging the Long Ditch (Changgou 長溝), he was not called humane. Now, these three were admirable deeds, yet the Sage did not approve of them because he disliked insincerity and did not value…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
皎皎以爲名沾沾以爲德也沾沾者不廣皎皎
者易已惟誠也不見而章鶴鳴于九皐聲聞于
天陽氣暢於泱漭而萌乎淵泉有聲之聲不過
百里無聲之聲充乎四海故君子兢兢脩之冥
冥而德立名附焉德誠脩而名不著君子弗以
爲患矣是夫子爲已之說也若曰古之學者爲
已可以及人今之學者爲人必且喪已爲已者
兩得之者也爲人者兩失之者也隱約而具曲
而中包含而有深思矯世之言也昔者曾子嘗
===
聞夫子速貧速朽之說以告有若有若曰夫子
有爲言之也其語樊遲曰舉直錯諸枉能使枉
者直而子夏曰富哉言乎二子蓋有味乎夫子
之指也吾於夫子爲已爲人之說亦云
表
擬虜酋俺荅率西夷烏思藏鎖南堅叅等
求
貢方物羣臣
賀表〔萬曆七年〕
punctuated:
皎皎以爲名，沾沾以爲德也。沾沾者不廣，皎皎者易已。惟誠也，不見而章。鶴鳴于九皐，聲聞于天。陽氣暢於泱漭，而萌乎淵泉。有聲之聲，不過百里；無聲之聲，充乎四海。故君子兢兢脩之冥冥，而德立名附焉。德誠脩而名不著，君子弗以爲患矣。是夫子爲已之說也。若曰：古之學者爲已，可以及人；今之學者爲人，必且喪已。爲已者，兩得之者也；爲人者，兩失之者也。隱約而具，曲而中，包含而有深思，矯世之言也。昔者曾子嘗聞夫子速貧速朽之說，以告有若。有若曰：「夫子有爲言之也。」其語樊遲曰：「舉直錯諸枉，能使枉者直。」而子夏曰：「富哉言乎！」二子蓋有味乎夫子之指也。吾於夫子爲已爲人之說亦云。

表

擬虜酋俺荅率西夷烏思藏鎖南堅叅等求貢方物羣臣賀表〔萬曆七年〕
translation_en:
… ostentatiously immaculate conduct for the sake of reputation, or petty self-satisfaction as virtue. What is petty is not broad; what is ostentatiously immaculate is easily sullied [?]. Only when there is sincerity does one become manifest without showing off. "The crane cries in the nine marshes, and its voice is heard in the heavens." Yang vital energy expands across the boundless expanse, yet it sprouts from deep springs. A sound that has audible voice reaches no farther than a hundred li; a sound without audible voice fills all within the Four Seas. Therefore, the gentleman cautiously cultivates himself in the unseen, wherefore his virtue is established and reputation attaches to it. If his virtue is truly cultivated and yet his name does not become prominent, the gentleman does not consider it cause for worry. This is the Master's doctrine of learning for oneself.

It is as if to say: the learners of antiquity learned for themselves, and thereby could extend it to others; learners today learn for the sake of others, and will inevitably lose themselves in the process. Those who learn for themselves attain both; those who learn for the sake of others lose both. Concise yet complete, indirect yet hitting the mark, all-encompassing and imbued with deep thought—these are words meant to rectify the age. In the past, Zengzi 曾子 once heard the Master's remarks on "wishing for speedy poverty and speedy decay" and told You Ruo 有若 about them. You Ruo said, "The Master had a particular reason for saying that." When the Master told Fan Chi 樊遲, "Raise up the straight and set them over the crooked, and you can make the crooked straight," Zixia 子夏 said, "How rich is this saying!" Those two worthies truly savored the Master's underlying intent. Of the Master's saying on learning for oneself and learning for others, I say the same.

Memorial

Simulated Congratulatory Memorial from the Officials on the Northern Caitiff Chieftain Altan 俺荅 Leading the Western Barbarians of Ü-Tsang 烏思藏, Sonam Gyatso 鎖南堅叅 and Others, to Request to Present Local Tribute [Seventh Year of the Wanli 萬曆 Reign (1579)]

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導魯批述今昔虜戎事歴歴如抵
掌詞亦莊整可錄
同考試官教諭周批美不忘規慮遠矣此子抱
忠悃者取之不獨詞也
考試官學正陳批屬對典則
考試官學正王批調雅詞嚴
萬曆七年某月某日虜酋俺荅率西夷烏
思藏鎖南堅粲等求
===
貢方物伏蒙
聖慈嘉其款誠
賜賚有差臣等謹奉
表稱
賀者伏以
帝德光敷北裔稱藩於朔漠
王猷允塞西羌奉篚於崑崙聯四極之歸心創
萬年之
盛事慶傳彌宇頌協羣衷臣等誠懽誠忭稽首
punctuated:
同考試官訓導魯批：述今昔虜戎事，歴歴如抵掌，詞亦莊整，可錄。
同考試官教諭周批：美不忘規，慮遠矣。此子抱忠悃者，取之，不獨詞也。
考試官學正陳批：屬對典則。
考試官學正王批：調雅詞嚴。

萬曆七年某月某日，虜酋俺荅率西夷烏思藏鎖南堅粲等求貢方物，伏蒙聖慈嘉其款誠，賜賚有差。臣等謹奉表稱賀者。

伏以帝德光敷，北裔稱藩於朔漠；王猷允塞，西羌奉篚於崑崙。聯四極之歸心，創萬年之盛事。慶傳彌宇，頌協羣衷。臣等誠懽誠忭，稽首…
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Lu's comment: It recounts past and present affairs concerning the northern and western tribes as clearly as if pointing to the palm of one's hand; the phrasing is also stately and well-ordered, worthy of recording.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhou's comment: In praising, he does not forget admonition; his foresight is far-reaching indeed. This candidate is one who harbors loyal sincerity—we select him not merely for his literary phrasing.
Examiner and Director of Studies Chen's comment: The parallel couplets are classical and regular.
Examiner and Director of Studies Wang's comment: The tone is elegant and the diction rigorous.

On a certain day of a certain month in the seventh year of the Wanli era [1579], the northern chieftain Altan Khan (Anda 俺荅), leading the Western Tibetan (Ü-Tsang 烏思藏) leader Sonam Gyatso (Suonan Jiancan 鎖南堅粲) and others, requested to present local tribute. Humbly receiving Your Sacred Benevolence, which praised their sincere allegiance, imperial gifts were bestowed upon them according to their rank. Your servants respectfully present this memorial to offer congratulations:

We humbly consider that as Imperial Virtue shines forth and spreads wide, the northern frontier declares itself a vassal in the desert wastes; as Kingly Counsel is truly fulfilled, the Western Qiang offer tribute baskets from the Kunlun Mountains. Uniting the allegiance of the four extremes, this inaugurates a glorious event for ten thousand years. Joy spreads throughout the universe, and songs of praise harmonize in the hearts of all. Your servants, with utmost joy and elation, bow our heads to the ground…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
首頓首竊惟
王者天地爲容并函華貊
聖人日月所照莫不
尊親但上世或有弗懷書言猾夏然至仁待以
不殺詩咏來威桀尔匈奴陸梁胡苑蠢玆
羌屬肘腋華陽即五帝不得臣雖三王莫
能制秦號虎狼之國辟舍西河漢馳肩臂
之戲漏師馬邑嫖姚窮追姑衍僅取和親
天姬結好烏孫慙當嫚辱納呼韓於神爵
===
計熟羈縻置都護於偏垂兵殘勞費政衰
末葉雲擾腥羶世泰
明朝天開
清穆百年胡運猶遺種於祁連五蘊鉢師尚拂
廬於哈剌犁庭空幕秪聞策勝禦戎謝域
閉關未見功成奉
朔欣逢
今日特邁前猷玆蓋伏遇
皇帝陛下
punctuated: 首頓首。竊惟王者天地爲容，并函華貊；聖人日月所照，莫不尊親。但上世或有弗懷，《書》言「猾夏」；然至仁待以不殺，《詩》咏「來威」。桀尔匈奴，陸梁胡苑；蠢玆羌屬，肘腋華陽。即五帝不得臣，雖三王莫能制。秦號虎狼之國，辟舍西河；漢馳肩臂之戲，漏師馬邑。嫖姚窮追姑衍，僅取和親；天姬結好烏孫，慙當嫚辱。納呼韓於神爵，計熟羈縻；置都護於偏垂，兵殘勞費。政衰末葉，雲擾腥羶；世泰明朝，天開清穆。百年胡運，猶遺種於祁連；五蘊鉢師，尚拂廬於哈剌。犁庭空幕，秪聞策勝禦戎；謝域閉關，未見功成奉朔。欣逢今日，特邁前猷。玆蓋伏遇皇帝陛下…
translation_en: …bow our heads to the ground, and again bow our heads to the ground. We humbly reflect that the True King takes Heaven and Earth as his capacity, encompassing both the Chinese and the Mo tribes; wherever the sun and moon of the Sage shine, there is none who does not honor and love him. Yet in high antiquity there were sometimes those who did not submit in heart, so the Book of Documents speaks of "disturbing the Xia"; nevertheless, supreme benevolence treated them by refraining from slaughter, and the Book of Odes sings of "coming in awe." Unruly were the Xiongnu, running rampant in the northern pastures; foolish were these Qiang tribes, pressing right against the flank of Huayang. Even the Five Emperors could not make them subjects; even the Three Kings could not bring them under control. Qin, called a state of tigers and wolves, retreated so far as to yield Xihe; Han, galloping about in martial sport like a flexed arm, leaked its military plans at Mayi. The Piaoyao General pursued them to the bitter end at Mount Guyan, yet it resulted only in marriage alliances; imperial princesses cemented friendship with Wusun, yet shamefully suffered insult and humiliation. Receiving Huhanye during the Shenjue era was a well-considered plan for loose-rein control; establishing the Protector-General on the remote frontier left the troops decimated and exhausted by expense. When governance declined in later ages, foul-smelling hordes threw the realm into turmoil like gathering clouds; when peace came to the Ming Dynasty, Heaven inaugurated a pure and harmonious rule. Yet after the century-long fortune of the Yuan Mongols ended, their remnant stock still lingered in the Qilian Mountains; and the monks of the Five Aggregates with their alms-bowls still pitched their tents in Qara-khoja [?]. Of plowing up their courts and emptying their desert tents, we have heard only of victorious strategies for defending against the western barbarians; of renouncing the Western Regions and closing the passes, we had never seen the accomplished achievement of their accepting our calendar. Joyfully encountering the present day, it uniquely surpasses all former plans. This is because we humbly meet with Your Majesty the Emperor…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
文武天成
英明神授
堯章煥
五位輯瑞萬方
舜孝隆
兩宮蕃釐百順
重公孤於鹽梅舟楫
化理登閎簡爪牙於炎朔金湯
聲靈布濩梯航日出爭睹漢官威儀冠帶月
===
支徧灑
天階雨露一家胡越無憂飲馬長城九塞管絃
共賀銷兵莫府惟茲俺答裔出匈奴素逞
天驕寔先風靡北面
緹帷馳道爵加順義之王西遊星海析支禮
建仰華之寺葵依
丹闕已易狼子野心膜拜青蓮切尚沙門慈
敎豈直身爲臣僕因之要領氐羌祇率堅
昆求通
punctuated: 文武天成，英明神授。堯章煥五位，輯瑞萬方；舜孝隆兩宮，蕃釐百順。重公孤於鹽梅舟楫，化理登閎；簡爪牙於炎朔金湯，聲靈布濩。梯航日出，爭睹漢官威儀；冠帶月支，徧灑天階雨露。一家胡越，無憂飲馬長城；九塞管絃，共賀銷兵莫府。惟茲俺答，裔出匈奴，素逞天驕，寔先風靡。北面緹帷馳道，爵加順義之王；西遊星海析支，禮建仰華之寺。葵依丹闕，已易狼子野心；膜拜青蓮，切尚沙門慈敎。豈直身爲臣僕，因之要領氐羌，祇率堅昆，求通
translation_en: …whose civil and martial virtues are naturally endowed, and whose heroic brilliance is divinely bestowed. With Yao-like resplendence shining upon the imperial throne, You gather the jade tokens of allegiance from the myriad regions; with Shun-like filiality exalting the Two Palaces, You multiply blessings in a hundredfold harmony. You esteem the Three Dukes and Three Solitaries as the salt and plum and the boat and oars of governance, elevating transformative rule to vast heights; You select fierce warriors as talons and fangs along the scorching south and freezing north, those ramparts of metal and boiling water, spreading Your renown and numinous might far and wide. Scaling mountains and sailing seas from where the sun rises, foreign peoples vie to behold the majestic deportment of Han officials; bestowing caps and sashes upon the Yuezhi, the rain and dew of the Imperial steps are sprinkled everywhere. Making one family of the northern Hu and southern Yue, there is no longer the worry of watering warhorses at the Great Wall; amidst pipes and strings along the Nine Frontiers, all rejoice together at the melting down of weapons in the frontier commands. Now this Anda [Altan Khan], a descendant of the Xiongnu who had long indulged his arrogance as a 'Proud Son of Heaven,' was truly the first to be swept along by Your moral wind. Facing north toward the crimson curtains and the imperial highway, he was granted the title of Shunyi Wang [Prince of Obedient Righteousness]; journeying west to the Starry Sea and Xizhi, he reverently built the Yanghua Temple [Temple of Looking Up to China]. Like a sunflower leaning toward the Vermilion Towers, he has already changed his wolf-cub's wild heart; prostrating himself before the Blue Lotus, he earnestly reveres the compassionate teachings of the śramaṇas [Buddhist monks]. Not only has he personally become a subject and servant, but through this he also holds the Di and Qiang peoples by the collar and reverently leads the Jiankun [Kyrgyz] in seeking to open relations and…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
朝貢物陳壤奠羣空大宛之昆蹏表乞原封
筐篚吐蕃之毳罽横草日閒虎落洗戈夜
挽天河入
覲以春秋輸享遵往來鴈候開屯休戍巳折衝
停上下魚書雖
盛世不忘兵但蹔息雲中之騎在
治朝豈愛佛惟遠懷徼外之人爰
錫絲言旌其懇款載
頒綺幣授以禪師偏譯拱辰環爻閤而繫組穹
===
居歸日睹陰羽而搖鼉盛矣
一統
皇輿大哉八埏
王會乾坤開闢而後未有玆勛
符命授繼以來獨當
鉅美是宜宣之
郊廟光昭
宗子之成功用以勒諸鼎彝永著
大君之有道上駕
punctuated: 朝貢。物陳壤奠，羣空大宛之昆蹏；表乞原封，筐篚吐蕃之毳罽。横草日閒虎落，洗戈夜挽天河。入覲以春秋，輸享遵往來鴈候；開屯休戍巳，折衝停上下魚書。雖盛世不忘兵，但蹔息雲中之騎；在治朝豈愛佛，惟遠懷徼外之人。爰錫絲言，旌其懇款；載頒綺幣，授以禪師。偏譯拱辰，環爻閤而繫組；穹居歸日，睹陰羽而搖鼉。盛矣！一統皇輿；大哉！八埏王會。乾坤開闢而後，未有玆勛；符命授繼以來，獨當鉅美。是宜宣之郊廟，光昭宗子之成功；用以勒諸鼎彝，永著大君之有道。上駕
translation_en: …tribute at court. As local offerings are arrayed, the herds of Dayuan are emptied of their finest steeds; as memorials beg for the confirmation of original investitures, baskets are filled with the felt and woolens of Tubo. Soldiers who once campaigned across the wild grasses now pass idle days by the bamboo palisades, while at night the Milky Way is drawn down to wash away the weapons of war. Coming for audience in spring and autumn, they present their offerings in keeping with the seasonal migration of wild geese; opening military farms to give rest to the Wuji Commandery garrisons, the border defenses halt the dispatch of urgent fish-tallies up and down the line. Although a flourishing age does not forget warfare, for the moment the cavalry in Yunzhong may rest; how could a well-governed court be fond of the Buddha, save that it cherishes from afar the peoples beyond the frontier? Thereupon silken words of imperial decree were bestowed to commend his earnest sincerity, and figured silks and gifts were granted along with the title of Chan Master. Through multiple interpreters they turn toward the Polar Star, encircling the decorated gates [?] to bind on the cords of allegiance; from theirdomed tents they turn toward the sun, gazing upon the crane-feather standards and beating their alligator-skin drums. How flourishing is the unified imperial domain! How grand is the Royal Assembly of the eight extremities of the world! Since heaven and earth were first separated, there has never been such merit; since the Mandate and its tallies were first bestowed and succeeded to, this reign alone claims such supreme beauty. It is fitting that this be proclaimed at the suburban altars and ancestral temple, to gloriously manifest the accomplished merit of the Imperial Scion; and by engraving it upon the tripods and sacrificial vessels, to forever make known the righteous Way of the Great Sovereign, surpassing…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
貢獒之治榮稱
獻雉之
朝臣等志固切於請纓籌實疎於借箸覯兩
階之干羽莫賛一詞同四海之謳歌惟勤
三祝伏願
柔遠能邇
居安思危
鳳沼集夔龍益密內修之計
雲臺收頗牧愈詳外攘之猷
===
御以和御以威固升平於
天保
莫不王莫不享宜豐大於
日中臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖欣躍屏營之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
punctuated: 貢獒之治，榮稱獻雉之朝。臣等志固切於請纓，籌實疎於借箸。覯兩階之干羽，莫賛一詞；同四海之謳歌，惟勤三祝。伏願柔遠能邇，居安思危。鳳沼集夔龍，益密內修之計；雲臺收頗牧，愈詳外攘之猷。御以和，御以威，固升平於天保；莫不王，莫不享，宜豐大於日中。臣等無任瞻天仰聖，欣躍屏營之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。
translation_en: …surpassing the rule when the Ao hound was presented as tribute, and gloriously rivaling the court to which the white pheasant was offered. Although the aspirations of Your servants are earnestly set on requesting the long cord to bind the foe, our strategic planning is truly too inept to borrow the chopsticks at Your banquet to devise schemes. Beholding the shields and feathers danced between the two staircases, we cannot add a single word of counsel; joining in the songs of praise across the Four Seas, we can only diligently offer the Three Blessings. We humbly pray that You will be gracious to the distant and supportive of the near, and remain mindful of danger while dwelling in peace. May the Phoenix Pool gather ministers like Kui and Long, further refining the plans for internal governance; may the Cloud Terrace recruit generals like Lian Po and Li Mu, making ever more thorough the strategies for repelling external threats. Governing with harmony and governing with majesty, may You consolidate great peace as celebrated in the ode "Heaven Protects" (Tianbao); when none fail to acknowledge Your kingship and none fail to present offerings, may You fittingly maintain abundance and greatness like the sun at midday (as in the hexagram Feng). Your servants, overcome to the utmost with awe and joyful trepidation as we gaze up at Heaven and look upon Your Sagely Majesty, respectfully present this memorial of congratulation for Your Majesty's hearing.

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第叁塲
策
第一問
同考試官訓導胡批據禮議更
廟制此
朝廷誕章足垂
憲萬世者即掌故案牒莫揣其指此作敷陳且悉本末奇瑋哉
同考試官訓導梁批儒者守章句闇于
===
國制何謂通今子纚纚條析之邃學玄覽士也
考試官學正陳批考據精覈非以臆決筴者
考試官學正王批立議準禮語無空設
聖王之制禮也時爲大順次之宜於時者
不必襲古之故而鑿於今者則當協禮之
經時者與世推移之法也順者一定不易
之分也夫古今異宜損益異制辟若四時
還相爲令誰能執之使一哉而律數味臭
要各有定不可得而移也議禮者亦由是
punctuated:
第叁塲
策
第一問
同考試官訓導胡批：據禮議更廟制，此朝廷誕章，足垂憲萬世者，即掌故案牒莫揣其指。此作敷陳，且悉本末，奇瑋哉！
同考試官訓導梁批：儒者守章句，闇于國制，何謂通今？子纚纚條析之，邃學玄覽士也。
考試官學正陳批：考據精覈，非以臆決筴者。
考試官學正王批：立議準禮，語無空設。

聖王之制禮也，時爲大，順次之。宜於時者，不必襲古之故；而鑿於今者，則當協禮之經。時者，與世推移之法也；順者，一定不易之分也。夫古今異宜，損益異制，辟若四時還相爲令，誰能執之使一哉？而律數味臭，要各有定，不可得而移也。議禮者亦由是
translation_en:
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Hu comments: Deliberating on the reform of the ancestral temple system on the basis of ritual principles is a grand statute of the imperial court, sufficient to hand down as a model for ten thousand generations; even experts in institutional precedents examining the archives can scarcely fathom its import. This essay sets it forth and furthermore thoroughly recounts it from beginning to end—how extraordinary and magnificent!
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Liang comments: Scholars cling to chapter and phrase while remaining ignorant of dynastic institutions—how can that be called understanding the present? You analyze it systematically and at length; you are a gentleman of profound learning and far-reaching vision.
Examiner and Director of Studies Chen comments: The evidential research is precise and thorough; this is not someone who answers policy questions by mere conjecture.
Examiner and Director of Studies Wang comments: The arguments are established in accordance with ritual, and the words are not set forth in vain.

When the sage kings instituted rituals, timeliness was the greatest principle, and accordance with right order came next. What is suited to the times need not repeat the precedents of antiquity; yet what is forced in the present ought to harmonize with the constant norms of ritual. Timeliness is the method of shifting along with the age; accordance with right order is the fixed and unchanging allotment. Now, antiquity and the present differ in what is appropriate, and additions and reductions result in different systems—just as the four seasons succeed one another as the governing order, who could hold fast to them and make them uniform? Yet pitch-pipes, numbers, flavors, and odors in essence each have their fixed nature and cannot be altered. Those who deliberate on ritual also proceed from this…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
矣是故有以疏爲貴者有以數爲貴者總
之奉神明之統美報答之情順仁孝之思
爲後世法程其義一也位次有列也版祝
有數也稱名有物也一不得其理卽陳信
愧而怨恫生矣物大之謂何蓋孔子入太
廟每事問執事以問諸生豈徒有所不知
審之也顧諸生者目不瞻宗廟之美足不
習駿奔之節其何藉以對雖然試頌言之
自古帝王之興曷不本始神聖肇廟祀以
===
仁祖考哉虞夏而往無述已見於王制曰
天子七廟三昭三穆與太祖之廟而七蓋
準乎商道矣有時享以祀在廟之主而舉
於四時有大祫以合已祧之主而行於歲
暮坐次曰位致詞曰祝揭主曰稱侑食曰
配雖不皆經見而禮宜具之未聞其有九
也九廟之制始自唐之玄宗至宋祔獻懿
以厭太祖而後世因沿遂不可變君子訾
之曰非古也夫禮有以多爲貴者王者德
punctuated: 矣。是故有以疏爲貴者，有以數爲貴者，總之奉神明之統、美報答之情、順仁孝之思，爲後世法程，其義一也。位次有列也，版祝有數也，稱名有物也，一不得其理，卽陳信愧而怨恫生矣，物大之謂何？蓋孔子入太廟，每事問；執事以問諸生，豈徒有所不知審之也？顧諸生者，目不瞻宗廟之美，足不習駿奔之節，其何藉以對？雖然，試頌言之。自古帝王之興，曷不本始神聖，肇廟祀以仁祖考哉？虞夏而往無述已。見於《王制》曰：「天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七。」蓋準乎商道矣。有時享以祀在廟之主，而舉於四時；有大祫以合已祧之主，而行於歲暮。坐次曰位，致詞曰祝，揭主曰稱，侑食曰配。雖不皆經見，而禮宜具之，未聞其有九也。九廟之制，始自唐之玄宗；至宋祔獻、懿以厭太祖，而後世因沿，遂不可變。君子訾之曰：「非古也。」夫禮有以多爲貴者，王者德…
translation_en:
…Indeed, for this reason, there are cases where infrequency is valued, and cases where frequency is valued. In sum, whether upholding the continuity of the spirits, perfecting the sentiment of reciprocation, or following the thoughts of benevolence and filial piety to establish a standard for later generations, the underlying principle is one and the same. The seating order has its ranks, the prayer boards have their set rules, and the titles and designations have their substance. If even one thing fails to accord with principle, then in presenting offerings of good faith one feels shame, and resentment and grief arise—what then would be the meaning of the "greatness of the ceremonial articles"? When Confucius entered the Grand Temple, he asked about everything. When the examiners now ask the candidates about these matters, is it merely to investigate something they do not know? Yet as a humble student whose eyes have never beheld the beauty of the ancestral temple and whose feet have never practiced the steps of swift attendance at sacrifices, on what basis can I reply? Even so, allow me to try to speak of it openly.

From antiquity, whenever emperors and kings arose, how could they not trace their origins back to divine sages and found temple sacrifices to show benevolence to their ancestors and deceased fathers? From the Yu and Xia dynasties and earlier, nothing is recorded. What appears in the "Royal Regulations" (Wang zhi) states: "The Son of Heaven has seven ancestral temples: three on the left (zhao) and three on the right (mu), which together with the temple of the Grand Progenitor make seven." This was modeled on the way of the Shang dynasty. There were seasonal offerings (shixiang) to sacrifice to the spirit tablets remaining in the temples, performed in the four seasons; and there was the great collective sacrifice (daxia) to unite the spirit tablets that had already been removed to the distant shrines (tiao), performed at the end of the year. The seating order was called "position" (wei), the delivery of the prayer text was called "invocation" (zhu), displaying the spirit tablet was called "designation" (cheng), and accompanying the meal at sacrifice was called "matching" (pei). Although these do not all appear in the Classics, ritual propriety requires that they be provided; yet one has never heard of there being nine temples.

The institution of nine ancestral temples began with Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang; by the Song dynasty, the tablets of Ancestors Xian and Yi were enshrined alongside to take precedence over the Grand Progenitor, and later generations followed this practice until it could no longer be changed. Gentlemen criticized this, saying: "It is not the way of antiquity." Now, in ritual there are cases where abundance is valued; when a true king's virtue…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
厚流光自仁率祖卽增七爲九何侈哉我
太祖高皇帝受命稽古首建
廟闕左以享
德
熙
懿
仁四親而
壽春諸王咸以次而侑享焉
文皇帝繼統上承
===
先德建廟北平以享
列祖
太祖四親而壽春諸王以次在侑於時廟數猶
未定也至
憲宗純皇帝以世代旣足始備
九廟之制四
列祖一
太祖一
成祖並
punctuated: 厚流光，自仁率祖，卽增七爲九，何侈哉！我太祖高皇帝受命稽古，首建廟闕左，以享德、熙、懿、仁四親，而壽春諸王咸以次而侑享焉。文皇帝繼統，上承先德，建廟北平，以享列祖、太祖四親，而壽春諸王以次在侑。於時廟數猶未定也。至憲宗純皇帝，以世代旣足，始備九廟之制，四列祖、一太祖、一成祖，並
translation_en: … has abundant virtue and far-reaching glory; proceeding from benevolence to trace back to his ancestors, even if seven are increased to nine, how could that be extravagant? When our Grand Progenitor Emperor Gao (Taizu, the Hongwu Emperor) received the Mandate and examined antiquity, he first built the Ancestral Temple to the left of the palace gates to sacrifice to the four ancestral generations—Dezu, Xizu, Yizu, and Renzu—while the Prince of Shouchun and the other princes all shared in the sacrifices in sequence as associates. When Emperor Wen (the Yongle Emperor) succeeded to the line of rule, continuing the virtue of his predecessors above, he built a temple in Beiping to sacrifice to the successive ancestors—Taizu and the four ancestral generations—while the Prince of Shouchun and the other princes were associated in the sacrifices in sequence. At that time, the number of ancestral shrines was not yet fixed. By the time of Emperor Chun, Xianzong (the Chenghua Emperor), because the number of generations was now sufficient, the system of nine shrines was first completed: four for the early ancestors, one for Taizu, one for Chengzu, together with…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
仁
宣
英三宗爲九而規制於是大定矣於時升祧之
禮猶未講也至
世宗肅皇帝以世數旣盈復更
九廟之制一
太祖一
成祖六
仁
===
宣
英
憲
孝
武並
獻帝升祔爲九而典禮於是乎益詳矣春月特
享則分祭於各室三時合享則共食於
前殿而已祧之廟不與焉時享之禮則以
太祖爲尊歲暮之祫則升
punctuated: 仁、宣、英三宗爲九，而規制於是大定矣。於時升祧之禮猶未講也。至世宗肅皇帝，以世數旣盈，復更九廟之制：一太祖，一成祖，六仁、宣、英、憲、孝、武，並獻帝升祔爲九，而典禮於是乎益詳矣。春月特享，則分祭於各室；三時合享，則共食於前殿，而已祧之廟不與焉。時享之禮，則以太祖爲尊；歲暮之祫，則升
translation_en: …the three ancestral emperors Renzong, Xuanzong, and Yingzong, making nine in all; and thus the institutional regulations were broadly settled. At that time, however, the rite of elevating and removing spirit tablets to the distant-ancestors shrine had still not been deliberated upon. When it came to Emperor Shizong Su, because the number of generations had reached its limit, he revised the system of the Nine Imperial Ancestral Temples once again: one for Taizu, one for Chengzu, six for Renzong, Xuanzong, Yingzong, Xianzong, Xiaozong, and Wuzong, together with Emperor Xian elevated and enshrined to make nine; and thus the ritual canons became ever more detailed. For the individual sacrifice in the spring month, offerings are presented separately in each chamber; for the joint sacrifices in the other three seasons, they partake together in the Front Hall, though the temples of those already removed to the distant shrine do not participate. In the rite of the seasonal sacrifices, Taizu is held as the most honored; in the great collective sacrifice at the close of the year, they elevate…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
四祖於上而祧廟之主咸出而共享焉當
憲廟時
四祖並列殆體
太祖之心乎而
九廟未足禮固不得而有祧也至
世廟之時
四祖並祧固尊
太祖之位乎而世數已足勢不容於無祧矣其
或祧或升之次合享分享之儀孰非酌之
===
今而諧揆之古而不悖者乎歷世滋久訛
舛相承鑿於名實莫可致詰矣以今日言
之弘治中時享祝文稱
八廟
太皇太后
皇考憲宗皇帝蓋親禰也而
九廟之數若減其一至嘉靖中
孝宗而上本七廟也而稱六及
仁宗奉祧猶六廟也而稱五偹損偹益何廟數
punctuated:
四祖於上，而祧廟之主咸出而共享焉。當憲廟時，四祖並列，殆體太祖之心乎？而九廟未足，禮固不得而有祧也。至世廟之時，四祖並祧，固尊太祖之位乎？而世數已足，勢不容於無祧矣。其或祧或升之次，合享、分享之儀，孰非酌之今而諧，揆之古而不悖者乎？

歷世滋久，訛舛相承，鑿於名實，莫可致詰矣。以今日言之，弘治中時享祝文稱「八廟」、「太皇太后」、「皇考憲宗皇帝」，蓋親禰也，而九廟之數若減其一。至嘉靖中，孝宗而上本七廟也，而稱六；及仁宗奉祧，猶六廟也，而稱五。偹損偹益，何廟數
translation_en:
… the Four Ancestors (Sizu 四祖) above, and the spirit tablets from the shrine of removed ancestors (tiaomiao 祧廟) are all brought out to share in the sacrifice together. During the time of Emperor Xianzong (Xianmiao 憲廟, r. 1465–1487), the Four Ancestors were arrayed together—was this not acting in sympathy with the heart of Taizu (太祖, r. 1368–1398)? Moreover, as the number of the Nine Ancestral Shrines (Jiumiao 九廟) had not yet been filled, ritual propriety indeed did not allow for any removal (tiao 祧). By the time of Emperor Shizong (Shimiao 世廟, r. 1522–1566), the Four Ancestors were all removed to the remote shrine—was this not to exalt the position of Taizu? Moreover, as the number of generations was already complete, circumstances did not permit the absence of removal. As for the order of either removing or elevating the tablets, and the ceremonies of joint sacrifice (hexiang 合享) and separate sacrifice (fenxiang 分享), which of them is not harmonious when adapted to the present, and uncontradictory when measured against antiquity?

As generations passed and time grew ever longer, errors and discrepancies were inherited one after another, and through forced interpretations of names and realities, they could no longer be thoroughly investigated. To speak of it from the standpoint of today: during the Hongzhi reign (1488–1505), the ritual prayer text (zhuwen 祝文) for the seasonal sacrifices referred to the "Eight Shrines," the "Grand Empress Dowager," and the "Imperial Deceased Father Emperor Xianzong." Because the latter was the immediate paternal shrine (qinni 親禰), the count of the Nine Shrines seemed to be reduced by one. Coming to the Jiajing reign (1522–1566), from Emperor Xiaozong (孝宗, r. 1488–1505) upward there were originally seven shrines, yet they were referred to as six; and when Emperor Renzong (仁宗, r. 1425) was reverently removed to the remote shrine, there were still six shrines, yet they were referred to as five. Now diminished, now augmented [偹損偹益, reading 偹 as 乍?]—why is the number of shrines…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之不常耶五廟之中
仁宗並祧惟三廟設祭而祝文猶五是祭省而
祝增矣自
皇高祖憲宗至
皇考穆宗旣備六廟而
太祖
成
英三廟猶仍五廟之稱是廟加而祝減矣何謂
號之無定耶
===
壽春王於
太祖爲叔
霍丘七王爲兄而
寶應七王姪也
英廟時誤稱壽春及霍丘七王爲
皇高伯祖寶應七王爲
皇曾伯祖紊矣今世系益遠而槩稱爲
皇曾伯祖是紊而又紊也何稱名之弗當耶夫
禮順人情辨尊卑定名分明嫌疑使生者
punctuated: 之不常耶？五廟之中，仁宗並祧，惟三廟設祭，而祝文猶五，是祭省而祝增矣。自皇高祖憲宗至皇考穆宗，旣備六廟，而太祖、成、英三廟猶仍五廟之稱，是廟加而祝減矣。何謂號之無定耶？壽春王於太祖爲叔，霍丘七王爲兄，而寶應七王姪也。英廟時，誤稱壽春及霍丘七王爲皇高伯祖，寶應七王爲皇曾伯祖，紊矣；今世系益遠，而槩稱爲皇曾伯祖，是紊而又紊也。何稱名之弗當耶？夫禮，順人情，辨尊卑，定名分，明嫌疑，使生者
translation_en: … be so inconsistent? Among the five temples, after Renzong was also removed to the distant ancestors' shrine, sacrifices were set out in only three temples, yet the prayer texts still spoke of five; thus the sacrifices were reduced while the prayer texts were augmented. From the August High-Great-Grandfather Xianzong down to the deceased Imperial Father Muzong, six temples were already complete, yet together with the three temples of Taizu, Chengzu, and Yingzong they still retained the designation of five temples; thus the temples were increased while the prayer texts were reduced. Why are the designations so unfixed? The Prince of Shouchun was an uncle to Taizu, the Prince of Huoqiu and seven other princes were his elder brothers, and the Prince of Baoying and seven other princes were his nephews. In the time of Yingzong, the Prince of Shouchun as well as the Prince of Huoqiu and the seven princes were erroneously addressed as August High-Great-Granduncles, while the Prince of Baoying and the seven princes were addressed as August Great-Granduncles, which was already a confusion of generational order. Now that the genealogical line has grown even more distant, to uniformly address them all as August Great-Granduncles is to compound confusion upon confusion. Why are the titles of address so inappropriate? Now ritual accords with human feelings, distinguishes superior and inferior, fixes names and statuses, and clarifies doubts and suspicions, causing the living …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
辨於席也行者辨於途也而後理得順人
心得安焉幽明一也夫祭者察鬼神之情
通幽明之交先王用之以禮神而鬼神享
人倫明矣故曰宗廟之禮所以序昭穆也
燕毛所以序齒也烏有處非其位席非其
次稱非其名而足以成禮者乎難以享矣
我
皇上睿哲誠敬通于神明一抉紕繆而釐正之
至篤孝也愚無所識知謹輒以臆决夫
===
太廟者
太祖之廟也我
皇祖開天啓運功德無比
德祖雖尊不得以情掩義謂宜世享南面東侑
成祖其餘升遐則祔親盡則遷位止於九而勿
之過則升祧定而世次明矣諸廟
帝后並揭徽稱及時享而謹核之祭必一其祝
祝必一其廟使神各有麗則繁簡當而位
號秩矣由
punctuated: 辨於席也，行者辨於途也，而後理得順、人心得安焉。幽明一也。夫祭者，察鬼神之情，通幽明之交。先王用之以禮神，而鬼神享，人倫明矣。故曰：「宗廟之禮，所以序昭穆也；燕毛，所以序齒也。」烏有處非其位、席非其次、稱非其名，而足以成禮者乎？難以享矣。我皇上睿哲誠敬，通于神明，一抉紕繆而釐正之，至篤孝也。愚無所識知，謹輒以臆决。夫太廟者，太祖之廟也。我皇祖開天啓運，功德無比；德祖雖尊，不得以情掩義。謂宜世享南面，東侑成祖；其餘升遐則祔，親盡則遷，位止於九而勿之過，則升祧定而世次明矣。諸廟帝后並揭徽稱，及時享而謹核之，祭必一其祝，祝必一其廟，使神各有麗，則繁簡當而位號秩矣。由
translation_en:
… distinguished at their mats, and travelers are distinguished along the road; only then is principle brought into harmony and the human heart set at ease. The unseen and the manifest worlds are one. Now, sacrifice is that which examines the sentiments of ghosts and spirits and connects the intercourse between the unseen and the manifest. The Former Kings used it to treat the spirits with ritual propriety, so that ghosts and spirits accepted the offerings and human moral relations were made clear. Thus it is said: "The rites of the ancestral temple serve to order the zhao and mu generations; the banquet arranged by hair color serves to order age." How could anyone occupy a place that is not his proper position, sit at a mat that is not in his proper sequence, or be addressed by a title that is not his proper name, and yet suffice to accomplish ritual propriety? It would be difficult for the spirits to accept such offerings!

Our Augustin Majesty, wise and reverent, communicates with the divine intelligence; sweeping away the errors at once to rectify them is the utmost of devoted filial piety. Ignorant and without knowledge as I am, I respectfully venture to offer my own conjecture.

Now, the Grand Temple (Taimiao) is the temple of Grand Progenitor (Taizu). Our Imperial Progenitor opened up Heaven and inaugurated the dynastic destiny, his merit and virtue beyond compare; although Progenitor of Virtue (Dezu) is of senior generation, private sentiment must not obscure righteous principle. I would say that Grand Progenitor ought to receive sacrifices for all generations facing south, with Grand Ancestor (Chengzu) as the eastern correlate; as for the rest, when they pass away they should be enshrined, and when kinship ties are exhausted after four generations they should be removed to the repository, keeping the tablets strictly to nine and not exceeding that number. Then the rules of enshrinement and removal will be fixed, and the generational sequence will be clear. In the various temples, the honorific titles of the Emperors and Empresses are displayed together; when the seasonal sacrifices arrive, they should be carefully verified so that each sacrifice has its unified prayer text and each prayer text corresponds to its specific temple, ensuring that each spirit has its proper attachment. Then elaboration and brevity will be appropriate, and the positions and titles will be in order. Tracing from …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
太祖而上下之諸王之分雖百世可知也或者
謂詳定爲難惟各稱本爵而勿概以
皇曾伯祖加焉則稱謂有經而名言順矣世次
明則昭穆定位號秩則孚假易名言順則
觀聽諧釐此三者庶幾哉盡倫乎嘻猶其
疏節爾記曰有其舉之莫敢廢也言率古
也曰耻無其實而有其名言思義也昭穆
之制非古乎曷名其爲昭也居祖之左面
南而明已爾曷名其爲穆也居祖之右面
===
北而穆已爾今也廟分九室室各南向卽
大祫前殿亦南上而旁列本楹也而曰廟本一
也而曰九本同堂異室之制而猶仍昭穆
世次之稱其於義何居焉或者曰祭從先
祖夫有所受之也蓋自
闕左而已然矣夫
聖祖之然也草創之未暇也
成祖之然也考据之未詳也至於
世廟斯不得已而遷就之爾語曰禮失求之野
punctuated: 太祖而上下之，諸王之分，雖百世可知也。或者謂詳定爲難，惟各稱本爵，而勿概以皇曾伯祖加焉，則稱謂有經，而名言順矣。世次明則昭穆定，位號秩則孚假易，名言順則觀聽諧。釐此三者，庶幾哉盡倫乎！嘻，猶其疏節爾。《記》曰：「有其舉之，莫敢廢也。」言率古也。曰：「耻無其實而有其名。」言思義也。昭穆之制，非古乎？曷名其爲昭也？居祖之左，面南而明已爾。曷名其爲穆也？居祖之右，面北而穆已爾。今也廟分九室，室各南向，卽大祫前殿，亦南上而旁列。本楹也，而曰廟；本一也，而曰九；本同堂異室之制，而猶仍昭穆世次之稱，其於義何居焉？或者曰：「祭從先祖，夫有所受之也，蓋自闕左而已然矣。」夫聖祖之然也，草創之未暇也；成祖之然也，考据之未詳也；至於世廟，斯不得已而遷就之爾。語曰：「禮失求之野。」
translation_en:
… the Grand Progenitor (Taizu) and reckon upward and downward from him, the proper status of the various princes can be known even for a hundred generations. Some may say that making such detailed determinations is difficult; yet if each is simply addressed by his own substantive title of nobility without indiscriminately affixing the designation "Imperial Great-Grand-Uncle" to them all, then the appellations will have a regular standard and names and speech will be in accord with reason. When generational order is clear, the luminous (zhao) and solemn (mu) temple ranks are settled; when ritual positions and titles are properly ordered, sincere communion with the spirits is easily achieved; when names and speech are in accord with reason, what is seen and heard is harmonious. By rectifying these three matters, might we not come close to fulfilling the principles of human relationships?

Alas, these are still only the broader outlines! The Record of Rites (Ji) says: "What has once been instituted, none dares abolish." This speaks of following antiquity. It also says: "One should be ashamed to have the name without the reality." This speaks of pondering true meaning. Is not the system of luminous (zhao) and solemn (mu) ranks from antiquity? Why is a rank named "luminous" (zhao)? Only because it occupies the left of the Founding Ancestor, facing south toward the light. Why is a rank named "solemn" (mu)? Only because it occupies the right of the Founding Ancestor, facing north in deep solemnity. Nowadays, however, the temple is divided into nine chambers, with each chamber facing south; even at the Great Combined Sacrifice (daxia) in the front hall, the seats are arranged with the south as superior and the rest arrayed to the sides. What is actually a bay of columns is called a "temple"; what is actually a single building is called "nine"; it is fundamentally the system of "a single hall with separate chambers," yet it still retains the designations of zhao and mu generational order—what meaning does this rest upon?

Some say: "In sacrifices, one follows the ancestors; this is something that has been handed down, for it has been so ever since the temple was built to the left of the palace gates." Yet the Sacred Progenitor's (Taizu's) doing so was because in the founding of the dynasty there was not yet leisure to perfect it; the Accomplished Progenitor's (Chengzu's) doing so was because historical textual examination had not yet been made in detail; and when it came to Emperor Shizong (Shimiao), he merely accommodated it out of necessity. As the saying goes: "When the rites are lost, seek them in the countryside." …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
今素封之家奉其始祖旁列四親犁然序
也安有生爲天子殁居一楹而屢世並列
廑廑然者商周之事豈其泯泯而奈何執
拘攣之說而隳閎廓之規躡沿流之蹤以
絀
神靈之尊乎草茅主臣雖然猶願有一言者革
除之歲削紀錄矣而五載之
正朔何所於頒監國之君歸郕邸矣而八年
之
===
重器誰與爲守今死事諸臣已蒙曠除
景帝位號旋已議復宜下掌故略議享祀所宜
以補
聖朝禮儀之闕夫
敦孝洽仁以光駿惠之烈有
聖天子陳禮致義以崇繼序之功有賢輔相公
卿詩曰永言孝思孝思維則又曰於穆清
廟肅雝顯相此之謂也諸生所謂綿蕞者
而惡足以知之
punctuated: 今素封之家，奉其始祖，旁列四親，犁然序也。安有生爲天子，殁居一楹，而屢世並列、廑廑然者？商、周之事，豈其泯泯？而奈何執拘攣之說，而隳閎廓之規，躡沿流之蹤，以絀神靈之尊乎？草茅主臣，雖然，猶願有一言者：革除之歲，削紀錄矣，而五載之正朔，何所於頒？監國之君，歸郕邸矣，而八年之重器，誰與爲守？今死事諸臣已蒙曠除，景帝位號旋已議復，宜下掌故，略議享祀所宜，以補聖朝禮儀之闕。夫敦孝洽仁，以光駿惠之烈，有聖天子；陳禮致義，以崇繼序之功，有賢輔相公卿。《詩》曰：「永言孝思，孝思維則。」又曰：「於穆清廟，肅雝顯相。」此之謂也。諸生所謂綿蕞者，而惡足以知之！
translation_en:
Nowadays, even wealthy commoner families without official rank enshrine their founding ancestor with the four generations of immediate ancestors arrayed beside him in clear and distinct order. How could it be that one who was the Son of Heaven in life should after death dwell in a single bay, with several generations crowded side by side in such cramped quarters? Are the precedents of the Shang and Zhou dynasties utterly lost to memory? Why, then, cling to narrow and pedantic theories so as to ruin a grand and spacious plan, or follow in the footsteps of inherited convention so as to diminish the dignity of the sacred spirits?

Though this humble scholar from the countryside is struck with awe and trepidation, I would still wish to offer one further word. The years of the annulled Jianwen reign were expunged from the historical records, yet from whom was the official calendar of those five years promulgated? The ruler who served as Regent of the State was returned to the residence of the Prince of Cheng, yet by whom were the sacred vessels of state guarded during those eight years? Now that the various ministers who died for the cause have already received a gracious amnesty, and the imperial title and reign name of Emperor Jing (Jingtai, r. 1450–1457) were subsequently restored after deliberation, the matter should be referred to the ritual authorities to deliberate in outline on what is appropriate for their sacrificial offerings, so as to supply what is lacking in the ceremonial rites of our Sacred Dynasty.

To cultivate filial piety and diffuse benevolence so as to glorify the illustrious legacy of his predecessors—for this there is the Sacred Son of Heaven; to set forth the rites and fulfill righteousness so as to exalt the achievement of continuing the ancestral line—for this there are the worthy chief councilors and high ministers. The Book of Odes (Shijing) says: "Forever he cherishes filial thoughts; his filial thoughts are the model." And again it says: "Oh, solemn is the pure temple; reverent and harmonious are the illustrious assistants." This is what is meant. As for a student like myself, who knows no more than practising ritual with ropes and bundled grass—how could I be worthy of understanding such things!

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第二問
同考試官訓導王批邪說蠭沸衞道者豈競為
辨囿哉不得已也誠有藉于斯文
同考試官訓導徐批漢儒以博學目聖輒傅會
應引大致不經此作敷答得旨
考試官學正陳批闡辯詳核
考試官學正王批議正辭綺
天下有竅言則聖人無眞詮竅言不作則
===
士不惑眞詮不贋則聖人益尊故一藝之
指必有師焉百家之市必有平焉當治敎
綦隆之世學術炳炳如日星然藉令其人
是非一不當則羣詫而異之攻而斥之矣
乃傳沿久遠睹記大盭率詆訾聖人以為
常一唱羣和誰復詫異哉月旦稱朔車軔
亦稱朔五爵六燕飛易其處軒輊豈足馮
耶於乎往牒浩繁不可勝辨矣有如孔子
者自天地以來一人而已何亦稯稯然行
punctuated:
第二問

同考試官、訓導王批：邪說蠭沸，衞道者豈競為辨囿哉？不得已也。誠有藉于斯文。
同考試官、訓導徐批：漢儒以博學目聖，輒傅會應引，大致不經。此作敷答得旨。
考試官、學正陳批：闡辯詳核。
考試官、學正王批：議正辭綺。

天下有竅言，則聖人無眞詮；竅言不作，則士不惑；眞詮不贋，則聖人益尊。故一藝之指，必有師焉；百家之市，必有平焉。當治敎綦隆之世，學術炳炳如日星然。藉令其人是非一不當，則羣詫而異之，攻而斥之矣。乃傳沿久遠，睹記大盭，率詆訾聖人以為常。一唱羣和，誰復詫異哉？月旦稱朔，車軔亦稱朔；五爵六燕，飛易其處，軒輊豈足馮耶？於乎！往牒浩繁，不可勝辨矣。有如孔子者，自天地以來一人而已，何亦稯稯然行
translation_en:
Second Policy Question

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Wang: Heretical doctrines are boiling up like swarms of bees. Why would defenders of the Way compete in the arena of disputation? Only because they have no choice. Truly, this piece lends support to This Culture of Ours (siwen).
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Xu: Han-dynasty scholars viewed the Sage merely through the lens of broad learning, and thus repeatedly made strained associations and responses in their citations, which were largely preposterous. This essay elaborates its reply and grasps the essential purport.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Chen: The exposition and refutation are detailed and well-substantiated.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang: The arguments are orthodox and the diction is exquisite.

When there are specious words in the world, the Sage lacks true explication; when specious words do not arise, scholars are not deluded; and when true explication is not counterfeited, the Sage is all the more revered. Therefore, for the mastery of a single art, there must be a teacher; in a market of a hundred stalls, there must be a standard balance. In an age when governance and moral instruction were at their peak of flourishing, scholarship was as brilliantly luminous as the sun and stars. Even if a person was once mistaken regarding right and wrong, the crowd would be astonished and regard it as strange, attacking and rejecting it. Yet as transmissions continued over a long time, observations and records became gravely perverse, and people routinely took slandering and disparaging the Sage as the norm. When one initiates the cry and the crowd echoes it, who any longer finds it astonishing or strange? The first day of the month is called shuo, and the chock of a carriage wheel is also called shuo [?]; if five sparrows and six swallows fly and trade places, how can their relative weight be relied upon? Alas! Past records are vast and numerous, beyond what can be fully refuted. Consider someone like Confucius: since the beginning of heaven and earth, there has been this one man alone. Why then were his actions also bundled together [?] and…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
詘于鄉里而名毀當世也彼號爲知道則
有莊周列禦寇博物則有左丘明司馬遷
韓嬰劉向傳信則有家語檀弓國語諸書
亡慮數十家矣乃人人詆訾之如一口是
遵何說哉蓋其故有三孔子之在春秋恂
恂如也不務爲可喜可愕之事以爲名高
故當世之人竊姍咲孔子無足稱也是見
杜德幾者也不知孔子者也又有鉛槧佔
畢之倫稍欲文采表著于後世則竊以其
===
言託之乎孔子以取信來世彼其書庨雜
易以蔑實此所謂魯贋讒鼎之見也蓋知
孔子而不恤失其眞者也又有異端者流
見謂孔子之道病已也而心害之則設爲
問答駁論欲以悠繆之言陵駕其上而不
自量其不勝此衛蚳徙澤之見也蓋知孔
子而故抑之者也此三者雖于孔子無加
損然吾不可以無辯夫孔子宋之後也其
先正考父佐戴武宣三命滋益恭因銘諸
punctuated: 詘于鄉里，而名毀當世也？彼號爲知道，則有莊周、列禦寇；博物，則有左丘明、司馬遷、韓嬰、劉向；傳信，則有《家語》、《檀弓》、《國語》諸書，亡慮數十家矣。乃人人詆訾之如一口，是遵何說哉？蓋其故有三：孔子之在春秋，恂恂如也，不務爲可喜可愕之事以爲名高，故當世之人竊姍咲孔子無足稱也。是見杜德幾者也，不知孔子者也。又有鉛槧佔畢之倫，稍欲文采表著于後世，則竊以其言託之乎孔子，以取信來世。彼其書庨雜，易以蔑實，此所謂魯贋讒鼎之見也。蓋知孔子而不恤失其眞者也。又有異端者流，見謂孔子之道病已也，而心害之，則設爲問答駁論，欲以悠繆之言陵駕其上，而不自量其不勝，此衛蚳徙澤之見也。蓋知孔子而故抑之者也。此三者雖于孔子無加損，然吾不可以無辯。夫孔子，宋之後也。其先正考父佐戴、武、宣，三命滋益恭，因銘諸
translation_en:
…stymied in his home village and his reputation slandered in his own age? Among those acclaimed for understanding the Way, there were Zhuang Zhou 莊周 and Lie Yukou 列禦寇; for broad learning, there were Zuo Qiuming 左丘明, Sima Qian 司馬遷, Han Ying 韓嬰, and Liu Xiang 劉向; and for transmitting trustworthy records, there were works such as the Family Sayings of Confucius (Jiayu 家語), "Tangong" 檀弓, and Discourses of the States (Guoyu 國語)—roughly several dozen schools in all. Yet everyone disparaged and criticized him as if with one voice; what explanation were they following? 

In truth, there were three reasons for this. During the Spring and Autumn period, Confucius was modest and unassuming, and did not strive to perform sensational or astonishing deeds to win lofty fame; therefore, people of his day secretly mocked and laughed at Confucius as unworthy of praise. This was the perspective of those who saw only "the mechanism of stopped-up virtue" [as in Zhuangzi], and who did not understand Confucius. Then there were the ranks of ink-and-tablet pedants and rote scholars who, wishing slightly to make their literary flair known to posterity, secretly attributed their own words to Confucius in order to gain credibility with future generations. Because their writings were hollow and motley, they easily obscured the reality; this is the perspective comparable to the state of Lu sending a counterfeit Candling [Chan tripod]. These were people who knew of Confucius, yet did not care if they lost his true character. Finally, there were adherents of heterodox teachings who, seeing that the Way of Confucius was detrimental to themselves and resenting it in their hearts, fabricated dialogues and refutations, wishing to use absurd and specious words to place themselves above him without realizing their own inability to prevail; this is the perspective of the millipede of Wei moving the marsh. These were people who knew Confucius, yet deliberately sought to belittle him.

Although these three groups neither add to nor detract from Confucius, I cannot leave the matter unexamined. Now, Confucius was a descendant of the house of Song. His ancestor Zheng Kaofu 正考父 assisted Dukes Dai 戴, Wu 武, and Xuan 宣; through three successive appointments he grew ever more reverent, and so he inscribed upon…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其鼎孟僖子曰聖人有明德者其後必有
達人今其在孔丘乎蓋孔子聖人之後也
孔子之父曰叔梁紇母曰徵在始叔梁紇
求婚於顏顏問三女皆莫對少女徵在曰
惟父所制之遂以妻叔梁紇叔梁紇與徵
在禱于尼丘而生孔子孔子生而徇齊長
而聖惡有平時一不問父墓者使不遇鄹
曼父之母將終不知耶五父衢之殯甚矣
史遷之誣也至於防墓既已封之崇四尺
===
矣又何至不旋踵以壞耶門人反告不應
者三但以古不修墓爲解甚矣檀弓之無
据也魯有三桓猶人附喉之癭也孔子誠
欲墮其三都即計不萬全肯出哉若不能
策其必勝而費人襲公公果入季氏之宮
登武子之臺靦靦然倉皇避之則謀不已
疎乎左氏蓋以趙鞅召晉陽之兵者目之
也非所以語孔子也夾谷之會齊人目中
無魯矣吾孔子立折其驕麾却萊夷戮其
punctuated: 其鼎。孟僖子曰：「聖人有明德者，其後必有達人，今其在孔丘乎！」蓋孔子，聖人之後也。孔子之父曰叔梁紇，母曰徵在。始，叔梁紇求婚於顏，顏問三女，皆莫對。少女徵在曰：「惟父所制之。」遂以妻叔梁紇。叔梁紇與徵在禱于尼丘而生孔子。孔子生而徇齊，長而聖，惡有平時一不問父墓者？使不遇鄹曼父之母，將終不知耶？五父衢之殯，甚矣史遷之誣也！至於防墓，既已封之崇四尺矣，又何至不旋踵以壞耶？門人反告，不應者三，但以「古不修墓」爲解，甚矣《檀弓》之無据也！魯有三桓，猶人附喉之癭也。孔子誠欲墮其三都，即計不萬全，肯出哉？若不能策其必勝，而費人襲公，公果入季氏之宮，登武子之臺，靦靦然倉皇避之，則謀不已疎乎？左氏蓋以趙鞅召晉陽之兵者目之也，非所以語孔子也。夾谷之會，齊人目中無魯矣。吾孔子立折其驕，麾却萊夷，戮其
translation_en: …his tripod. Meng Xizi 孟僖子 said, "When a sage possesses illustrious virtue, among his descendants there will surely be a man of eminent achievement—today, is that not found in Kong Qiu 孔丘 [Confucius]?" Thus Confucius was the descendant of sages. Confucius's father was named Shuliang He 叔梁紇, and his mother was named Zhengzai 徵在. In the beginning, when Shuliang He sought marriage from the Yan 顏 family, Yan asked his three daughters, and none replied. The youngest daughter, Zhengzai, said, "It is solely as Father decides." Thereupon she was given in marriage to Shuliang He. Shuliang He and Zhengzai prayed at Mount Ni (Niqiu 尼丘) and gave birth to Confucius. Since Confucius was quick and discerning from birth and became a sage upon growing up, how could it be that in ordinary times he never once inquired after his father's grave? Had he not encountered the mother of Манfu of Zou (Zou Manfu 鄹曼父), would he have remained ignorant of it to the end? As for the temporary interment at the Wufu 五父 crossroads, extreme indeed is the fabrication of Historian Qian (Sima Qian 司馬遷)! As for the grave at Fang 防, once it had already been mounded to a height of four feet, how could it have collapsed before he even turned on his heel? And that when his disciples returned to report it, he thrice gave no reply, excusing himself only by saying that "the ancients did not repair graves"—extreme indeed is the groundlessness of the "Tangong" 檀弓 [chapter of the Record of Rites]! Lu 魯 had the Three Huan 三桓 clans, which were like a goiter attached to a person's throat. When Confucius truly wished to demolish their three fortified cities, if his plan had not been completely foolproof, would he have been willing to embark upon it? If he could not calculate a certain victory, so that when the men of Bi 費 attacked the Duke, the Duke indeed entered the palace of the Ji 季氏 clan, ascended the terrace of Wuzi 武子, and bashfully fled from them in a panic—would his planning not have been altogether too careless? Master Zuo (Zuoshi 左氏) was viewing him in the same light as Zhao Yang 趙鞅 summoning the troops of Jinyang 晉陽; this is no way to speak of Confucius. At the meeting at Jiagu 夾谷, the men of Qi 齊 had no regard for Lu in their eyes. Our Confucius immediately broke their arrogance, waved back the Laiyi 萊夷 tribesmen, executed their…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
侏儒歸我汶陽田此豈無不戰而屈人者
乎使僅如史記所載歷階而上堇堇然以
口舌爭是叱咤者曹沫藺相如等耳奚足
聖也蓋其料齊變詐請兩司馬以從備矣
故曰有文事者必有武備聖人乎折衝尊
俎之間豈以倉卒虛喝幸哉適周而見老
聃蓋問禮也莊子乃謂孔子見聃而歸三
日不譚曰吾見老子其猶龍乎丘之於道
其猶醯雞與吾不知天地之大全也是何
===
尊之之過也吾意莊周老聃之流欲藉孔
子以尊聃耳孔子嘗望季以教其弟蹠矣
又安肯往見蹠也而莊子云見蹠泰山之
陽出門上車執轡三失曰疾走幾不免虎
口哉何聖人而愚若是今觀其所為蹠語
此徒莊周欲詆堯舜孔子之道而託之于
蹠者也過泰山逢婦人而問焉嘆曰苛政
猛于虎此孔子之言也韓詩外傳則稱游
于少源見婦人亡蓍簪而泣嘆曰彼不忘
punctuated: 侏儒，歸我汶陽田，此豈無不戰而屈人者乎？使僅如《史記》所載，歷階而上，堇堇然以口舌爭，是叱咤者曹沫、藺相如等耳，奚足聖也？蓋其料齊變詐，請兩司馬以從備矣。故曰：「有文事者，必有武備。」聖人乎！折衝尊俎之間，豈以倉卒虛喝幸哉？適周而見老聃，蓋問禮也。《莊子》乃謂孔子見聃而歸，三日不譚，曰：「吾見老子，其猶龍乎！丘之於道，其猶醯雞與！吾不知天地之大全也。」是何尊之之過也？吾意莊周，老聃之流，欲藉孔子以尊聃耳。孔子嘗望季以教其弟蹠矣，又安肯往見蹠也？而《莊子》云見蹠泰山之陽，出門上車，執轡三失，曰：「疾走！幾不免虎口哉！」何聖人而愚若是？今觀其所為蹠語，此徒莊周欲詆堯、舜、孔子之道，而託之于蹠者也。過泰山，逢婦人而問焉，嘆曰：「苛政猛于虎。」此孔子之言也。《韓詩外傳》則稱游于少源，見婦人亡蓍簪而泣，嘆曰：「彼不忘
translation_en:
…dwarfs, and secured the return of our fields of Wenyang—how could this have occurred without that whereby one subdues others without fighting? Had he merely, as recorded in the Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji), ascended the steps and contended narrowly by means of tongue and lips, then those who shouted in anger would be no different from the likes of Cao Mo and Lin Xiangru—how would that suffice to make him a sage? Indeed, having anticipated Qi's deceit and treachery, he had requested that the two Marshals (Sima) accompany him in readiness. Hence he said: "Whoever has civil business must also have military preparations." O Sage! Subduing the enemy amidst the wine-vessels and meat-stands—how could he have relied on good fortune through hasty, empty bluster?

When he went to Zhou and met Lao Dan, it was to inquire about ritual. Yet the Zhuangzi claims that after Confucius met Dan and returned, for three days he did not speak, and then said: "I have seen Laozi—is he not like a dragon! As for me, Qiu, in relation to the Way, am I not like a vinegar-fly! I would not have known the grand wholeness of Heaven and Earth." How excessive is such veneration of him! In my view, Zhuang Zhou was of Lao Dan's stream and merely wished to borrow Confucius in order to exalt Dan.

Confucius once looked toward Liu Xiahui (Ji) to instruct his younger brother Zhi [Robber Zhi]; how then would he ever have been willing to go and visit Zhi himself? Yet the Zhuangzi says that he visited Zhi on the southern slope of Mount Tai, and that upon going out the gate and mounting his carriage, he dropped the reins three times from his grasp, saying: "Drive fast! I nearly failed to escape the tiger's jaws!" How could a sage be as foolish as this? Now, examining the words he attributes to Zhi, this is merely Zhuang Zhou wishing to slander the Way of Yao, Shun, and Confucius, and placing his words into the mouth of Zhi.

Passing by Mount Tai, he met a woman, had someone inquire of her, and sighed, saying: "Oppressive government is fiercer than a tiger." These are the words of Confucius. Yet the Outer Commentary to the Book of Odes by Master Han (Han Shi waizhuan) claims that while traveling at Shaoyuan, he saw a woman weeping over a lost yarrow-stalk hairpin and sighed, saying: "She does not forget…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其故矣此非孔子之言也禮男女有别以
明嫌也而田野之間輒從婦人語哉史記
載衛南子召見孔子自絺帷中再拜環珮
之聲璆然此誠孔子之事也至韓嬰則稱
孔子游于阿谷見處子珮瑱而浣者抽觴
與琴授子貢而與之語蓋詩多婦人之詞
韓說詩欲託諸婦人而藉孔子爲信顧言
何卑卑也學琴師襄傳紀之矣乃謂乆之
見有人焉黯然而黑頎然而長眼如望羊
===
心期四方襄辟席再拜曰此文王之操也
何其誕也語曰思之惟精其形乃成豈謂
是與登泰山之巔傳載之矣至謂望見吳
閶門外有白馬繫者引顏回問焉回曰見
之若一疋練也又誕之誕者也語曰不視
之見其見萬里殆不然矣六尺之杖以别
親疎之倫其說蓋見諸吕氏春秋及賈誼
新書謂子貢自其家來孔子舉杖磬折而
問其父母已放杖而問其兄弟已乃曳杖
punctuated: 其故矣」，此非孔子之言也。禮，男女有别以明嫌也，而田野之間輒從婦人語哉？《史記》載衛南子召見孔子，自絺帷中再拜，環珮之聲璆然，此誠孔子之事也。至韓嬰則稱孔子游于阿谷，見處子珮瑱而浣者，抽觴與琴授子貢而與之語。蓋《詩》多婦人之詞，韓說《詩》欲託諸婦人而藉孔子爲信，顧言何卑卑也！學琴師襄，傳紀之矣，乃謂乆之見有人焉，黯然而黑，頎然而長，眼如望羊，心期四方，襄辟席再拜曰：「此文王之操也。」何其誕也！語曰：「思之惟精，其形乃成。」豈謂是與？登泰山之巔，傳載之矣，至謂望見吳閶門外有白馬繫者，引顏回問焉，回曰：「見之若一疋練也。」又誕之誕者也！語曰：「不視之見，其見萬里。」殆不然矣。六尺之杖以别親疎之倫，其說蓋見諸《吕氏春秋》及賈誼《新書》，謂子貢自其家來，孔子舉杖磬折而問其父母，已放杖而問其兄弟，已乃曳杖
translation_en: … what is old.” These are not the words of Confucius. According to ritual propriety, men and women are kept distinct in order to make clear the avoidance of suspicion; would he then casually go up and converse with women in the open fields? The Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji) records that when Nanzi of Wei summoned Confucius for an audience, she bowed twice from behind a curtain of fine linen, the sound of her jade pendants tinkling clearly—this is truly an event in the life of Confucius. Yet Han Ying claims that when Confucius was traveling in Agu, he saw a maiden wearing ear-plugs and washing clothes, whereupon he took out a goblet and a zither, handed them to Zigong, and had him speak with her. Now, because the Odes (Shi) contain many words spoken by women, Han in explaining the Odes wished to attribute them to women and borrow Confucius to lend them credence; yet how base and vulgar are such words! That he studied the zither with Master Xiang is recorded in tradition; yet it goes on to say that after a long time he saw a man there, dark of complexion, tall of stature, with eyes gazing afar and a mind set on ruling the four quarters, whereupon Xiang stepped off his mat, bowed twice, and said, “This is the air of King Wen!” How absurd that is! The saying goes, “When one thinks with utmost concentration, the form then takes shape”—could it possibly mean something like this? That he climbed to the summit of Mount Tai is recorded in tradition; yet when it goes so far as to say that looking into the distance he saw a white horse tethered outside the Chang Gate of Wu, and drew Yan Hui forward to ask about it, to which Hui replied, “I see it, like a bolt of white silk”—this is the height of absurdity! The saying goes, “The sight that does not rely on looking can see ten thousand li”—surely it is not like this. As for using a six-foot staff to distinguish the degrees of kinship and distance, this story appears in the Spring and Autumn of Master Lü (Lüshi chunqiu) and Jia Yi’s New Writings (Xinshu), which claim that when Zigong came from his home, Confucius raised his staff and bent like a musical stone to inquire after his parents, then set down the staff to inquire after his brothers, and finally dragged his staff…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而問其妻子吾意聖人教人自有章程而
必爲是狀者毋乃勞而不情乎一飯之桃
以定貴賤之等其說具家語新序中謂魯
公以黍雪桃孔子侍食則先啗黍曰君子
不以貴承賤吾謂聖人誠不可則當謝罷
不食直告之故耳奚待左右之人掩口而
唉而後發其旨也原壤登木而歌大故也
乃爲弗聞也者而過之而曰親者毋失其
爲親故者毋失其爲故信也其友誼之謂
===
何必不然矣陳恒篡齊大變也第聲大義
以討之可矣而曰齊民之不與者半以魯
之衆加齊之半可克也校量於衆寡之間
豈聖人之言耶春秋書災異而不書應乃
魯廟災謂孔子在陳聞之嘆曰其桓僖乎
彼其親盡不毁也而其言卒驗當術數之
學聖人不道也子張問十世可知但以因
革損益推之奚爲書誡其後曰不知何一
男子名秦始皇上我堂恐讖緯之書聖人
punctuated: 而問其妻子。吾意聖人教人自有章程，而必爲是狀者，毋乃勞而不情乎？一飯之桃以定貴賤之等，其說具《家語》、《新序》中，謂魯公以黍雪桃，孔子侍食則先啗黍，曰：「君子不以貴承賤。」吾謂聖人誠不可，則當謝罷不食，直告之故耳，奚待左右之人掩口而唉，而後發其旨也？原壤登木而歌，大故也，乃爲弗聞也者而過之，而曰：「親者毋失其爲親，故者毋失其爲故。」信也，其友誼之謂何？必不然矣。陳恒篡齊，大變也，第聲大義以討之可矣，而曰：「齊民之不與者半，以魯之衆加齊之半，可克也。」校量於衆寡之間，豈聖人之言耶？《春秋》書災異而不書應，乃魯廟災，謂孔子在陳聞之，嘆曰：「其桓、僖乎！」彼其親盡不毁也，而其言卒驗，當術數之學，聖人不道也。子張問十世可知，但以因革損益推之，奚爲書誡其後曰「不知何一男子，名秦始皇，上我堂」？恐讖緯之書，聖人
translation_en:
… and inquired after his wife and children. In my view, the Sage had his own established guidelines for teaching others; to insist on putting on such a display—would that not be tiresome and unnatural?

As for using the peaches at a single meal to determine the hierarchy of noble and base, this story appears in the Family Sayings of Confucius (Kongzi jiayu) and the New Arrangements (Xinxu). It claims that the Duke of Lu used broomcorn millet to wipe the fuzz off peaches, and when Confucius attended him at the meal, he ate the millet first, saying, "A gentleman does not use what is noble to serve what is base." In my view, if the Sage truly considered this improper, he should simply have declined and abstained from eating, stating the reason directly. Why wait until the attendants covered their mouths and laughed before revealing his point?

When Yuan Rang登木 (mounted the coffin wood) and sang [at his mother's death]—a grave transgression—it is said that Confucius passed by pretending not to hear, saying, "With kinsmen, one must not lose the bond of kinship; with old friends, one must not lose the bond of old friendship." If this were true, what would that say of the duty of friendship? It certainly could not have been so.

When Chen Heng usurped the state of Qi, it was a great upheaval. It would have sufficed simply to proclaim great righteousness in order to punish him. Yet Confucius is quoted as saying, "Half the people of Qi do not support him; if we add the forces of Lu to half of Qi, he can be defeated." To calculate and weigh relative numbers in this way—how could these be the words of the Sage?

The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records calamities and anomalies without recording their correspondences. Yet when the ancestral temple of Lu caught fire, it is said that Confucius heard of it while in Chen and sighed, "Was it the temples of Huan and Xi?"—because their kinship degree had expired and yet their shrines had not been demolished—and his words ultimately proved true. This belongs to the art of prognostic calculation, of which the Sage did not speak.

When Zizhang asked whether ten generations hence could be known, Confucius merely inferred it from what is continued, altered, added to, or subtracted from. Why then would he leave a written warning for posterity saying, "I know not what man, named First Emperor of Qin (Qin Shihuang), will ascend my hall"? I fear that prognostic and apocryphal texts (chenwei) are things the Sage…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不爲也萍實徵霸商羊占雨奚皆使人問
于孔子乎猶亡足異也至宋人黑牛生白
犢此何吉祥哉而命以薦上帝則幾乎語
怪矣毋亦東方朔射覆者之流託言之乎
土之怪曰羵羊防風氏之骨專車又奚皆
問于孔子知之乎此猶足信也至謂有隼
集于陳侯之庭貫楛矢石砮其長尺有咫
曰肅慎氏之矢也抑何不經之甚耶或者
多識如張茂先之流爲之也大都尊孔子
===
者欲加以神明多智之稱則爲童謠遺讖
之說而妬孔子者卽又置問發難如小兒
辯日之類欲以詘孔子而謂聖人徒有所
不知是皆竅言也是皆善亂聖人之眞者
也距之則息而揚之復焰核其實則悖而
聽其言則美恐鄭亂雅屏去其書不觀者
實鮮而以雅爲鄭又從而哜嚌之掎角之
者則什家而九也亦奚足怪哉故曰取摶
黍與十金以示小兒則小兒必取摶黍矣取
punctuated: 不爲也。萍實徵霸，商羊占雨，奚皆使人問于孔子乎？猶亡足異也，至宋人黑牛生白犢，此何吉祥哉？而命以薦上帝，則幾乎語怪矣，毋亦東方朔射覆者之流託言之乎？土之怪曰羵羊，防風氏之骨專車，又奚皆問于孔子知之乎？此猶足信也，至謂有隼集于陳侯之庭，貫楛矢石砮，其長尺有咫，曰：「肅慎氏之矢也。」抑何不經之甚耶？或者多識如張茂先之流爲之也。大都尊孔子者，欲加以神明多智之稱，則爲童謠遺讖之說；而妬孔子者，卽又置問發難，如小兒辯日之類，欲以詘孔子，而謂聖人徒有所不知。是皆竅言也，是皆善亂聖人之眞者也。距之則息，而揚之復焰；核其實則悖，而聽其言則美。恐鄭亂雅，屏去其書不觀者實鮮；而以雅爲鄭，又從而哜嚌之、掎角之者，則什家而九也，亦奚足怪哉？故曰：取摶黍與十金以示小兒，則小兒必取摶黍矣；取
translation_en:
… would not produce. As for the ping-fruit portending hegemony and the shangyang bird foretelling rain, why in every case was someone sent to ask Confucius about them? Even if those are not strange enough to wonder at, when it comes to the man of Song whose black cow bore a white calf—what auspicious omen was there in that? Yet he ordered that it be offered to the Lord on High, which comes close to speaking of prodigies! Was this not fabricated and attributed to him by people of the ilk of Dongfang Shuo 東方朔, who played at guessing hidden objects? That the prodigy of the earth is called the fenyang ram, and that a single bone of the Fangfeng 防風 clan filled an entire cart—why again did they always have to ask Confucius before knowing of them? And even if these are still credible, when it comes to the story that a falcon alighted in the courtyard of the Marquis of Chen 陳, pierced by a hu-wood arrow with a stone arrowhead measuring a foot and eight inches long, and that he declared, "This is an arrow of the Sushen 肅慎 clan"—how utterly uncanonical is that! Perhaps men of wide learning, of the ilk of Zhang Maoxian 張茂先 (Zhang Hua 張華), fabricated it.

In general, those who revered Confucius wished to confer upon him a reputation for godlike prescience and vast knowledge, and so they invented stories of children's rhymes and posthumous prophecies; whereas those who envied Confucius would in turn pose questions and raise difficulties, such as the tale of the two children debating the distance of the sun, wishing thereby to stump Confucius and claim that the Sage merely had things he did not know. All of these are hollow words [? 竅言], and all of them are adept at confounding the true nature of the Sage. If one rejects them, they subside, yet if one promotes them, they flare up again; if one examines their reality, they are perverse, yet if one listens to their words, they sound appealing. Those who fear that the tunes of Zheng 鄭 will confound the Elegantiae (Ya 雅), and therefore cast aside such books and refuse to read them, are truly few; whereas those who take the Elegantiae to be the tunes of Zheng, and furthermore savor them and band together to champion them, make up nine out of ten schools—so what is there to wonder at? Thus it is said: If you take a ball of cooked millet and ten pieces of gold and show them to a small child, the small child will certainly take the ball of millet; if you take …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
十金與道德之言以示庸眾人則庸眾人
必取十金矣後之人率持兒子庸眾之見
所取彌庳如魯論鄉黨諸篇孔子言語行
事之實大中至正之道往往屑越之如遺
至於列子稱力拓北門之關王充論衡稱
有百觚之量淮南子稱智過萇弘足躡郊
菟也則爭引以薦談申申夭夭之容可想
見也而乃亟述其東門纍纍之誚豈無誦
其江漢秋陽之盛美也而不多於麕裘無
===
戾之歌日與七十子講藝杏壇之上濟濟
雍雍弗稱也而商也以假蓋見疑參也以
受杖見斥輒置喙焉故曰天下有竅言則
聖人鮮真詮可慨也今人聞人呼其父祖
之名則艴然不悅設有詆詈之者且攘臂
前矣憂心悄悄慍于羣小無如吾孔子之
遭也此非後死者之責與昔季由見毀於
魏而誣孔子以自解子順勃然為爭諸魏
侯之前主侍人瘠環之謗孟子亟辭而斥
punctuated: 十金與道德之言以示庸眾人，則庸眾人必取十金矣。後之人率持兒子、庸眾之見，所取彌庳。如《魯論》〈鄉黨〉諸篇，孔子言語行事之實，大中至正之道，往往屑越之如遺；至於《列子》稱「力拓北門之關」，王充《論衡》稱「有百觚之量」，《淮南子》稱「智過萇弘，足躡郊菟」也，則爭引以薦談。「申申夭夭」之容可想見也，而乃亟述其東門「纍纍」之誚；豈無誦其「江漢秋陽」之盛美也？而不多於「麕裘無戾」之歌。日與七十子講藝杏壇之上，濟濟雍雍，弗稱也；而商也以假蓋見疑，參也以受杖見斥，輒置喙焉。故曰：天下有竅言，則聖人鮮真詮。可慨也！今人聞人呼其父祖之名，則艴然不悅；設有詆詈之者，且攘臂前矣。「憂心悄悄，慍于羣小」，無如吾孔子之遭也，此非後死者之責與？昔季由見毀於魏，而誣孔子以自解，子順勃然為爭諸魏侯之前；主侍人瘠環之謗，孟子亟辭而斥
translation_en: … ten pieces of gold and words of the Way and virtue to show to ordinary, mediocre people, then ordinary, mediocre people will certainly take the ten pieces of gold. People of later times generally hold the views of children and ordinary folks, and what they choose is ever more base. For example, in chapters such as "Xiangdang" (In the Local Community) of the Lu Analects (Lunyu), the realities of Confucius's words and deeds, and his Way of great centrality and utmost correctness, are often carelessly passed over as if forgotten; yet when it comes to the Liezi claiming that "his strength could lift the bolt of the northern gate," Wang Chong's Lunheng (Balanced Discourses) claiming that "he had a capacity for a hundred goblets of wine," and the Huainanzi claiming that "his wisdom surpassed that of Chang Hong and his feet could overtake a suburban hare," they vie to cite these as conversational topics. His "relaxed and congenial" bearing can well be imagined, yet they eagerly recount the mockery of him at the eastern gate as looking "haggard like a stray dog." Is it that no one recites the abundant praise of him as being like "washed in the Jiang and Han rivers and bleached in the autumn sun"? Yet such recitations are outnumbered by the song of the "fawn skin coat that brings no offense." That he daily discussed the arts with his seventy disciples above the Apricot Altar, in dignified and harmonious company, goes unmentioned; whereas Bu Shang (Zixia) being doubted over lending a canopy, or Zeng Can being rebuked for taking a beating with a staff, are things people readily chatter about. Therefore it is said: when the world has specious words, the true meaning of the Sage is rarely found. How lamentable! Today, if someone hears another person call out the personal name of his father or grandfather, he flushes with displeasure; and suppose someone were to slander or revile them, he would roll up his sleeves and step forward. "My heart is anxious and distressed, / Resented by the crowd of petty men"—nothing matches what our Confucius encountered. Is this not the responsibility of those of us who die later? In the past, when Jiyou was slandered in Wei and falsely implicated Confucius to exonerate himself, Zishun indignantly contested it before the Marquis of Wei; as for the slander that he lodged with the attendant Jihuan, Mencius urgently refuted and rejected …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之生也孔子之徒也卽執事者不以問二
三子固將請之
第三問
同考試官敎諭蕭批人才之難自古記之衡鏡
所在世道繋焉善哉子之言是
同考試官訓導魯批古稱才德非二道也後乃
科別之以爲評品異矣此作得題旨宜錄
考試官學正陳批援古辨才皆繩尺語
===
考試官學正王批引據悉對爛然有第
今之譚才德者離其指矣夫天性之謂道
體道之謂德德應於物焉之謂才夫德內
以脩身外以治人以正君臣以親父子以
序兄弟長幼以順夫婦以成朋友之交以
辨庶政理萬物之宜天子用之以治天下
諸侯用之以治其國卿大夫用之以治其
官士庶人用之以治其家廣之塞宇宙窮
日月遠之施乎後世無出乎德者也大哉
punctuated:
之。生也，孔子之徒也，卽執事者不以問，二三子固將請之。

第三問

同考試官敎諭蕭批：人才之難，自古記之。衡鏡所在，世道繋焉。善哉，子之言是！
同考試官訓導魯批：古稱才德非二道也，後乃科別之以爲評品，異矣。此作得題旨，宜錄。
考試官學正陳批：援古辨才，皆繩尺語。
考試官學正王批：引據悉對，爛然有第。

今之譚才德者，離其指矣。夫天性之謂道，體道之謂德，德應於物焉之謂才。夫德，內以脩身，外以治人，以正君臣，以親父子，以序兄弟長幼，以順夫婦，以成朋友之交，以辨庶政、理萬物之宜。天子用之以治天下，諸侯用之以治其國，卿大夫用之以治其官，士庶人用之以治其家。廣之塞宇宙、窮日月，遠之施乎後世，無出乎德者也。大哉，
translation_en:
… it. I, the candidate, am a follower of Confucius; even if Your Excellency had not asked about this, we disciples would surely have begged to speak of it.

Third Question

Associate Examiner and Instructor Xiao comments: "The scarcity of talent has been recorded since antiquity. Where the balance and mirror of evaluation lie, the Way of the world is bound up with them. Excellent! What you say is right."
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Lu comments: "In antiquity it was said that talent and virtue are not two separate Ways; later generations divided them into categories for grading and evaluation, which was strange indeed. This essay grasps the intent of the question and ought to be selected."
Examiner and Director of Studies Chen comments: "Drawing upon antiquity to distinguish talent, every word conforms to the standard."
Examiner and Director of Studies Wang comments: "The citations and proofs all match the questions, brilliantly arranged in proper order."

Those who discuss talent and virtue today have departed from the true meaning. Now, what is endowed by Heavenly nature is called the Way; embodying the Way is called virtue; and virtue responding to things is called talent. As for virtue: inwardly it serves to cultivate the self, and outwardly to govern others; to rectify the relation between ruler and minister, to foster affection between father and son, to order elder and younger brothers, to harmonize husband and wife, to perfect intercourse among friends, and to distinguish the various affairs of administration and regulate what is fitting for the myriad things. The Son of Heaven uses it to govern All under Heaven; the feudal lords use it to govern their states; the chamberlains and grandees use it to govern their offices; and servicemen and commoners use it to govern their households. Broadened, it fills the cosmos and reaches to the limits of the sun and moon; extended afar, it is bestowed upon later generations—there is nothing that goes beyond virtue. Great indeed …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
洋洋乎德之施也由斯以譚才藏之爲德
德徵之爲才德者才之統才者德之名可
以名之爲德亦可名之爲才非二物也請
以書記明之書稱高陽氏才子八人曰齊
聖廣淵明允篤誠高辛氏才子八人曰忠
肅恭懿宣慈惠和其所號爲才率皆德行
之稱而窮奇檮杌饕餮諸悖德者卽所謂
不才者也迺言九德曰寬而栗柔而立愿
而恭亂而敬擾而毅直而溫簡而廉剛而
===
塞彊而義類皆與才雜稱之而用之俊明
有家亮采有邦者卽九德也故當其時上
下咨美功業禹稷咎繇並以德著而仲尼
嘆才難五臣十亂皆以才稱蓋其指才德
一也善夫孟子之言性善也曰乃若其情
則可以爲善矣若夫爲不善非才之罪也
又曰富歲多賴凶歲多暴非天之降才殊
也吾是以明才者性之能也德也昔人蓋
並言之後之儒者不喻其指而徒睹其跡
punctuated: 洋洋乎德之施也！由斯以譚，才藏之爲德，德徵之爲才；德者，才之統，才者，德之名。可以名之爲德，亦可名之爲才，非二物也。請以書記明之：《書》稱高陽氏才子八人，曰齊、聖、廣、淵、明、允、篤、誠；高辛氏才子八人，曰忠、肅、恭、懿、宣、慈、惠、和。其所號爲才，率皆德行之稱；而窮奇、檮杌、饕餮諸悖德者，卽所謂不才者也。迺言九德，曰：寬而栗，柔而立，愿而恭，亂而敬，擾而毅，直而溫，簡而廉，剛而塞，彊而義，類皆與才雜稱之；而用之俊明有家、亮采有邦者，卽九德也。故當其時，上下咨美功業，禹、稷、咎繇並以德著，而仲尼嘆「才難」，五臣、十亂皆以才稱，蓋其指才德一也。善夫！孟子之言性善也，曰：「乃若其情，則可以爲善矣。若夫爲不善，非才之罪也。」又曰：「富歲多賴，凶歲多暴，非天之降才殊也。」吾是以明才者，性之能也，德也，昔人蓋並言之。後之儒者不喻其指，而徒睹其跡，
translation_en: …and vast is the reach of virtue! Discussing it from this perspective, talent when stored within is virtue, and virtue when manifested is talent; virtue is the unifying whole of talent, and talent is the name given to virtue. One may call it virtue, or one may call it talent; they are not two different things. Allow me to clarify this through the historical records. The historical records state that the clan of Gaoyang 高陽氏 had eight talented sons, described as orderly, sagely, broad-minded, profound, perceptive, trustworthy, earnest, and sincere; and the clan of Gaoxin 高辛氏 had eight talented sons, described as loyal, reverent, respectful, admirable, communicative, compassionate, benevolent, and harmonious. What were there designated as "talent" were in every case terms for virtuous conduct; whereas those who rebelled against virtue—such as Qiongqi 窮奇, Taowu 檮杌, and Taotie 饕餮—were precisely the ones called "untalented." Furthermore, the Document of Shun speaks of the Nine Virtues, namely: affable yet莊嚴 (tremblingly attentive), mild yet firm, blunt yet respectful, apt at governance yet reverent, docile yet resolute, straightforward yet gentle, easy-going yet discerning, rigid yet sincere, and strong yet righteous. All such qualities were spoken of interchangeably with talent; and what were employed by the eminent and enlightened in governing their households, or in aiding the affairs of the state, were none other than the Nine Virtues. Therefore, in those times, when superiors and inferiors acclaimed great achievements, Yu 禹, Ji 稷, and Gao Yao 咎繇 were all renowned for their virtue; yet when Zhongni 仲尼 [Confucius] sighed that "talent is hard to find," the five ministers of Shun and the ten capable ministers of King Wu were all praised for their talent. This is because, in their intent, talent and virtue were one and the same. How well did Mencius 孟子 speak of the goodness of human nature! He said: "As for one's genuine disposition, one is capable of doing good. If one does what is not good, that is not the fault of one's natural talent." He also said: "In good years the young men are mostly lazy [reliable], and in bad years they are mostly violent; this is not because Heaven has conferred different natural talents upon them." From this I understand clearly that talent is the capacity of one's nature, which is virtue; the ancients indeed spoke of them together. Later scholars failed to grasp this meaning, and merely observed their outward traces…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
於是支離才德科列序途用以剽剝士林
考鏡失得其言犂然可喜而本之謬於初
指焉亢倉子曰賢可以正國才亦可以治
國賢者沈運無迹人不知其方才者勤率
其事人知所於德一賢統衆才而有餘衆
才度一賢猶不足此尊德而卑才上德者
之所因也而顧未知德亦才也華丘游曰
事父母使家人稱孝孰與治官難束帶而
敎吏民使國人愛之孰與鼓三軍之士以
===
走强敵難故德可勉而才不可强此難才
而易德喜才者之所託也而惡知才卽德
耶劉常侍有言偏至之才以才自名兼材
之人以德爲目兼德之人更爲美號兼德
而至謂之中庸具體而微謂之德行一至
謂之偏才一徵謂之依似一至一違謂之
間雜其指蓋以兼材爲大德一德爲偏材
而因廣其流焉淮南子曰天下不可以智
爲也不可以慧識也不可以事治也不可
punctuated: 於是支離才德，科列序途，用以剽剝士林，考鏡失得。其言犂然可喜，而本之謬於初指焉。亢倉子曰：「賢可以正國，才亦可以治國。賢者沈運無迹，人不知其方；才者勤率其事，人知所於德。一賢統衆才而有餘，衆才度一賢猶不足。」此尊德而卑才，上德者之所因也，而顧未知德亦才也。華丘游曰：「事父母使家人稱孝，孰與治官難？束帶而敎吏民，使國人愛之，孰與鼓三軍之士以走强敵難？故德可勉而才不可强。」此難才而易德，喜才者之所託也，而惡知才卽德耶？劉常侍有言：「偏至之才，以才自名；兼材之人，以德爲目；兼德之人，更爲美號。兼德而至，謂之中庸；具體而微，謂之德行；一至謂之偏才；一徵謂之依似；一至一違謂之間雜。」其指蓋以兼材爲大德，一德爲偏材，而因廣其流焉。淮南子曰：「天下不可以智爲也，不可以慧識也，不可以事治也，不可以
translation_en: …Thereupon they fragmented talent and virtue, categorizing and ranking their paths, using this to dissect the community of scholars and examine their successes and failures. Their words are neatly arranged and pleasing, yet at their root they deviate from the original meaning. Master Kangcang (Kangcangzi 亢倉子) said: "A worthy person can rectify a state, and a talented person can also govern a state. The worthy operates profoundly without leaving a trace, so that people do not know his method; the talented diligently leads in affairs, so that people know whom to credit with gratitude. One worthy can command a multitude of talents with ease, whereas a multitude of talents measuring up to a single worthy will still fall short." This exalts virtue and demeans talent; it is what those who prize virtue rely upon, yet they fail to realize that virtue is also talent. Hua Qiuyou 華丘游 said: "Serving one's parents so that the family praises one's filial piety—how does that compare in difficulty with governing an office? Donning court sash to instruct clerks and the people so that the people of the state love one—how does that compare in difficulty with rousing the soldiers of the Three Armies to rout a powerful enemy?
