Therefore, virtue can be striven for, whereas talent cannot be forced." This treats talent as difficult and virtue as easy; it is what those who delight in talent take as their pretext, yet how could they know that talent is itself virtue? Regular Attendant Liu (Liu Shao 劉劭) had a saying: "Those of one-sided attainment in talent take 'talent' as their designation; those who combine multiple capabilities take 'virtue' as their label; those who combine multiple virtues are given an even finer title. Combining virtues to the utmost is called the Mean (zhongyong); possessing the whole body of virtues in miniature is called 'virtuous conduct' (dexing); reaching the utmost in a single aspect is called 'one-sided talent'; having a single manifestation is called 'approximate resemblance'; attaining in one respect while erring in another is called 'admixture.'" His point was蓋 to regard combined capabilities as great virtue and a single virtue as one-sided capability, thereby broadening their categories. The Master of Huainan (Huainanzi 淮南子) said: "The world cannot be managed through cleverness, nor understood through shrewdness, nor governed through mere affairs, nor…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以仁附也不可以强勝也五者皆才也德
不盛不能成一德立則五無殆五見而德
無位其指蓋謂才爲德之施德行乎才之
中而原本於德矣二子之言才德一貫吾
猶有取焉自後方人者乃爲之科曰某也
德某也才甲曰寧德勝才乙曰無寧才勝
德彼其稱量或有當乎而才德裂矣以彼
其言則抱德者何其不當於用而亡德之
人安所取才乎吾不知德何施而才又何
===
物也吾求其說而不得竊意者其毋乃後
世之所謂才德非古之才德乎管子能脫
檻車合諸侯以齊國富强而內行不脩不
能致王孔子小之吳起能修法令戰勝攻
取以張楚魏而刻覈積怨困於王錯詘於
田文蘇秦張儀用口舌以縱衡之策聲震
諸侯而押闔變詐智窮身及儒者羞而不
道何者彼所謂才者權數揣摩之智耳令
四子而古之才也安有而卑卑若是尾生
punctuated: 以仁附也，不可以强勝也。五者皆才也，德不盛，不能成一；德立，則五無殆，五見而德無位。」其指蓋謂才爲德之施，德行乎才之中，而原本於德矣。二子之言，才德一貫，吾猶有取焉。自後方人者，乃爲之科曰：「某也德，某也才。」甲曰：「寧德勝才。」乙曰：「無寧才勝德。」彼其稱量，或有當乎？而才德裂矣。以彼其言，則抱德者何其不當於用，而亡德之人安所取才乎？吾不知德何施，而才又何物也！吾求其說而不得，竊意者，其毋乃後世之所謂才德，非古之才德乎？管子能脫檻車，合諸侯，以齊國富强，而內行不脩，不能致王，孔子小之。吳起能修法令，戰勝攻取，以張楚、魏，而刻覈積怨，困於王錯，詘於田文。蘇秦、張儀用口舌，以縱衡之策聲震諸侯，而押闔變詐，智窮身及，儒者羞而不道。何者？彼所謂才者，權數揣摩之智耳。令四子而古之才也，安有而卑卑若是？尾生
translation_en:
… attached through benevolence, nor overcome through strength. All five of these are talents; if virtue is not abundant, not a single one of them can be brought to completion. Once virtue is established, the five are free from peril; when the five are displayed, virtue has no fixed position." Its purport is roughly that talent is the application of virtue, that virtue operates within talent, and that talent has its root in virtue. In the words of these two masters, talent and virtue form a single thread, and I still find something worth adopting in them.

Later on, however, those who evaluated people set up separate categories for them, saying: "So-and-so has virtue; so-and-so has talent." One person says, "Better that virtue surpass talent," while another says, "Rather let talent surpass virtue." Even if their weighing and measuring might hit the mark in some respects, talent and virtue were thereby torn apart! According to their words, why would someone who possesses virtue be so unsuited for practical use, and where would a person devoid of virtue get his talent? I would not know how virtue is applied, nor what sort of thing talent is!

I have sought a rationale for their theory without success, and I privately suspect: could it not be that what later ages call "talent" and "virtue" are not the talent and virtue of antiquity? Master Guan (Guan Zhong 管仲) was able to step out of a prisoner's cart, assemble the feudal lords, and make the state of Qi rich and strong; yet his personal conduct was uncultivated and he could not bring about true kingship, so Confucius considered him of small capacity. Wu Qi 吳起 was able to reform laws and ordinances, win battles and conquer territory, and thereby expand the power of Chu and Wei; yet he was harsh and unforgiving, accumulating resentment, and he was thwarted by Wang Cuo 王錯 and humbled by Tian Wen 田文. Su Qin 蘇秦 and Zhang Yi 張儀 used their tongues to shake the feudal lords with their strategies of vertical and horizontal alliances, yet through their manipulative schemes and shifting deceit, their wits were exhausted and disaster overtook their own persons, so that Confucian scholars are ashamed even to speak of them. Why is this? What those men called "talent" was nothing more than the cleverness of tactical calculation and sizing up others. Supposing these four men had possessed the talent of antiquity, how could they have been so base and petty as this? Wei Sheng 尾生…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之信也而愚子羔之孝也而愚孟公綽優
於趙魏老不可以爲滕薛大夫鮑叔牙忠
信廉潔而不可以託國當彼所謂德者顓
固曲方之行耳令四子而古之德也有不
可以大受者乎是故有伊尹傅說之德則
必能阿衡商業舟楫大川有周公之德則
必能勝殷遏劉朝委裘而致太平孔子曰
有德者必有言仁者必有勇又曰我戰則
克祭則受福故仕魯三月男女別于途道
===
不拾遺市不預價魯國大治四方則之夾
谷之會兵萊夷歸侵田折齊奸謀以重魯
於天下徒道大春秋莫能究其用而其門
人高第各能以其道用之諸侯若子路用
蒲而治言游用武城而治不齊用單父而
治顏淵雖不仕而深潛純粹王佐之才已
具有其德而無其用者吾未之前聞也夫
良劔昆吾冶之越砥礪之清水淬之鸊鵜
膏之則必割矣否則必惡劔也騏驥直中
punctuated: 之信也，而愚；子羔之孝也，而愚；孟公綽優於趙魏老，不可以爲滕薛大夫；鮑叔牙忠信廉潔，而不可以託國。當彼所謂德者，顓固曲方之行耳。令四子而古之德也，有不可以大受者乎？是故有伊尹、傅說之德，則必能阿衡商業，舟楫大川；有周公之德，則必能勝殷遏劉，朝委裘而致太平。孔子曰：「有德者必有言，仁者必有勇。」又曰：「我戰則克，祭則受福。」故仕魯三月，男女別于途，道不拾遺，市不預價，魯國大治，四方則之。夾谷之會，兵萊夷，歸侵田，折齊奸謀，以重魯於天下。徒道大，春秋莫能究其用，而其門人高第，各能以其道用之諸侯。若子路用蒲而治，言游用武城而治，不齊用單父而治；顏淵雖不仕，而深潛純粹，王佐之才已具。有其德而無其用者，吾未之前聞也。夫良劔，昆吾冶之，越砥礪之，清水淬之，鸊鵜膏之，則必割矣；否則必惡劔也。騏驥，直中…
translation_en: …trustworthiness was foolish; Zigao's (子羔) filial piety was foolish; Meng Gongchuo (孟公綽) was more than adequate to serve as steward to the great families of Zhao (趙) and Wei (魏), yet could not be a grand master (daifu) in the small states of Teng (滕) or Xue (薛); Bao Shuya (鮑叔牙) was loyal, trustworthy, and incorruptible, yet could not be entrusted with the state. What can be considered "virtue" in their case is merely obstinate, narrow-minded, and one-sided conduct. Had these four men possessed the virtue of antiquity, how could they have been incapable of taking on great responsibilities? Therefore, if one possesses the virtue of Yi Yin (伊尹) and Fu Yue (傅說), one will surely be able to serve as the balancing pillar (Aheng) of the Shang (商) enterprise and act as boat and oars across the great river; if one possesses the virtue of the Duke of Zhou (周公), one will surely be able to vanquish Yin (殷) and halt the slaughter, holding court with draped furs while bringing about great peace. Confucius (孔子) said: "One who possesses virtue will surely have worthy words to say; one who is humane will surely have courage." He also said: "When I do battle, I conquer; when I sacrifice, I receive blessings." Thus, after he served in Lu (魯) for three months, men and women kept to separate paths on the road, lost items were not picked up from the wayside, merchants in the market did not inflate prices, the state of Lu was in great order, and the four quarters took it as their model. At the meeting at Jiagu (夾谷), he drove back the Laiyi (萊夷) tribesmen by force of arms, recovered the encroached lands, and thwarted the treacherous plots of Qi (齊), thereby giving Lu great weight across the realm. Only because his Way was so vast, no one in the Spring and Autumn period could fully exhaust his usefulness; yet his preeminent disciples were each able to take his Way and apply it among the feudal lords. For instance, Zilu (子路) was employed in Pu (蒲) and brought about order; Yan You (言游) was employed in Wucheng (武城) and brought about order; Fu Buqi (不齊) was employed in Shanfu (單父) and brought about order; and although Yan Yuan (顏淵) did not take office, he was deeply immersed and pure, already possessing in full the talent to assist a true king. Of someone possessing such virtue yet lacking its practical application, I have never before heard. Now, as for a fine sword: when cast of Kunwu (昆吾) metal, honed on a whetstone of Yue (越), quenched in clear water, and oiled with grebe fat, it will surely cut; otherwise, it must be an inferior sword. As for a thoroughbred steed (qiji): when its straight movement hits…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
繩曲中鉤方中矩圓中規則必馳矣否則
必駑馬也相士者蓋亦若是矣而世之人
往往失之則何以故聲實不辨一好惡偏
私二毀譽亂真三古之善相馬者寒風氏
相口齒麻朝相頰子女厲相目衛忌相鬚
許鄙相脕投伐褐相胸脅管青相臏膓陳
悲相股脚秦牙相前賛君相後非一徴也
迺九方歅又得之牝牡驪黃之外矣夫士
亦然固不可以淺見一方知也是故秉禮
===
勑躬近乎傲正靜遠俗近乎迂內辨少言
近乎愚虛體謙遜近乎卑持法不敧近乎
武健是非不回近乎訐直薄名寡交儉於
奔走周容近乎疏士之不耦於俗者大都
若此矣剽輕儇捷者似敏嘽咺多偶者似
信炙輠滑稽者似智秉權隻立者似剛窒
拗自是者似執詼詭跅弛者似豪脫毛察
瑣委者似精明嫗呴悅人者似和愛虛譚
隱借者似高邈敝衣冠設辭讓者似乎廉
punctuated: 繩，曲中鉤，方中矩，圓中規，則必馳矣；否則必駑馬也。相士者蓋亦若是矣。而世之人往往失之，則何以故？聲實不辨，一；好惡偏私，二；毀譽亂真，三。古之善相馬者，寒風氏相口齒，麻朝相頰，子女厲相目，衛忌相鬚，許鄙相脕，投伐褐相胸脅，管青相臏膓，陳悲相股脚，秦牙相前，賛君相後，非一徴也。迺九方歅又得之牝牡驪黃之外矣。夫士亦然，固不可以淺見一方知也。是故秉禮勑躬近乎傲，正靜遠俗近乎迂，內辨少言近乎愚，虛體謙遜近乎卑，持法不敧近乎武健，是非不回近乎訐直，薄名寡交、儉於奔走周容近乎疏：士之不耦於俗者，大都若此矣。剽輕儇捷者似敏，嘽咺多偶者似信，炙輠滑稽者似智，秉權隻立者似剛，窒拗自是者似執，詼詭跅弛者似豪，脫毛察瑣委者似精明，嫗呴悅人者似和愛，虛譚隱借者似高邈，敝衣冠、設辭讓者似乎廉…
translation_en:
…the plumblines when going straight, the hook when curving, the carpenter's square when turning corners, and the compass when going in circles, then it is sure to gallop; otherwise, it must be an inferior nag. Judging scholars is surely just like this. Yet people in the world often misjudge them—for what reason? First, failing to distinguish between reputation and reality; second, being biased in one's likes and dislikes; and third, letting slander and praise confound the truth.

Among the skilled judges of horses in antiquity, Hanfeng judged the mouth and teeth, Ma Chao judged the cheeks, Zinü Li judged the eyes, Wei Ji judged the whiskers, Xu Bi judged the rump, Tou Fahe judged the chest and ribs, Guan Qing judged the kneecaps and bowels, Chen Bei judged the thighs and legs, Qin Ya judged the forequarters, and Zanjun judged the hindquarters—they did not rely on a single sign. Yet Jiufang Yin grasped the horse's quality entirely beyond whether it was mare or stallion, black or yellow. Now, it is the same with scholars: they certainly cannot be known through shallow views or a single aspect.

Therefore, holding to ritual and disciplining oneself comes close to arrogance; being upright, calm, and aloof from the vulgar comes close to impracticality; being inwardly discerning yet speaking little comes close to stupidity; being modest and humble in demeanor comes close to servility; upholding the law without leaning to either side comes close to harsh aggressiveness; not bending on right and wrong comes close to abrasive bluntness; caring little for fame, having few acquaintances, and being sparing in rushing about to curry favor comes close to coldness. Scholars who do not conform to the vulgar world are generally like this.

Those who are frivolous, nimble, and quick-witted resemble the perceptive; those who are affable, expansive, and readily agreeable [?] resemble the trustworthy; those who are glib as a greased axle and smooth-talking resemble the wise; those who grasp power and stand alone resemble the resolute; those who are obstinate, perverse, and self-righteous resemble the steadfast; those who are eccentric and unrestrained resemble the heroic; those who split hairs and scrutinize petty details resemble the astute; those who coddle and flatter to please others resemble the harmonious and benevolent; those who engage in empty talk and veiled pretensions [?] resemble the lofty and transcendent; and those who wear tattered caps and robes while putting on a show of declining and yielding resemble the pure and…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
約士之鮮實行者大都若此矣語曰相馬
失之肥相劒失之室是以仲尼重信於子
羽卞和垂泣於荆璞故形實不可不辨也
人固難知知人亦不易有味乎其言之也
世晩士不聞道褊中隂賊難以勝數有識
鑒卑闇本不足以知之者有好惡偏頗垂
其所知者有明知之而倒植臧否者又常
好其從諛而和已者不好其介特而異已
者好其柔媚而下已者不好其莊競而抗
===
===
已者好其綢繆而親已者不好其疏節而
遠已者見人之長則忌之從而掎摘之矣
聞人譽人之善則妬之隨而巧詆之矣好
惡若此可不爲太息乎於是毁譽紛淫不
可方物其譽人也刓方比周而當之允達
之士矯譎姡𡟎而當之亮直之士響應單
至而當之速敏之士伺色窺指而當之警
穎之士纍瓦結繩而當之該通之士其毁
人也方正醜汙而少之曰乖盭深堅不奪
punctuated: 約；士之鮮實行者，大都若此矣。語曰：「相馬失之肥，相劒失之室。」是以仲尼重信於子羽，卞和垂泣於荆璞。故形實不可不辨也。「人固難知，知人亦不易」，有味乎其言之也！世晩，士不聞道，褊中隂賊，難以勝數。有識鑒卑闇，本不足以知之者；有好惡偏頗，垂其所知者；有明知之而倒植臧否者。又常好其從諛而和已者，不好其介特而異已者；好其柔媚而下已者，不好其莊競而抗已者；好其綢繆而親已者，不好其疏節而遠已者。見人之長則忌之，從而掎摘之矣；聞人譽人之善則妬之，隨而巧詆之矣。好惡若此，可不爲太息乎？於是毁譽紛淫，不可方物。其譽人也，刓方比周，而當之允達之士；矯譎姡𡟎，而當之亮直之士；響應單至，而當之速敏之士；伺色窺指，而當之警穎之士；纍瓦結繩，而當之該通之士。其毁人也，方正醜汙，而少之曰乖盭；深堅不奪，
translation_en: …and frugal; scholars who lack genuine conduct are mostly like this. The saying goes: "In judging horses, one errs by looking at their fatness; in judging swords, one errs by looking at their scabbards." Thus Confucius placed renewed trust in Ziyu, and Bian He wept tears over the uncut jade of Jing. Therefore, outward appearance and inner reality must be distinguished. "People are certainly hard to know, and knowing people is also not easy"—how meaningful are those words! In a degenerate age, scholars do not hear the Way; those who are narrow-minded and secretly malicious are too numerous to count. There are those whose discernment is low and benighted, originally insufficient to know others; there are those whose likes and dislikes are biased, running counter [?] to what they know; and there are those who clearly know someone yet invert praise and blame. Moreover, they constantly like those who flatter and echo them, and dislike those who are independent and differ from them; they like those who are pliant, ingratiating, and deferential to them, and dislike those who are dignified, resolute, and stand up to them; they like those who are closely bound and intimate with them, and dislike those who are casual in ceremony and distant from them. When they see others' strengths, they resent them and proceed to nitpick and find fault with them; when they hear someone praising another's goodness, they are jealous of them and immediately slander them with artful malice. When likes and dislikes are like this, how can one not heave a deep sigh? Thereupon slander and praise become confused and excessive, impossible to sort out. When they praise people: those who round off their corners to form partisan cliques, they regard as sincere and adaptable scholars; those who are deceitful, crafty, and sly, they regard as upright and straightforward scholars; those who answer like an echo and come at a single summons, they regard as quick and agile scholars; those who watch countenances and spy out intentions, they regard as alert and sharp-witted scholars; those who pile up tiles and knot cords in useless verbiage, they regard as comprehensive and erudite scholars. When they slander people: those who are square, upright, and loathe corruption, they disparage as perverse; those who are deeply firm and immovable…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而少之曰愚戇靖恭伏職而少之曰巽懦
欲傅人以椎鈍不曰椎鈍而譽之曰天性
懚厚欲傅人以鷙擊不曰鷙擊而譽之曰
峭厲善理欲傅人以眥窳不曰眥窳而曰
政尚寬平昔之傾人者毁之今之傾人者
譽之矣昔之毁人者搆誣之今之毁人者
嘆息之矣昔也謂貞女爲淫今也以桑中
而詆貞女矣昔也謂鏌釼爲鈍今也以鈆
刀而咲鏌釼矣毁譽若此安得無亂眞乎
===
夫迷謬好惡者逆蘭茝而悅雝糜者也錯
糅毁譽者刻畫無鹽而點毛嬙者也信耳
者羣犬吠聲者也信目者見攫煤飯者也
重信耳目者膽胥之疑耳目人終無巳者
也惑於形似者燕石爲玉之類也惑於聲
似者鼠璞爲璞之類也失於似而因疑其
眞者黎丘丈人之智懲於祟而失其子者
也是數者皆士之害也而好惡爲尤好惡
正而後可與言辨材之道焉夫九方歅之
punctuated:
而少之曰愚戇，靖恭伏職而少之曰巽懦。欲傅人以椎鈍，不曰椎鈍，而譽之曰天性懚厚；欲傅人以鷙擊，不曰鷙擊，而譽之曰峭厲善理；欲傅人以眥窳，不曰眥窳，而曰政尚寬平。昔之傾人者毁之，今之傾人者譽之矣；昔之毁人者搆誣之，今之毁人者嘆息之矣。昔也謂貞女爲淫，今也以桑中而詆貞女矣；昔也謂鏌釼爲鈍，今也以鈆刀而咲鏌釼矣。毁譽若此，安得無亂眞乎？
夫迷謬好惡者，逆蘭茝而悅雝糜者也；錯糅毁譽者，刻畫無鹽而點毛嬙者也；信耳者，羣犬吠聲者也；信目者，見攫煤飯者也；重信耳目者，膽胥之疑耳目人終無巳者也；惑於形似者，燕石爲玉之類也；惑於聲似者，鼠璞爲璞之類也；失於似而因疑其眞者，黎丘丈人之智懲於祟而失其子者也。是數者，皆士之害也，而好惡爲尤。好惡正，而後可與言辨材之道焉。夫九方歅之
translation_en:
… they belittle them by calling them foolish and blunt; those who are quietly respectful and devoted to their duties, they belittle by calling them timid and weak. When they wish to pin the label of dullness and stupidity on someone, they do not call them dull and stupid, but praise them as being naturally sincere and generous; when they wish to pin the label of ruthless cruelty on someone, they do not call them ruthlessly cruel, but praise them as being stern and skilled at governance; when they wish to pin the label of negligence and sloth on someone, they do not call them negligent and slothful, but say that their administration values leniency and calm. In the past, those who sought to bring others down slandered them; today, those who seek to bring others down praise them! In the past, those who slandered others fabricated false charges against them; today, those who slander others sigh over them! In the past, they called a chaste woman licentious; today, they use the licentious airs of "In the Mulberries" (Sangzhong) to disparage a chaste woman! In the past, they called the legendary Moye sword blunt; today, they use a lead knife to laugh at the Moye sword! When slander and praise are like this, how can they fail to confound what is true?

Now, those who are deluded and mistaken in their likes and dislikes are like people who reject fragrant orchids and angelica while delighting in foul-smelling weeds [?]; those who jumble together slander and praise are like people who adorn the ugly Wuyan while sullying the beautiful Mao Qiang; those who trust only their ears are like a pack of dogs barking at a sound; those who trust only their eyes are like someone who saw another snatching soot-stained rice; those who overly trust their ears and eyes are like the retainers of Dan [?], whose suspicions through their informants never cease; those who are deluded by similarity of form are of the sort who mistake a stone from Yan for jade; those who are deluded by similarity of sound are of the sort who mistake an unskinned rat ("rat-in-the-rough," shupu) for uncut jade (pu); and those who are misled by a resemblance and consequently doubt the real thing are like the old man of Liqiu, whose wits, chastened by agoblin, caused him to lose his own son. Every one of these is harmful to scholars, and biased likes and dislikes are the worst of all. Only when likes and dislikes are rectified can one speak of the way of discerning talent. That Jiufang Yin …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不失馬也豈獨其技殊絕哉彼無好惡於
馬以亂其視也故鑑之所貴不在乎明而
在乎空空則妍醜隨形而明矣衡之所貴
不在於星而在於權以意行權則低昂失
而星廢矣是以嫫女不怨鑑而貪夫服於
衡嗚呼人皆正大不私怨惡則賢不肖白
而人心服士不下蔽賢才輻湊而
聖君賢臣設燎捉髮之心庶幾哉無負矣執事
所謂共由大道者意在斯乎
===
第四問
同考試官訓導王 批 纘序譜牒以存古宗法意
遠矣子能縷悉之可謂多聞
考試官學正陳 批 譜家互持異說此作折衷
得其要領
考試官學正王 批 博辯閎辭而其道本根詳
核有體
譜牒者其古道之遺乎其起於古道之廢
punctuated:
不失馬也，豈獨其技殊絕哉？彼無好惡於馬以亂其視也。故鑑之所貴，不在乎明而在乎空，空則妍醜隨形而明矣；衡之所貴，不在於星而在於權，以意行權則低昂失而星廢矣。是以嫫女不怨鑑，而貪夫服於衡。嗚呼！人皆正大，不私怨惡，則賢不肖白而人心服，士不下蔽，賢才輻湊，而聖君賢臣設燎捉髮之心，庶幾哉無負矣！執事所謂共由大道者，意在斯乎？

第四問
同考試官訓導王批：纘序譜牒以存古宗法，意遠矣。子能縷悉之，可謂多聞。
考試官學正陳批：譜家互持異說，此作折衷，得其要領。
考試官學正王批：博辯閎辭，而其道本根，詳核有體。
譜牒者，其古道之遺乎？其起於古道之廢
translation_en:
… never failed to judge a horse rightly—was it merely because his skill was unsurpassed? It was because he harbored no personal likes or dislikes toward horses to cloud his vision. Therefore, what is prized in a mirror lies not in its brightness, but in its emptiness; being empty, beauty and ugliness appear clearly just as their forms are. What is prized in a steelyard lies not in its markings, but in its sliding weight; if one moves the weight according to personal whim, the balance of high and low is lost and the markings become useless. Thus, an ugly woman like Mo Mu does not resent the mirror, and a greedy man submits to the steelyard. Alas! If everyone is upright and magnanimous, harboring no private resentments or aversions, then the worthy and the unworthy will be clearly distinguished and people's hearts will submit; scholars will not be obscured below, worthy talents will gather like spokes at a hub, and the earnest devotion of the sage ruler and worthy ministers—setting out torches at dawn to receive guests and grasping their hair mid-wash to welcome the worthy—will perhaps not have been in vain! Is this not the meaning of what Your Excellency calls "the great Way followed by all"?

Question Four

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Wang: Compiling genealogies to preserve the ancient lineage system is a far-reaching idea. That you are able to recount it in such detail shows that you are a person of wide learning.

Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Chen: Genealogists hold conflicting views among themselves; this essay adjudicates between them and grasps the essential points.

Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang: Broad in argument and grand in diction, yet its exposition of the fundamental principles is detailed, accurate, and well-structured.

Are genealogies a remnant of the ancient Way? Or did they arise from the decline of the ancient Way…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
乎古有之大宗者收族者也譜牒者其
大宗之遺乎雖然有大宗則無譜牒故
譜牒者起於大宗之廢也古者因族而
立之宗因宗而示之統握其權於上則
聯屬之勢似渙而實合明其制於下則
綱維之法似疎而實詳夫是可以勸忠
可以作孝可以收族亦可以廣仁敎化
行而廉耻重愛敬漸而德讓流職此故
也晩近世宗法廢而天下無世家歷世
===
滋蔓子孫至不知先人名行長老倒植
視宗黨乃如路人異時殊勢陵敎墮義賢
者傷之於是官有簿狀以紀民之盛衰家
有譜系以紀族之分合保姓鳩族扶義翼
敎使民相親長敦本不忘蓋有宗法之遺
焉且姓氏之學譚非易易也雖司馬遷劉
知幾博聞良史猶以周公爲姬旦文王爲
姬伯尚以姬姜嬴姒爲女婦之稱而况於
愚生乎然甞聞之矣三代之前姓氏分爲
punctuated: 乎？古有之：「大宗者，收族者也。」譜牒者，其大宗之遺乎！雖然，有大宗則無譜牒，故譜牒者，起於大宗之廢也。古者因族而立之宗，因宗而示之統。握其權於上，則聯屬之勢似渙而實合；明其制於下，則綱維之法似疎而實詳。夫是可以勸忠，可以作孝，可以收族，亦可以廣仁。敎化行而廉耻重，愛敬漸而德讓流，職此故也。晩近世宗法廢而天下無世家，歷世滋蔓，子孫至不知先人名行，長老倒植，視宗黨乃如路人，異時殊勢，陵敎墮義，賢者傷之。於是官有簿狀以紀民之盛衰，家有譜系以紀族之分合，保姓鳩族，扶義翼敎，使民相親長，敦本不忘，蓋有宗法之遺焉。且姓氏之學，譚非易易也。雖司馬遷、劉知幾，博聞良史，猶以周公爲姬旦、文王爲姬伯，尚以姬、姜、嬴、姒爲女婦之稱，而况於愚生乎？然甞聞之矣：三代之前，姓氏分爲
translation_en: …? There is an ancient saying: "The great lineage (dazong) is that which gathers the kin together." Are genealogical registers not the remnant of the great lineage! Even so, when there was the great lineage, there were no genealogical registers; therefore, genealogical registers arose from the decline of the great lineage. In antiquity, on the basis of kin groups they established lineages, and on the basis of lineages they demonstrated the line of descent. When the authority over this was held above, the dynamic of their solidarity seemed diffuse yet was truly cohesive; when the regulations governing this were made clear below, the method of their overarching bond seemed loose yet was truly detailed. Thus it was possible to encourage loyalty, to foster filial piety, to gather the kin together, and also to broaden benevolence. That moral transformation was carried out and a sense of integrity and shame was esteemed, and that love and respect steeped the people while virtuous deference spread, was due precisely to this. In more recent ages, the lineage system fell into disuse and the empire had no hereditary houses. As generations passed and branches multiplied, descendants reached the point of not knowing the names and conduct of their forebears; seniority was inverted, and people regarded their own lineage members and kinsmen just like strangers on the road. With changing times and differing circumstances, moral teaching was transgressed and righteousness ruined, and worthy men grieved over it. Thereupon, the government had official registers to record the rise and decline of families among the people, and private households had genealogical tables to record the branching and coming together of their kin—preserving surnames and assembling clans, upholding righteousness and assisting moral teaching, causing the people to be affectionate toward one another and respect their elders, and to esteem their roots without forgetting. In this there was indeed something of the remnant of the lineage system. Moreover, the study of surnames (xing) and clan names (shi) is no easy matter to discuss. Even Sima Qian 司馬遷 and Liu Zhiji 劉知幾, erudite and fine historians though they were, still referred to the Duke of Zhou 周公 as Ji Dan 姬旦 and King Wen 文王 as Ji Bo 姬伯, and still took Ji 姬, Jiang 姜, Ying 嬴, and Si 姒 to be appellations reserved for women and wives—how much more so for an ignorant student like myself? Yet I have heard it said: before the Three Dynasties, surnames and clan names were divided into…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
二三代之後姓氏混而爲一古者姓氏之
權出於上故族類易明後世姓氏之柄寄
於民故枝派難考善乎東萊呂氏之言曰
姓者統其祖考之所自出百世而不變者
也氏者別其子孫之所自分數世而一變
者也古者天子胙諸侯公卿大夫之土則
各命之氏諸侯公卿大夫士之家各按其
氏系以宗法行世祿之典其比閭州黨之
民不及以世祿者亦繇口受之業長子孫
===
於其土而太宰又以九兩之法繫之故其
族不散洽敘敦固而俗不漓有以也中世
以來諸侯公卿大夫士之世不及祿支離
分散枝蔓于中國又革命之際所當兵燹
戰陳與夫饑饉亡徙者不可勝數州郡之
間求如春秋世家者且不可得而况於古
者氏系所出乎此學士大夫所以歔戲嘆
息而譜所由作也漢司馬子長採世本世
系而作帝紀摭周譜國語而作世家姓氏
punctuated: 二；三代之後，姓氏混而爲一。古者姓氏之權出於上，故族類易明；後世姓氏之柄寄於民，故枝派難考。善乎東萊呂氏之言曰：「姓者，統其祖考之所自出，百世而不變者也；氏者，別其子孫之所自分，數世而一變者也。」古者天子胙諸侯、公卿、大夫之土，則各命之氏；諸侯、公卿、大夫、士之家，各按其氏系，以宗法行世祿之典。其比閭州黨之民，不及以世祿者，亦繇口受之業，長子孫於其土，而太宰又以九兩之法繫之。故其族不散，洽敘敦固而俗不漓，有以也。中世以來，諸侯、公卿、大夫、士之世不及祿，支離分散，枝蔓于中國。又革命之際，所當兵燹戰陳，與夫饑饉亡徙者，不可勝數。州郡之間，求如春秋世家者且不可得，而况於古者氏系所出乎？此學士大夫所以歔戲嘆息，而譜所由作也。漢司馬子長採《世本》世系而作《帝紀》，摭《周譜》、《國語》而作《世家》，姓氏
translation_en: … two; after the Three Dynasties, ancestral names (xing 姓) and clan names (shi 氏) were conflated into one. In antiquity, the authority over ancestral and clan names emanated from above, so kindred lineages were easy to clarify; in later ages, control over ancestral and clan names rested with the common people, so branch lines became difficult to verify. Well spoken are the words of Master Lü of Donglai [Lü Zuqian 呂祖謙]: "The ancestral name (xing) unifies the origin from which one's ancestors sprang, remaining unchanged for a hundred generations; the clan name (shi) distinguishes the branches into which one's descendants divided, changing after a few generations." In antiquity, when the Son of Heaven bestowed lands upon the feudal lords, Dukes, Ministers, and Grand Masters, he conferred upon each of them a clan name. The families of feudal lords, Dukes, Ministers, Grand Masters, and servicemen (shi 士) each followed their clan genealogy, practicing the institution of hereditary emoluments through the lineal descent system (zongfa 宗法). As for the common people of the neighborhoods, villages, districts, and communities who did not receive hereditary emoluments, they too raised their children and grandchildren on their native soil through the land allotments they received per capita, while the Grand Councilor (Taizai 太宰) further bound them together through the method of the Nine Bonds (jiu liang 九兩). Thus their clans did not scatter, harmonious order was thick and firm, and customs did not degenerate—there was a reason for this. Since the middle ages, the descendants of feudal lords, Dukes, Ministers, Grand Masters, and servicemen have not inherited emoluments, becoming fragmented, scattered, and ramified across the central states. Moreover, during times of dynastic change, those who suffered from the fires of war and battle arrays, or who fled and migrated because of famine, were beyond count. Among the prefectures and commanderies, even if one sought families like the hereditary houses of the Spring and Autumn period, they could no longer be found—how much less the ancient origins of clan genealogies! This is why scholars and Grand Masters heave sighs of lamentation, and how genealogies came to be composed. In the Han dynasty, Sima Zichang [Sima Qian 司馬遷] drew upon the genealogical tables of the Book of Origins (Shiben 世本) to compose the "Basic Annals of the Emperors" (Diji 帝紀), and gathered material from the Genealogies of Zhou (Zhoupu 周譜) and the Discourses of the States (Guoyu 國語) to compose the "Hereditary Houses" (Shijia 世家), whereby the ancestral and clan names' …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之源始著晉魏而降區區綜核百氏以門
第官人雖卑姓雜譜皆藏有司迄於李唐
猶相崇重故應邵則有氏族篇王僧孺則
有百家譜徐勉之則有百官牒河南則有
官氏志諸儒則有氏族志栁冲則有百姓
系錄路淳則有衣冠譜韋述則有開元譜
栁芳則有永泰譜栁璨則有韻略張九齡
則有韻譜非不綦然列也然槩之有三種
焉論字者以偏旁爲主是字書之工也論
===
聲者以四聲爲主是韻聲之資也論地望
者以貴賤爲主是升沈之恒也其弊也尚
婚姻者先外族而後本宗尚人物者進庶
孽而退嫡長尚冠冕者略伉儷而慕榮華
尚貴戚者狥勢利而忘禮教人無反本之
思而族鮮敦睦之道尚安望其久安而長
治也哉嗚呼譜牒之盛也晉魏氏之失也
非自晉魏氏始也其始於宗法之亡乎至
於今譜又不存學士大夫莫知所自而仁
punctuated: 之源始著。晉、魏而降，區區綜核百氏，以門第官人，雖卑姓雜譜，皆藏有司，迄於李唐，猶相崇重。故應邵則有《氏族篇》，王僧孺則有《百家譜》，徐勉之則有《百官牒》，河南則有《官氏志》，諸儒則有《氏族志》，栁冲則有《百姓系錄》，路淳則有《衣冠譜》，韋述則有《開元譜》，栁芳則有《永泰譜》，栁璨則有《韻略》，張九齡則有《韻譜》，非不綦然列也。然槩之有三種焉：論字者以偏旁爲主，是字書之工也；論聲者以四聲爲主，是韻聲之資也；論地望者以貴賤爲主，是升沈之恒也。其弊也，尚婚姻者先外族而後本宗，尚人物者進庶孽而退嫡長，尚冠冕者略伉儷而慕榮華，尚貴戚者狥勢利而忘禮教。人無反本之思，而族鮮敦睦之道，尚安望其久安而長治也哉！嗚呼！譜牒之盛也，晉、魏氏之失也。非自晉、魏氏始也，其始於宗法之亡乎？至於今，譜又不存，學士大夫莫知所自，而仁
translation_en: … the origins of [surnames and clans] first became clearly known. From the Wei and Jin dynasties onward, people busied themselves with compiling and verifying the hundred clans, appointing men to office on the basis of family status. Even the miscellaneous genealogies of lowly surnames were all deposited with the authorities, and down to the Tang dynasty of the Li house, they continued to hold them in high esteem. Thus Ying Shao had the Treatise on Clans and Lineages (Shizu pian), Wang Sengru had the Genealogy of the Hundred Families (Baijia pu), Xu Mianzhi [Xu Mian] had the Registers of the Hundred Officials (Baiguan die), Henan [the Northern Wei court at Luoyang] had the Treatise on Official Clans (Guanshi zhi), the various scholars had the Treatise on Clans and Lineages (Shizu zhi), Liu Chong had the Lineage Records of the Hundred Surnames (Baixing xilu), Lu Chun [Lu Jingchun] had the Genealogy of Officialdom (Yiguan pu), Wei Shu had the Kaiyuan Genealogy (Kaiyuan pu), Liu Fang had the Yongtai Genealogy (Yongtai pu), Liu Can had the Summary in Rhymes (Yunlüe), and Zhang Jiuling had the Rhymed Genealogy (Yunpu)—it is not that these were not arrayed in intricate detail. Yet broadly speaking, they fell into three categories: those that arranged surnames by character focused on radicals, which is the craft of character dictionaries; those that arranged them by sound focused on the four tones, which is an aid to rhyme and pronunciation; and those that arranged them by choronym and prestige focused on noble and base status, which reflects the conventional measure of rise and fall. As for their abuses: those who prized marriage alliances put affinal relatives first and their own patrilineal clan second; those who prized personal talent advanced concubines' sons and demoted eldest sons of the principal wife; those who prized official caps and robes slighted proper matrimonial matches and coveted worldly splendor; and those who prized noble in-laws pursued power and profit while forgetting ritual teaching. People had no thought of returning to their roots, and clans rarely practiced the way of cordial harmony—how then could one still hope for long-lasting peace and enduring order! Alas! The flourishing of genealogical registers was the failing of the Wei and Jin dynasties. Yet it did not begin with the Wei and Jin dynasties; did it not begin with the demise of the lineage law (zongfa)? Down to the present day, genealogies in turn have ceased to survive, scholars and grandees do not know from where they descend, and the [hearts of] benevolent…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
人孝子之心茫乎無所寄於是扼腕而嘆
抵掌而譚以求復宗法而宗卒不可立其
亦未明於古今之變乎夫宗法不可行於
今者有三封建不復舉矣學校不復修矣
井田不復制矣其不可行者勢也古者諸
侯世其國別子世大夫故宗立而族人莫
不聽焉今之大夫起於白屋非有尺寸之
籍也載符而出受代而旋非有定位可以
長子孫也故紈袴之後同於隸廝怙惡之
===
踪不齒族黨其身之不自淑而又皇恤其
他此其不可行者一也書曰世祿之家鮮
克由禮故師氏正其行保氏授其文而又
司過議其宥故其教易尊而宗可久也漢
承秦制破滅世家二千石皆以鋤治彊宗
豪右爲政於是景屈諸田之族且下隸編
氓矣況望其纘世業而明禮教哉此其不
可行者二也三代之制各有夫田分業定
而衣食足然後民依於宗而不麗於法今
punctuated: 人孝子之心，茫乎無所寄，於是扼腕而嘆、抵掌而譚，以求復宗法，而宗卒不可立，其亦未明於古今之變乎！夫宗法不可行於今者有三：封建不復舉矣，學校不復修矣，井田不復制矣。其不可行者，勢也。古者諸侯世其國，別子世大夫，故宗立而族人莫不聽焉。今之大夫起於白屋，非有尺寸之籍也；載符而出，受代而旋，非有定位可以長子孫也。故紈袴之後，同於隸廝；怙惡之踪，不齒族黨。其身之不自淑，而又皇恤其他？此其不可行者一也。《書》曰：「世祿之家，鮮克由禮。」故師氏正其行，保氏授其文，而又司過議其宥，故其教易尊而宗可久也。漢承秦制，破滅世家，二千石皆以鋤治彊宗豪右爲政，於是景、屈、諸田之族，且下隸編氓矣，況望其纘世業而明禮教哉？此其不可行者二也。三代之制，各有夫田，分業定而衣食足，然後民依於宗而不麗於法。今
translation_en: … the minds of benevolent men and filial sons are left bewildered with nothing to rely upon. Thereupon, they clasp their wrists in sighs and clap their hands in discussion, seeking to restore the lineage system (zongfa); yet the lineage ultimately cannot be established. Is it not because they have failed to understand the changes between antiquity and the present? There are three reasons why the lineage system cannot be practiced today: enfeoffment is no longer carried out, the ancient schools are no longer maintained, and the well-field system is no longer instituted. That it cannot be practiced is a matter of historical circumstance. In antiquity, feudal lords inherited their states from generation to generation, and secondary sons inherited the rank of Great Officer from generation to generation; therefore, once the lineage head was established, none among the kinsmen failed to obey him. The Great Officers of today rise from humble thatched cottages, possessing not a single inch of hereditary status; they carry their tallies to go out and serve, and return home when replaced, having no permanent position that can be passed down to preside over their sons and grandsons. Thus, the descendants of silk-trousered aristocrats sink to the level of menial servants, and those who persist in wrongdoing are disowned by their clansmen and neighbors. When they cannot even cultivate their own persons, how could they have the leisure to care for others? This is the first reason it cannot be practiced. The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "Families of hereditary emolument rarely abide by ritual." Therefore, in antiquity the Master of Instruction (shishi) rectified their conduct, the Master of Protection (baoshi) taught them the cultural arts, and the Official in Charge of Faults (siguo) deliberated on pardoning their offenses; thus, their teachings were easily honored and the lineage could endure for a long time. The Han inherited the system of the Qin, breaking and destroying hereditary houses, and the Two-Thousand-Bushel Officials (Prefects) all made the eradication of powerful lineages and local magnates their administrative priority. Thereupon, the clans of Jing, Qu, and the various Tians were reduced to the status of registered commoners—how much less could one hope for them to continue their hereditary enterprises and clarify ritual teachings! This is the second reason it cannot be practiced. Under the system of the Three Dynasties, each household had its allotment of fields; once allotted occupations were fixed and clothing and food were sufficient, the people depended on their lineages and did not fall foul of the law. Today…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者民無常業士鮮固志即使士師議刑憲
人執法尚不能使遊食者外無異謀乃欲
假服制聯親屬抗宗法以復古道豈不謬
哉此其不可行者三也然則有志反本者
將聽其宗之離散而不屬乎抑亦外譜牒
而必復古大宗小宗之舊乎夫離散則有
所不忍矣泥古則有所不可矣惟於重譜
之中寓所以立宗之意焉可耳宋世言宗
譜者二家曰廬陵歐陽氏曰眉山蘇氏二
===
家之法厥各不同歐陽氏則世經人緯取
法於史氏之年表蘇氏則系聯派屬如禮
家所謂宗圖者及論所爲同則皆使人重
其本之所自出有尊尊之義焉各詳其支
之所由分有親親之道焉其法具在可攷
鏡也愚以謂民間支派悠邈莫可究詰者
不必强爲之附而諸所指觀可以譜牒行
者俾之族各爲譜譜各有表表各有圖上
自始祖下及子孫各以類系屬不相紊亂
punctuated: 者，民無常業，士鮮固志，即使士師議刑，憲人執法，尚不能使遊食者外無異謀，乃欲假服制、聯親屬、抗宗法以復古道，豈不謬哉？此其不可行者三也。然則有志反本者，將聽其宗之離散而不屬乎？抑亦外譜牒而必復古大宗、小宗之舊乎？夫離散則有所不忍矣，泥古則有所不可矣，惟於重譜之中，寓所以立宗之意焉可耳。宋世言宗譜者二家：曰廬陵歐陽氏，曰眉山蘇氏。二家之法，厥各不同。歐陽氏則世經人緯，取法於史氏之年表；蘇氏則系聯派屬，如禮家所謂宗圖者。及論所爲同，則皆使人重其本之所自出，有尊尊之義焉；各詳其支之所由分，有親親之道焉。其法具在，可攷鏡也。愚以謂民間支派悠邈，莫可究詰者，不必强爲之附；而諸所指觀可以譜牒行者，俾之族各爲譜，譜各有表，表各有圖，上自始祖，下及子孫，各以類系屬，不相紊亂，
translation_en:
… nowadays the common people have no constant livelihood and scholars rarely possess a firm resolve. Even if the Judicial Officers deliberate on punishments and the upholders of the law enforce the statutes, they still cannot prevent idle consumers from harboring seditious schemes outside. If one then wishes to rely on mourning grades, bind kin together, and elevate the descent-line system in order to restore the ancient way, is this not absurd? This is the third reason it cannot be practiced.

That being so, should those who aspire to return to the root simply allow their lineages to scatter and remain unconnected? Or should they disregard genealogical registers and insist upon restoring the ancient institutions of the great descent-line and lesser descent-lines? Now, to let them scatter is something one cannot bear, yet to cling rigidly to antiquity is something that cannot be done. The only viable course is to lodge the intention of establishing the descent-line within the emphasis on genealogies. In the Song dynasty, there were two masters who spoke of clan genealogies: the Ouyang family of Luling (Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修) and the Su family of Meishan (Su Xun 蘇洵). The methods of the two families were each different. The Ouyang method used generations as the warp and individuals as the weft, modeling itself on the chronological tables of the historians; the Su method linked lineages and connected branches, like what ritualists call a descent-line chart. Yet when we discuss what they had in common, both caused men to honor the root from which they sprang, embodying the principle of venerating the honorable; and each detailed how its branches divided, embodying the way of loving one's kin. Their methods are preserved in full and can be examined as a mirror.

In my humble opinion, where collateral branches among the people are so distant and obscure that they can no longer be traced and verified, there is no need to forcibly attach them. But for all those whose relationships can be pointed out and observed so that genealogical registers can be put into practice, let each clan compile a genealogy, each genealogy have tables, and each table have charts. From the founding ancestor above down to the sons and grandsons below, let each be connected according to category without confusion or disorder, …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
略如二氏之制仍擇族之長且賢者司之
凡歲時伏臘朔望之旦無少長悉詣祠牒
者相敎以孝相率以友相勸以義相賙以
財諸不率者譙讓之斥不與齒則雖未嘗
強天下之勢以立之宗而宗法亦未嘗不
寓由是尊尊則人知有祖而分自明故曰
可以勸忠親親則人知有宗而恩愈篤故
曰可以作孝忠孝咸備故曰可以鳩族可
以廣仁焉嗚呼世道陵夷民窮而散編戶
===
之畒堇堇治其家人生產以爲是固慮足
仁義之譚乆遠之事里巷所詘卽語之未
遑也此其風非得世家大族薦紳先生儼
然爲齊民倡導安可幾乎夫日月星辰無
情也而皆宗於天百穀草木無情也而皆
宗於土別生分類無窮也而皆宗於祖宗
之義大矣哉然其權統於天子而其制成
於世臣此哲王所以達天親之本蓋臣所
以明人道之懿而置天下於雍煕敦睦以
punctuated: 略如二氏之制，仍擇族之長且賢者司之。凡歲時、伏臘、朔望之旦，無少長悉詣祠。牒者相敎以孝，相率以友，相勸以義，相賙以財；諸不率者譙讓之，斥不與齒。則雖未嘗強天下之勢以立之宗，而宗法亦未嘗不寓。由是尊尊，則人知有祖而分自明，故曰可以勸忠；親親，則人知有宗而恩愈篤，故曰可以作孝；忠孝咸備，故曰可以鳩族，可以廣仁焉。嗚呼！世道陵夷，民窮而散。編戶之畒，堇堇治其家人生產，以爲是固慮足；仁義之譚、乆遠之事，里巷所詘，卽語之未遑也。此其風，非得世家大族、薦紳先生儼然爲齊民倡導，安可幾乎？夫日月星辰無情也，而皆宗於天；百穀草木無情也，而皆宗於土；別生分類無窮也，而皆宗於祖。宗之義大矣哉！然其權統於天子，而其制成於世臣。此哲王所以達天親之本，蓋臣所以明人道之懿，而置天下於雍煕敦睦，以
translation_en:
…roughly following the system of the two masters [Ouyang and Su], and further selecting someone senior and worthy within the clan to take charge of it. On the mornings of seasonal festivals, the summer and winter sacrifices, and the new and full moons, let all, young and old alike, assemble at the ancestral shrine. Those recorded in the genealogy shall teach one another filial piety, lead one another in fraternal affection, encourage one another in righteousness, and succor one another with wealth; those who do not comply shall be reprimanded and excluded from taking their place in the ranks of the clan. Thus, even without forcing the circumstances of the world in order to establish descent-line heirs, the descent-line system will nonetheless be embodied therein. Through this, by honoring the honorable, people will know they have ancestors and hierarchical distinctions will naturally be clear—hence it is said that it can encourage loyalty; by treating kin as kin, people will know they have a descent line and mutual affection will grow ever deeper—hence it is said that it can foster filial piety; when both loyalty and filial piety are complete, hence it is said that it can gather the clan together and broaden benevolence.

Alas! The ways of the world have declined, and the people are impoverished and scattered. The registered commoners of the fields [? 畒, for 氓] barely manage their household livelihoods, taking this alone to be sufficient cause for concern; talk of benevolence and righteousness and matters of long-term consequence are slighted in the village lanes, and even if one speaks to them of such things, they have no leisure for it. How could such customs ever be hoped for unless hereditary houses, great clans, and gentry elderssolemnly take the lead in guiding the common people? Now, the sun, moon, and stars have no conscious feelings, yet all take Heaven as their sovereign source; the hundred grains, grasses, and trees have no conscious feelings, yet all take the earth as their sovereign source; the differentiation of births and division into lineages are无穷 (endless), yet all take their ancestors as their sovereign source. Great indeed is the principle of the descent line! Yet its authority is unified under the Son of Heaven, while its institutional form is brought to completion by hereditary ministers. This is how wise kings reach the root of heavenly kinship, and how devoted [? 蓋, for 藎] ministers clarify the beauty of the human way, placing the world in harmonious prosperity and cordiality, so as to…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
庶幾復見三代之治者恃有此也可徒曰
宗法之廢也久矣遂聽其人之自相殘賊
也而莫爲之所哉而非諸生所知也
第五問
同考試官教諭周批治在人不在法此根極之
論亟錄之
考試官學正陳批陶心研慮計有餘矣
考試官學正王批議畫有裨時事
===
法可變乎曰過然則不可變乎曰過夫法
變亦過不變亦過嘵言而無所中有說乎
凡法久則必敝敝則民病病而不變過也
變之而不得其當當而不得其人行之無
益徒易之敝耳故曰變亦過也夫稷雖善
藝不能使禾冬生時也俞扁之方不必盡
用鄭衛之音不及輿諤宜也病變而藥不
變眾醫弗爲矣人皆曰秦開阡陌罷侯置
守壞先王之法不知封建之法壞則不得
punctuated:
庶幾復見三代之治者，恃有此也。可徒曰宗法之廢也久矣，遂聽其人之自相殘賊也，而莫爲之所哉？而非諸生所知也。

第五問

同考試官教諭周批：治在人不在法，此根極之論，亟錄之。
考試官學正陳批：陶心研慮，計有餘矣。
考試官學正王批：議畫有裨時事。

法可變乎？曰：過。然則不可變乎？曰：過。夫法變亦過，不變亦過，嘵言而無所中，有說乎？凡法久則必敝，敝則民病，病而不變，過也。變之而不得其當，當而不得其人，行之無益，徒易之敝耳，故曰變亦過也。夫稷雖善藝，不能使禾冬生，時也；俞、扁之方不必盡用，鄭、衛之音不及輿諤，宜也。病變而藥不變，眾醫弗爲矣。人皆曰秦開阡陌，罷侯置守，壞先王之法；不知封建之法壞，則不得
translation_en:
… thereby almost see once again the governance of the Three Dynasties, relies on this. Could one merely say that the lineage system has long been abolished, and thus allow people to mutually harm and destroy one another without making any provision for them? Yet this is beyond what a student could know.

Fifth Question

Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhou, comments: Governance lies in men, not in laws. This is an argument that reaches the fundamental root; record it at once.
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Chen, comments: Moulding the mind and refining deliberation, the plans are more than sufficient.
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang, comments: The discussions and plans are beneficial to current affairs.

Can laws be changed? One says: That is an error. Then can they not be changed? One says: That is an error. Now if changing the laws is an error, and not changing them is also an error—arguing clamorously without hitting the mark [?]—is there an explanation for this? Whenever laws endure for a long time, they inevitably deteriorate; when they deteriorate, the people suffer; when they suffer and no change is made, that is an error. Yet if one changes them without achieving what is appropriate, or if the change is appropriate but one does not obtain the right men, putting it into practice brings no benefit and merely exchanges one deterioration for another; therefore it is said that changing them is also an error. Now although Hou Ji 后稷 was skilled at sowing, he could not make grain grow in winter—this is a matter of seasonal timing. The prescriptions of Yu Fu 俞跗 and Bian Que 扁鵲 need not be used in every case, and the airs of Zheng 鄭 and Wei 衛 do not match the chants of the multitude [? 輿諤]—this is a matter of suitability. When an illness changes yet the medicine does not change, even ordinary physicians would not act thus. Everyone says that when Qin 秦 opened up the paths and ridges between fields, abolished the feudal lords, and established Commandery Governors, it destroyed the laws of the former kings; they do not realize that once the system of enfeoffment had broken down, one could not…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不盡為郡縣井田之法壞則不得不開阡
陌時與勢固然也秦之悖先王者固多此
未可以盡罪秦也今夫民情寒則欲火暑
則欲水燥則欲濕濕則欲燥寒暑燥濕相
反其於利民同也夫變法者亦以利民耳
然法無全利善變者審其所宜取其大利
略其小害譬之治病診其脉理調和其元
氣已其大痼而後一指之痛一癬之害是
故一不勝而再勝善戰者趋之矣利十而
===
害一良賈爭之矣十人言便而一人言不
便從十人矣害不勝利猶利也然法雖利
用法以人非其人不能成功今夫飴美食
也展禽得之以養老盜蹠得之以開閉鍵
飴非有異也故法一也得其人則展禽之
養不得其人則蹠蹻之飴而已矣夫禹貢
之制周官之法往代悠邈時移俗異不可
施之今日愚不敢復云矣
國家賦役之法十年若五年而一事歲差次
punctuated: 不盡為郡縣，井田之法壞，則不得不開阡陌，時與勢固然也。秦之悖先王者固多，此未可以盡罪秦也。今夫民情寒則欲火，暑則欲水，燥則欲濕，濕則欲燥；寒暑燥濕相反，其於利民同也。夫變法者，亦以利民耳。然法無全利，善變者審其所宜，取其大利，略其小害。譬之治病，診其脉理，調和其元氣，已其大痼，而後一指之痛、一癬之害。是故一不勝而再勝，善戰者趋之矣；利十而害一，良賈爭之矣；十人言便而一人言不便，從十人矣。害不勝利，猶利也。然法雖利，用法以人，非其人不能成功。今夫飴，美食也，展禽得之以養老，盜蹠得之以開閉鍵，飴非有異也。故法一也，得其人則展禽之養，不得其人則蹠蹻之飴而已矣。夫《禹貢》之制、《周官》之法，往代悠邈，時移俗異，不可施之今日，愚不敢復云矣。國家賦役之法，十年若五年而一事，歲差次
translation_en: …not be entirely converted into commanderies and counties; when the well-field system broke down, the field paths and ridges had to be opened up. Times and circumstances naturally made it so. There were indeed many ways in which Qin went against the former kings, but for this one cannot entirely blame Qin. Now, as for the feelings of the people: when cold, they desire fire; when hot, they desire water; when dry, they desire moisture; when wet, they desire dryness. Cold and heat, dryness and moisture are opposites, yet in benefiting the people they are the same. Changing the laws is likewise simply a matter of benefiting the people. Yet no law is wholly advantageous. Those skilled at reform examine what is appropriate, seizing the great benefits and overlooking the minor harms. It is like treating an illness: one diagnoses the patterns of the pulse, harmonizes the vital energy, and cures the major chronic malady, putting last the pain of a single finger or the harm of a single patch of ringworm. Therefore, if there is one defeat followed by two victories, a skilled commander will pursue it; if there are ten parts profit to one part harm, a good merchant will vie for it; if ten men say something is convenient and one man says it is inconvenient, one follows the ten men. When the harm does not outweigh the benefit, it is still a benefit. However, even if a law is beneficial, implementing the law depends on men; without the right men, it cannot succeed. Now, malt sugar is a fine food. When Zhan Qin (Liuxia Hui) obtained it, he used it to nourish the elderly; when Robber Zhi obtained it, he used it to unfasten bolts and locks. The malt sugar itself was no different. Thus, the law is one and the same: if you get the right men, it is the nourishment of Zhan Qin; if you do not get the right men, it is nothing more than the malt sugar of Robber Zhi and莊 Qiao (Zhuang Qiao). As for the institutions of the Tribute of Yu (Yu gong) and the laws of the Offices of Zhou (Zhou guan), those past eras are distant and remote; times have changed and customs differ, so they cannot be applied today, and this foolish one dares not speak of them again. In our dynasty's system of taxation and corvée labor, reviews are conducted once every ten or five years, and each year in sequence…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
里甲戶考其民數之盈縮以賦於民民得
番休孰謂不便民哉行之旣久豪民俠夫
私其吏胥變亂藏籍以逃征繇而又賦斂
繁多科求時出愚民不知吏因緣多取爲
姦閭閻秏矣有司患之於是請歲通計其
所入而總賦之戶頒之以所賦之數而罷
前法問之父老皆曰便百姓人人知所宜
入當數而止一約法畫一吏牘大損而狙
公之弊巳二豪猾不得規走輕重而賦役
===
均三公家易催征四子弟得罷歸農五胥
隸受其直於官不得多取六此六者今法
之利也其言不便者諸供億悉在官官率
取之市人或給之直不當又百姓巳罷歸
有私役之者所頒賦數間爲吏所匿山谷
窮民不能盡見因而多賦之蓋聞之人言
云然今上官督之密吏凜凜奉法事恐不
然卽有之可百邑之一二邑中數戶而止
耳然此非法之弊也謂宜博選良吏而諸
punctuated: 里甲戶，考其民數之盈縮，以賦於民，民得番休，孰謂不便民哉？行之旣久，豪民俠夫私其吏胥，變亂藏籍以逃征繇；而又賦斂繁多，科求時出，愚民不知，吏因緣多取爲姦，閭閻秏矣。有司患之，於是請歲通計其所入而總賦之，戶頒之以所賦之數，而罷前法。問之父老，皆曰便：百姓人人知所宜入，當數而止，一；約法畫一，吏牘大損，而狙公之弊巳，二；豪猾不得規走輕重，而賦役均，三；公家易催征，四；子弟得罷歸農，五；胥隸受其直於官，不得多取，六。此六者，今法之利也。其言不便者：諸供億悉在官，官率取之市人，或給之直不當；又百姓巳罷歸，有私役之者；所頒賦數，間爲吏所匿，山谷窮民不能盡見，因而多賦之。蓋聞之人言云然。今上官督之密，吏凜凜奉法，事恐不然；卽有之，可百邑之一二，邑中數戶而止耳。然此非法之弊也，謂宜博選良吏，而諸
translation_en: …the lijia households, examining the increase and decrease of their population figures in order to levy taxes and service on the people. The people were able to take turns resting—who could say this was not convenient for the people? Yet after it had been practiced for a long time, powerful commoners and local toughs colluded privately with the subofficial clerks, altering and throwing into confusion the stored registers in order to evade tax and corvée. Moreover, taxes and exactions became numerous and varied, and extra levies were frequently imposed. The ignorant people did not know what was due, so the clerks took advantage of the situation to extract more and commit fraud, and the village communities were exhausted. The authorities were troubled by this, and thereupon requested that each year a comprehensive calculation be made of what was to be paid in, levying it as a single combined sum, distributing to each household a notice of the amount it was to pay, and abolishing the former method. When one asks the elders about it, they all say it is convenient: first, each and every one of the common people knows what they ought to pay in, and stops once the proper amount is met; second, the simplified rules are uniform, official paperwork is greatly reduced, and the abuses of crafty manipulation are ended; third, the powerful and cunning cannot scheme to shift burdens between light and heavy, so taxes and labor services are equalized; fourth, it is easy for the state to press for and collect taxes; fifth, the young men are released from service and able to return to farming; sixth, clerks and runners receive their wages from the government and cannot extract extra payments. These six points are the advantages of the present method. As for those who say it is inconvenient: all provisioning and supplies now rest entirely with the officials, who generally procure them from market merchants and sometimes pay them an inadequate price; furthermore, although the common people have been released to return home, there are still some who privately press them into service; and the notices of tax amounts distributed are occasionally concealed by the clerks, so that poor people in mountain valleys cannot all see them, and the clerks take the opportunity to over-assess them. Such, at least, is what one hears people say. Yet today higher officials supervise the matter closely, and subofficials observe the law in fearful awe, so I suspect things are not actually so; even if such abuses do occur, they amount to perhaps one or two counties out of a hundred, and no more than a few households within a county. However, this is not a flaw of the method itself. I would say that we ought to broadly select good officials, and that the various…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
分部使者與其郡長吏嚴察之則其所捄
也又歳郡縣傜賦悉從所司主賦者考而
書其數頒之簿書上下當留時日有煩細
之病宜令諸郡各審所部賦書而上之司
賦覆覈之轉請得報行之便
國家天下土田十歳而一籍戸進退之以登
民租其初亦稱便焉自賦役繁倍貧人之
産漸入富室畝稅不相當豪民黠吏陰移
其田稅遁之絶籍負之蚩氓幻不可詰又
===
水濱之民田地亡沒而供不毛之賦若田
賦本重懸致殊科一畝之田而輸一釜者
民以大困而號不均於是有司言均田之
利吏行丈量計其畝辨其壤之上下以輕
重其稅蓋以一邑之土受一邑之稅可使
戸無羨田人無虛賦豪民無所匿其奸而
貧人解於重負田賦旣定徵發不煩又利
公家便矣顧計必屬之良吏乃可施行卽
令得良吏又安能一一履畝而親之此其
punctuated:
分部使者與其郡長吏嚴察之，則其所捄也。又歳郡縣傜賦，悉從所司主賦者考而書其數頒之，簿書上下當留時日，有煩細之病。宜令諸郡各審所部賦書，而上之司賦覆覈之，轉請得報行之便。
國家天下土田，十歳而一籍，戸進退之，以登民租，其初亦稱便焉。自賦役繁倍，貧人之産漸入富室，畝稅不相當，豪民黠吏陰移其田稅，遁之絶籍，負之蚩氓，幻不可詰。又水濱之民，田地亡沒而供不毛之賦；若田賦本重，懸致殊科，一畝之田而輸一釜者。民以大困，而號不均。於是有司言均田之利，吏行丈量，計其畝，辨其壤之上下，以輕重其稅。蓋以一邑之土，受一邑之稅，可使戸無羨田，人無虛賦，豪民無所匿其奸，而貧人解於重負；田賦旣定，徵發不煩，又利公家，便矣。顧計必屬之良吏，乃可施行；卽令得良吏，又安能一一履畝而親之？此其
translation_en:
… regional circuit commissioners and the prefectural chief administrators strictly inspect them, that is how it may be remedied. Furthermore, every year the labor services and taxes of the prefectures and counties are all examined by the fiscal officials of the competent authorities, who write down the quotas and promulgate them; as the registers pass back and forth between superior and subordinate offices, they inevitably take up time, suffering from the defect of cumbersome pettiness. Instead, each prefecture should be ordered to review the tax registers of its own jurisdiction and submit them to the fiscal commissioner to verify and recheck; once forwarded for approval and a reply is received, putting them into effect will be convenient.

As for the lands of the Empire under our Dynasty, every ten years a register is compiled, upgrading or downgrading households so as to record the people's taxes; in the beginning this too was praised as convenient. Since taxes and corvée have multiplied, the property of poor people has gradually passed into wealthy households, so that acreage and tax no longer correspond. Overbearing commoners and cunning clerks secretly shift their land taxes, hiding them under extinct household registrations or saddling them upon ignorant commoners, with deceptions impossible to investigate. Moreover, for people along the watersides, their fields have been washed away and yet they still pay taxes on barren nothingness; or where the land tax was originally heavy, disparities have led to extreme assessments, such that a single mu of land pays a whole fu [six-dou measure] of grain. The people are thus in great distress and cry out against the inequity. Thereupon the authorities spoke of the benefits of equalizing land (juntian): officials carry out cadastral surveys, calculate the acreage, and distinguish the upper and lower grades of soil in order to make the taxes lighter or heavier accordingly. Indeed, by making the land of an entire county bear the tax of that entire county, one can ensure that households have no unrecorded surplus fields and individuals pay no baseless taxes; overbearing commoners have nowhere to hide their fraud, and the poor are relieved of heavy burdens; once the land tax is fixed, collection is not troublesome, and it also benefits the state—convenient indeed! Yet the plan must be entrusted to upright officials before it can be carried out; and even supposing one obtains upright officials, how could they personally tread every single mu to inspect it? Among these …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
中寧無豪民猾胥相倚爲市以高下其手
而盈縮其數倒置其壤則者乎或不肖之
吏馮法喜怒以快其私臆矣而其弊旣已
見矣又匹夫匹婦傭竭其筋骨誅斥甌簍
於窮谷之隈絶澗之濱以旦夕糊其口者
今皆籍而賦之矣此其初非本賦籍也且
幾何而幷舉之使無所置其錐若是苛也
然此皆吏奉職之過也愚以謂諸言均田
者宜詳見父老咨其利病其無大困於公
===
私者已不可已者屬良吏謹奉行之與之
約諸前所云占田不實者則壤不當者若
吏胥爲奸及擾民者謹督察之不得有一
焉有卽其害百於已矣不可也吏者民之
師帥諸爲吏者宜一以孔子爲師孔子曰
道之以政齊之以刑民免而無耻道之以
德齊之以禮有耻且格又曰君子學道則
愛人小人學道則易使也然而吏治一切
未聞有以禮導民者何其故世俗卑卑沿
punctuated:
中寧無豪民猾胥相倚爲市，以高下其手而盈縮其數，倒置其壤則者乎？或不肖之吏，馮法喜怒，以快其私臆矣，而其弊旣已見矣。又匹夫匹婦，傭竭其筋骨，誅斥甌簍於窮谷之隈、絶澗之濱，以旦夕糊其口者，今皆籍而賦之矣。此其初非本賦籍也，且幾何而幷舉之，使無所置其錐，若是苛也！然此皆吏奉職之過也。愚以謂諸言均田者，宜詳見父老，咨其利病；其無大困於公私者已，不可已者，屬良吏謹奉行之。與之約：諸前所云占田不實者，則壤不當者，若吏胥爲奸及擾民者，謹督察之，不得有一焉。有卽其害百於已矣，不可也。
吏者，民之師帥；諸爲吏者，宜一以孔子爲師。孔子曰：「道之以政，齊之以刑，民免而無耻；道之以德，齊之以禮，有耻且格。」又曰：「君子學道則愛人，小人學道則易使也。」然而吏治一切，未聞有以禮導民者，何？其故世俗卑卑，沿
translation_en:
… midst of this, how could there not be powerful commoners and cunning subofficial functionaries colluding to make deals, manipulating the measurements to inflate or reduce the figures and inverting the soil-grade classifications? Or else unworthy officials rely on the law to vent their pleasure or anger and gratify their private whims—and the abuses of this have already become apparent. Furthermore, ordinary men and women who exhaust their sinews and bones as hired laborers, clearing away scrub and cultivating tiny elevated plots in the corners of remote valleys or along the banks of precipitous ravines just to eke out a living from day to day, now all have their plots registered and taxed. Originally, these were not part of the basic tax registers; moreover, how much can they possibly yield that they should be swept up together, leaving the poor nowhere even to stick an awl, with such harshness! Yet all of these are faults in how officials carry out their duties. In my humble opinion, regarding all proposals to equalize land taxes, one ought to meet thoroughly with the local elders to inquire into the advantages and disadvantages. Where there is no great distress to public or private interests, let the matter rest; where action cannot be avoided, entrust upright officials to implement it carefully. Make a strict covenant with them: regarding the aforementioned cases of false reporting of landholdings, improper grading of soil, or officials and clerks committing fraud and harassing the people, carefully supervise and investigate them so that not a single instance is allowed. If even one occurs, its harm will be a hundred times worse than leaving things alone; it must not be permitted.

Officials are the teachers and leaders of the people; all who serve as officials ought exclusively to take Confucius (Kongzi) as their teacher. Confucius said: "Lead them by means of government regulations and keep them in order by means of punishments, and the people will evade them and have no sense of shame. Lead them by means of virtue and keep them in order by means of ritual propriety, and they will have a sense of shame and moreover correct themselves." He also said: "When the gentleman learns the Way, he loves the people; when the small man learns the Way, he is easy to employ." And yet in administrative governance across the board, one never hears of anyone guiding the people through ritual propriety—why is this? The reason is that worldly customs are base and petty, following …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
襲故常而莫之知卽知者又見謂闊遠未
遑也故曰下士聞道大笑之此之謂也曩
吾見郡縣有設爲鄕約敎民者嘗過其里
閭見其父老子弟衣冠言動率循循能遵
用其敎矣故知敎不可已民在所道當少
漸積效實耳以爲虛文而罷之謂其不可
猝道而棄之然則禮敎之興無時巳
高皇帝著爲訓諭歲時令長老諷誦以鐸徇於
里巷固此道也宜令郡縣因
===
高帝訓辭稍爲之約擇里中賢者爲之長而禮
焉使月旦朢集其里之少長敎之孝弟德
義習以禮讓察其善否某也善指其事而
揚之某也過指其事而敎之如此可使人
人自勸重爲不善而俗大創也而又稍以
朱子所著冠婚喪祭儀禮與父老約行之
行之不止將斌斌禮義之俗太平之跡可
睹矣第恐吏不暇行不實又重姍咲耳古
者敎化行而法令備民出入相友守朢相
punctuated: 襲故常，而莫之知；卽知者，又見謂闊遠未遑也。故曰：「下士聞道，大笑之。」此之謂也。曩吾見郡縣有設爲鄕約敎民者，嘗過其里閭，見其父老子弟，衣冠言動，率循循能遵用其敎矣。故知敎不可已，民在所道，當少漸積效實耳。以爲虛文而罷之，謂其不可猝道而棄之，然則禮敎之興，無時巳。高皇帝著爲訓諭，歲時令長老諷誦，以鐸徇於里巷，固此道也。宜令郡縣因高帝訓辭，稍爲之約，擇里中賢者爲之長而禮焉。使月旦、朢集其里之少長，敎之孝弟德義，習以禮讓，察其善否：某也善，指其事而揚之；某也過，指其事而敎之。如此，可使人人自勸，重爲不善，而俗大創也。而又稍以朱子所著冠、婚、喪、祭儀禮，與父老約行之。行之不止，將斌斌禮義之俗、太平之跡可睹矣。第恐吏不暇、行不實，又重姍咲耳。古者敎化行而法令備，民出入相友，守朢相
translation_en:
…follow old routines without understanding this; and even those who do understand regard it as impractical and remote, something for which they have no leisure. Thus it is said: "When a petty scholar hears of the Way, he laughs loudly at it." This is what is meant. Formerly, I saw prefectures and counties that established community compacts (xiangyue) to instruct the people. When I once passed through their villages and neighborhoods, I saw that the elders and youths, in their dress and demeanor, speech and conduct, generally followed in an orderly manner and were able to abide by their teachings. From this I know that instruction must not cease; the people respond to how they are guided, and one need only gradually accumulate actual results over time. If one dismisses it as empty formality and abolishes it, or claims that the people cannot be guided all at once and abandons it, then there will never be a time when ritual teaching flourishes.

When the Exalted Emperor (Gao Huangdi, i.e., Emperor Taizu) composed his instructive edicts and ordered that at seasonal intervals the elders should recite them and go through the village lanes with a wooden-tongued bell to proclaim them, it was assuredly this very Way. Prefectures and counties should be ordered to take the Exalted Emperor's instructive words and formulate concise community compacts based upon them, selecting worthy men within the villages to serve as leaders and treating them with ritual courtesy. Have them assemble the young and old of their village on the first and fifteenth days of each month to instruct them in filial piety, fraternal submission, moral virtue, and righteousness, accustoming them to ritual propriety and yielding, and examining their good and bad conduct: when a certain person does good, point out his deed and praise him; when a certain person errs, point out his deed and instruct him. In this way, everyone can be made to encourage himself, be reluctant to do wrong, and customs will be greatly reformed. Furthermore, one should gradually take the rituals for capping, weddings, funerals, and sacrifices written by Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹) and agree with the elders to put them into practice. If this is practiced without cease, then refined customs of ritual and righteousness and the signs of Great Peace will be seen. I only fear that officials will claim they have no leisure, that execution will lack substance, and that it will once again invite heavy ridicule.

In antiquity, moral transformation was carried out and laws and ordinances were complete; the people befriended one another in their comings and goings, and in keeping watch and ward they mutually…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
助故風俗美厚無盜賊之患今天下憂於
盜矣夫盜賊者此其人不自天降自地出
也由四方遊俠得容於鄉里而吾遊惰暴
桀子弟得出而爲之黨也及於緩急又不
相救則保甲之法不行也宋王介甫嘗爲
保甲之法其法十家爲保五十家爲大保
十大保爲都保而擇衆所服者爲都保正
若副聽其自置弓矢習武藝而自相糾察
摘其奸宄故里閈不敢犯禁觸罪雖有盜
===
===
蹠企足之奸不得逞焉安石新法病民而
玆法良善實可施行今世多倣行之然上
下相蒙虛文耳無益於俗亦未徧行也宜
如其法立之長使戶計其丁男書之而時
察其出入以禁切其子弟且使姦人無所
容否者十家坐之約里中盜至衆共救之
不如約者告于官當以罪如是而姦安從
生何憂盜乎而愚見今之保甲法不然直
榜之門爲官長容過則藏之矣故曰在人
punctuated: 助，故風俗美厚，無盜賊之患。今天下憂於盜矣。夫盜賊者，此其人不自天降、自地出也。由四方遊俠得容於鄉里，而吾遊惰暴桀子弟得出而爲之黨也；及於緩急，又不相救，則保甲之法不行也。宋王介甫嘗爲保甲之法，其法：十家爲保，五十家爲大保，十大保爲都保，而擇衆所服者爲都保正若副。聽其自置弓矢，習武藝，而自相糾察，摘其奸宄。故里閈不敢犯禁觸罪，雖有盜蹠企足之奸，不得逞焉。安石新法病民，而玆法良善，實可施行。今世多倣行之，然上下相蒙，虛文耳，無益於俗，亦未徧行也。宜如其法，立之長，使戶計其丁男書之，而時察其出入，以禁切其子弟，且使姦人無所容；否者，十家坐之。約里中盜至，衆共救之；不如約者，告于官，當以罪。如是而姦安從生？何憂盜乎？而愚見今之保甲法不然，直榜之門，爲官長容，過則藏之矣。故曰：在人
translation_en: … assist one another, so customs were fine and generous, and there was no trouble from bandits and thieves. Today the empire is worried about bandits. Now, as for bandits and thieves, such people do not drop from heaven or spring from the earth. It is because wandering bravos from all quarters are tolerated within the rural communities, and our own idle, lazy, violent, and unruly youths are able to go out and form gangs with them; and when an emergency arises, people do not come to one another's rescue—this is because the tithing-based mutual security system (baojia) is not put into practice. In the Song dynasty, Wang Jiefu [Wang Anshi 王安石] once instituted the mutual security system. Under his law, ten households formed a guard (bao), fifty households formed a large guard (dabao), and ten large guards formed a superior guard (dubao), and those whom the multitude respected were chosen as Superior Guard Head (dubao zheng) or Deputy (fu). They were permitted to procure their own bows and arrows, practice martial arts, mutually police one another, and expose villains and traitors. Therefore, the village neighborhoods dared not violate prohibitions or incur punishment, and even if there were villains standing on tiptoe in eagerness to be like Robber Zhi, they could not get their way. Anshi's New Policies harmed the people, yet this law was good and sound, and can truly be carried out. In the present age it is often imitated and practiced, yet superiors and inferiors deceive one another—it is mere empty paperwork, of no benefit to customs, nor is it universally practiced. We ought to follow his method, establish heads for them, have each household count its adult males and register them in writing, and periodically inspect their comings and goings in order to strictly restrain their youths and moreover leave wicked people nowhere to hide; if they fail to do so, all ten households should be held collectively liable. Make a compact in the village that when bandits arrive, everyone will jointly rescue one another; those who do not abide by the compact should be reported to the officials and sentenced for the offense. If this is done, from where could villainy arise? What worry would there be about bandits? Yet in my humble observation, the mutual security system of today is not like this: they merely post a placard on the gate to put on a show for the presiding officials, and once the officials pass by, they put it away. Therefore it is said: it depends on the men…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也崔寔曰教化者治平之粱肉刑法者止
病之藥石世皆善其言然愚以為粱肉雖
美必饜飫而後能養人藥石雖良不浸灌
不能已病豈可未啖一臠而謂粱肉無補
甫甞一餌而輒求藥石之功乎夫教化法
度亦非一臠一餌之功也計在必行而成
於積久自古及今未有不然者也商君有
言民不可與慮始而可與樂成昔甞過之
今迺知其切於事情也徒鞅斷於刻覈之
===
術耳假令斷於帝王之道豈足過哉書生
之言惟執事擇焉
punctuated: 也。崔寔曰：「教化者，治平之粱肉；刑法者，止病之藥石。」世皆善其言。然愚以為粱肉雖美，必饜飫而後能養人；藥石雖良，不浸灌不能已病。豈可未啖一臠而謂粱肉無補，甫甞一餌而輒求藥石之功乎？夫教化法度，亦非一臠一餌之功也。計在必行，而成於積久，自古及今，未有不然者也。商君有言：「民不可與慮始，而可與樂成。」昔甞過之，今迺知其切於事情也。徒鞅斷於刻覈之術耳，假令斷於帝王之道，豈足過哉？書生之言，惟執事擇焉。
translation_en: … [Thus it is said that it depends on the people]. Cui Shi (崔寔) said: "Moral transformation is the fine grain and meat of an era of peace and order; penal law is the medicine andacupuncture stone for curing illness." The world all praises his words. Yet I foolishly consider that although fine grain and meat are delicious, one must eat one's fill before they can nourish a person; although medicine and stone needles are effective, unless they steep and pervade the body they cannot cure an illness. How could one before even tasting a single slice of meat claim that fine grain and meat offer no nourishment, or having barely tasted a single dose immediately demand the efficacy of medicine and stone needles? Now, moral transformation and legal institutions are likewise not matters achieved by a single slice of meat or a single dose of medicine. The plan lies in resolute implementation, and success comes from long accumulation; from antiquity to the present, it has never been otherwise. Lord Shang (商君, Shang Yang 商鞅) had a saying: "The people cannot be consulted at the beginning of an undertaking, but one can rejoice with them in its completion." In the past I used to fault this remark, but now I realize how closely it hits the reality of affairs. It is merely that Shang Yang applied this decisiveness to the techniques of harshness and severity; had he applied such decisiveness to the Way of the Five Emperors and Three Kings, how would it merit criticism? Such are the words of a mere scholar; may Your Excellency select from them as you see fit.

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄後序
皇上垂拱之七年己卯秋八月浙
江舉文學弟子九十人于鄉
令與計偕燕而爲之勸駕節
具官校事用申告于多士曰
皇皇乎文哉綜統道德威儀
人倫經緯羣物潤色專與無
===
所不貫者乎徒腴辭騖說云
爾哉余讀典謨訓誥及於王
風雅頌之篇盖喟然嘆曰大
哉唐虞三代之文固若此乎
夫其功業登閎與辭命並爛
焉故仲尼之稱陶唐曰巍乎
成功煥乎其文章而美周之
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄後序

皇上垂拱之七年己卯，秋八月，浙江舉文學弟子九十人于鄉，令與計偕。燕而爲之勸駕，節具官校事，用申告于多士曰：皇皇乎文哉！綜統道德、威儀、人倫，經緯羣物，潤色專與，無所不貫者乎？徒腴辭騖說云爾哉？余讀典、謨、訓、誥，及於王風、雅、頌之篇，盖喟然嘆曰：大哉！唐、虞、三代之文，固若此乎！夫其功業登閎，與辭命並爛焉。故仲尼之稱陶唐曰：「巍乎成功，煥乎其文章！」而美周之
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn of the jimao year, the seventh year of His Majesty's tranquil reign [1579], Zhejiang selected ninety literary disciples in the Provincial Examination and ordered them to travel to the capital with the tribute accounts [for the Metropolitan Examination]. A banquet was held to send them off on their journey, at which Jie [?], holding office and having examined the papers, addressed a parting admonition to the many gentlemen, saying:

How magnificent is literary culture (wen)! Does it not synthesize and unify moral virtue, dignified demeanor, and human relationships, weave together the myriad things, and give luster to imperial decrees and institutions [?], penetrating everything without exception? Or is it merely a matter of florid phrases and extravagant theories? When I read the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements [of the Book of Documents], as well as the Airs of the Royal Domain, Odes, and Hymns [of the Book of Odes], I cannot help but sigh in admiration and say: How great! Was the literary culture of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties truly like this! Indeed, their achievements and enterprises reached lofty heights and shone forth alongside their state pronouncements and commands. Thus Confucius praised Yao of陶唐 (Taotang), saying, "How lofty were his achievements! How resplendent were his cultural institutions (wenzhang)!" And in praising the literary culture of the Zhou…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
文以爲郁郁思深哉其指也
今上聰明文武右賢勸學尊仲尼
之敎明王道之途
臨御以來屢申使臣廣
勅功令放逐浮淫而奏雅筩海內
學士彬彬嚮風意者靈書八
會玉劵十華其當之乎夫四
===
方之風卽四方薦紳先生能
言之矣節辱聘于子大邦言
大邦乎吳越山川鉅麗禹所
從會玉帛誕敷文命者也故
太史公司馬遷弱冠而南遊
上會稽探禹穴以大肆其文
傳述至于今其著世家言咨
punctuated: 文以爲郁郁，思深哉其指也！今上聰明文武，右賢勸學，尊仲尼之敎，明王道之途。臨御以來，屢申使臣，廣勅功令，放逐浮淫，而奏雅筩。海內學士，彬彬嚮風，意者靈書八會、玉劵十華，其當之乎？夫四方之風，卽四方薦紳先生能言之矣。節辱聘于子大邦，言大邦乎？吳越山川鉅麗，禹所從會玉帛、誕敷文命者也。故太史公司馬遷弱冠而南遊，上會稽，探禹穴，以大肆其文，傳述至于今。其著《世家》言，咨…
translation_en: …culture as "rich and glorious." How profound is the meaning of these words! His Present Majesty, intelligent and perceptive, accomplished in both civil and martial arts, honors the worthy and encourages learning, revering the teachings of Confucius (Zhongni 仲尼) and illuminating the path of the Kingly Way. Since ascending the throne, he has repeatedly instructed his envoys and broadly promulgated the examination regulations, banishing superficiality and extravagance while advancing elegant standards. Scholars throughout the realm, refined and cultivated, turn toward this moral wind; perhaps this truly matches the "numinous writings of the eight convergences" and the "jade tallies of the ten splendors"? Now, as for the customs of the four quarters, the gentry and elders of those regions can speak of them themselves. Having had the honor of being invited to serve in your great province, shall I, Jie 節, speak of this great province? The mountains and rivers of Wu 吳 and Yue 越 are vast and magnificent; this is where Yu 禹 assembled the lords with their jade and silk and broadly spread his civilizing mandate. Thus, when the Grand Historian Sima Qian 司馬遷 came of age at twenty and traveled south, he ascended Mount Kuaiji 會稽 and explored the Cave of Yu to give full rein to his literary power, which has been transmitted down to the present day. In writing his Hereditary Houses (Shijia 世家), he sighed in admiration…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
嗟於越以爲有禹之遺烈焉
何其盛也
高皇帝受天命光明函夏
定鼎金陵則吳越之間屬之
畿輔覲光文德斯亦曩時東南
鎬洛也
列聖纘承滲漉鴻涌及乎嘉隆之
===
際繄我
今上至章顯矣今觀其謠俗無論
六藝之士即四民者類無不
勱業務時以脩其能而著名
於天下工斲巧善器商賈善
計然之策農力田豐年善獲
歲時杭秫之租山海之利錦
punctuated: 嗟於越，以爲有禹之遺烈焉，何其盛也！高皇帝受天命，光明函夏，定鼎金陵，則吳越之間，屬之畿輔，覲光文德，斯亦曩時東南鎬洛也。列聖纘承，滲漉鴻涌，及乎嘉、隆之際，繄我今上，至章顯矣。今觀其謠俗，無論六藝之士，即四民者，類無不勱業務時，以脩其能，而著名於天下。工斲巧善器，商賈善計然之策，農力田，豐年善獲，歲時杭秫之租，山海之利，錦
translation_en:
…sighed in admiration over Yue, considering that it possessed the lingering illustriousness of Yu. How flourishing it was!

When the Exalted Emperor (Gao Huangdi, i.e., Emperor Taizu) received the Mandate of Heaven, bringing brilliance to all China and establishing the imperial capital at Jinling (Nanjing), the region between Wu and Yue became attached to the metropolitan area. Beholding the radiance of his civilizing virtue, this too was the Hao and Luo of the southeast in bygone days. Successive sacred emperors carried on the line, their grace soaking down and surging forth, down to the transition between the Jiajing (1522–1566) and Longqing (1567–1572) reigns, and truly under our reigning Sovereign, it has reached utmost splendor and manifestation.

Now, observing its folk songs and customs: not to mention the scholars of the Six Arts, even among the four categories of people as a whole, there is none who does not strive at his occupation and seize the season to cultivate his abilities and make his name known throughout the empire. Artisans carve skillfully and make fine implements; merchants excel at the strategies of Jiran; farmers work hard in the fields and reap fine harvests in years of plenty. At the seasonal times of the year, the taxes of non-glutinous [reading 杭 as 秔] and glutinous grain, the profits of mountains and seas, and the precious brocades…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
繡機組之貴相屬以貢於
京師而給縣官下者紛詭羨溢
流布四方以共里閭之用士
翩翩然喜文學率循其父兄
長老之教若饑渴之於食飲
也三歲而貢貢者九十人大
比都試之中
===
制科者常五十人語曰世治百
里而得一賢士比肩也賢者
若此其難也而何越之多才
也
主上以謂諸生吾養之庠序數十
年而拔之數千萬人之中皆
瑰瑋醇茂之士也吾為布之
punctuated: 繡機組之貴，相屬以貢於京師，而給縣官；下者紛詭羨溢，流布四方，以共里閭之用。士翩翩然喜文學，率循其父兄長老之教，若饑渴之於食飲也。三歲而貢，貢者九十人；大比都試之中制科者，常五十人。語曰：「世治百里而得一賢，士比肩也。」賢者若此其難也，而何越之多才也！主上以謂：「諸生吾養之庠序數十年，而拔之數千萬人之中，皆瑰瑋醇茂之士也。吾為布之
translation_en: …and the prized products of brocade, embroidery, loom-work, and silk cords follow one after another as tribute to the capital to supply the imperial government; while goods of the next grade, varied, wondrous, and overflowing in abundance, circulate throughout the four quarters to meet the needs of local communities. The scholars, refined and spirited, delight in literature and learning, following the teachings of their fathers, elder brothers, and elders just as the hungry and thirsty crave food and drink. Every three years they are presented for the examination, and those presented number ninety men; at the great triennial Metropolitan Examination, those who pass the imperial examination regularly number around fifty men. The saying goes: "When the world is well-governed, if one worthy is found in every hundred li, scholars are standing shoulder to shoulder." Worthies are thus so difficult to come by—how is it, then, that Yue [Zhejiang] has so many men of talent! His Majesty considers: "These students whom I have nurtured in the local schools for decades, and selected from among tens of thousands of people, are all extraordinary, pure, and flourishing scholars. I shall place them…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
中外大者規畫小者錯事賢
知輻湊眾職咸得吾何憂天
下乎惡謂多也豈其使數十
人者被服饜祿以贍妻子徼
榮涂巷而已哉則已多矣諸
生知梓人乎梓人畫宮于堵
依而搆之大廈旣成不謬尺
===
寸其墨度素定也夫士稱引
古今畫當世亦梓人之圖室
也惟諸生察
上意念所以報
上德者無謬今所稱說寕於梓人
卽
國家甚幸於是九十人者前曰
punctuated: 中外，大者規畫，小者錯事，賢知輻湊，眾職咸得，吾何憂天下乎？惡謂多也！豈其使數十人者，被服饜祿以贍妻子、徼榮涂巷而已哉？則已多矣。」諸生知梓人乎？梓人畫宮于堵，依而搆之，大廈旣成，不謬尺寸，其墨度素定也。夫士稱引古今，畫當世，亦梓人之圖室也。惟諸生察上意，念所以報上德者，無謬今所稱說，寕於梓人，卽國家甚幸。於是九十人者前曰：
translation_en:
… both at the court and in the provinces: those in major offices formulate grand plans, while those in lesser posts attend to specific affairs. With worthy and wise men gathering from all directions like spokes at a hub, and every office finding its right man, what worry should I have for the realm? How could that be called too many! Could the intention merely be to let several dozen men wear official robes and gorge on salaries to support their wives and children and seek glory in the streets and lanes? In that case, they would indeed be too many."

Do you students know of the master builder? The master builder draws the plan of a palace upon a wall and constructs it accordingly; when the great edifice is completed, it does not err by a foot or an inch, because his inked measurements were settled beforehand. Now, when scholars cite antiquity and the present to map out plans for their own age, it is just like the master builder drafting a house. May you students discern His Majesty's intention and reflect on how to repay His Majesty's grace: do not depart from what you have professed today, and be no less true to your plans than the master builder; then the state will be most fortunate indeed.

Thereupon the ninety men stepped forward and said: …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
唯唯謹受教願因卒教諸生
節曰然
國家以六籍教士而以六籍取
之子佩服六籍足矣余聞之
師云潔淨精微易教也疏通
知遠書教也溫柔敦厚詩教
也恭儉莊敬禮教也廣博易
===
良樂教也屬辭比事春秋教
也夫六教者非徒設其辭而
已也嫻其辭固將有以服之
其身也士服此六教者廼可
以列於儒者之林矣是故喬
宇委瑣小言詹詹非易教也
繁塞苛繞政事糺棼非書教
punctuated: 「唯唯，謹受教。願因卒教諸生。」節曰：「然。國家以六籍教士，而以六籍取之，子佩服六籍足矣。余聞之師云：『潔淨精微，《易》教也；疏通知遠，《書》教也；溫柔敦厚，《詩》教也；恭儉莊敬，《禮》教也；廣博易良，《樂》教也；屬辭比事，《春秋》教也。』夫六教者，非徒設其辭而已也；嫻其辭，固將有以服之其身也。士服此六教者，廼可以列於儒者之林矣。是故喬宇委瑣，小言詹詹，非《易》教也；繁塞苛繞，政事糺棼，非《書》教…
translation_en:
…“Yes, yes, we respectfully receive your instruction, and we hope that you will go on to instruct us students to the end.”

Jie [I] said: “Indeed. The Dynasty educates scholars through the Six Classics and selects them through the Six Classics; for you to take the Six Classics to heart and put them into practice is quite enough. I have heard from my teacher the saying: ‘Purity and subtlety are the teaching of the Changes (Yi); broad comprehension and far-reaching vision are the teaching of the Documents (Shu); gentleness and sincere thickness of character are the teaching of the Odes (Shi); reverence, thrift, gravity, and respect are the teaching of the Rites (Li); breadth and easy goodness are the teaching of the Music (Yue); and connecting words and comparing events are the teaching of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu).’

“Now these six teachings are not merely a matter of setting forth their words; being well-versed in their words surely means that one intends to embody and practice them in one’s own person. Only when a scholar practices these six teachings can he take his place in the forest of true Confucians. Therefore, being詭-minded [喬宇] and petty, indulging in endless trivial chatter, is not the teaching of the Changes; being bogged down in pedantic minutiae and harsh complexities, throwing administrative affairs into tangled confusion, is not the teaching of the Documents…”…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也齪齪淺中色同意忌非詩
敎也恣睢佚嫚吏固辟違非
禮敎也懁而賊盭和則燕比
非樂敎也是非汶汶倒植臧
否非春秋之敎也故士湛思
竑議鉤玄發藻雲蒸霞變淵
浸川逝而原本道德歸之雅
===
馴六籍之華也言有量衡行
有繩軌內不媿其室外不負
其友祿而使之篤躬壹意以
奉
主上而脩先民之業六籍之質也
夫華諸生旣已采之矣而余
旣睹之矣此豈足當諸生乎
punctuated: 也；齪齪淺中，色同意忌，非《詩》敎也；恣睢佚嫚，吏固辟違，非《禮》敎也；懁而賊盭，和則燕比，非《樂》敎也；是非汶汶，倒植臧否，非《春秋》之敎也。故士湛思竑議，鉤玄發藻，雲蒸霞變，淵浸川逝，而原本道德，歸之雅馴，六籍之華也；言有量衡，行有繩軌，內不媿其室，外不負其友，祿而使之，篤躬壹意，以奉主上而脩先民之業，六籍之質也。夫華，諸生旣已采之矣，而余旣睹之矣，此豈足當諸生乎？
translation_en: … [Documents]. Being narrow-minded and shallow within, agreeing in countenance while harboring jealousy in the heart, is not the teaching of the Odes (Shi). Being willful, dissolute, and arrogant, stubborn in office and perverse in conduct [?], is not the teaching of the Rites (Li). Being急-tempered and maliciously perverse, or when harmonious, being overly familiar and partisan, is not the teaching of the Music (Yue). Blurring right and wrong in confusion, and inverting praise and blame, is not the teaching of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu). Therefore, when a scholar meditates deeply and argues grandly, probing the abstruse and putting forth literary flourishes—rising like clouds and shifting like rosy mists, soaking like deep pools and flowing on like rivers—yet roots it all in morality and virtue and brings it back to elegance and propriety, this is the flower of the Six Classics. When his words have measure and balance and his conduct follows the marking-line and the wheel-track, so that within the home he brings no shame to his household, and abroad he does not fail his friends; and when given emolument and official employment, he devotes himself earnestly and single-mindedly to serving the Sovereign above and cultivating the legacy of the worthy men of old—this is the substance of the Six Classics. Now as for the flower, you students have already gathered it, and I have already witnessed it. Yet how could this alone be enough to fulfill what is expected of you students? …

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
必且脩其質也諸生僂然曰
鄙儒今迺聞六籍之指廣大
矣請得退而自惟切磋究之
曰然未也將更進焉子曰繪
事後素傳曰衣錦尚絅惡其
文之著也故君子之道闇而
章文在中也今夫日其光全
===
===
乎內者也故晦明升降不失
其體月之光受之外者也故
盈虧燠寒狥乎時夫日陽道
也月陰道也知陰陽之道則
辨乎人矣是故迅霆揚颺者
氣蕩繁華蔓葉者實衰脩己
者務其根求士者在其內其
punctuated: 必且脩其質也。諸生僂然曰：「鄙儒今迺聞六籍之指，廣大矣！請得退而自惟，切磋究之。」曰：「然，未也，將更進焉。子曰：『繪事後素。』《傳》曰：『衣錦尚絅，惡其文之著也。』故君子之道，闇而章，文在中也。今夫日，其光全乎內者也，故晦明升降，不失其體；月之光，受之外者也，故盈虧燠寒，狥乎時。夫日，陽道也；月，陰道也。知陰陽之道，則辨乎人矣。是故迅霆揚颺者氣蕩，繁華蔓葉者實衰。脩己者務其根，求士者在其內。其
translation_en: … One must also cultivate their substance.” The students bowed respectfully and said, “Only now have we vulgar scholars heard the purport of the Six Classics—how vast and great it is! We beg leave to withdraw and reflect upon it ourselves, cutting and polishing to investigate it thoroughly.” I replied, “Indeed, but there is more; let us go further still. The Master said, ‘The business of painting comes after the plain groundwork.’ The Commentary says, ‘Over a brocade robe one adds a plain unlined garment, disliking the overly conspicuous display of its pattern.’ Thus the Way of the gentleman is hidden yet grows daily more illustrious, because his refinement lies within. Now consider the sun: its light is complete within itself, and thus through darkness and light, rising and setting, it never loses its substance. The light of the moon is received from without, and thus in waxing and waning, warmth and cold, it merely follows the seasons. The sun is the way of yang; the moon is the way of yin. When one understands the ways of yin and yang, one can discern men. Therefore, where there are swift thunderclaps andwhirling gales, the vital breath is dissipated; where there are luxuriant blossoms and sprawling leaves, the fruit withers. Those who cultivate themselves attend to the root; those who seek out scholars look to what is within. Let them…

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
無若秦鄭人昔秦伯嫁女艷
其媵娣晉人貴媵而賤公女
周客賣珠華其櫝鄭人買櫝
而還其珠夫飾其末而亡其
本是嬴伯之棄女也取其外
而遺其內是鄭人之買櫝也
仲尼不云乎聲色末也上天
===
之載無聲無臭至矣夫不大
聲色者固文王之所以爲文
也諸生聽之無曰是吾儕童
子所誦說耳夫庸言非卑也
嵬言非深也子反諸其身而
試以徵諸其人儻可信吾言
乎
punctuated: 無若秦、鄭人。昔秦伯嫁女，艷其媵娣，晉人貴媵而賤公女；周客賣珠，華其櫝，鄭人買櫝而還其珠。夫飾其末而亡其本，是嬴伯之棄女也；取其外而遺其內，是鄭人之買櫝也。仲尼不云乎：「聲色，末也。上天之載，無聲無臭，至矣。」夫不大聲色者，固文王之所以爲文也。諸生聽之，無曰：「是吾儕童子所誦說耳。」夫庸言非卑也，嵬言非深也，子反諸其身，而試以徵諸其人，儻可信吾言乎！
translation_en: …not be like the people of Qin and Zheng. In the past, when the Earl of Qin married off his daughter, he gorgeously adorned her accompanying maids and younger sisters, so that the people of Jin prized the maids and slighted the lord's daughter; when a merchant from Zhou sold a pearl, he lavishly decorated its casket, so that the man of Zheng bought the casket and returned the pearl. Now, to embellish the nonessential and lose sight of the fundamental—this is the Earl of Ying abandoning his daughter; to take the exterior and leave behind the interior—this is the man of Zheng buying the casket. Did Confucius not say: "Sound and appearance are nonessential. 'The workings of High Heaven have neither sound nor odor'—this is the ultimate!" Indeed, not making a great display of sound and appearance is precisely whereby King Wen was culturally accomplished (Wen). Listen to this, students, and do not say: "This is merely what we recited and talked about as boys." Ordinary words are not shallow, and lofty,奇異 words are not profound. If you reflect upon this within yourselves and try verifying it in others, perhaps you may find my words trustworthy!

title: 萬曆七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
湖廣承天府荆門州儒學學
正陳節謹序
punctuated: 湖廣承天府荆門州儒學學正陳節謹序。
translation_en: Respectfully prefaced by Chen Jie 陳節, Director of Studies (xuezheng) of the Confucian School of Jingmen Subprefecture, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang.
